problems.conjecture: Conjecture: read يَرْفَعِ (jussive in sequence) اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنكُمْ (Q. 58:11).

problems.issue: The chunk opens mid-sentence at a page turn: only the governed noun واسطة and its colon survive, with no governing preposition or verb. Translated as it stands (“intermediary:”); no beginning supplied.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the lost clause most likely read بلا واسطة / بغير واسطة (“without an intermediary”) — i.e. Allah taught Ādam directly, with no intermediary — but this is not recoverable from the chunk.

problems.arabic: "وَعَلَّمْنٰهُ مِن لَدَنا عِلماً)  /  "رَبِّ قَدَ اتَيْتَنِي ... الأَحَادِيثِ)
problems.issue: Unbalanced lemma delimiters: two Qurʾanic lemmata open with a double quotation mark and close with a round bracket. The lemma boundary is therefore editorial, not transmitted.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: both are complete lemmata whose closing quotation mark was OCR-read as „)“; the delimiter set in the printed page is probably uniform (“ … ”), and I have taken the span up to the bracket as the lemma.

problems.arabic: عُلِمْنا مَنطِقَ الطَّيْرِ  /  وَعَلَّمَكَ مَا لَمْ تَكْنْ تَعلَمْ  /  الْكِتَب وَالتَّوْرِيةَ  /  بِذَلكِ تلميذا
problems.issue: Pervasive vowel/letter corruption inside the lemmata and around them: عُلِمْنا for عُلِّمْنا (lost shadda), تَكْنْ for تَكُن, قَدَ for قَدْ, وَعَلَّمْتَنِىِ for وَعَلَّمْتَنِي, missing alif in الْكِتَب/التَّوْرِية, and a stray kasra on بِذَلكِ. The consonantal skeletons are legible, so each lemma was translated.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: all are OCR noise, not variant readings; the underlying lemmata are the standard ʿUthmānic texts of Q. 27:16, 4:113, 3:48 and 12:101 respectively.

problems.issue: Footnote numeral [9] sits inside the running text, immediately after the colon that introduces the seven items. Left in place as a separate run.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: it keys a page-foot note sourcing the saying to ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib; the note text is not in this chunk.

problems.arabic: العلم يحتاج الناس كلا إليه في دينهم
problems.issue: كلا is ungrammatical here as transmitted; the sentence also inverts the expected word order (يحتاج الناس كلا إليه). Rendered as “all people need it” without emending the Arabic.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: كلا stands for كلًّا (adverbial accusative) or, more likely, for كلّهم, the hāʾ-mīm having been lost in OCR.

problems.issue: Case endings corrupted in the Q. 36:58 lemma: رَحِيمٌ (nominative) for رَحِيمٍ, and سَلَمٌ for سَلَامٌ with the alif lost. Translated from the standard text.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: OCR damage to the vowel layer only; the lemma is سَلَامٌ قَوْلًا مِن رَبِّ رَحِيمٍ.

problems.arabic: أولِّئِكَ مَعَ اَلْذِينَ ... وَالصَّلِحِينُ وَحَسُن أوْلَئكَ رَفِيقًا
problems.issue: Q. 4:69 lemma damaged: the lemma begins أولئك without the Qurʾanic فـ; وَالصَّلِحِينُ carries a nominative ending where the genitive is required; وَحَسُن lacks its final fatḥa; النَبِيِيِّنَ is misdotted. Translated from the standard text; the missing فـ was not supplied, since Niasse may be citing the lemma from أولئك.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: vowel-layer OCR damage throughout; the quoted span is Q. 4:69 فأولئك مع الذين أنعم الله عليهم … وحسن أولئك رفيقا.

problems.issue: Footnote numeral [10] sits inside the running text, mid-sentence, before the وما دام clause. Left in place as a separate run.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: it keys a note on the ḥadīth that the angels spread their wings for the seeker of knowledge (the “إن الملائكة تضع أجنحتها” tradition); the note itself is not in this chunk.

problems.issue: This span sits in round brackets, which in this transcription normally mark a Qurʾanic lemma, but it is not Qurʾān — it is a divine saying (ḥadīth qudzī / ḥadīth ilāhī). Classified “h” and set in double quotation marks rather than as “q”. Footnote numeral [11] follows it inside the running text.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the brackets here are the transcriber's quotation marks, not lemma brackets; the saying is the one usually transmitted as أنا عند المنكسرة قلوبهم من أجلي, and [11] keys its source note.

problems.arabic: ما لم يجدوا … أعطاه من العلم | ما لم يجدوا
problems.issue: The ¶25/¶26 break falls mid-sentence at a page turn: ¶25 ends أعطاه من العلم and ¶26 resumes with its object ما لم يجدوا. ¶26 likewise ends mid-sentence at فلا. Both paragraphs were translated from where they start; nothing was supplied across the breaks.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the ¶26-final فلا introduces Iblīs's refusal — something like فلا يسجد له (“so he would not prostrate to him”) — completed on the next page, outside this chunk.

problems.arabic: (وَ) اذكر يا محمد صلى الله عليك وسلم ف {إِذْ قُلنَا …}
problems.issue: An orphaned ف stands between the Jalālayn-style gloss اذكر يا محمد … and the lemma {إذ قلنا للملائكة}. It attaches to nothing and was not translated; marked in place as illegible.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: either a stray OCR fragment, or the remains of a word broken by the lemma bracket — most plausibly في (“in”, i.e. اذكر … في وقت إذ قلنا) or the فـ of a following فقال/فأقول. Not recoverable; not guessed in the translation.

problems.issue: A bare digit 1 sits in the running text immediately before footnote numeral [12] — page-foot apparatus that has migrated into the line. Both left exactly where they stand, each as its own run; the 1 was not merged into [12] and not deleted.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the 1 is a stray second footnote marker or a page/line number pulled up from the foot of the page by OCR; it is not part of Niasse's sentence.

problems.arabic: لِلْمَلِيِكَةِ  /  وَكَانَ مِنَ اَلْكَفِرِينَ  /  إِلا إِبلِيسَ  /  أَبِى
problems.issue: Letter and vowel corruption in the Q. 2:34 lemmata: لِلْمَلِيِكَةِ for لِلْمَلآئِكَةِ (hamza lost, alif dropped), الْكَفِرِينَ for الْكَافِرِينَ, إِلا for إِلَّا, أَبِى for أَبَى. All consonantal skeletons legible; translated from the standard text of Q. 2:34.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: OCR damage only, not variant readings.

problems.issue: Footnote numerals [13] and [14] sit inside the running text, after ʿAzāzīl and after the forty-thousand-year figure. Left in place, each as its own run.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: [13] keys a note on the name ʿAzāzīl as Iblīs's angelic name; [14] keys a note on the numbers for his worship and custodianship of the Garden. Neither note text is in this chunk.

problems.issue: The chunk opens mid-clause. The perfect سجد stands with no subject and no governing verb; both fell on the preceding printed page, and the sequence (prostration, then refusal) only coheres if a command verb preceded. Translated as the fragment it is, with nothing supplied and no reordering.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the lost words ran along the lines of أمر الله إبليس أن يسجد له, 'Allah commanded Iblīs to prostrate to him', which would make سجد a transcription of يسجد. Not adopted; the English keeps the bare 'prostrate to him'.

problems.arabic: ولكن لما سجد الملائكة نصف يوم خسمائة عام
problems.issue: خسمائة is not a word: the mīm of خمسمائة has dropped out. Translated as a numeral rather than marked illegible, since the reading is not in doubt.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: خمسمائة, 'five hundred'. The gloss of نصف يوم as five hundred years is standard, so rendered 'half a day — five hundred years'.

problems.issue: Both predicates stand in the nominative after كان, where the accusative is required, and ركوع (bowing) enters without preparation — nothing earlier in the chunk mentions bowing. Translated as it stands.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the printed text read كان ركوعا واحدا وسجودا واحدا; the case endings are a transcription slip, not a different sense.

problems.issue: The subject is unexpressed and carries over from the material lost before ¶27; the English keeps the bare pronoun 'He' rather than supplying a name.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the subject is Iblīs, who is the subject of فامتنع at the head of ¶27 and the speaker of the whole paragraph. Not inserted into the text.

problems.arabic: كل هذه الشبهات جوابها أن كلمته الأولى ليست بحق عنده فقط
problems.issue: فقط sits at the end of the clause with ambiguous scope: it may qualify the whole answer ('the answer is simply that…') or كلمته الأولى ('his first statement alone is not true'). The loose syntax may itself be a transcription slip.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فقط qualifies the clause, hence 'the answer … is simply that his first statement is not true in his own case'. ¶30 repeats the claim without فقط (فقوله إنه عبد لله هذا ليس بحق عنده), which supports this reading.

problems.arabic: إن كان هذا حقا ليس | عليه إلا أن يتمثل كل ما أمره به
problems.issue: ¶29 breaks off mid-sentence at the page turn and ¶30 resumes it, splitting ليس from عليه إلا. Each half is translated where it stands; nothing invented at either seam.
problems.conjecture: No reconstruction needed: read continuously, ليس عليه إلا أن يتمثل كل ما أمره به — 'there is nothing incumbent upon him except that he carry out everything He commanded him'.

problems.issue: The initial hamza carries a fatḥa where the waṣl alif should be unvowelled, and a stray sukūn sits on the final alif. Reading not in doubt.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: اهبطوا (Q. 2:36), 'Go down'.

problems.issue: The chunk opens mid-clause. The predicate it completes stands at the end of the preceding chunk (L03-01, ¶32): وكانت الحية دابة ذات أربع. Translated from where it starts; no beginning supplied.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (secure): the printed sentence reads وكانت الحية دابة ذات أربع قوائم جميلة في الجنة — "the serpent was a beast with four beautiful legs in the Garden." The break is paginational, not a lacuna.

problems.issue: OCR defects in the Q. 7:22 lemma: أَلَمَ for أَلَمْ and أَنْهَكْمَا for أَنْهَكُمَا. Printed inside double quotation marks although it is Qurʾān, so it is tagged "q" and set without quotation marks.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (secure): أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا عَن تِلْكُمَا الشَّجَرَةِ (Q. 7:22).

problems.issue: كلا is not a possible reading here; the pronominal ها has dropped. Translated "all of them".
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (secure): كلّها.

problems.issue: The place of Iblīs's descent. Translated as it stands ("al-Ayla", i.e. Ayla/ʿAqaba), but the standard form of this descent-list (Sarandīb — Jidda — the serpent at Iṣfahān) gives al-Ubulla, near Baṣra, for Iblīs.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (uncertain): بالأُبُلَّة — "at al-Ubulla". The printed page is needed to settle it.

problems.issue: The paragraph ends mid-phrase on the numeral; the counted noun (سنة) stands at the head of ¶34. Left unfinished in the English, with nothing supplied. Also فاستحي for فاستحيا.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (secure): فاستحيا آدم ثلاثمائة سنة — "three hundred years", continued at ¶34.

problems.arabic: أخذها منه جل جلاله قَتَابَ عَلَيْهُ الكلمات قيل "رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنا أَنجْسَنَا" الآية، فدعا بها فتاب عليه، قبل توبته
problems.issue: Lines read out of sequence. قَتَابَ عَلَيْهُ (OCR for the lemma فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ) stands before الكلمات قيل…, and the same lemma recurs in its Jalālayn position after فدعا بها. Not reordered: both occurrences are translated where they stand, the first without a reference since the 2:37 run closes later.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the printed order follows the Jalālayn — ألهمه إياها … الكلمات قيل «ربنا ظلمنا أنفسنا» الآية، فدعا بها «فتاب عليه» قبل توبته — so the first قتاب عليه is a displaced duplicate of the lemma and should be struck in a critical text.

problems.issue: OCR defect in the Q. 7:23 lemma: أَنجْسَنَا for أَنفُسَنَا. Printed in double quotation marks although it is Qurʾān; tagged "q" and set without quotation marks. Cited mid-run from another sūra, so it carries its own reference.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (secure): رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَا أَنفُسَنَا (Q. 7:23).

problems.arabic: (إِنَّهُو هُوَ أَلتَّوَّابٌ) على عباده الرَحِين بهم
problems.issue: Three defects in one line. إِنَّهُو for إِنَّهُ and أَلتَّوَّابٌ for التَّوَّابُ; and الرَحِين for الرَّحِيمُ, which has additionally lost its brackets. The lemma/gloss boundary (الرحيم = lemma, بهم = gloss) was restored from the Jalālayn and tagged accordingly, so "the Merciful" is set as "q" although unbracketed in the transcription.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (secure): إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ على عباده (الرَّحِيمُ) بهم (Q. 2:37).

problems.arabic: وإبليس الذي تاب بكلمانت أخذها من عند نفسه
problems.issue: كلمانت is a transposition of كلمات; translated "words". Also ليس عنده إذنُ earlier in the paragraph carries a stray ḍamma on an indefinite noun that should be إذنٌ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (secure): بكلمات; and ليس عنده إذنٌ.

problems.issue: وتعلى for وتعالى; rendered with the fixed "Blessed and Exalted".
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (secure): تبارك وتعالى.

problems.arabic: "إِنَّا عَرَضْنَا ألاَمَانَةَ عَلَى السَّمَوَاتِ وَالاَرْضِ وَالْجِبَالِ بَأَيْنَ أَنْ يَحْمِلْنَهَا وأَشْفَقْنَ مِنْهَا وَحَمَلَهَا ألإنسَنُ"
problems.issue: OCR defects in the Q. 33:72 lemma: بَأَيْنَ for فَأَبَيْنَ, ألاَمَانَةَ for الأَمَانَةَ, وَالاَرْضِ for وَالأَرْضِ, ألإنسَنُ for الإنسَانُ. Printed in double quotation marks although it is Qurʾān; tagged "q" and set without quotation marks.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (secure): إِنَّا عَرَضْنَا الأَمَانَةَ عَلَى السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ وَالْجِبَالِ فَأَبَيْنَ أَن يَحْمِلْنَهَا وَأَشْفَقْنَ مِنْهَا وَحَمَلَهَا الإنسَانُ (Q. 33:72).

problems.arabic: قال آدم: إذا كان في هذا رضاك فأنا أمثله
problems.issue: أمثله yields no sense in context and the resolution is not secure, so the verb is marked illegible rather than guessed. The two available readings differ in substance: complying with the charge, or bearing the trust.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (uncertain): فأنا أمتثله — "then I will comply with it"; alternatively فأنا أحمله — "then I will bear it", which would pick up وَحَمَلَهَا الإنسَانُ in the āya just cited. The printed page is needed.

problems.arabic: قال ابن العربي الحاتمي: لما أكل آدم الشجرة نزل إلى الأرض
problems.issue: The quotation from Ibn al-ʿArabī al-Ḥātimī is cut by the page break and runs on into ¶37. The opening quotation mark is set in ¶36 and left unclosed there; it closes in ¶37. The inner قال before the closing line ("Had I been in Ādam's place…") is kept as Niasse's resumptive verb and tagged "p".
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: no text is missing — the break is paginational, not a lacuna.

problems.issue: Second occurrence of كلا for كلّها (cf. ¶33); translated "all of them". The same dropped ها twice in one chunk points to a systematic defect in this transcription rather than two accidents.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (secure): وأكلت عروقها كلّها.

problems.arabic: ولي نكتة غرا هنا سأقولها = وحق لها أن ترعويها المسامع
problems.issue: Two defects in the opening line of al-Jīlī's verses: غرا for غرّاء (metre and sense both want the full form), and ترعويها, which is not a possible verb form here. The sense of the second hemistich is nonetheless fixed by المسامع and the idiom أرعى سمعه, so it is translated rather than marked illegible. The six lines ¶39–¶44 are one continuous quotation: quotation marks open at ¶39 and close at ¶44, and the printed hemistich separator = is rendered as a spaced slash.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: ولي نكتة غرّاء هنا سأقولها = وحُقَّ لها أن تُرعِيَها المسامعُ — "and it deserves that ears be lent to it."

problems.issue: فأجني is translated at face value ("so I reap"), but the line is textually troubled: the feminine suffix of مرادها has no clear antecedent in the transcription, and the first-person verb may have been misread. The same feminine pronoun returns in ¶43 (أرى منها الإرادة), rendered neutrally as "it".
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (uncertain): فأُجري الذي يقضيه — "so I carry out what He decrees"; مرادها may refer back to النكتة of ¶39, or to الحقيقة. Collation against the printed dīwān of al-Jīlī is needed before this line is set.

problems.issue: OCR defects in the Q. 20:121 lemma: وَعَصِىً for وَعَصَىٰ and و مَغَوِى for فَغَوَىٰ. Printed in double quotation marks although it is Qurʾān; tagged "q" and set without quotation marks. The same āya is quoted again, with different defects (رَبَّهُو بَغَوِىْ), at the head of the next chunk (L03-03, ¶47).
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (secure): وَعَصَىٰ آدَمُ رَبَّهُ فَغَوَىٰ (Q. 20:121).

problems.issue: برور is not a possible form here; translated "dutifulness toward our father".
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (secure): بِرُّ أبينا.

problems.issue: OCR defect in the Q. 20:122 lemma: إَجْتَبِهُ for اجْتَبَاهُ. Printed in double quotation marks although it is Qurʾān; tagged "q" and set without quotation marks. The object of وَهَدى is elided in the Arabic and supplied as "[him]".
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (secure): ثُمَّ اجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدَىٰ (Q. 20:122).

problems.issue: The chunk ends mid-sentence on an introducing verb; the quotation it governs falls in the next chunk (L03-03, from ¶47). Nothing supplied.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: no lacuna — the break is paginational, and ¶47 opens with the Q. 20:121 lemma that completes the sentence.

problems.issue: Five corruptions in one lemma: أَؤُلِّيِكَ for أُولَٰئِكَ; أَصْحَبُ missing the alif of أَصْحَابُ; أَلبَّارِ for النَّارِ, with nūn read as bāʾ and the article given hamzat qaṭʿ, and run together with the following هُمْ; جِيهَا for فِيهَا; خَلِدُونَ missing the alif of خَالِدُونَ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (أُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ) (Q. 2:39).

problems.issue: Two defects. خَلِدِيرَ reads rāʾ for the nūn of خَالِدِينَ and lacks its alif. More seriously, أَبَدًا is missing from the quotation, although the sentence that follows ("they would not have needed abadan") turns entirely on its presence. The argument is unintelligible without it.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا (e.g. Q. 4:57, 4:122, 5:119, 98:8). Translated as it stands, without supplying the missing word in the lemma itself.

problems.arabic: لو كان الخلود يودن بالخلود الدائم
problems.issue: يودن is not a word; the construction يــ ب and the sense require a verb of signifying.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: يُؤْذِن ("conveys, implies"), with the hamza and the dot of the dhāl lost. Translated as "conveyed".

problems.issue: A third-person plural verb with no stated subject; nothing in the preceding clause supplies "they". The sense is impersonal ("there would have been no need for abadan").
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: لما احتيج إلى أبدا, or لما احتاجوا إلى [ذكر] أبدا. Translated with the plural kept and abadan left transliterated, glossed [‘forever’].

problems.issue: أبِيِ stands where the relative pronoun الَّتِي belongs; the article has been dropped and the lām–tāʾ read as bāʾ, yielding a spurious "my father". Also نِعْمَتِىَ for نِعْمَتِيَ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتِيَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ (Q. 2:40), as at ¶49 and ¶56. Translated from the conjecture.

problems.issue: آبالكم reads lām for the hamza of آبائكم.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: أي على آبائكم. Translated "that is, upon your forefathers".

problems.issue: وَوْمُوا has lost the hamza and the fāʾ of وَأَوْفُوا and gained a mīm; بِعَهْدِة reads tāʾ marbūṭa for the yāʾ of the first-person pronoun بِعَهْدِي.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِي) (Q. 2:40), which the gloss الذي عهدته إليكم confirms.

problems.issue: الإهان is not a word in this construction; the yāʾ–mīm of الإيمان has been read as a single hāʾ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: من الإيمان, as the Jalālayn gloss reads (من الإيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم) and as ¶53 confirms by continuing بمحمد. Translated "belief".

problems.issue: وأُو has lost the fāʾ of وَأُوفِ. The lemma also carries no delimiters of any kind, so its extent is unmarked in the transcription; I have closed it at بعهدكم and taken الذي عهدت as the gloss.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (وَأُوفِ بِعَهْدِكُمْ) (Q. 2:40).

problems.issue: The gloss is truncated: the pronoun and complement are missing. The Jalālayn reads الذي عهدته إليكم من الثواب.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: الذي عهدته إليكم من الثواب. Translated as it stands ("which I pledged"), without supplying the lost words.

problems.issue: وَإِيَّى for وَإِيَّايَ; بَارْهَبُون reads bāʾ for the fāʾ of فَارْهَبُونِ. The lemma is again undelimited.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (وَإِيَّايَ فَارْهَبُونِ) (Q. 2:40).

problems.issue: Not a licit form here. The gloss on فارهبون in the Jalālayn is خافون. The word also straddles the page break: ¶53 ends with خوفوا and ¶54 opens with مني.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: خافوا (مني) or خافون. Translated "fear" at the end of ¶53, with "Me" resumed at the head of ¶54 where the transcription places it.

problems.arabic: مني في ترك الوفاء بي دون غيري
problems.issue: بي gives "fulfilment with Me", which duplicates دون غيري and leaves the covenant unreferenced. The Jalālayn gloss reads به — failing to fulfil it.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: في ترك الوفاء به دون غيري. Translated from the conjecture ("in failing to fulfil it").

problems.issue: مَعَكَمْ carries fatḥa where the muṣḥaf has مَعَكُمْ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا مَعَكُمْ) (Q. 2:41).

problems.issue: بِهُ carries ḍamma for the genitive بِهِ, and a comma has been introduced inside the lemma, which the muṣḥaf does not have.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (بِهِ وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا) (Q. 2:41).

problems.issue: The madda of آيَات, the internal alif, and the final yāʾ of the first-person pronoun are all lost.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (بِآيَاتِي) (Q. 2:41), which the gloss التي في كتابكم من نعت محمد confirms.

problems.issue: لَمَنا for ثَمَنًا (lām for thāʾ) and فَلِيلا for قَلِيلًا (fāʾ for qāf).
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا) (Q. 2:41), which the gloss عرضا يسيرا confirms.

problems.issue: وَإِيَّى for وَإِيَّايَ; قَاتَّفُول for فَاتَّقُونِ, with qāf and fāʾ transposed and the final nūn read as lām. The bracket is opened and never closed, so the gloss خوفوا مني falls inside it.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (وَإِيَّايَ فَاتَّقُونِ) (Q. 2:41), closing before خوفوا مني.

problems.issue: The opening bracket of the lemma is missing — only the closing one survives — and the article is given hamzat qaṭʿ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (الْحَقَّ) (Q. 2:42).

problems.issue: The wāw is set twice: once as a lemma of its own, as the Jalālayn has it, and again inside the following bracket, where it does not belong. الْحَوَّ also stands for الْحَقَّ (wāw for qāf), as the gloss نعت محمد confirms.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (و) لا (تَكْتُمُوا الْحَقَّ) (Q. 2:42). Translated from the conjecture; the duplicated wāw is not rendered twice in English.

problems.arabic: (وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ الزَّكَوةَ وَارْكَعُواْ مَعَ الرَّكِعِينَ ))
problems.issue: الرَّكِعِينَ is missing the alif of الرَّاكِعِينَ, and the lemma closes with two brackets where one is wanted.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ وَارْكَعُوا مَعَ الرَّاكِعِينَ) (Q. 2:43).

problems.issue: Legible, but the Jalālayn reads لقرابتهم. Either is translatable as "their kinsmen"; noted in case the printed edition reads otherwise.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: possibly لقرابتهم. Translated as it stands.

problems.issue: أتَامُرُونَ has lost the hamza of أَتَأْمُرُونَ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (أَتَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبِرِّ) (Q. 2:44).

problems.issue: أَنْمُسَكُمْ reads mīm for the fāʾ of أَنفُسَكُمْ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (وَتَنسَوْنَ أَنفُسَكُمْ) (Q. 2:44).

problems.issue: وَأَنتَمْ for وَأَنتُمْ; تَثْلُونَ for تَتْلُونَ (thāʾ for tāʾ); الْكِتَبَ missing the alif of الْكِتَابَ. The brace is opened and never closed, so the gloss التوراة falls inside the lemma delimiter.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: {وَأَنتُمْ تَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ} (Q. 2:44), closing before التوراة.

problems.issue: أَبَلا for أَفَلَا (bāʾ for fāʾ) and تَعْفِلُونَ for تَعْقِلُونَ (fāʾ for qāf).
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ) (Q. 2:44).

problems.issue: The lemma ends in kasratān where the genitive after the conjunction requires a single kasra.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (وَالصَّلَاةِ) (Q. 2:45).

problems.arabic: وفي الحديث كان صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا حزبه أمر بادر إلى الصلاة . [28]
problems.issue: The ḥadīth is reported indirectly and carries no opening or closing quotation mark, so its extent is unmarked. I have closed it at الصلاة, the point at which footnote 28 is keyed, and taken وقيل الخطاب لليهود as Niasse's resumption.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: quotation closed at بادر إلى الصلاة and set in the ḥadīth register despite the indirect construction.

problems.issue: بالصير for بالصبر (yāʾ for bāʾ); the apposition وهو الصوم and the pairing with الصلاة require صبر.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: فأمروا بالصبر وهو الصوم. Translated with ṣabr left transliterated.

problems.issue: اِلَّا carries kasra on the alif for إِلَّا; عَلَي lacks the alif maqṣūra of عَلَىٰ; and الَّذِينَ has lost its shadda. The article is twice written اَڬل, with a superscript mark over the alif — this looks like the printed edition's own Warsh-tradition orthography rather than OCR damage, and it does not affect the reading.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: إِلَّا عَلَى الْخَاشِعِينَ الَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ (Q. 2:45–46).

problems.issue: مُلَقُواْ has lost the alif of مُّلَاقُو and gained a spurious final alif; رَبّهِمْ is unvocalised.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (أَنَّهُم مُّلَاقُو رَبِّهِمْ) (Q. 2:46).

problems.issue: الْعَلَمِين is missing the alif of الْعَالَمِينَ and its final vowel.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ) (Q. 2:47).

problems.arabic: (وَاتَّقوا يَوْماً لاَّ تَجْزِى نَمْسُّ عَى نَصْسٍ شَيْأَ
problems.issue: Four corruptions plus a delimiter failure: نَمْسُّ for نَفْسٌ (mīm for fāʾ, with a spurious shadda); عَى for عَن; نَصْسٍ for نَفْسٍ (ṣād for fāʾ); شَيْأَ for شَيْئًا. The bracket is opened and never closed, so the gloss هو يوم القيامة falls inside it.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمًا لَّا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَن نَّفْسٍ شَيْئًا) (Q. 2:48), closing before هو يوم القيامة.

problems.issue: بَمَا for فَمَا (bāʾ for fāʾ); مِ for مِن; شَعِعِينَ for شَافِعِينَ, with the alif lost and the fāʾ read as ʿayn.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: فَمَا لَنَا مِن شَافِعِينَ (Q. 26:100), the proof-text the Jalālayn cites at Q. 2:48.

problems.issue: The opening bracket is missing — only the closing one survives. يُوخَذُ has lost the hamza of يُؤْخَذُ, and عَدْلَ carries fatḥa where the subject of the passive is nominative عَدْلٌ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (وَلَا يُؤْخَذُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ) (Q. 2:48).

problems.issue: The opening bracket of the lemma is missing.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ) (Q. 2:48).

problems.issue: The wāw lemma is closed but never opened: the transcription has و) where the Jalālayn has (و).
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (و) اذكروا (إِذْ نَجَّيْنَاكُم) (Q. 2:49). اذكروا set as Niasse's gloss.

problems.issue: The worst-damaged lemma in the chunk. مِنْ is lost entirely; آلِ has lost its madda and stands as a bare ال detached from what follows; and مِرْعَوْنَ reads mīm for the fāʾ of فِرْعَوْنَ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (مِنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ) (Q. 2:49), which the gloss من فرعون وآله immediately following puts beyond doubt. Translated from the conjecture.

problems.issue: The lemma closes with two brackets where one is wanted.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (نِسَاءَكُمْ) (Q. 2:49).

problems.arabic: لقول بعض الكهنة إن مولودا يولد في بني إسرائيل يكون سببا لذهاب ملكك
problems.issue: The له of the Jalālayn (لقول بعض الكهنة له) is missing, which leaves the second-person ملكك ("your kingship") without an addressee; the addressee is Firʿawn.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: لقول بعض الكهنة له. Translated as it stands, keeping the second person of the soothsayers' speech.

problems.issue: وَمِي reads mīm for the fāʾ of وَفِي, and ذَلِكُم lacks the dagger alif of ذَٰلِكُم.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (وَفِي ذَٰلِكُم) (Q. 2:49), which the gloss في ذلكم العذاب confirms.

problems.issue: عَظِيمَ carries fatḥa where the adjective agrees with the nominative بَلَاءٌ; the lemma also lacks its closing bracket in the transcription of the following line.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (بَلَاءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ) (Q. 2:49).

problems.arabic: بلاء عظيم من ربكم، أو في ذلكم الإنجاء
problems.issue: The chunk opens mid-gloss by restating, in a different word order, the lemma that closes ¶59 (بَلآَءُ مِن رَبِّكُمْ عَظِيمَ): عظيم has moved forward to stand next to بلاء. Translated as it stands; no line has been reordered.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: a page-turn repetition of the lemma in the printed edition rather than a second citation. The gloss runs on across the break without a gap — ¶59 glosses في ذلكم as العذاب, ¶60 supplies the alternative أو ... الإنجاء and then the second gloss إنعام for بلاء — which matches Jalālayn ad Q. 2:49: «وفي ذلكم» البلاء أو الإنجاء «بلاء» ابتلاء أو إنعام «من ربكم عظيم».

problems.issue: The brackets around the one-letter lemma وَ have dropped out, so the Qurʾanic wāw and Niasse's gloss اذكروا run together as though both were his own prose.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: read (وَ) اذكروا (إِذْ فَرَقْنَا). Secured by ¶57 of the same lesson, where the identical formula survives with its bracket intact: و) اذكروا (إِذْ نَجَّيْنَـكُم). Marked on that reading: "And" as lemma, "recall:" as prose.

problems.issue: جَرَقْنَا is not a word: fāʾ read as jīm.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: إِذْ فَرَقْنَا (Q. 2:50), secured by Niasse's own gloss فلقنا immediately after; translated "when We parted".

problems.issue: Three corruptions in one lemma: أغرفنا for أغرقنا, عال for آل, مرعون for فرعون.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وَأغرَقْنَا آلَ فِرعَونَ (Q. 2:50), confirmed by the gloss فرعون وقومه; translated "and We drowned the folk of Firʿawn".

problems.arabic: ([30]ثُمَّ إتَّحَدتَّم أَلْعِجْلَ الذي صاغه السامري إلهاً
problems.issue: Three defects. (i) إتَّحَدتَّم for اتَّخَذْتُمُ. (ii) The footnote marker [30] has drifted inside the lemma's opening bracket, where it cannot belong. (iii) The lemma's closing bracket is missing, so the gloss الذي صاغه السامري إلهاً stands inside the Qurʾanic bracket.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: read ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ (Q. 2:51), bracket closing after العجل; cf. Jalālayn, «العجل» الذي صاغه لكم السامري إلهاً. Marked on that reading: "the calf" as lemma, the rest as prose. [30] is placed at the end of the preceding gloss (التوراة), the last word it could attach to.

problems.issue: Final wāw for hāʾ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: مِنْ بَعْدِهِ (Q. 2:51), confirmed by the gloss من بعد ذهابه إلى ميعادنا; translated "after him".

problems.issue: The paragraph is a single lemma plus a four-word gloss, and the gloss's last word الكتاب carries no bracket, so it is open to being read either as Niasse's metalinguistic reference back to the lemma or as a fresh citation of it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: الكتاب here is governed by the preposition in تفسير للكتاب and so belongs to the gloss, not to the lemma; cf. Jalālayn ad Q. 2:53, «والفرقان» عطف تفسيري. The whole of "an explication of the Book" is therefore marked as prose.

problems.issue: A spurious وَ stands between verb and object, and أَنْجُسَكَم is miswritten (jīm for fāʾ, and the final mīm unvocalised).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: إِنَّكُمْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنفُسَكُمْ (Q. 2:54); the وَ is an OCR artefact and is not translated.

problems.issue: Four corrupted words (ج for ف twice, باربكم for بارئكم, أنمسكم for أنفسكم), plus broken bracketing throughout the paragraph: this lemma has no opening bracket and a doubled closing bracket, and the next lemma (ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرْ لَّكُمْ عِندَ بَارِئِكُمْ)) likewise closes twice.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فَتُوبُوا إِلَى بَارِئِكُمْ فَاقْتُلُوا أَنفُسَكُمْ (Q. 2:54), with a single opening and closing bracket in each case; both spans treated as lemmata throughout.

problems.issue: الجرم lacks the mīm of the participle, and البريئ carries a final hamza on yāʾ rather than on the line.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: المجرم; cf. Jalālayn ad Q. 2:54, ليقتل البريء منكم المجرم; translated "let the innocent among you kill the guilty".

problems.arabic: سحابة سوداء لقلا يبصر بعضكم بعضا
problems.issue: لقلا is not a word.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لئلا (or لكي لا); translated "so that none of you would see another".

problems.issue: Initial qāf for fāʾ, and a stray trailing wāw inside the bracket.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ (Q. 2:54), confirmed by the gloss قبل توبتكم; the trailing wāw is not translated.

problems.arabic: (إِنَّهُ هُوَ ألتَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ ذكر اللٰه تبارك وتعالى في هذه الآية ...
problems.issue: The lemma's closing bracket is missing, so the whole of Niasse's exposition for the paragraph — some three hundred words — stands inside the Qurʾanic bracket.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the bracket closes after الرَّحِيمُ (Q. 2:54), where the āya ends. Marked on that reading: "He is the Ever-Relenting, the Merciful" as lemma, the remainder as prose.

problems.issue: كلا is ambiguous as transcribed: كلّها ("all of them") or the emphatic كلا (kallā), which is plainly how the same spelling functions in ¶64 (ليس كصومنا لياليها وأيامها كلا).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: كلّها, since it follows a two-term object (دوره وممالكه) and needs a resumptive pronoun; translated "all of them". If kallā is intended, read "utterly" instead.

problems.arabic: "مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِن اِلَهِ غَيْرِى" / "أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ أَلاَعْلِى"
problems.issue: Both of Firʿawn's citations are orthographically deformed (اِلَهِ for إِلَهٍ, أَلاَعْلِى for الْأَعْلَى) and stand in double quotation marks rather than in Niasse's usual Qurʾanic brackets.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرِي (Q. 28:38) and أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْأَعْلَى (Q. 79:24). Both marked as Qurʾanic lemmata, without quotation marks, per the convention.

problems.arabic: حتى قتل تسعين ألف مولود مع عشرين ألفا، هذا مائة ألف وعشرة آلاف
problems.issue: The numerals invite emendation at first sight, since "one hundred thousand and ten thousand" is an unusual way to name the sum.
problems.conjecture: No emendation needed: 90,000 + 20,000 = 110,000, which is exactly مائة ألف وعشرة آلاف. The figures are internally consistent and have been translated literally; logged only to record that the reading was checked and left alone.

problems.arabic: أربعين ليلة ليس كصومنا لياليها وأيامها كلا، هذا ثمانون ليلة
problems.issue: Elliptical oral syntax rather than OCR damage: كلا (kallā) stands alone with nothing stated for it to negate, and the comparison with "our fasting" is left unfinished.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the sense is that Mūsā's forty were nights and days together, unlike our fast, which covers the days only — hence the reckoning ثمانون ليلة that follows. Kept elliptical, with "[alike]" supplied in brackets and كلا rendered flatly as "not at all"; nothing has been added to complete the comparison.

problems.issue: الحضر (ḥāʾ) for الخضر (khāʾ): a one-dot error that turns the proper name into a common noun. The risk of confusion is real, since ¶64 ends with the genuine الحضرة, "the Presence", four words earlier.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: الخضر, al-Khiḍr, secured by the citation of Q. 18:62 that immediately follows and by the contrast Niasse then draws between المخلوق and الحق; translated "al-Khiḍr".

problems.arabic: "عَاتِنَا عَدآَءَنَا لَقَدْ لَفِينَا صِ سَجَرنًا هَلذَا تَصْباً
problems.issue: The most heavily damaged span in the chunk: six words corrupted, the two-letter صِ standing for a whole word, and no closing quotation mark.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: آتِنَا غَدَاءَنَا لَقَدْ لَقِينَا مِن سَفَرِنَا هَذَا نَصَبًا (Q. 18:62), with صِ = مِن. The reconstruction is secure rather than speculative: the words are a verbatim Qurʾanic citation, every corrupted form differs from the received text by a dot or a tooth, and the context (Mūsā with al-Khiḍr, hunger after half a day) fixes the verse. Translated on that reading and marked as a lemma.

problems.issue: A stray comma and an Arabic-Indic digit eight stand between the end of the Q. 18:62 citation and ذهب إلى المخلوق. Not translatable as text; emitted as an illegible span.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: either the citation's missing closing quotation mark misread as ٨, or a stray footnote digit. No word appears to be lost, since the sentence runs on without a gap.

problems.arabic: "ثَلَئَةَ أَيَّامِ إِلَّ رَمزًا / "سَبْعَ لَيَالِ وَثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَيَّامِ حُسُومًا
problems.issue: ثَلَئَةَ for ثَلَاثَةَ and إِلَّ for إِلَّا; both proof-texts for the three-day and seven-night khalwa are left unclosed, and both stand in quotation marks rather than brackets.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ إِلَّا رَمزًا (Q. 3:41) and سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًا (Q. 69:7); both marked as lemmata.

problems.issue: Two corrupted phrases inside the final lemma.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لَن نُّومِنَ لَكَ and فَأَخَذَتْكُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ (Q. 2:55); translated "we will not believe you" and "so the thunderbolt seized you".

problems.issue: The paragraph, and the chunk, break off inside the lemma: the bracket never closes and the citation stops one word short.

problems.issue: كلا is ambiguous as transcribed: كلّها ("all of them") or the emphatic كلا (kallā, "not at all"), which is plainly how the same spelling functions in ¶64 (ليس كصومنا لياليها وأيامها كلا).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: كلّها, since it follows a two-term object (دوره وممالكه); translated "all of them". If kallā is intended, read "utterly" instead.

problems.arabic: "مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِن اِلَهِ غَيْرِى" / "أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ أَلاَعْلِى"
problems.issue: Both of Firʿawn's citations are orthographically deformed (اِلَهِ for إِلَهٍ, أَلاَعْلِى for الْأَعْلَى) and stand in double quotation marks rather than Niasse's usual Qurʾānic brackets.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرِي (Q. 28:38) and أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْأَعْلَى (Q. 79:24). Both marked as Qurʾānic lemmata, without quotation marks, per the convention.

problems.issue: الحضر (ḥāʾ) for الخضر (khāʾ): a one-dot error that turns the proper name into a common noun.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: الخضر, al-Khiḍr, secured by the citation of Q. 18:62 that immediately follows and by the contrast drawn with المخلوق and الحق; translated "al-Khiḍr".

problems.arabic: "عَاتِنَا عَدآَءَنَا لَقَدْ لَفِينَا صِ سَجَرنًا هَلذَا تَصْباً
problems.issue: The most heavily damaged span in the chunk: six words corrupted, صِ standing for a whole word, and no closing quotation mark.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: آتِنَا غَدَاءَنَا لَقَدْ لَقِينَا مِنْ سَفَرِنَا هَذَا نَصَبًا (Q. 18:62). The reconstruction is secure because the words are a verbatim Qurʾānic citation and the context (Mūsā with al-Khiḍr, hunger after half a day) fixes it; translated on that reading and marked as a lemma.

problems.issue: A stray comma and an Arabic-Indic digit eight stand between the end of the Q. 18:62 citation and ذهب إلى المخلوق. Not translatable as text; emitted as an illegible span.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: either the citation's missing closing quotation mark misread as ٨, or a stray footnote digit. No word appears to be lost, since the sentence runs on without a gap.

problems.issue: Two corrupted phrases inside the final lemma.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لَن نُّومِنَ لَكَ and فَأَخَذَتْكُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ (Q. 2:55); translated "we will not believe you" and "so the thunderbolt seized you".

problems.arabic: "ثَلَئَةَ أَيَّامِ إِلَّ رَمْزًا / "سَبْعَ لَيَالِ وَثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَيَّامِ حُسُومًا
problems.issue: ثَلَئَةَ for ثَلَاثَةَ and إِلَّ for إِلَّا; both of these two proof-texts for the three-day and seven-night khalwa are left unclosed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ إِلَّا رَمْزًا (Q. 3:41) and سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًا (Q. 69:7).

problems.issue: The paragraph, and the chunk, break off inside the lemma: the bracket never closes and the citation stops before its last word.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the lemma continues الْغَمَامَ (Q. 2:57), which in fact opens the next chunk as ألغمم}. No completion has been supplied; the English stops where the Arabic stops.

problems.arabic: مُوسۊيٰٓ / مُوسَي / مُوسِىٰ ; تَشْكَرُونٌ ; تَهْتَدُونُ ; اَڬلْكِتَٰبَ
problems.issue: Systematic vowel-sign and final-ḥaraka corruption runs through every Qurʾānic lemma in the chunk (¶¶60–65): موسى appears in three deformed spellings, final nūns carry wrong ḥarakāt (تشكرونٌ, تهتدونُ), and stray superscript marks attach to the article.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: scanner noise on the printed vocalisation, not textual variants. The consonantal skeletons are sound, so these were read against the standard text and are not logged individually.

problems.issue: The paragraph carries nothing but a full stop: the printed line was lost in transcription. ¶68 breaks off mid-sentence at فقالوا الشمس تضر بنا، and ¶70 resumes with فأتى الله بغمام سترهم, so a clause is missing between them. Marked illegible; nothing supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the lost line completed the Israelites' complaint about the sun and their request for shade (something on the order of فمن أين لنا الظلّ؟), which ¶70 answers. Needs collation against the printed edition.

problems.issue: كلا occurs twice, unpointed and unvocalised, in parallel positions (في صحراء التيه كلا، كل هذا ببركة موسى and وأعطوا هذا من أنواع النعم كلا بسبب موسى وهارون). The word is legible but its reading is not fixed, so it was translated rather than marked illegible.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: كُلّاً, an oral emphatic 'all of it', translated as such in both places; possibly OCR for كلها. Reading it as the negative particle كَلّا does not fit either context.

his garment and put it on.

[The cloud] ringed Medina round, and the rain came down from that Friday to the Friday that followed it.

Mūsā's people asked Mūsā to pray to Allah for water for them, and Mūsā prayed at the bidding of his people, and Allah answered his prayer. All the more fitting, then, that Muḥammad ﷺ prayed for us at the bidding of Allah, Blessed and Exalted:
And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and the believing women (Q. 47:19).

This is a command from Allah that the Prophet ﷺ ask forgiveness for us; he asked forgiveness for us at Allah's command. And since Mūsā was answered when he prayed at the bidding of his people, that Muḥammad be answered — he who prayed at the command of Allah, Blessed and Exalted — is stronger and more to be hoped for. So we have great hope in Allah's having commanded His Prophet to pray to Allah for us and to ask forgiveness for us.
Eat and drink of Allah's provision (Q. 2:60).
He commanded them to eat an unrestricted eating and to drink an unrestricted drinking, and this carries them into expansiveness and excess that leads to corruption; so He appended to it His words:
and do not go about the earth spreading corruption (Q. 2:60).
Eat and drink, and do not go about the earth spreading corruption.
Eat and drink, and do not be extravagant; He does not love the extravagant (Q. 7:31).

Just as the Mūsā of the Banū Isrāʾīl sought water for his people, who were the Banū Isrāʾīl, and twelve springs burst forth from the rock, so too the Mūsā of the spirit in every human being seeks water for his people, who are the five outward senses, the five inward senses, the
and the heart — twelve senses. So when the rock of the servant's existence is struck with the staff of

is acts of worship and acts of striving; the drinking place of the heart is fear and hope; the drinking place of the intellect is contraction and expansion; the drinking place of the spirit is the witnessing of beauty and of majesty; the drinking place of the innermost secret is intimacy and awe.

, and this has never been observed. This

of praying for rain has remained today, whether for crops, or for livestock, or for people's drinking: the imām goes out, and the Muslims with him, in a state of humility and self-abasement, and they perform the prayer for rain, and Allah answers them.

Mūsā sought water for his people. He remained a long while praying and supplicating, and he was not answered. He said: 'My Lord, we call upon You — and we are more than three thousand persons of the righteous — because of the need of Your creation, and You have not answered us.' He said: 'I have not answered you because among you there is a talebearer, one who goes about with slander among people.' He said to Him: 'My Lord, make known to me who he is.' He said: 'If I made him known to you, I should be like him: I reproach him for a thing and then practise it myself. This does not befit [Me].'
A day later Allah revealed to Mūsā that that talebearer had died and that his bier was at the door of the mosque. Mūsā hurried to reach the bier and to learn who he was, and he found seventy biers.
[Such is] the covering of Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
And when you said: Mūsā, we shall not endure a single food (Q. 2:61)

So the Children of Israel in the wilderness, when they grew weary of life, said that they had grown weary of this food that came down from heaven, it being a single kind, the manna and the quails. They lied: they had not grown weary of the food; they had grown weary only of life.

of what the earth grows — of its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils and its onions (Q. 2:61)
from the earth. They knew that this was possible only if they returned to the villages and the towns, and this was in truth what they were after.

— nobler; that is, would you take it in its place?) They said: We want nothing but this alone. So he prayed to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and the Exalted said:
and you shall have what you asked for

— of plant food. So they settled in Bayt al-Maqdis, or in Arīḥā, a village near Bayt al-Maqdis, and they planted, and Allah provided them with these plants, and so it became their livelihood down to this day of ours.
And humiliation was stamped upon them

— the mark of poverty and inertness and shame. It clings to them even if they are rich, as the struck dirham clings to its die; you never see a Jew without seeing in him the traces of poverty and humiliation and wretchedness, even if he is rich.
used to disbelieve in Allah's signs and to kill the prophets

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, appointed for every community a day in the week to be a feast day; He gave them Friday. He went off to the forest and said: O Lord of Ibrāhīm and Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb, I place this cow of mine in Your keeping; when my son grows up, hand her over to him. When day came he gathered firewood, and when he brought the firewood he sold it and divided its price into three portions: a portion he ate himself, a portion he gave to his mother, and a portion he gave as alms. and Exalted, until his mother came to feel pity for him. She said to him: Go to the forest, for your father deposited a cow for you there with the Lord of Ibrāhīm. He said: No, my mother did not command me to ride you. She said: Had you ridden me, you would have been powerless over me and would have had no command over any part of me. So he brought the cow to his mother. She said to him: Go to the market and sell her for three dinars. This cow — her price is three dinars; let it be no less than that. But settle nothing except after consulting me. So he came to the market, and a man presented himself to him and said to him: For how much do you sell this cow?

He said: I sell her for three dinars, subject to my mother's counsel. He said: I will give you six dinars, and do not consult your mother. He said to him: I shall consult my mother. So he came to his mother. She said to him: Sell her for six dinars, with my counsel. When he returned, the man said to him: I will give you twelve dinars, and do not consult your mother. He said: No, not until I consult my mother. So he went back to his mother. She said to him: This is no man; this is perhaps an angel. If you go back to him, say to him: My mother commands me to consult you — shall I sell this cow or shall I not sell her? So he consulted him, and he said to him: Do not sell this cow. Keep her with you, for Mūsā will send you a people who will buy her, and do not sell her to them except for her hide filled with gold. So they went about seeking the cow that Mūsā, upon him be blessing and peace, had described to them, and they found her description in none but this cow. So they bought her for the fill of her

— that is, her hide — with gold. When they had slaughtered the cow they returned to Mūsā and said to him: We have slaughtered the cow. He said: Take her tongue, or the base of her tail, and strike the dead man with it — that alone — and he will live. They took the cow's tongue and struck the man with it, and he rose up with his jugular veins gushing blood. He said: So-and-so and so-and-so, these two are the ones who killed me. Then he went back dead, and the two were barred from the inheritance. This is what our Law has affirmed: whoever kills the one from whom he inherits is barred from the inheritance.

problems.conjecture: Conjecture: أَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ / فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ / فِيهِمْ / فَاصْطَادُوا / قِرَدَةً / يَقُولُ / فِيهَا / تَسْقِي.

Nothing has been supplied in the translation; the thirteen as transmitted are translated as they stand.

problems.issue: Beyond the dot-loss, عَلِمْتَمْ carries fatḥa for ḍamma.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ إِنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا (Q. 24:33).

problems.issue: Both lemmata are formulae occurring at several places in the muṣḥaf, and Niasse quotes too little to localise either with certainty.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture on the citations only: أَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ cited to Q. 2:43, the first and standard locus; رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي cited to Q. 38:35, where it stands without the additions carried at Q. 7:151 and Q. 71:28. The references are editorial, not Niasse's.

problems.issue: Vocalisation damage: أَشْهِدْوَاْ carries sukūn on the dāl with a following wāw and a stray alif.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وَأَشْهِدُوا إِذَا تَبَايَعْتُمْ (Q. 2:282).

problems.arabic: كُونُواْ حِجَارَةً آوْ حَدِيداً / اصْبِرُواْ أَوْلا تَصْبِرُواْ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ
problems.issue: آوْ written with madda for أَوْ; and أَوْ لَا run together as one word أَوْلا.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: كُونُوا حِجَارَةً أَوْ حَدِيدًا (Q. 17:50); اصْبِرُوا أَوْ لَا تَصْبِرُوا سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ (Q. 52:16).

problems.issue: The mīm of وَتَمَتَّعُوا has dropped out, leaving a bare shadda.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: كُلُوا وَتَمَتَّعُوا (Q. 77:46). Translated 'Eat and enjoy yourselves'.

problems.arabic: ألا أيها الليل الطويل ألا انجل][19]
problems.issue: A stray closing bracket stands before the footnote marker, with no opening bracket anywhere; the rhyme letter of انجلِ is unvocalised, and the verse is given in its first hemistich only.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ألا أيها الليل الطويل ألا انجلِ — the opening of a line of Imruʾ al-Qays whose second hemistich, بصبح وما الإصباح منك بأمثل, is not quoted. Translated as transmitted, without supplying the missing hemistich. Marked "h" as a verbatim quotation introduced by قال الشاعر, though the poet is not named.

problems.issue: The lemma has lost its opening alif and its opening delimiter, and closes with a quotation mark; بِسَلَمِ and امِنِينَ have lost alif and madda respectively.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ادْخُلُوهَا بِسَلَامٍ آمِنِينَ (Q. 15:46).

problems.issue: منذوب for مندوب — dāl read as dhāl.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: مندوب. Translated 'recommended', matching the ندب of the list in ¶18.

problems.arabic: (وَإذْ قَتَلْتُمْ تَنْسةٌ فَادَّرَأتُمْ بِيهَا وَاللَّهُ مُخْرِجْ مَا كُنتُمْ تَكْتَمُونَ)
problems.issue: Five corruptions in one lemma: تَنْسةٌ for نَفْسًا (with tāʾ marbūṭa for the tanwīn), the alif of فَادَّارَأْتُمْ lost, مُخْرِجْ with sukūn for the nominative, and تَكْتَمُونَ for تَكْتُمُونَ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وَإِذْ قَتَلْتُمْ نَفْسًا فَادَّارَأْتُمْ فِيهَا وَاللَّهُ مُخْرِجٌ مَّا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ (Q. 2:72). Translated from the conjectured reading.

problems.issue: خبات is not a word that fits the construction.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: أخبار — لموالاة أخبار بني إسرائيل, 'to keep the reports of the Children of Israel consecutive', which is the idiom and suits Niasse's point that the exegetes take Q. 2:72 out of its numerical place. Translated accordingly.

problems.arabic: قتلوا وأحدا منهم أسمه عاميل / عمر طويلا / فأستعجل
problems.issue: Orthographic damage of a routine kind: وأحدا for واحدًا, أسمه for اسمه with hamzat qaṭʿ, فأستعجل for فاستعجل.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: قتلوا واحدًا منهم اسمه عاميل … عُمِّر طويلًا فاستعجل. The name عاميل (ʿĀmīl) is the one the exegetical tradition gives the murdered man and is kept.

problems.arabic: (إِلَّ أللَّهَ يَامَرُكُمُ وَ أَن تَذْبَحُواْ بَفَرَةَ م اقتلوا بقرة
problems.issue: The lemma is heavily damaged and unclosed: إِلَّ أللَّهَ for إِنَّ اللَّهَ, يَامَرُكُمُ وَ with an intrusive wāw, بَفَرَةَ for بَقَرَةً. A bare mīm then stands between the lemma and the gloss اقتلوا بقرة; it is not readable as a word and is marked illegible in the translation.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تَذْبَحُوا بَقَرَةً (Q. 2:67), and the stray م a remnant of معناه — 'its meaning is: kill a cow' — which is how Niasse introduces glosses elsewhere in the lesson.

problems.arabic: (وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسِىٰ لِفَوْمِهِة إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَامُرُكُمْوَ أَن تَذْبَحُواْ بَقَرَةٌ قَالُوْا أَتَتَّخِذْنَا هُزُوا … قَالَ أَعْوذَ)
problems.issue: Six corruptions: مُوسِىٰ for مُوسَى, لِفَوْمِهِة for لِقَوْمِهِ with tāʾ marbūṭa for the hāʾ, يَامُرُكُمْوَ with the same intrusive wāw as above, بَقَرَةٌ for the accusative بَقَرَةً, أَتَتَّخِذْنَا for أَتَتَّخِذُنَا, أَعْوذَ for أَعُوذُ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَى لِقَوْمِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تَذْبَحُوا بَقَرَةً قَالُوا أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوًا … قَالَ أَعُوذُ (Q. 2:67).

problems.issue: أمتنع for امتنع (hamzat qaṭʿ for waṣl), and أَنَ اَكْونَ for أَنْ أَكُونَ. The paragraph opens with the gloss of أعوذ left hanging at the end of ¶19, with the Jalālayn's من supplied between the two lemmata.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: امتنع (باللَّهِ) من (أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ) (Q. 2:67). Translated 'I take protection in Allah from that I should be of the ignorant', keeping the gloss word من outside the lemma as the edition sets it.

problems.arabic: (قَالَوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّر لَنَا مَا هِيّ … (وَلَابِكْرِّ)
problems.issue: قَالَوا for قَالُوا, يُبَيِّر for يُبَيِّن (nūn read as rāʾ), هِيّ with shadda for the final fatḥa, and وَلَابِكْرِّ written as one word with a shadda for the tanwīn.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَ … وَلَا بِكْرٌ (Q. 2:68).

problems.issue: ضغيرة for صغيرة (ṣād read as ḍād), عَوَانْ with sukūn for the nominative tanwīn, and نُصُف misvocalised.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: صغيرة (عَوَانٌ) نَصَف (Q. 2:68) — نَصَف being the Jalālayn's gloss, a female of middle age. Translated 'small [in age] … middling — of middle age'.

problems.arabic: ( ابْعَلُوا مَا تُوقَرُون كهم به من ذبحها
problems.issue: ابْعَلُوا for فَافْعَلُوا and تُوقَرُون for تُؤْمَرُونَ, the lemma unclosed; then كهم, which is not readable as a word and is marked illegible. The words that follow it, به من ذبحها, are legible and are translated.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فَافْعَلُوا مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ (Q. 2:68) بِهِ مِنْ ذَبْحِهَا — the Jalālayn's gloss on the lemma. كهم is probably a corrupt remnant of أُمِرْتُم or أمرتكم; nothing has been supplied for it.

problems.arabic: ( قَالَوا ادْعُ لَتَا رَبَّكَ يُبَسِّ لَتَا مَا لَوْنَهَا قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَفُولُ إِنَّهَا
problems.issue: لَتَا twice for لَنَا, يُبَسِّ for يُبَيِّن, لَوْنَهَا for the nominative لَوْنُهَا. The paragraph breaks off inside the lemma, which continues in ¶22; the citation is therefore given in ¶22 where the run closes.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا لَوْنُهَا قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا (Q. 2:69).

problems.issue: تَرَ is too corrupt to read and is marked illegible. صَبْرَاةَ for صَفْرَاءُ, قَافِع for فَاقِعٌ with the consonants transposed, لَوْتَهَا for لَوْنُهَا.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: بَقَرَةٌ صَفْرَاءُ فَاقِعٌ لَّوْنُهَا (Q. 2:69). بَقَرَةٌ is secure from the āya and from the إِنَّهَا that ends ¶21, but the glyphs of تَرَ do not support it, so it is left as illegible rather than translated.

problems.arabic: (تَسَرُ التَّظِينَ) إليها بحسنها أي تعجمهم له
problems.issue: تَسَرُ for تَسُرُّ, التَّظِينَ for النَّاظِرِينَ with the alif and the ṣād-ẓāʾ group reduced, تعجمهم for تعجبهم. The له that follows has no referent and appears to be an intrusion.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (تَسُرُّ النَّاظِرِينَ) إليها بحسنها أي تُعْجِبُهُمْ (Q. 2:69), which is the Jalālayn's gloss verbatim; له deleted. Translated 'she delights the beholders — those who look at her, by her beauty; that is, she pleases them'.

problems.issue: The word that closes ¶22 and the lemma that opens ¶23 belong to one Qurʾānic run, but قالوا is set without its opening delimiter, which first appears as a closing bracket after مَا هِي in ¶23.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَ) (Q. 2:70). قالوا is marked "q" accordingly.

problems.issue: تَشَبَةَ for تَشَابَهَ, with tāʾ marbūṭa for the hāʾ and the alif lost; a stray hāʾ attached to عَلَيْنَا; يْبَيِّن with sukūn on the prefix.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: تَشَابَهَ عَلَيْنَا … يُبَيِّن (Q. 2:70).

problems.arabic: (..لو لم يستثنوا لما بُينت لهم آخر الأبد)[23]
problems.issue: The ḥadīth is quoted from the middle: the two dots in the edition mark an elision at its head, and no isnād or source is given. The transcription is otherwise sound.
problems.conjecture: No conjecture on the wording. The elision is carried into the English as a leading ellipsis. بُيِّنت is read as feminine of the cow, not impersonal — 'she would never have been made clear to them' — since the question throughout is which cow was meant.

problems.arabic: قَالَ إِنَّهُو يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لاَّ ذَلُولٌ) / (وَلَا تَسْفِ الْحَرْثَ)
problems.issue: إِنَّهُو written with a wāw for the ḍamma; the lemma has no opening delimiter, only a closing one; تَسْفِ for تَسْقِي.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا ذَلُولٌ) … (وَلَا تَسْقِي الْحَرْثَ) (Q. 2:71).

problems.issue: ألَنَ for الْآنَ and جِيْتَ for جِئْتَ. The lemma is also cut off by the end of the printed page: the āya continues بِالْحَقِّ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: قَالُوا الْآنَ جِئْتَ (Q. 2:71). Translated 'They said: Now you have come', with nothing supplied for the بِالْحَقِّ that the chunk does not reach.

problems.issue: The chunk opens mid-gloss. نطقت is a second-person perfect glossing a lemma that fell on the preceding printed page; it stands here with no lemma before it. Translated as the fragment it is, with nothing supplied and no reordering.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the preceding page closed with the lemma (الآن جِئْتَ) of Q. 2:71, giving the Jalālayn-style sequence «الآن جئت» نطقت «بالحق». Not adopted; the English begins at 'you have spoken'.

problems.arabic: وقسم يتعبد فيه لله تبارك ‖ [¶27] وتعالى
problems.issue: The printed page break falls inside the fixed formula تبارك وتعالى: ¶26 ends at تبارك and ¶27 opens at وتعالى. Not OCR damage. Translated as it stands, ¶26 closing with 'Blessed' and ¶27 opening with 'and Exalted', with no invented beginning for ¶27.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: in continuous text the phrase reads لله تبارك وتعالى, 'Allah, Blessed and Exalted'. A press edition may wish to close the formula across the paragraph join.

problems.arabic: بملء مَسْكها ذهبا ‖ [¶28] بملء مسكها وهو جلدها ذهبا
problems.issue: Rendering note, not damage. مَسْك occurs twice. At its first, unglossed occurrence in ¶26 it is translated 'hide'; in ¶28, where Niasse glosses it (وهو جلدها), the term is kept in transliteration as 'mask' (register i) so that the gloss has something to gloss.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: none needed. If the press prefers uniformity, ¶26 could also read 'the fill of her mask', though nothing in ¶26 explains the word.

problems.arabic: قال له: بكم تبيع هذه البقرة)
problems.issue: Unmatched closing parenthesis at the end of the paragraph. No Qurʾānic lemma stands here — the clause is the buyer's question inside Niasse's narrative — so nothing is marked 'q' and the bracket is not honoured.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: a stray OCR artifact, or a bracket migrated from the lemma run that resumes at (فَذَبَحُوهَا) in ¶28. To be deleted.

problems.arabic: فإن والدك أودع لرب إبراهيم لك بقرة هنالك
problems.issue: أودع governs لرب here, where the verb normally takes عند, and لك repeats the preposition. Translated 'deposited a cow for you there with the Lord of Ibrāhīm', which is what the clause can only mean.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: أودع عند رب إبراهيم لك بقرة هنالك, matching the father's own words in ¶26 (أستودع عندك بقرتي هذه).

problems.arabic: هذا ليس برجل هذا لعله ملك
problems.issue: ملك is unvocalized and may be read مَلَك ('angel') or مَلِك ('king'). Rendered 'an angel'.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: مَلَك. The speaker is contrasted with رجل ('this is no man') and knows what Mūsā will demand in the future, which the narrative tradition assigns to an angel.

problems.arabic: (وَإِذْ قَتَلْتُمْ نَمْساً بَادَّرَأتُمْ جِيهَا وَالَّهُ مُخْرِجَ مَا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونُ فَقْلْنَا إضْرِبُوه)
problems.issue: OCR damage running through a Qurʾānic lemma. Consonantal damage: نَمْساً for نَفْساً; بَادَّرَأتُمْ for فَادَّارَأْتُمْ; جِيهَا for فِيهَا; وَالَّهُ for وَاللَّهُ (dropped lām). Vocalization or orthography only: مُخْرِجَ for مُخْرِجٌ; تَكْتُمُونُ for تَكْتُمُونَ; فَقْلْنَا for فَقُلْنَا; إضْرِبُوه for اضْرِبُوهُ. Three of the four consonantal errors are a single defective letter, ف read as م, ب and ج. The span is translated rather than marked illegible because the underlying text is fixed and identifiable; the damage is recorded here instead.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَإِذْ قَتَلْتُمْ نَفْساً فَادَّارَأْتُمْ فِيهَا وَاللَّهُ مُخْرِجٌ مَا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ * فَقُلْنَا اضْرِبُوهُ, Q. 2:72–73.

problems.arabic: فضرب بلسانها أو عجب ذنبها فحبي وقال قتلني فلان وفلان
problems.issue: فحبي is not a word in this context. Marked [illegible: فحبي] in the translation rather than restored, since the span is Niasse's own prose and not a fixed text.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فحَيِيَ, 'and he came to life', a ب for ي misreading. Supported by the parallel فسيحي earlier in the same paragraph and by the Jalālayn gloss on Q. 2:73.

problems.arabic: وقال قتلني فلان وفلان ابني عمه ومات
problems.issue: ابني is an oblique dual standing in apposition to the nominative فلان وفلان, where ابنا would be required. Translated as a parenthetical apposition, 'his two paternal cousins', which the case does not affect.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لابنَي عمه, as in the Jalālayn (قتلني فلان وفلان لابني عمه), where the phrase names the two men rather than qualifying them; OCR appears to have dropped the lām.

problems.issue: وقتلا is unvocalized and may be read as the passive وقُتِلا, 'and the two were put to death', or the active وقَتَلا, 'and the two killed'. Rendered as a passive, matching the passive فحُرِما immediately before it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وقُتِلا, following the Jalālayn sequence فحرما الميراث وقتلا, where the two cousins lose the inheritance and are then executed for the killing.

problems.issue: Missing opening parenthesis: the lemma كذلك carries only a closing bracket. Treated as a lemma ('q') on the evidence of the gloss الإحياء that follows it; the paragraph then ends mid-gloss at the chunk boundary, so the English stops there too.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (كَذَلِكَ) الإحياء, Q. 2:73, the opening bracket lost to OCR. The run continues on the following page with (يُحْيِ اللَّهُ المَوْتَى). The supplied words of the English gloss, '[that is, such]', are bracketed.

problems.arabic: جَعَلْنها تلك العقوبة (تكالا عبرة مانعة من ارتكاب مثل ما عملوا ولِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا) ... وَمَا خَلْفَهَا
problems.issue: Lemma brackets displaced across the whole of Q. 2:66: جَعَلْنها stands unbracketed and has lost its fāʾ and its alif; تكالا stands for نَكَالاً; the parenthesis opens at that lemma, swallows Niasse's gloss عبرة مانعة من ارتكاب مثل ما عملوا, and closes only after ولما بين يديها; وما خلفها is then left unbracketed. Registers assigned on the reconstruction below; nothing reordered.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): فَجَعَلْنَاهَا نَكَالاً لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَمَا خَلْفَهَا وَمَوْعِظَةً لِلْمُتَّقِينَ, Q. 2:66, with تلك العقوبة and عبرة مانعة... as glosses, not lemma. The transcription's ولِمَا carries a wāw the muṣḥaf does not have; it is translated as transmitted ("and for those before it") rather than deleted, since Niasse may be re-citing rather than reading.

problems.arabic: (وَمَوْعِظَةُ لِلْمَتَّقِينَ) خصوا بالذكر لأنهم هم المتفعون بها
problems.issue: المتفعون has lost its nūn; also مَوْعِظَةُ for مَوْعِظَةً and الْمَتَّقِينَ for الْمُتَّقِينَ. Translated as restored.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: المنتفعون بها, as in the Jalālayn on Q. 2:66 (خصوا بالذكر لأنهم المنتفعون بها).

problems.arabic: اله تبارك وتعالى جعل لكل أمة يوما
problems.issue: A lām has dropped out of the divine name. Translated as restored.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى, "Allah, Blessed and Exalted."

problems.arabic: أنتم الآخرون السابقون أعطوا يوم الجمعة
problems.issue: The chunk opens inside the ḥadīth introduced by the colon that ends ¶14. Translated from its first word and set in double quotation marks, with nothing supplied at the opening.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the received wording is نحن الآخرون السابقون (al-Bukhārī, Muslim); the transcription's أنتم may be Niasse's own address to his audience rather than OCR damage, so it is left as transmitted.

problems.arabic: إن من توضأ وجلس ينتظر الصلاة ‖ [¶17] فهو في الصلاة.
problems.issue: The ḥadīth is cut by the page break: the protasis ends ¶16 and the apodosis opens ¶17. The double quotation marks therefore open in ¶16 and close in ¶17; nothing is supplied at either edge. Not OCR damage.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: in continuous text the ḥadīth reads من توضأ وجلس ينتظر الصلاة فهو في الصلاة; a press edition may wish to close the quotation at the paragraph join.

problems.arabic: الحوت الذي ابتلع يونس عليه الصلاة والسلام كان يسكن تلك القرية
problems.issue: No connective before كان, so the relative clause and the predicate stand asyndetically. Rendered as a second relative clause ("which used to dwell in that village"); no word supplied in the text.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وكان يسكن تلك القرية.

problems.arabic: "[17]إِذْ تَاتِيهِمْ حِيتَانُهُمْ يَوْمَ سَبْتِهِمْ شُرَّعاً وَيَوْمَ لا يَسْبِئُونَ لا تَاتِيهِمْ
problems.issue: The citation carries a stray opening double quotation mark, no closing mark of any kind, and none of the brackets the rest of the chunk uses for lemmata; the footnote marker [17] has migrated inside it. تَاتِيهِمْ lacks its hamza (twice) and يَسْبِئُونَ has tāʾ read as hamza-on-yāʾ. Treated as a Qurʾānic lemma ("q") and translated as restored.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): إِذْ تَأْتِيهِمْ حِيتَانُهُمْ يَوْمَ سَبْتِهِمْ شُرَّعاً وَيَوْمَ لا يَسْبِتُونَ لا تَأْتِيهِمْ, Q. 7:163 — a citation from sūra 7 inside the commentary on Q. 2:65.

problems.arabic: افترقوا ثلاثة أقسام: فرقة امتنعت عن الصيد ولم تَنه، وفرقة
problems.issue: The chunk ends mid-enumeration at the page break: the first of the three groups is described and the second breaks off after وفرقة. Translated as it stands, with nothing supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the remaining groups — those who forbade the fishing and those who transgressed — follow on the next printed page; ولم تَنه is ولم تنهَ (jussive of نهى), "and did not forbid [it]."

problems.arabic: أَفِيمُواْ الصَّلَوةً / بَكَاتِبُوهُمُ / بَاصْطَادُوا / بِيهِمْ / بِيهَا
problems.issue: Systematic OCR dot-loss runs through the whole chunk: ق is read as ف and ف as ب. The affected lemmata are identifiable only against the Qurʾānic text. Translated with ق and ف restored throughout; the same substitution recurs in ¶¶19–25 and is not logged again word by word.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: أَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ / فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ (Q. 24:33) / فَاصْطَادُوا (Q. 5:2) / فِيهِمْ / فِيهَا.

problems.issue: Grammatically anomalous as it stands (masculine singular pronoun with a plural predicate). Translated with a bracketed supply, '[the province of] uṣūl'.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: هذا هو في الأصول ('this belongs to uṣūl al-fiqh'), or هذا هو الأصل ('this is the ground'), the latter supported by أصل الأمر للوجوب in the next clause.

problems.issue: Opening « with no closing mark; قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ reduced. Rendered from the Qurʾānic text.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ. Cited as Q. 2:65 rather than Q. 7:166 — both carry the phrase, but Q. 2:65 is the verse under commentary and Niāsse refers the destruction forward to al-Aʿrāf.

problems.issue: Letters dropped from the second word; not readable on its own.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: كُلُوا وَتَمَتَّعُوا (Q. 77:46), 'Eat and enjoy yourselves'. Translated on that reading.

problems.arabic: ألا أيها الليل الطويل ألا انجل][19]
problems.issue: Final yāʾ lost from انجلي, and a stray closing bracket stands before the footnote marker. Set as register 'h' (a verbatim quoted authority) although the poet is designated and not named.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: ألا انجلِي — the opening hemistich of Imruʾ al-Qays, continuing بِصُبْحٍ وما الإصباحُ منكَ بأمثلِ. The stray ] is OCR noise.

problems.issue: Bare lemma with many possible loci (Q. 2:43, 2:83, 2:110, 24:56 and others). No reference supplied in the translation rather than assert one.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: Q. 2:43, the locus in the sūra under commentary. Left uncited pending AK's decision.

problems.issue: Bare lemma with several possible loci (Q. 7:151, 38:35, 71:28). No reference supplied in the translation rather than assert one.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: Q. 38:35, the locus usually cited for amr al-duʿāʾ in uṣūl works. Left uncited pending AK's decision.

problems.arabic: فعل الأمر في القرآن يأتي على خمسة عشر معنى
problems.issue: Fifteen meanings are announced twice, but only thirteen are enumerated in the transcription: wujūb, nadb, ibāḥa, irshād, ishhād, taḥqīr, ihāna, taswiya, indhār, tahdīd, tamannī, duʿāʾ, ikrām. Nothing supplied; the list is translated as it stands.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: two members lost in transmission or transcription — taʿjīz and takhyīr are the usual candidates in the uṣūl lists — or an unfilled gap in the oral delivery. Not reconstructed in the text.

problems.issue: Not a readable word in context ('لموالاة خبات بني إسرائيل'). Emitted as [illegible: خبات].
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: أخبار — 'لموالاة أخبار بني إسرائيل', i.e. the exegetes advance Q. 2:72 so as to keep the accounts of the Children of Israel continuous. This also explains why Niāsse treats Q. 2:72 before Q. 2:67 — the order is deliberate, not a scrambled line.

problems.issue: Consonant skeleton damaged; not readable on its own.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: نَفْسًا (Q. 2:72), 'a soul'. Translated on that reading, which the surrounding وإذ قتلتم … فادارأتم فيها fixes.

problems.issue: A stray م stands between the lemma and the gloss, and a stray و stands before أن in يَامَرُكُمُ و أن تَذْبَحُواْ. Translated as lemma plus gloss, with the strays dropped.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: بَقَرَةً، أي اقتلوا بقرة — the م is probably the remnant of أي or of ما introducing the gloss.

problems.issue: Dotting error.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: ومندوب, 'and recommended' (mandūb). Translated on that reading.

problems.issue: Final nūn of يُبَيِّنْ misread as rāʾ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: يُبَيِّنْ لَنَا مَا هِيَ (Q. 2:68).

problems.issue: صاد misread as ضاد. The word is the second half of the Jalālayn gloss on بِكْر, broken across the printed page break at the end of ¶20.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: صغيرة, 'young'. Translated on that reading.

problems.arabic: ( ابْعَلُوا مَا تُوقَرُون كهم به من ذبحها
problems.issue: Two problems in one span. The lemma is doubly damaged. The gloss that follows it has lost the word carrying كهم, which is not readable; emitted as [illegible: كهم به].
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: lemma فَافْعَلُوا مَا تُؤمَرُونَ (Q. 2:68), translated on that reading. Gloss أمرَكم به من ذبحها, '[what He] commanded you, namely her slaughter'.

problems.arabic: ( قَالَوا ادْعُ لَتَا رَبَّكَ يُبَسِّ لَتَا مَا لَوْنَهَا
problems.issue: Nūn lost from لنا twice; يُبَيِّن reduced to يُبَسِّ. The opening round bracket is never closed — the lemma runs over the page break into ¶22, where the closing bracket does not appear either.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَنَا مَا لَوْنُهَا (Q. 2:69). The bracket should close after لَوْنَهَا in ¶22; line order itself is sound.

problems.issue: The opening of the lemma is lost at the page break; ¶21 ends with إِنَّهَا and ¶22 begins with this fragment. Not readable on its own; emitted as [illegible: تَرَ].
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: بَقَرَةٌ (Q. 2:69), 'a cow' — the word split across the printed page break.

problems.issue: Dots scrambled in all four words; النَّاظِرِينَ is reduced past independent recognition.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: صَفْرَاءُ فَاقِعٌ لَوْنُهَا … تَسُرُّ النَّاظِرِينَ (Q. 2:69). The Jalālayn glosses that follow (شديدة الصفرة, إليها بحسنها) confirm the reading.

problems.issue: تعجبهم misread; the trailing له has no antecedent and is left untranslated.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: أي تعجبهم, 'that is, she pleases them' (Jalālayn). له is probably a stray or لها.

problems.issue: تَشَابَهَ reduced and a stray hāʾ attached to علينا.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: تَشَابَهَ عَلَيْنَا (Q. 2:70).

problems.arabic: (..لو لم يستثنوا لما بُينت لهم آخر الأبد)[23]
problems.issue: Printed in round brackets, which elsewhere in this text mark a Qurʾānic lemma, but introduced by في الحديث at the end of ¶23. Set as register 'h', not 'q'. The leading '..' marks an elision in the printed edition and is rendered as an ellipsis.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: a ḥadīth as transmitted in the tafsīr tradition on Q. 2:70; بُينت to be read بُيِّنَت. Source not verified here — flag for AK's apparatus.

problems.issue: Stray wāw on إنه; تَسْقِي reduced to تَسْفِ. The opening round bracket of قَالَ إِنَّهُو … is also missing.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ … وَلَا تَسْقِي الْحَرْثَ (Q. 2:71).

problems.issue: الْآنَ reduced to ألَنَ. The lemma breaks off at the chunk boundary, so no reference is given on this run; the verse continues بِالْحَقِّ in Q. 2:71.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: قَالُوا الْآنَ جِئْتَ (Q. 2:71). Nothing supplied beyond جئت.

problems.issue: Footnote markers of the printed edition. They run in ascending order across ¶¶18–24, which confirms the printed lines were read in sequence — no scrambling to report in this chunk. Retained inline in the translation as 'p' material so the apparatus stays keyed.
problems.conjecture: Not a conjecture: markers preserved as transcribed, at the positions they occupy in the Arabic.

problems.arabic: وقسم يتعبد فيه لله تبارك ‖ [¶27] وتعالى
problems.issue: The printed page break falls inside the fixed formula تبارك وتعالى: ¶26 ends at تبارك and ¶27 opens at وتعالى. Not OCR damage. Translated as it stands — ¶26 closes with "Blessed" and ¶27 opens with "and Exalted" — with no invented beginning for ¶27.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: in continuous text the phrase reads لله تبارك وتعالى, "Allah, Blessed and Exalted"; a press edition may wish to close the formula at the paragraph join.

problems.arabic: قال له: بكم تبيع هذه البقرة)
problems.issue: Unmatched closing parenthesis at the end of the paragraph. No Qurʾānic lemma stands here — the clause is the buyer's question inside Niasse's narrative — so nothing is marked "q".
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: stray OCR artifact (or a bracket migrated from the lemma run that resumes at فذبحوها in ¶28); to be deleted.

problems.arabic: (وَإِذْ قَتَلْتُمْ نَمْساً بَادَّرَأتُمْ جِيهَا وَالَّهُ مُخْرِجَ مَا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونُ فَقْلْنَا إضْرِبُوه)
problems.issue: OCR damage throughout a Qurʾānic lemma: نَمْساً for نَفْساً; بَادَّرَأتُمْ for فَادَّارَأْتُمْ; جِيهَا for فِيهَا; وَالَّهُ for وَاللَّهُ; مُخْرِجَ for مُخْرِجٌ; تَكْتُمُونُ for تَكْتُمُونَ; فَقْلْنَا for فَقُلْنَا; إضْرِبُوه for اضْرِبُوهُ. The span is translated rather than marked illegible because the underlying text is fixed and identifiable as Q. 2:72–73; the damage is recorded here instead.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَإِذْ قَتَلْتُمْ نَفْساً فَادَّارَأْتُمْ فِيهَا وَاللَّهُ مُخْرِجٌ مَا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ * فَقُلْنَا اضْرِبُوهُ.

problems.arabic: فضرب بلسانها أو عجب ذنبها فحبي وقال قتلني فلان وفلان
problems.issue: فحبي is not a word in this context. Marked [illegible: فحبي] in the translation rather than restored, since this is Niasse's own prose (via the Jalālayn) and not a fixed text.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فحَيِيَ, "and he came to life" — supported by the parallel فسيحي earlier in the same paragraph and by the Jalālayn gloss on Q. 2:73 (فضرب بلسانه أو عجب ذنبه فحيي).

problems.issue: Missing opening parenthesis: the lemma كذلك carries only a closing bracket. Treated as a lemma ("q") with الإحياء as Niasse's gloss ("p"); the paragraph then ends mid-gloss at the chunk boundary.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (كَذَلِكَ) الإحياء, i.e. the Jalālayn-style gloss أي مثل هذا الإحياء يحيي الله الموتى; the gloss word is supplied in the English as "[that is, like this] quickening".

problems.arabic: وقال قتلني فلان وفلان ابني عمه ومات
problems.issue: ابني عمه stands without its governing lām, leaving the apposition ungoverned.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لابني عمه, as in the Jalālayn (قتلني فلان وفلان لابني عمه) — "[naming] his two paternal cousins"; rendered as a parenthetical apposition in the English, which the missing lām does not affect.

problems.issue: OCR damage across the Q. 2:73 lemma run: يَحْي for يُحْيِي; أُلْمَوْتَبى for الْمَوْتَى (a spurious ب and a prothetic hamza on the article); عايَتِهِ for آيَاتِهِ. In Niasse's own gloss, فتومنون for فتؤمنون. Translated rather than marked illegible, since the underlying text is fixed and identifiable as Q. 2:73; the damage is recorded here.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): كَذَٰلِكَ يُحْيِي اللَّهُ الْمَوْتَىٰ وَيُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ. The reconstruction of فتؤمنون is orthographic only.

problems.arabic: هكذا يحيي الموتى كلا، من قدر على إحياء واحد قادر على إحياء الجماعة
problems.issue: كلا is unpointed for case and admits two readings: كُلًّا, "all [of them]," and كَلَّا, the particle of rebuttal. Nothing in the transcription decides it.
