problems.conjecture: Conjecture: كُلًّا, "all [of them]," taken as the object of يحيي and prepared for by the following من قدر على إحياء واحد قادر على إحياء الجماعة, which argues from one to the many. Rendered "all [of them]" in brackets. A press edition may wish to vocalise it.

problems.issue: بَهِيَ is not a word here, and the lemma carries only a closing parenthesis. Treated as the Qurʾānic فَهِيَ ("q"), with القلوب as the Jalālayn-style gloss ("p").
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَهِيَ) القلوب (كَالْحِجَارَةِ) — bāʾ for fāʾ, a routine confusion of one dot below for one dot above; the reading is fixed by Q. 2:74 فَهِيَ كَالْحِجَارَةِ and by the gloss القلوب that follows.

problems.issue: Word division broken in the lemma: أَوَ اشَدُّ for أَوْ أَشَدُّ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً (Q. 2:74). Orthographic only; the English is unaffected.

problems.issue: نموت (first person plural) cannot govern النفس. The clause is Niasse's own prose, so it is not fixed by a canonical text; the verb is restored from agreement rather than guessed at silently.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: تموت النفس فيحيا القلب, "the soul dies and the heart comes to life" — nūn for tāʾ (two dots above for two dots above, differently placed), and the parallel إذا حيي القلب ماتت النفس two clauses later fixes the sense. Rendered "the soul may die and the heart come to life."

problems.issue: حيبت is not a word. Niasse's own prose again, restored from the immediately following parallel rather than marked illegible.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: حَيِيَتِ النفس, "when the soul lives" — supported by وإذا حيي القلب ماتت النفس in the same sentence and by the same defect (فحبي for فحَيِيَ) recorded at ¶28 of the preceding chunk.

problems.arabic: "يَخْرِجُ الْحَىَّ مِنَ ألْمَيِّتِ وَيُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ ألْحَيِ"
problems.issue: The quotation is set in double quotation marks rather than in the parentheses the edition uses for lemmata, which would suggest ḥadīth; it is Qurʾān, and is marked "q". OCR damage: يَخْرِجُ for يُخْرِجُ; الْحَىَّ for الْحَيَّ; prothetic hamzas on ألْمَيِّتِ and ألْحَيِ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the words are Q. 10:31, يُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ وَيُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ الْحَيِّ, cited as such. Q. 6:95 has وَمُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتِ مِنَ الْحَيِّ and so is not the source. The bracketing should be normalised to the edition's lemma parentheses.

problems.arabic: إن من بعض الحجارة لما يتفجر ‖ [¶30] منه الأنهار
problems.issue: The printed page break falls inside Niasse's paraphrase of Q. 2:74: ¶29 ends at يتفجر and ¶30 opens at منه الأنهار. Not OCR damage. Also in ¶29, الاَنْهَرْ for الْأَنْهَارُ in the lemma. Translated as it stands — ¶29 closes "there are those that burst forth" and ¶30 opens "from it, rivers" — with no invented beginning for ¶30.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: in continuous text the clause reads إن من بعض الحجارة لما يتفجر منه الأنهار, "among some stones there are those from which rivers burst forth"; the lemma word is الْأَنْهَارُ.

problems.issue: OCR damage in the lemma: بِعَاعِلٍ for بِغَافِلٍ and عَدًّا for عَمَّا. The lemma also opens with a brace and is never closed. Translated rather than marked illegible, the text being fixed as Q. 2:74.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ. Bracketing to be normalised.

problems.issue: The lemma opening Q. 2:75 is damaged and unbracketed: وأَقْتَطْمَعُونَ carries a prefixed wāw and an intrusive ق and ط, and is followed by an asterisk where the edition's lemma parenthesis should stand. يُومِنُوا for يُؤْمِنُوا is orthographic.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (أَفَتَطْمَعُونَ) ... (أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا). The prefixed wāw and the asterisk are OCR artifacts to be deleted. The gloss order — أيها المؤمنون on أفتطمعون, then اليهود on أن يؤمنوا — follows the Jalālayn and is not disturbed.

problems.issue: ولَتَمْ, the last word of the paragraph, is not a word. It stands in the lemma position that Q. 2:75 requires and is marked [illegible: ولَتَمْ] in the translation rather than restored, because the prefixed wāw is unexplained by the āya and cannot be accounted for as a simple letter confusion.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لَكُمْ, "for you" — Q. 2:75 reads أَفَتَطْمَعُونَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوا لَكُمْ, and ¶31 resumes with وَقَدْ كَانَ فَرِيقٌ, which is the continuation of that āya. On this reading the tāʾ is a misread kāf and the initial wāw is an artifact, perhaps dittography from the وَقَدْ that opens the next printed line.

problems.arabic: لَمَا يَهْبِطُ ) يَنزل من علو إلى أسفل مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ وقلوبكم لا تتأثر
problems.issue: مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ stands unbracketed between Niasse's gloss ينزل من علو إلى أسفل and his comment وقلوبكم لا تتأثر. It is Qurʾān (Q. 2:74) and is marked "q"; the gloss before it belongs to يهبط.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the lemma parentheses dropped in transcription — (مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ). Also in the same lemma run, يَشْقَّقُ for يَشَّقَّقُ and فَيَخْرَجْ for فَيَخْرُجُ, orthographic only.

problems.arabic: وَقَدْ كَانَ قَرِيقٌ) طائفة مِنْهُمْ يَسْمَعُولَ كَلَمَ اللَّهِ
problems.issue: OCR damage through the lemma, which also carries a closing parenthesis with no opening one: قَرِيقٌ for فَرِيقٌ; يَسْمَعُولَ for يَسْمَعُونَ (final nūn read as lām); كَلَمَ for كَلَامَ. مِنْهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ كَلَامَ اللَّهِ is unbracketed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (وَقَدْ كَانَ فَرِيقٌ) طائفة (مِنْهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ كَلَامَ اللَّهِ) — Q. 2:75.

problems.arabic: (ثُمَّ يُحَرِّجُونَهُ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا عَفَلَوهْ فهموه { هُمْ يَعْلَمَونُكَ
problems.issue: يُحَرِّجُونَهُ for يُحَرِّفُونَهُ; عَفَلَوهْ for عَقَلُوهُ; and هُمْ يَعْلَمَونُكَ for وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ, with a dropped wāw and a spurious final kāf. The second lemma opens with a brace and neither lemma is closed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (ثُمَّ يُحَرِّفُونَهُ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا عَقَلُوهُ) فهموه (وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ) — Q. 2:75. The spurious kāf is to be deleted; it cannot be a pronoun, since the subject is third person plural throughout.

problems.arabic: (وَاذَا لَفُوأ منافقوا اليهود (الذِيرَ ءَامَنُوا قَالوَاْ ءَامَنَّا))
problems.issue: لَفُوأ for لَقُوا; الذِيرَ for الَّذِينَ (final nūn read as rāʾ); وَاذَا for وَإِذَا. The second lemma closes with two parentheses. منافقوا for منافقو in Niasse's gloss.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (وَإِذَا لَقُوا) منافقو اليهود (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قَالُوا آمَنَّا) — Q. 2:76. The doubled closing parenthesis is an artifact.

problems.issue: Doubled opening parenthesis on the lemma. No text is lost.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (لِيُحَاجُّوكُم) — the second parenthesis is an artifact, to be deleted. The paragraph also ends mid-āya: the lemma run continues at (بِهِ، عِندَ رَبِّكُمُ) in ¶33, so Q. 2:76 is cited at both page-break ends of the run.

problems.arabic: (أَبَلا تَعْقِلُونَ) ... (أَوَلا يَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمْ مَا يُسِرُّونَ
problems.issue: أَبَلا for أَفَلا (fāʾ read as bāʾ, the same one-dot confusion as بَهِيَ at ¶29); يَعْلَمْ for يَعْلَمُ; the second lemma is not closed. In ¶33 the comma inside (بِهِ، عِندَ رَبِّكُمُ) is also intrusive.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ), Q. 2:76; and (أَوَلَا يَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ) ... (وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ), Q. 2:77. ¶33 ends mid-gloss at من, completed by ذلك at the head of ¶34; translated as it stands.

problems.arabic: ومنْهُم اليهود أمّيُّونَ) عوام (لا يَعْلَمُونَ الْكِتَبَ)
problems.issue: Bracket damage: ومنهم carries no parentheses at all and أميون only a closing one, so the lemma–gloss–lemma sequence has to be recovered from the Jalālayn. الْكِتَبَ for الْكِتَابَ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَمِنْهُمْ) اليهود (أُمِّيُّونَ) عوام (لَا يَعْلَمُونَ الْكِتَابَ) — Q. 2:78, with اليهود glossing ومنهم and عوام glossing أميون, as in the Jalālayn. Marked that way in the translation.

problems.issue: إِلَّ twice for إِلَّا; هُمُوَ for هُمْ; and جَوَبْلٌ for فَوَيْلٌ, in which the fāʾ is read as jīm and a spurious bāʾ intrudes. Translated rather than marked illegible: the lemma is fixed as the opening of Q. 2:79, and the gloss شدة عذاب that opens ¶36 belongs to it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (إِلَّا) لكن (أَمَانِيَّ) أكاذيب (وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ), Q. 2:78; then (فَوَيْلٌ), Q. 2:79. The page break separates فويل from its gloss شدة عذاب, which stands at the head of ¶36.

problems.arabic: (لِلِيرَ يَكْتَبُونَ الْكِتَبَ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ) ... هَذَا مِنْ عِندِ الَّهِ ... ( قَوَيْلٌ لَهُم مِمَّا كَتَبَتَ
problems.issue: لِلِيرَ for لِلَّذِينَ; الْكِتَبَ for الْكِتَابَ; الَّهِ for اللَّهِ; قَوَيْلٌ for فَوَيْلٌ (fāʾ read as qāf); كَتَبَتَ for كَتَبَتْ. The last lemma is not closed, and the paragraph ends mid-phrase.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (لِلَّذِينَ يَكْتُبُونَ الْكِتَابَ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ) ... (ثُمَّ يَقُولُونَ هَذَا مِنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ لِيَشْتَرُوا بِهِ ثَمَناً قَلِيلاً) ... (فَوَيْلٌ لَهُم مِمَّا كَتَبَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ) — Q. 2:79. The break falls between كَتَبَتْ and أَيْدِيهِمْ, so ¶36 closes "So woe to them for what" and ¶37 opens "their hands have written," with no invented beginning.

problems.issue: يمَّا for مِمَّا and يَكْيبونَ for يَكْسِبُونَ (sīn lost). Translated rather than marked illegible; the text is fixed as Q. 2:79 and the gloss من الرشا confirms the reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (وَوَيْلٌ لَهُم مِمَّا يَكْسِبُونَ). ¶37 also ends mid-clause at لما وعدهم النبي, completed by النار at the head of ¶38.

problems.arabic: (والتَّارُ إِلَّ أَيَّاماً مَعْدُودَةَ) قليلة أي أُربعين، مادة عبادة آبائهم العجل ثم تزول
problems.issue: والتَّارُ for النَّارُ, with a prefixed wāw and tāʾ for nūn; إِلَّ for إِلَّا; مَعْدُودَةَ for مَعْدُودَةً. In the gloss, مادة is not a word in context, and أي أربعين is elliptical, lacking the counted noun.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (النَّارُ إِلَّا أَيَّاماً مَعْدُودَةً), Q. 2:80. For مادة read مدة, "the span" — the Jalālayn glosses أياماً معدودة as أربعين يوماً مدة عبادة آبائهم العجل ثم يزول عنهم, which also supplies the missing يوماً, rendered "forty [days]" in brackets. The prefixed wāw on النار is an artifact.

problems.arabic: (فَلَ )لهم يا محمد (اتَّخَذْتُمْ) ما اتخدتم ... ( تَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ مَا لا تَقْلَمَونَ
problems.issue: فَلَ for قُلْ; اتَّخَذْتُمْ for أَتَّخَذْتُمْ (the interrogative hamza lost, which is what the gloss ما اتخذتم turns on); اتخدتم for اتخذتم in the gloss; تَقْلَمَونَ for تَعْلَمُونَ; عَهْدَهَ for عَهْدَهُ. Translated rather than marked illegible, since قل is fixed by both the muṣḥaf and the gloss لهم يا محمد that follows it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (قُلْ) لهم يا محمد (أَتَّخَذْتُمْ) ما اتخذتم (عِندَ اللَّهِ عَهْداً) ... (فَلَنْ يُخْلِفَ اللَّهُ عَهْدَهُ أَمْ) بل (تَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ) — Q. 2:80. The gloss ما اتخذتم reads the interrogative as a denial and is rendered "you have not taken." The paragraph then ends mid-gloss at تمسكم, completed by النار وتخلدون فيها at the head of ¶39.

problems.arabic: (من كسب سيئة) شركا (و أحَظَتْ بِهِ خَطِيئته) من كل جانب
problems.issue: أحَظَتْ for أَحَاطَتْ; the first lemma is printed without vocalisation, unlike the rest of the chunk; word division broken at و أحظت.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (مَن كَسَبَ سَيِّئَةً) شركا (وَأَحَاطَتْ بِهِ خَطِيئَتُهُ) من كل جانب — Q. 2:81. خَطِيئَتُهُ (singular) is the reading the transcription carries; the Ḥafṣ text has خَطِيئَاتُهُ, so this may be a variant reading rather than OCR damage, and is translated as it stands ("his sin").

problems.issue: The chunk opens mid-clause. The printed page breaks inside the gloss on ¶40's preceding lemma (وأحاطت به خطيئته, Q. 2:81, glossed at the end of ¶39 as من كل جانب), so بأن مات مشركا has no governing term here. Translated from where it starts, with no invented beginning.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the sense is completed by the preceding gloss — ‹أحاطت به خطيئته من كل جانب› بأن مات مشركا, "his sin encompassed him from every side in that he died an idolater." No text is missing from the transcription itself.

problems.arabic: (جَأَوْلَيِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ مِيْهَا عَالِدُونّ وَالذِيسَ عَامَنُواْ وَعَبَلُوا الصَّلِحَتِ أَوْلَبِكَ أَصْحَبُ الْجَنَّةِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ)
problems.issue: Dense OCR damage across the whole Q. 2:81–82 lemma: جَأَوْلَيِكَ for فَأُولَٰئِكَ (jīm for fāʾ); مِيْهَا for فِيهَا (mīm for fāʾ); عَالِدُونّ for خَالِدُونَ (ʿayn for khāʾ); وَالذِيسَ for وَالَّذِينَ (sīn for nūn); عَامَنُواْ for آمَنُوا; وَعَبَلُوا for وَعَمِلُوا (bāʾ for mīm); أَوْلَبِكَ for أُولَٰئِكَ. Translated rather than marked illegible: the reading is fixed by Q. 2:81–82, and the second half of the lemma (هُمْ فِيهَا خَـلِدُونَ) comes through clean and supplies the parallel for the damaged first half.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): فَأُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ أُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ.

problems.arabic: قرن الجملة الأولى بالفاء لأن دخوهم النار تسببوا فيه فيجاء بفاء السبية، والجملة الأخيرة ليس فيها فاء
problems.issue: The grammatical point depends on a letter the OCR destroyed. Niasse observes that the first sentence carries the fāʾ and the second does not — which is correct of Q. 2:81–82 — but the transcription prints جَأَوْلَيِكَ, with a jīm where the fāʾ belongs. The exposition is itself the witness that restores the lemma, and the English keeps the connective ("So those are...") so that the observation about causation has something to attach to.
problems.conjecture: Not a conjecture about the sense: Niasse's own argument fixes فَأُولَٰئِكَ against أُولَٰئِكَ in Q. 2:82. A press edition should restore the fāʾ in the Arabic text.

problems.arabic: لأن دخوهم النار تسببوا فيه فيجاء بفاء السبية
problems.issue: Two words lost a letter each: دخوهم for دخولهم (dropped lām) and السبية for السببية (dropped bāʾ). Both are determined by the syntax and by the standard grammatical term فاء السببية.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لأن دخولهم النار تسببوا فيه فيجاء بفاء السببية. Orthographic only; the English is unaffected.

problems.arabic: (لن يدخِل أحدكم عملُه الجنة قالوا: ولا أنت يا رسول اللّه، قال ولا أنا إلا أن يتغمدني اللّٰه برحمته)[28]
problems.issue: Transmission variant, not OCR. The ḥadīth as transcribed reads لن يدخِل أحدكم عملُه الجنة and ends برحمته; al-Bukhārī (Riqāq) has لن يدخل أحدا عمله الجنة and ends بمغفرة ورحمة. Translated as transcribed; the footnote [28] of the printing should be checked against whatever it cites.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: an oral paraphrase rather than a corruption — أحدكم for أحدا suits a lesson addressed to those present, and برحمته is a common short form of بمغفرة ورحمة.

problems.issue: Set in the same parentheses the printing uses for Qurʾanic lemmata, but it is not Qurʾān; it carries a footnote of its own. Marked "h" on the strength of that footnote and of its circulation as a ḥadīth (al-Ṭabarānī, al-Muʿjam al-kabīr), although its attribution is contested and it is often cited without isnād.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the printing's parentheses here mark a quotation, not a lemma. A press edition should distinguish the two sets of brackets, since the paragraph turns on the difference between what the āya says and what the saying adds.

problems.arabic: المؤمن ينوي أنه مؤمن وطائع ولو عمر أبدا
problems.issue: ¶40 ends mid-sentence: the conditional ولو عمر أبدا has no apodosis here. It is completed by the first words of ¶41 (لكان مؤمنا أبدا). Left incomplete, as the paragraph stands.
problems.conjecture: Not a conjecture: the continuation is present in ¶41 of this same chunk. عُمِرَ is read as the passive ("were he granted life"), parallel to ولو عاش أبدا of the unbeliever in ¶41.

problems.issue: ¶41 opens mid-sentence, as the apodosis of the conditional left hanging at the end of ¶40. Translated from where it starts; the subject is carried by the Arabic verb, so "he" is not bracketed as an editorial addition.
problems.conjecture: Not a conjecture: the protasis is ¶40's المؤمن ينوي أنه مؤمن وطائع ولو عمر أبدا.

problems.arabic: و اذكر ( إِذّ آخَذْنَا مِيثَقَ بَنِه إِسْرَأَءِيلَ)
problems.issue: The paragraph is a page-break fragment of the Q. 2:83 lemma block, and the lemma is damaged: إِذّ for إِذْ, آخَذْنَا for أَخَذْنَا, بَنِه for بَنِي (hāʾ for yāʾ), إِسْرَأَءِيلَ for إِسْرَائِيلَ. و اذكر is not part of the lemma — it is the elided imperative supplied in the manner of the Jalālayn, and is marked "p".
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ. The glosses في التوراة and وقلنا are the Jalālayn's own on this āya, which confirms the identification.

problems.issue: Three faults in one span: the opening bracket of the lemma is lost, so the Qurʾanic words run on from the gloss وقلنا with no delimiter; a wāw stands before لا تعبدون where Q. 2:83 has none; and اللَّةً is written with tāʾ for hāʾ. Translated as it stands, wāw included ("and you shall not worship"), rather than silently conformed to the muṣḥaf.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وقلنا (لَا تَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ). The stray wāw is most likely the lost opening bracket misread, or the wāw of the following وبالوالدين pulled forward.

problems.issue: ¶42 ends on a bare wāw and a closing bracket, with nothing to read. Marked illegible rather than guessed, since the span carries no word of its own.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the wāw of وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ (Q. 2:83), caught at the page break and completed at the start of ¶43, where the same word appears — also damaged — as وياأوليتني. The closing bracket is misplaced: the lemma does not end here.

problems.issue: وياأوليتني is not a word. Three witnesses fix it: Q. 2:83, the إحْسَنا that immediately follows, and the gloss برا, which is the Jalālayn's gloss on إِحْسَانًا in this very āya. Translated rather than marked illegible on that basis; the damage is recorded here because the span is too corrupt to be read on its own.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): أحسنوا (وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا) برا — the rasm وبالولدين read letter by letter as وياأوليتني. أحسنوا is Niasse's supplied imperative, marked "p", not part of the lemma.

problems.issue: Damage through the whole lemma: وَذِ for وَذِي, ٱلْقَرَبِى for الْقُرْبَى, وَالْيَتَبِى for وَالْيَتَامَى, وَالْمَسَاْكَينُ for وَالْمَسَاكِينِ, وَقَوَلُواْ for وَقُولُوا, لِتَايِ for لِلنَّاسِ. ¶44 re-cites والمساكين and وقولوا للناس cleanly, which settles the readings.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَذِي الْقُرْبَى وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَقُولُوا لِلنَّاسِ.

problems.issue: ¶43 ends inside the lemma, on لِتَايِ (= لِلنَّاسِ), and ¶44 opens on the word that completes it, حسْنأه (= حُسْنًا). No Qurʾanic reference is given at the end of ¶43, since the run it belongs to is referenced at the end of ¶42.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لِلنَّاسِ حُسْنًا (Q. 2:83), split by the printed pagination. حسْنأه shows a stray hamza and hāʾ for the tanwīn of حُسْنًا.

problems.arabic: (وَذِ ٱلْقَرَبِى وَالْيَتَبِى وَالْمَسَاْكَينُ وَقَوَلُواْ لِتَايِ ... «وَقُولُواْ لِلنَّاس» جميعا « حُسْناً»
problems.issue: The same stretch of Q. 2:83 is cited twice: once as a continuous lemma block in ¶42–¶43 (closing with حسنا at the head of ¶44), then again in ¶44 word by word with fresh glosses, and with different delimiters — ( ) for the block, « » for the gloss pass. This is not scrambled transcription but the printing's layout, and the English repeats the lemmata as the Arabic repeats them. Nothing has been reordered or merged.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the double citation reflects the oral delivery — the āya read through first, then taken apart — and the printing's two bracket sets preserve the distinction. A press edition may wish to normalise the delimiters while keeping both passes.

problems.issue: برورهما admits two readings and the transcription does not decide between them: بِرُّهُمَا ("dutifulness to them") with a stray wāw, or the plural بُرُورهما ("acts of dutifulness toward them"). The English is the same either way, so the span is translated rather than marked.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: بِرُّهُمَا واجب, the singular, which is the standard formula and matches the singular predicate واجب.

problems.issue: Transmission variant, not OCR. al-Bukhārī has أنا وكافل اليتيم في الجنة هكذا, with the gesture of the two fingers reported in the narration; the transcription has كهاتين ("like these two"), which absorbs the gesture into the words. Translated as transcribed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: an oral form in which the gesture is made while speaking, so that كهاتين stands for هكذا وأشار بالسبابة والوسطى. "These two" is left unexplained in the English, as in the Arabic.

problems.issue: أَلصَّلَوةَ carries a prothetic hamza on the article, and وَءَاتُواْ writes the hamza of وَآتُوا as a separate letter. Both are scan artefacts of the printing's vocalisation.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ (Q. 2:83). Orthographic only.

problems.issue: إِلَّ for إِلَّا (the same loss recurs later in إِلَّ خِزْيٌ); مُعْرِضُون for مُعْرِضُونَ; and the closing bracket is missing, so the gloss كابائكم (= كآبائكم, "like your forefathers") runs on from the lemma with no delimiter. The gloss is marked "p" and the lemma "q" on the authority of Q. 2:83.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf and the Jalālayn): (إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنكُمْ وَأَنتُم مُعْرِضُونَ) كآبائكم.

problems.issue: مِيقَفَكُمْ for مِيثَاقَكُمْ — qāf for thāʾ and fāʾ for the alif of the rasm, two faults in one word; وَإذَ for وَإِذْ and اخَذُّنَا for أَخَذْنَا. The reading is fixed by the parallel formula in ¶42 (إِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ) and by the gloss قبلتم ذلك الميثاق below.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ (Q. 2:84).

problems.arabic: (وَلَاَ تُخْرِجُونَ أَنْفُسَكْم صِ دِيْرِكُمْ ثُمَّ أَقْرَرْتُمْ)
problems.issue: صِ stands where the preposition مِن belongs — the heaviest single loss in the paragraph — and دِيْرِكُمْ for دِيَارِكُمْ. Translated rather than marked illegible, since Q. 2:84 and the same construction a few lines later (مِن دِيَارِهِمْ, which comes through clean) both fix it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَلَا تُخْرِجُونَ أَنفُسَكُم مِّن دِيَارِكُمْ ثُمَّ أَقْرَرْتُمْ.

problems.arabic: تتعاونون على القتل بالاثم بالمعصية والظلم
problems.issue: The gloss is compressed to the point of ellipsis: in the Jalālayn, بالمعصية glosses بِالْإِثْمِ and الظلم glosses وَالْعُدْوَانِ, but the transcription runs the lemma words and their glosses together with no marker. Kept elliptical, with "[that is,]" supplied in brackets, as the conventions direct.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: تتعاونون على القتل بالإثم ‹أي› بالمعصية والعدوان ‹أي› الظلم — i.e. a second والعدوان has dropped out before الظلم.

problems.issue: تُجَدِّوهُمْ for تُفَادُوهُمْ (jīm for fāʾ, alif lost, shādda for the long vowel); a stray wāw stands between يَاتوكُمّ and أُسَرِى; وَان for وَإِن, يَاتوكُمّ for يَأتُوكُمْ, أُسَرِى for أُسَارَى. Niasse's own gloss تفادونهم بالمال settles the verb; the stray wāw is not translated.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَإِن يَأتُوكُمْ أُسَارَى تُفَادُوهُمْ (Q. 2:85).

problems.issue: A wāw stands before إِخْرَاجُهُمْ where Q. 2:85 has none. إخراجهم is the delayed subject of محرم, and the wāw breaks that construction. The English keeps the Arabic order ("though it is forbidden to you, their expulsion") rather than smoothing it to "though their expulsion was forbidden to you"; the stray wāw is not translated.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَهُوَ مُحَرَّمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ إِخْرَاجُهُمْ.

problems.arabic: وبنو قريطة وبنو النضير ممنوعون من القتال بينهم في التوراة ... بقتل بني قريطة ونفي بني النضير
problems.issue: قريطة with ṭāʾ twice, against قريظة with ẓāʾ elsewhere in the same paragraph — an inconsistency within one page. Rendered Qurayẓa throughout.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: قريظة, as the paragraph's other occurrences have it; ṭāʾ and ẓāʾ differ only by the dot.

problems.arabic: قالوا تقاتلونهم وإذا أتى أساراهم تفادونهم قالوا أمرنا بهذا في التوراة
problems.issue: قالوا carries two different subjects in one sentence — the questioners, then the Jews answering — and the transcription names neither. The exchange is intelligible only from the sense. Translated with قالوا rendered "They said" both times, keeping the Arabic's own indeterminacy rather than supplying a subject.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the first قالوا was قيل لهم ("it was said to them"), on the pattern of the parallel exchange a few lines earlier — فإذا قيل لهم أتقاتلون إخوانكم؟ قالوا...

problems.issue: وبّحتهم is not a word; وبّختهم ("rebuked them") is determined by the sense and by الآية as its subject, the rebuke being the أَفَتُؤْمِنُونَ that follows.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فلهذا وبّختهم الآية — khāʾ read as ḥāʾ, the dot lost.

problems.issue: Two faults, the second substantive. أَبَتَومِنُونَ يِبَعْضِ for أَفَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِبَعْضِ is orthographic. But وَتَكْبُرُونَ stands for وَتَكْفُرُونَ (bāʾ for fāʾ), and as it stands it would read "you grow proud at part of it" rather than "you disbelieve in part of it." The rebuke of the āya is about kufr, and Niasse's own gloss وهو ترك القتل والإخراج identifies the part they reject, not a part they boast of. Translated "and disbelieve in part"; the damaged form is recorded here because it changes the sense.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): أَفَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِبَعْضِ الْكِتَابِ وَتَكْفُرُونَ بِبَعْضٍ (Q. 2:85).

problems.arabic: (بَمَا جَزَاءَ مَنْ يَبْعَلُ ذَلِكَ مِنْكُمُو إِلَّ خِزْيٌ
problems.issue: بَمَا for فَمَا (bāʾ for fāʾ, which turns the interrogative into a relative); يَبْعَلُ for يَفْعَلُ; مِنْكُمُو with a trailing wāw for مِنكُمْ; إِلَّ for إِلَّا; and the closing bracket is missing, so the gloss هوان وذل runs on from the lemma. Translated as the interrogative, which Q. 2:85 and the إلا of the exceptive both require.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): فَمَا جَزَاءُ مَن يَفْعَلُ ذَٰلِكَ مِنكُمْ إِلَّا خِزْيٌ.

problems.issue: هِ stands for the preposition فِي, and the lemma again lacks a closing bracket. الدَّنْيَا for الدُّنْيَا is a vowel fault only. Fixed by Q. 2:85 and by the خزي it depends on.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا (Q. 2:85).

problems.issue: فرِيفاً is not a word: the qāf of فَرِيقًا has been read as fāʾ (two dots above for one). The correct form stands in the gloss immediately following, فكذبتم فريقا منهم.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf and from the gloss): فَرِيقًا كَذَّبْتُمْ (Q. 2:87).

problems.issue: The paragraph ends mid-lemma at the page break with the bracket open; its verb (تَقْتُلُونَ) stands at the head of ¶47. Each half is translated where it stands and nothing has been carried across the break.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وَفَرِيقًا تَقْتُلُونَ (Q. 2:87), the lemma split by the printed pagination.

problems.issue: The lemma resumed at the head of the paragraph carries a wāw — وتقتلون — where Q. 2:87 has تَقْتُلُونَ, the wāw belonging to وَفَرِيقًا at the end of ¶46; the same word is then repeated immediately as the opening of the gloss, so that it stands twice with only the closing bracket between. Translated as transcribed, lemma then gloss, with no reordering.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وَفَرِيقًا (¶46) تَقْتُلُونَ) وتقتلون فريقا بالمضارع. The duplication is a feature of the transcription at the page join, not of the Arabic sense.

problems.issue: ويحي for يَحْيَى: the final alif maqṣūra has dropped.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: زَكَرِيَّاءَ وَيَحْيَى. Orthographic only; rendered Zakariyyāʾ and Yaḥyā.

problems.arabic: قال: (أنشدكم بالله هل تصْدقونني؟ … استرحنا منك[33]
problems.issue: The quoted exchange at Khaybar opens with a parenthesis that is never closed; the quotation runs to استرحنا منك, where the footnote marker [33] falls. Parentheses elsewhere in the chunk mark Qurʾānic lemmata, but the content here is ḥadīth, so it is set in the ḥadīth register with double quotation marks and the bracket is not reproduced.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the printed text closes the quotation at استرحنا منك, immediately before the footnote marker. The embedded dialogue (قالوا … قال) is kept inside the single quotation, as in the preceding chunks.

problems.issue: اللَّهَ is vocalised accusative although it is the subject of لَعَنَ; Q. 2:88 reads لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): بَل لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِكُفْرِهِمْ (Q. 2:88). Vocalisation only.

problems.arabic: فَقَلِيلاࣰ مَّا يُومِنُونَ … نُومِلُ … مُومِنِين … يَامُرُكُم … بيسمَا … قَالوأْ
problems.issue: The transcription loses hamza systematically: ؤ is written و (يُومِنُونَ, مُومِنِين), أ is written alif or dropped (يَامُرُكُم), ئ is written ي (بيسمَا for بِئْسَمَا), and in one place a final hamza is added where none belongs (قَالوأْ for قَالُوا). Logged once here for the whole chunk; each instance is translated as the unimpaired form.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: يُؤْمِنُونَ, نُؤْمِنُ, مُؤْمِنِينَ, يَأْمُرُكُم, بِئْسَمَا, قَالُوا. Orthographic throughout; the English is unaffected.

problems.issue: The word that opens the paragraph glosses يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ at the end of ¶48, but يستنكرون ("they disavow") cannot gloss it and contradicts what follows, يقولون اللهم انصرنا عليهم. Marked illegible rather than translated, since the gloss is Niasse's own prose and no fixed text secures the reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: يستنصرون ("they sought victory"), the Jalālayn gloss on يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ at Q. 2:89, with ص read as ك. The following clause — O Allah, grant us victory over them — supports it, but the restoration remains a conjecture.

problems.issue: كَبَرْوا for كَفَرُوا (bāʾ for fāʾ, as at ¶45) and بِهُ for بِهِ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): كَفَرُوا بِهِ (Q. 2:89). The gloss that follows, حسدا وخوفا على الرئاسة, fits only unbelief.

problems.issue: Three defects in one lemma: أَنْمُسَهُم for أَنفُسَهُم (as at ¶45), a stray وَ after هُمُ, and يَكْبُرُوا for يَكْفُرُوا (bāʾ for fāʾ again).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): بِئْسَمَا اشْتَرَوْا بِهِ أَنفُسَهُمْ أَن يَكْفُرُوا (Q. 2:90). The gloss كفرهم immediately after confirms يَكْفُرُوا.

problems.issue: The gloss من القرآن stands inside the lemma's brackets, between أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ and بَغْيًا. Set as Niasse's prose, per the rule that bracket content is treated as Qurʾān only when it is Qurʾān.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (بِمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ) من القرآن (بَغْيًا) (Q. 2:90) — a dropped bracket pair, not a variant reading.

problems.issue: وَلِلْكَبِرِيَ is not a word. The ductus of الكافرين has collapsed: the alif of الكافرين is lost, the fāʾ read as bāʾ, and the final nūn as yāʾ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَلِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابٌ مُهِينٌ (Q. 2:90). The reading is fixed by the āya and by the gloss ذو إهانة that follows. Translated rather than marked illegible because the underlying text is a fixed one.

problems.arabic: ( قَالواْ نُومِلُ بِمَآ أَنزِلَ عَلَيْنَا أي التوراة قال تعالى
problems.issue: The lemma's bracket is never closed, so both the gloss أي التوراة and the formula قال تعالى that introduces the next lemma fall inside it; both are set as prose. Also نُومِلُ for نُؤْمِنُ (nūn read as lām as well as the hamza loss logged at ¶48) and أَنزِلَ for أُنزِلَ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (قَالُوا نُؤْمِنُ بِمَا أُنزِلَ عَلَيْنَا) أي التوراة، قال تعالى (Q. 2:91).

problems.arabic: بِمَا وَرَآءَهُو أي بما سواه وهو القرآن
problems.issue: بِمَا وَرَآءَهُ stands outside any bracket although it is Qurʾānic; treated as a lemma on the strength of Q. 2:91 and of the gloss أي بما سواه that follows it. Also وَرَآءَهُو, with a stray wāw for the pronoun ـهُ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (وَيَكْفُرُونَ بِمَا وَرَاءَهُ) (Q. 2:91). The brackets have dropped; the final wāw is orthographic.

problems.issue: The lemma reads تَقْتُلُونَ where Q. 2:91 has قَتَلْتُمْ, and the gloss immediately after is قتلتم — the Qurʾānic past tense. Both are translated as they stand: the lemma as a present, the gloss as a past.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the lemma should read قُلْ فَلِمَ قَتَلْتُمْ (Q. 2:91), with قتلتم as the gloss retained from the transcription. Alternatively the transcription has carried the imperfect over from وَفَرِيقًا تَقْتُلُونَ at ¶46–47; the gloss, either way, preserves the Qurʾānic reading.

problems.issue: The lemma's closing bracket is missing, so the gloss باتخاذه falls inside it; also ظَلِمُون for ظَالِمُونَ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (وَأَنتُمْ ظَالِمُونَ) باتخاذه (Q. 2:92).

problems.arabic: (ثُمَّ إتَّخَذْتُّمْ الْعِجْلَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ) … (وَإِذَ آخَذْنَا مِيثَقَكُمْ)
problems.issue: إتَّخَذْتُّمْ for اتَّخَذْتُمُ, with the shadda displaced onto the tāʾ of the suffix; وَإِذَ آخَذْنَا for وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا; مِيثَقَكُمْ for مِيثَاقَكُمْ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ مِن بَعْدِهِ (Q. 2:92); وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ (Q. 2:93). Orthographic only.

problems.issue: Three corruptions in one lemma: وَرَبَعْنَا for وَرَفَعْنَا (bāʾ for fāʾ), بَوْفَكُم for فَوْقَكُم (fāʾ read as bāʾ and qāf as fāʾ), and الظُّورَ for الطُّورَ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ (Q. 2:93). The reading is fixed by the āya and by Niasse's gloss الجبل, "the mountain." Translated rather than marked illegible for that reason.

problems.issue: The lemma's closing bracket is missing, so the gloss falls inside it; and يجد stands for بِجِدٍّ (bāʾ read as yāʾ, two dots below for one).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf and the Jalālayn gloss): (خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُم بِقُوَّةٍ) بجدٍّ واجتهادٍ (Q. 2:93).

problems.issue: بِكُبْرِهِمْ for بِكُفْرِهِمْ and فُلْ for قُلْ — the same fāʾ/bāʾ and qāf/fāʾ confusions as at ¶45 and ¶50. The gloss لهم stands outside the bracket, which closes after a space.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): بِكُفْرِهِمْ قُلْ (Q. 2:93). The gloss "to them" belongs to قُلْ.

problems.issue: إِيمَنُكُم for إِيمَانُكُمْ (the alif of إيمان lost); and the paragraph ends mid-clause at إن كان, whose predicate stands at the head of ¶52. Translated to the break, with nothing supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): بِئْسَمَا يَأْمُرُكُم بِهِ إِيمَانُكُمْ (Q. 2:93); the clause completes as إن كان الإيمان بالتوراة هذا مقتضاه عندكم (¶52).

problems.issue: فبيس for فَبِئْسَ (the hamza loss logged at ¶48).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فبئس الإيمان إيمانكم. Orthographic only.

problems.issue: كْنتُم for كُنتُم; and a bare و stands before كما زعمتم, where the gloss "as you claimed" needs no conjunction. Translated as "and as you claimed."
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: إِن كُنتُم مُؤْمِنِينَ (Q. 2:93), glossed كما زعمتم. The wāw is probably a duplicated letter from the line above; a press edition may drop it.

problems.issue: Doubled closing parenthesis, as at ¶45, with no unmatched opening bracket nearby.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (عِندَ اللَّهِ خَالِصَةً) (Q. 2:94). Typographic only.

problems.issue: مِ دُولِ for مِن دُونِ: the nūn of مِن has dropped and دُونِ has been read with a lām.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): مِن دُونِ النَّاسِ (Q. 2:94).

problems.issue: حَبَوَةٌ for حَيَاةٍ — yāʾ read as bāʾ and alif as wāw — with a nominative ending where the genitive is required.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): عَلَىٰ حَيَاةٍ (Q. 2:96). The reading is fixed by the āya and by Niasse's gloss حرص اليهود على الحياة immediately after, so the span is translated.

problems.arabic: (يَوَدُّ) يتمنى ( أَحَدُهُمْ لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ )
problems.issue: The lemma of Q. 2:96 is broken into two brackets around the gloss يتمنى, so that يَوَدُّ and أَحَدُهُمْ — verb and subject — are separated. Translated in the order transcribed, with no reordering.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمْ لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ) يتمنى تعميره ألف سنة (Q. 2:96) — the gloss displaced into the lemma by the transcription.

problems.issue: The chunk ends mid-āya: the predicate of وَمَا هُوَ (بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ) falls in the next chunk. Translated to the break, with nothing supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وَمَا هُوَ بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ (Q. 2:96), the lemma split by the printed pagination.

problems.issue: The closing lemma of Q. 2:97 and the opening lemma of Q. 2:98 share one parenthesis, and the second is corrupt: عَدْوَا for عَدُوًّا, and يَدِ, which is not a word in this position. Translated rather than marked illegible, because the reading is fixed by the muṣḥaf and by the gloss that immediately follows it — عداوته لجبريل أكسبته عداوته لله, which only makes sense as a gloss on عدوًّا لله.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): مَن كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِلَّهِ, “Whoever is an enemy to Allah” (Q. 2:98). يَدِ is a misreading of لِلَّهِ.

problems.issue: Orthographic only: المومنين for المؤمنين, with a spurious ḍamma on the final nūn in place of the genitive. The English is unaffected.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ.

problems.arabic: (وَمَلَٰٓيكتِهِ )لِه الأناء وَبْرِيل كل) الذي قالوا إنه
problems.issue: The worst-damaged span in the chunk. After the legible lemma وملائكته the parenthesis boundaries collapse — a closing bracket stands where an opening one belongs — and three or four words are garbled. The span is marked illegible as it stands and neither reordered nor restored in the translation, because one of the damaged words (الأناء) belongs to Niasse's own interlinear gloss and so cannot be recovered from the muṣḥaf. The words that follow, الذي قالوا إنه صديقهم (running into ¶59), gloss the last item of the lemma.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ) الأنبياء (وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ) — “and His angels and His messengers” — the prophets — “and Jibrīl and Mīkāl” (Q. 2:98). Reading )لِه as ورسله, الأناء as الأنبياء (the gloss on ورسله), وَبْرِيل as وجبريل, and كل as وميكال. The identification of كل with وميكال is supported by the gloss that follows it: Mīkāʾīl is the angel the Jews have just claimed in ¶56 as their friend (نحن أحباء ميكائيل).

problems.issue: Misdotting across the whole clause: يَكُبُرْ for يَكْفُرُ, إِلَّ for إِلَّا, and الْعِيفُونُ, which is not a word. The closing parenthesis is also missing. Translated rather than marked illegible, since the clause is the remainder of Q. 2:99 and is fixed by the muṣḥaf.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَمَا يَكْفُرُ بِهَا إِلَّا الْفَاسِقُونَ (Q. 2:99).

problems.issue: No opening parenthesis on the lemma, and كُلَّتَا is ungrammatical here (كلتا is the dual “both”). عَهَدُواْ also stands for the form III عَاهَدُوا. Translated from the muṣḥaf reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): أَوَكُلَّمَا عَاهَدُوا عَهْدًا (Q. 2:100), “and is it not so that whenever they made a covenant.”

problems.issue: بَرِيقٌ (“gleam”) for فَرِيقٌ (“a party”) — one dot below for one dot above. Decided internally as well as by the muṣḥaf: the same word is set correctly a few lines later in this same paragraph, نَبَذَ فَرِيقࣱ مِّنَ اَ۬لذِينَ أُوتُواْ اُ۬لْكِتَٰبَ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): نَبَذَهُ فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ (Q. 2:100), “a party of them cast it aside.”

problems.issue: تَثْلُوا for تَتْلُو, and وَاتَّبَعْواْ for وَاتَّبَعُوا. The gloss that follows, ما تلت, puts the verb in the perfect and so confirms which verb is meant.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَاتَّبَعُوا مَا تَتْلُو (Q. 2:102).

problems.issue: سُلَيْمَتَ is not a name; the final ـتَ stands for ـانَ. مَلْكِ is also unvocalised for مُلْكِ, and the closing parenthesis is missing. Translated from the muṣḥaf reading, the name being secure from the surrounding narrative, which is entirely about Sulaymān.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): مُلْكِ سُلَيْمَانَ (Q. 2:102).

problems.issue: Orthographic residue that does not affect the English: a doubled hamza-alif in آَنزَلْنَآ, ءَايَتٍ for آيَاتٍ (the second alif lost), and كَأَنَّهَمْ for كَأَنَّهُمْ. Listed for the proofreader, not as a translation problem.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): أَنزَلْنَا, آيَاتٍ, كَأَنَّهُمْ.

problems.arabic: أنولهما اللّه بلاء يعلمان الناس السحر
problems.issue: أنولهما is not a word: the zāʾ of أنزلهما has been read as a wāw. The clause is the Jalālayn-style gloss on وما أنزل على الملكين ببابل هاروت وماروت, whose lemma stands in the preceding chunk, so ¶61 opens in mid-gloss. Translated rather than marked illegible, since the gloss is a fixed text; the damage is recorded here.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: أنزلهما الله بلاءً, "Allah sent the two of them down as a trial" — the Jalālayn's gloss on Q. 2:102 (بل أنزلهما الله بلاءً للناس يعلمان الناس السحر).

problems.issue: A Qurʾānic lemma damaged in both words: جَلا for فَلا (jīm for fāʾ, one dot below for one above) and تَكْبُرٌ for تَكْفُرْ (bāʾ for fāʾ, with a spurious tanwīn on a jussive). The earlier part of the verse (وما يعلمان من أحد حتى يقولا إنما نحن فتنة) is not quoted here, so the lemma stands abruptly after the gloss ويعلمانهم أن السحر كفر. Translated rather than marked illegible, because the following فيتعلمون منهما fixes the position in Q. 2:102.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): فَلا تَكْفُرْ, "so do not disbelieve" (Q. 2:102).

problems.arabic: مَا يُعَرِّفُونَ بِهِ، بَيْرَ الْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِ
problems.issue: Two defects in one lemma: يُعَرِّفُونَ for يُفَرِّقُونَ and بَيرَ for بَينَ (rāʾ for nūn). يعرفون is itself a word ("they make known"), so the damage does not announce itself and would otherwise pass into the English as a false reading of the āya; the muṣḥaf reading is translated and the damage recorded here. The comma after بِهِ and the closing bracket after وَزَوْجِهِ without an opening one are typesetting artefacts.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِ بَينَ الْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِ, "that by which they separate a man and his wife" (Q. 2:102).

problems.arabic: فإذا تعليم السحر كان لاجتنابه فقط
problems.issue: فإذا here is the conclusion-marker, not the conditional إذا: as printed it invites the reading "so when the teaching of sorcery was...", which leaves the sentence without a main clause. Rendered "So the teaching of sorcery was for avoiding it alone."
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فإذاً (فإذن), "so then / therefore." Orthographic only; the English is unaffected.

problems.issue: امتلثوا is not a word — a metathesis of امتثلوا. The clause is Niasse's own gloss on آمنوا واتقوا and so is not fixed by a canonical text; it is restored from agreement (أمر الله as its object, لأثيبوا as the apodosis) rather than guessed at silently.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: امتثلوا أمر الله لأُثيبوا, "had they complied with Allah's command they would have been rewarded."

problems.issue: Not treated as damage, and so not marked. The lemma run is printed in Warsh orthography throughout (اِڬللَّهِ, ءَامَنُواْ, فِے, اِڪشْتَرڪيٰهُ), and لَبِيسَ reflects Warsh's ibdāl of the hamza of بِئْسَ into yāʾ rather than an OCR substitution for لَبِئْسَ. Flagged because a reader collating against a Ḥafṣ text will see a discrepancy.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: read وَلَبِيسَ with Warsh ʿan Nāfiʿ against وَلَبِئْسَ in Ḥafṣ; the English ("and evil is that for which they sold themselves") is the same either way. To be confirmed against the muṣḥaf used by the printed edition.

problems.issue: The printed page break falls inside the phrase من الرعونة: ¶61 ends at من and ¶62 opens at الرعونة. Not OCR damage. Translated as it stands — ¶61 closes with "from" and ¶62 opens with al-ruʿūna — with no invented beginning for ¶62.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: in continuous text the clause reads وهو سبٌّ عندهم من الرعونة, "and with them it is an insult, from al-ruʿūna [folly]" — the point of the sabab al-nuzūl: the Jews' راعنا was heard as derived from رعونة, not رعاية. A press edition may wish to close the phrase at the paragraph join.

runs: Whatever āya We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or the like of it (Q. 2:106)

The occasion for this āya's revelation is that the Jews and the polytheists impugned the abrogation of some of the āyas of the Qurʾān. They said: had it been the speech of Allah it would not have been abrogated, since abrogation is not permissible in the speech of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And this [is] from the extremity of their ignorance. Abrogation did occur in the Qurʾān, by transmission, by the text of the Qurʾān, and the intellect accepts it. Abrogation came in three modes: an āya whose recitation and whose ruling were abrogated, as in His words:

this was an āya that was recited and whose ruling was in force; then its recitation was abrogated and its ruling was abrogated. And an āya whose recitation was abrogated and whose ruling remained, as in His words:
“The aged man and the aged woman, if they commit fornication, stone them both outright,”
this was an āya that was recited; its recitation was lifted and its ruling is in force. And an āya whose ruling was lifted and whose recitation remained
It is prescribed for you, when death comes to one of you, if he leaves wealth
This is an āya that is recited to this day and whose ruling is abrogated. It was abrogated by the āya of inheritance, and the Prophet ﷺ made its abrogation clear by his words:
“There is no bequest to an heir”

The āya is not abrogated by the ḥadīth; rather the ḥadīth makes clear that this āya is abrogated. For the āya has made clear that whatever Allah abrogates, He brings something better than it, and the speech of the created being is never better than the speech of the Creator. Except that revelation is of two kinds: something that is recited and something that is sent down upon the Prophet ﷺ and he then makes it clear to us. In any case, abrogation occurs in the Qurʾān by transmission
As for [abrogation] rationally: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the freely choosing Agent, disposing of existence as He wills
He puts a ruling into effect for a time; and if He wills, He brings it to an end and brings a new ruling. There is no objection against Him in this. So this āya was revealed.
we remove its ruling, either together with its wording or its ruling alone
or cause it to be forgotten
we defer its recitation and do not remove its ruling, its recitation being lifted
that is, one more beneficial to the servants than it, in ease or in the abundance of its reward
in obligation and in reward; and [this is] the conclusive proof
Do you not know that Allah has power over all things (Q. 2:106)
and abrogation and substitution are among [the things in His power]
Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth (Q. 2:107)
He is the Owner who disposes as He wills. If they acknowledge that He is the One
the Overwhelming, the Doer of what He wills, they will not object to Him over the abrogation of some of the rulings.
And you have no, apart from Allah
who would ward off His chastisement from you if it came to you.
Allah, Blessed and Exalted, set out in the last āya of what we read yesterday

the ruling on sorcery. The ruling on sorcery is that it is forbidden, a grave sin and unbelief, and it never goes together with faith, and no one practises it but an unbeliever. The proof that sorcery is unbelief is Allah's denial, Blessed and Exalted, of sorcery of Sulaymān. He said:

meaning he did not practise sorcery. On this basis sorcery is unbelief. And the angels whom Allah sent down came to teach sorcery, to teach that it is evil so that they would avoid it. The exegetes bring a story about these two angels, Hārūt and Mārūt, and the story has no basis. Many of the exegetes have affirmed it, but they took it from the

alone, and the Qurʾān gives it the lie. The story: they said that the angels reproached the children of Ādam for the multitude of their sins. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: I created them and set in them an appetite that demands these acts of disobedience from them, and had I set this appetite in you, the like of what occurred from them would have occurred from you. They said: It is not possible for us that we should ever disobey You. This answer no angel could ever give. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: Choose from among your righteous. So they chose Hārūt and Mārūt, and the two were among the most righteous of the angels. So Allah set in the two of them the appetite for food, for drink and for sexual intercourse, and sent them down to the earth, and commanded them to associate nothing with Allah, to kill no soul, not to commit fornication, to judge by nothing but what Allah had sent down, and not to drink wine. So the two came down and began to judge among the people by the truth. And when night came the two would invoke the Name and return to the Highest Assembly, and when morning broke they would return as well, and when night came they would recite the Name that Allah had taught them and they would ascend to heaven, until a woman fell into a dispute with her husband and the two of them stood before the two [angels]. When one of the two angels looked at her, she took hold of the whole of his heart, and he turned to his companion and said to him: Has the like of what has befallen me befallen you? He said to him: Yes. What is to be done? He said: We shall only try [to win] her. He said: Did not

[Do] you know that Allah is severe in punishment? He said: He is forgiving, merciful. The two of them solicited the woman, and she refused unless they would rule in her favour against her husband. So they ruled in her favour at once, that the right was with her. Then she said: You must drink some wine. So they drank. Each [time] she wanted a sin, one of them said: Allah is severe in punishment, and the other said: He is forgiving, merciful. The woman said that it did not suffice her that they rule in her favour against him, but rather that they kill him. So they killed him. Then they sought her again, and she said: You must prostrate yourselves to the idol. So they prostrated to it. Every single thing they had been forbidden came to pass from them. When night came the woman said: You must teach me the Greatest Name by which the two of you ascend to heaven. So they taught her, and she uttered the Name and flew up to heaven, and she was transformed; she is the star

[Venus] to this day — so they say — and as for the two of them, when night came they were unable to fly and to ascend to heaven, so they went to Idrīs, the prophet of that age. Allah revealed to him that the two of them were to choose between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the hereafter, and they chose the punishment of this world because it passes away. They were cast into a well, and they are being punished in that well to this day. This is the story of Hārūt and Mārūt, and it is a falsehood with no basis.
[7], and envy is among the grave sins. He said ﷺ:
“Envy devours good deeds as fire devours firewood.”
[8] — because the envier detests the blessing of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and attributes injustice to
the Creator, and shows enmity to the

of Allah, and strives to render Allah's power incapable and to stand in the way of the servants' obedience to Him. The envious man does not become master. Man is constituted to hate subordination: you will not find any man who likes to be a follower of his like except for some cause, and when that cause ceases the subordination ceases. Even our Creator has conferred upon us such benefits and goods as require of us that we be obedient to Him, and whoever wants these goods to cease wants only to remove the very existence of obedience to Him, Blessed and Exalted. The envier harms none but himself; you will not find a wrongdoer more like one wronged than the envier. Each time he does something to the one he envies, the harm of it returns upon him, so he grows the more enraged, and he does more, and it returns upon him. You find him perpetually angered by his own act. His case is the case of one who takes a stone and wants to throw it at a man's hand to break it, and the throw comes back and breaks his own hand; and he throws another stone and it comes back to his other hand; and he throws a third stone and it gouges out his eye; and he throws a fourth and it gouges out his other eye. Such is the act of the envier.
There was a king among the kings to whom a scholar used to come, and he was accepted with him, and he honoured him constantly. Each time he sat down he would say to him:
Do good to everyone who does good to you, and as for the wrongdoer, his own wrongdoing suffices him.

A man beside him envied him for his standing with this king, so he went to the king and said to him: This so-and-so whom you bring near talks about you; he says that your breath stinks. He said to him: How am I to know that he says this about [me]? He said: When he returns to you, observe what he does and you will find that he says your breath stinks. So he went out and invited the man to his house and fed him leeks and onions and garlic — these foods that have foul odours — and after that he said to him: Go to the king, he is summoning you. So he came and said to him: Do good to everyone who does good to you, and as for the wrongdoer, his own wrongdoing suffices him. He said to him: Come close to me — wanting to speak with him in confidence — and he pressed his garment to his mouth, and so he believed what had been said to him about him. The king grew angry, to the point that he wrote with his own hand, and he never wrote except for a reward; he wrote with his own hand to one of his agents: When the bearer of my letter comes to you, slaughter him and flay him and stuff his skin with straw and send it to me at once. When he had written it and sealed it he handed it to the scholar, and the envier intercepted him and said to him: Make me a gift of this letter; and he pleaded by every means until he gave him the letter. So he went to the agent and handed it to him, and

the agent read the letter and said: The king has ordered me to slaughter you and stuff your skin with straw and send it to him. He said: No, I am not the one the letter is about; go back to the king, I am not the one the letter is about. He said to him: I do not question the king's order; I carry out his order and do not question it. So he slaughtered him and flayed him and stuffed his skin with straw and sent it to the king. When the king saw it and knew that it was the envier, he sent for the scholar. The scholar entered and said: Do good to everyone who does good to you, and as for the wrongdoer, his own wrongdoing suffices him. He said to him: Tell me, what is your story? Did you not say that my breath stinks? He said: I seek refuge with Allah — am I to say about the king what I do not know? He said to him: When I brought you close to me, you covered your mouth? He said to him: That so-and-so fed me food that had an odour, and I disliked that the king should smell a foul odour [from me]. The king said to him:
Do good to everyone who does good to you, and as for the wrongdoer, his own wrongdoing suffices him.
Or do you want to ask your Messenger as Mūsā was asked (Q. 2:108)

— rather, you want to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The occasion of this āya's revelation was that the people of Mecca gathered and came to the Messenger ﷺ and said to him: If you want us to believe in you, then widen the lands of Mecca for us. Move these mountains so that we may find land to sow in; and make al-Ṣafā gold for us; and send to us Quṣayy b. Kilāb, our ancestor, that we may consult him about believing in you; and bring us the angels, that they may testify for you that you are a prophet.
Or do you want to ask your Messenger as Mūsā was asked
And whoever exchanges belief for unbelief

has strayed from the right way (Q. 2:108)

Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back into unbelievers after your belief, out of envy from within themselves

When ʿAmmār and Bilāl came back from the Prophet’s campaigns ﷺ, they would pass by a church and listen to the sermons, finding in them some reports that strengthened them in their belief in the Prophet ﷺ and in the Qurʾān. They said: Like this — it is like killing. He said: We have made a covenant with Muḥammad ﷺ to follow him for the span of our lives, so we will never break his covenant. Then this āya was revealed:
Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back into unbelievers after your belief, out of envy from within themselves

And he began to weep most bitterly, [insisting] that he must go to the House of Allah — he supposed the matter to be as it is with the state of human beings. He persisted in weeping until the people said: Carry him with you. So he carried him with him, until he came near the House; and when he said, This is the House of Allah, the boy died [31]. The righteous man lamented the death of his son: My son, the fruit of my heart. It was said to him: You wanted the House and you reached the House, and he wanted the Lord of the House — he met the Lord of the House and could not bear Him, and he died. When he heard only the House of Allah, he supposed that Allah was present there, and he longed for Him; and when he arrived, Allah made his hope come true, and he reached the Presence while he was weak, and the poor creature died.
