It breaks off at the page turn and resumes at the head of ¶2 (الوصية للوالدين); the citation (Q. 2:180) is therefore given at the end of the run in ¶2, not here.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ إِن تَرَكَ خَيراً (Q. 2:180)

problems.issue: Page-foot apparatus numerals [1] and [2] sit inside the running text. They are left exactly where they stand, each as its own run, so that they are not mistaken for editorial brackets. واية is also unpointed for the madda (وآية).
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: وآية رفع حكمها وبقيت تلاوتها — no textual loss beyond the madda.

problems.arabic: كقوله: "عشر رضعات ..." / "الشيخ والشيخة إن زنيا فارجموهما البتة
problems.issue: Register decision, flagged for the editor: both abrogated texts are introduced by كقوله and carry quotation marks in the Arabic, but neither stands in the muṣḥaf and neither is being glossed. They are tagged “h” (verbatim quoted authority, double quotation marks) rather than “q”.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: if the press prefers to treat putative abrogated revelation as “q”, these two runs should be re-tagged; the English is unaffected.

problems.arabic: وببن صلى الله عليه وسلم نسخها
problems.issue: ببن is not a word; the tooth-count of the OCR has dropped a yāʾ and the shadda.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: وبَيَّن — “and [the Prophet] ﷺ, made clear”; translated on this reading.

problems.issue: Bracketed material that is not Qurʾān: a ḥadīth sitting in round brackets. Tagged “h” with double quotation marks per the bracket rule, and the numeral [3] left in place after it.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: none needed; the text is sound.

problems.arabic: النسخ واقع في القرآن نقلا[4]  وأما عقلا
problems.issue: Footnote numeral [4] is followed by a double space — the page-foot apparatus intervened here in the printed page. Numeral left in place; the following clause is elliptical (وأما عقلا with no repeated verb), so “[abrogation]” is supplied in brackets.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: وأما عقلا فهو واقع أيضا — not supplied in the English beyond the bracketed subject.

problems.arabic: هو الفاعل المختار المتصرف في الوجود كيف شاء
problems.issue: The paragraph ends mid-sentence at the page turn and continues at the head of ¶3 (يجري حكما زمنا). No ending has been supplied, and no beginning supplied at ¶3.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the sentence continues “... as He wills: He puts a ruling into effect for a time ...” across the two paragraphs.

problems.arabic: (وَمَا لَكُم مِ دُوبِ الله غيره (مِنْ وَلِيِّ وَلاَ نَصِيرٍ)
problems.issue: مِ دُوبِ is corrupt and the brackets are mismatched: the first lemma opens but never closes, so the one-word gloss غيره stands inside it. Segmented as lemma / gloss / lemma / gloss on the sense, without reordering; the citation (Q. 2:107) is placed after the second lemma, which ends the run.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (وَمَا لَكُم مِن دُونِ اللهِ) غيره (مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلا نَصِيرٍ)

problems.issue: Footnote numeral [6] falls between the verb's prepositional phrase and its object (حكم السحر). Left in place, which splits the English sentence across two “p” runs in the same order as the Arabic.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: none; the numeral is apparatus, not text.

problems.issue: كَبَرَ cannot stand: the argument requires the denial of unbelief, and the gloss that follows (يعني ما سحر) confirms it. Tagged “q” despite the quotation marks in the Arabic, since this is actual Qurʾān.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: وَمَا كَفَرَ سُلَيْمَانُ (Q. 2:102) — fāʾ read as bāʾ; translated on this reading.

problems.arabic: والملائكة الذين أنزلهم الله جاءوا لتعليم السحر، لتعليم أنه شر حتى يجتنبوه
problems.issue: Doctrinally load-bearing and possibly damaged: as it stands the angels “came to teach sorcery”, which sits awkwardly with the claim just made that sorcery is unbelief, and the second clause reads as a correction of the first. A negation may have been lost. Translated exactly as it stands, with no negation supplied.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: ما جاءوا لتعليم السحر بل لتعليم أنه شر — “they did not come to teach sorcery, but to teach that it is evil”; flagged for the editor, not adopted.

problems.issue: بالّه has lost a lām in OCR.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: بالله — “with Allah”; translated on this reading.

problems.arabic: وإذا أصبح الصبح برجعان أيضا وإذا جاء الليل قرآ الإسم الذي علمهما الله
problems.issue: برجعان for يرجعان (bāʾ for yāʾ). The night clause is also stated twice with the morning clause between the two — either the transcriber's dittography or Niasse's own oral repetition. Kept in the order and the repetition of the Arabic; nothing reordered or collapsed.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: يرجعان — “they would return”; the doubled night clause left as transmitted.

problems.issue: The chunk breaks off mid-sentence at the page turn, on ألم. Nothing supplied: the English ends “He said: Did not”.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: a question of the form ألم ينهنا الله ... (“Did Allah not forbid us ...”) continues on the next page; not supplied.

problems.issue: The paragraph opens mid-sentence at a page turn: the interrogative particle governing تعلم is lost with the preceding page, and the speaker of this question is not named in the surviving text.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: أما تعلم or ألم تعلم (“do you not know”), the first angel addressing the second. Rendered with a bracketed “[Do]”; no beginning supplied.

problems.issue: OCR corruption: a non-word, with a stray final hamza-alif.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فشربا (“so they both drank”). Translated on that reading.

problems.issue: Ungrammatical as it stands; كلا cannot govern the following verb.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: كلما أرادت معصية (“each time she wanted a sin”). Rendered “Each [time] she wanted a sin” with the supplement bracketed.

problems.arabic: قال أحدهما: اللّٰه شديد العقاب، قال الآخر: هو غفور رحيم
problems.issue: This exchange duplicates the one that opens the paragraph, and it sits between the wine episode and the killing of the husband, where the narrative does not call for it. The lines look displaced or doubled at the page turn.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: a compositor's repetition of the exchange carried over from the foot of the previous page. Both occurrences retained in place; nothing reordered.

problems.arabic: فحكما لها حينا / وأرسله إلي حينا
problems.issue: حينا appears twice in the chunk (¶5 and ¶9) where the sense requires “at once,” not the normal “for a time.”
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: في الحين or حينئذ in both places. Rendered “at once”; the orthography is left unemended.

problems.issue: The word is broken by OCR: an exclamation mark stands where the final letter or letters were, immediately before footnote marker 7. Not recoverable from the transcription alone, so it is left as an illegible span.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: الحسد (“envy”), the clause reading وذكر الحسد, “He mentioned envy,” which the following clause والحسد من الكبائر supports.

problems.issue: Two footnote numerals sit inside the running text rather than at the page foot: [7] after the broken word الحس!, and [8] immediately after the ḥadīth إن الحسد يأكل الحسنات. The notes themselves are not in the chunk.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: note 7 keys the lemma or source for envy, note 8 the ḥadīth reference. Both markers left where they stand, as “p” runs; neither note text is available to translate.

problems.arabic: أحسن إلى كل من أحسن إليك والمسيئ تكفيه إساءته[9]
problems.issue: Footnote numeral [9] sits inside the running text, after the scholar's maxim at the head of the paragraph. The note text is not in the chunk.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: note 9 keys the maxim to a source or parallel. Marker left where it stands, as its own “p” run.

problems.arabic: كيف أعلم أنه يقول في هذا؟
problems.issue: في هذا leaves the king's question without its object; the sense requires a first-person pronoun after يقول.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: يقول فيَّ هذا (“says this about me”). Rendered “says this about [me]” with the supplement bracketed.

problems.arabic: فكرهت أن يشم الملك في رائحة كريهة
problems.issue: في stands without a pronoun suffix, so the clause lacks the source of the smell.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: يشم الملك فيَّ رائحة كريهة (“smell a foul odour from me”). Rendered with “[from me]” bracketed.

problems.issue: Recurring hamza and alif spellings in the transcription (¶5, ¶8, ¶9): ياتيه for يأتيه, ودعى for ودعا, الإسم for الاسم, المسيئ for المسيء.
problems.conjecture: Non-substantive orthographic variants, not textual damage; translated on the standard forms. Flagged only so the emendations are not silent.

problems.issue: Opening lemma mildly deformed: ود without shadda, أهل with a stray madda, الكتب defective for الكتاب. Translated on the corrected reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ودّ كثير من أهل الكتاب (Q 2:109).

problems.issue: The lemma re-cited after فنزلت هذه الآية opens with no bracket though it closes with one; كثيرمِّر runs two words together, أنمسهم stands for أنفسهم, كفاراٌ carries a stray tanwīn.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ودّ كثير من أهل الكتاب لو يردونكم من بعد إيمانكم كفارا حسدا من عند أنفسهم (Q 2:109).

problems.issue: الخبيئة for الخبيثة; translated on the corrected reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: الخبيثة (‘malignant’).

problems.issue: تبيّى lacks the final nūn; neither this bracket nor the following one around الحق is ever closed, so the gloss في التوراة sits inside an open lemma. Order preserved as transcribed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: من بعد ما تبيّن لهم ... الحقُّ (Q 2:109).

problems.issue: Final lemma of the paragraph is not readable as an Arabic word; translated on the reading below rather than marked illegible, because the gloss opening ¶15 fixes it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فاعفوا (‘so pardon’, Q 2:109), fixed by the gloss عنهم أي اتركوهم with which ¶15 opens.

problems.issue: ʿAmmār and Bilāl pass a كنيسة, but the people who then court them are اليهود. Translated literally as ‘church’; not a transcription fault.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: كنيسة here means a synagogue, the word being used of either house of worship in this register.

problems.issue: ماطرأ run together as one word; reading unaffected.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ما طرأ (‘what has come about’).

problems.arabic: ما قتمنا وجدناه وما تركا عدمناه
problems.issue: قتمنا and تركا are corrupt; the maxim is translated on the corrected reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ما قدّمنا وجدناه وما تركنا عدمناه (‘what we sent ahead we found, and what we left behind we lost’).

problems.issue: Footnote numeral [10] stands inside the running text, between the voice’s reply and هذا مصداق قوله. Left in place as a ‘p’ run; the page-foot note itself is not in this chunk.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: an apparatus call on the maxim reported at al-Baqīʿ, probably sourcing the report.

problems.arabic: "وَمَا تُقَدِّمُواْ لَ نَجْسِكُم مِنْ عَيْرِ تجدرة عِندة ألَه
problems.issue: The re-citation is heavily corrupt and is marked with double quotation marks rather than brackets: لَ نَجْسِكُم, عَيْرِ, تجدرة and عِندة ألَه are all deformed. Translated on the corrected reading, since the same āya is cited intact in ¶15.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله (Q 2:110).

problems.issue: وقالوا deformed, and the bracket is closed before the gloss اليهود rather than after it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وقالوا) اليهود (Q 2:111).

problems.arabic: (لَنْ يَدْخَلَ ألْجَبَّةَ اِلأَمَى كَتَانَ هُو دأكه
problems.issue: The lemma is corrupt throughout and its bracket is never closed: الجبة for الجنة, الأمى for إلا من, كتان for كان, هو دأكه for هودا. Translated on the corrected reading, which the gloss جمع هائد and ¶18’s من كان يهوديا both confirm.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لن يدخل الجنة إلا من كان هودا (Q 2:111).

problems.issue: The chunk opens mid-sentence at a page turn, inside the ḥadīth of Jibrīl: the conditional particle and the clause governing it stood on the previous page, and the closing parenthesis has no opener here. Translated from where the text starts; no beginning supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (flagged as conjecture): the full clause is أن تعبد الله كأنك تراه فإن لم تكن تراه فإنه يراك, i.e. '[that you worship Allah as though you saw Him; and if] you do not see Him, then He sees you'. Nothing of this has been added to the translation.

problems.issue: Footnote numeral in the running text: [11] stands immediately after the closing parenthesis of the ḥadīth of Jibrīl and before من دخل في الإسلام. Left where it stands, as its own run; the note itself is not in the chunk.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (flagged as conjecture): a page-foot reference for the ḥadīth of Jibrīl. Not supplied.

problems.arabic: أي علاماتها ... إذا كثر السراري حتى أن الأمة تلد سيدتها، الأمة إذا ولدت من سيدها يكون ولدها سيدها ومعتقها
problems.issue: Register decision, not damage: both glosses sit inside the single pair of parentheses that runs from ما المسؤول عنها to يعلمكم دينكم. They are Niasse's interlinear exposition, so they are marked 'p' although they stand within the quotation's brackets; the ḥadīth around them is marked 'h'.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (flagged as conjecture): the transcriber closed the parenthesis late rather than the glosses belonging to the ḥadīth text.

problems.issue: The paragraph ends mid-sentence at the page turn; the object of فعل stands at the head of ¶21 (أفعالا قبيحة). Each half is translated in its own paragraph and no sentence is completed across the break.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (flagged as conjecture): reads وكان دحية فعل أفعالا قبيحة, 'and Diḥya had committed foul acts'.

problems.arabic: قال له الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم: قل أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله ...
problems.issue: Register decision, not damage: ¶21–¶22 retell the Diḥya al-Kalbī story in Niasse's own narration, with no citation brackets anywhere. Speech attributed to the Prophet ﷺ, and to Jibrīl is marked 'h' and carries double quotation marks; the narration, and the speech of Diḥya and of the Companions, is kept as 'p'.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (flagged as conjecture): none required; recorded so that the marking can be reversed in one pass if the press prefers all of ¶21–¶22 as 'p'.

problems.issue: OCR damage: وثهارا is not an Arabic word (thāʾ for nūn). The span is marked illegible where it stands rather than read through.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (flagged as conjecture): نهارا, giving ليلا ونهارا, 'by night and by day'.

problems.arabic: وهم مصدقون كيف لا | تغفر لهم؟
problems.issue: The Prophet's address to Allah is split across the page turn: ¶22 breaks after كيف لا and ¶23 carries only تغفر لهم؟. The English breaks at the same point. The doubled interrogative فكيف ... كيف is kept doubled.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (flagged as conjecture): continuous text reads كيف لا تغفر لهم, 'how should You not forgive them'.

problems.issue: Footnote numeral in the running text: [12] closes ¶23, which consists of nothing but the tail of the sentence begun in ¶22. Left where it stands, as its own run; the note itself is not in the chunk.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (flagged as conjecture): a page-foot reference for the Diḥya al-Kalbī report. Not supplied.

problems.issue: Not damage: the Qurʾānic lemmata of ¶24–¶25 are set in a Warsh-style rasm with non-standard Unicode (اِڬ for the article, ࣲ for tanwīn, الكتب for الكتاب, اێسمهۥ for اسمه). Read as standard Qurʾānic text and translated; the rasm is not represented in the English.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (flagged as conjecture): the lemmata are Q. 2:113–114 in the Warsh transmission used through the printing.

problems.arabic: "وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَبِ مَرْيَمَ إِذْ إنتَبَذَّتْ مِنَ أَهْلِهَا مَكَاناً شَرْفِيّا
problems.issue: OCR damage: الْكِتَبِ for الْكِتَابِ, إِذْ إنتَبَذَّتْ for إِذِ انتَبَذَتْ, شَرْفِيّا for شَرْقِيًّا. The closing quotation mark is missing, so the end of the citation is unmarked.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (fixed by the Qurʾānic text, Q. 19:16): وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ مَرْيَمَ إِذِ انتَبَذَتْ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا مَكَانًا شَرْقِيًّا. Citation taken to end at شَرْقِيًّا, where Niasse's exposition (لما كان مولد عيسى...) resumes.

problems.arabic: وقالوا لا تصح الصلاة | إلا إلى الشرق
problems.issue: The page turn falls mid-sentence between ¶27 and ¶28. ¶27 ends without a period and ¶28 opens with the completing phrase; both translated as they stand, with no invented beginning or ending.
problems.conjecture: No emendation needed; recorded for the typesetter.

problems.issue: Q. 28:44 cited in double quotation marks; final iʿrāb lost (الْغَرْبِيّ for الْغَرْبِيِّ).
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (fixed by the Qurʾānic text): وَمَا كُنتَ بِجَانِبِ الْغَرْبِيِّ. Tagged "q".

problems.arabic: وتأديب للنفس كي تالف. إفراد الوجهة، إذا كان العبد كلما أراد التعبد
problems.issue: Punctuation misplaced in the transcription: a full stop after تالف leaves إفراد الوجهة as a verbless fragment, and the following sentence opens with إذا. تالف is also unvowelled for تَأْلَفَ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: كي تَأْلَفَ إفرادَ الوجهة. إذا كان العبد... — the stop belongs after الوجهة. Translated as one clause ("so that it may grow accustomed to singling out one direction of facing"); the lines are not reordered.

problems.issue: Footnote numeral sitting inside the running text. Left where it stands, attached to the end of the run it follows; not moved to the paragraph end and not renumbered.
problems.conjecture: No emendation. Note for the typesetter: the numeral is to be set close up to the preceding word, not as a separate token.

problems.arabic: (لا تفضلوني على يونس بن متى)[14] ... (لا أحصي ثناء عليك أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك)[15] ... (لا تفضلوني على يونس بن متى)[16]
problems.issue: Three further footnote numerals inside the running text, each immediately after a quoted ḥadīth. Left where they stand. The ḥadīth themselves are given in round brackets, the same brackets the transcription uses for Qurʾānic lemmata; they are tagged "h" (double quotation marks), not "q".
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the round brackets around the ḥadīth are the transcriber's quotation device, not a lemma marker. No emendation to the numerals.

problems.issue: Mismatched delimiters: the lemma opens with « and closes with ). أللَّةَ is the same corrupt orthography for اللَّهَ as in ¶26.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE (fixed by the Qurʾānic text): إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ (Q. 2:115), the lemma Niasse returns to before the khalīfa exposition. Translated from this restored reading.

problems.arabic: ويونس غرق في البحر فابتلعه حوت فابتلعه حوت آخر في قعر البحر في جوف الحوت والحوت في جوف حوت آخر
problems.issue: The doubled فابتلعه حوت could be read as dittography, but the clause that follows (والحوت في جوف حوت آخر) confirms the two-fish motif, so the repetition is substantive.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: text as transmitted; no emendation. Repetition reproduced in the English per the verbatim rule rather than collapsed.

problems.arabic: كلنا رب لشيء إلا أن الرب لا يطلق على غير اللّه إلا إذا أضيف
problems.issue: The paragraph, and the chunk, break off mid-sentence after أضيف: the complement of أضيف (what the construct is annexed to) is lost at the page turn.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: something like إلا إذا أضيف إلى ما يربه / إلى مربوبه. Nothing supplied; the English is left unpunctuated at the break.

problems.issue: A free-standing semicolon preceded by a space stands before كلنا, where the transcription's punctuation has drifted from the Arabic.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the semicolon closes the preceding clause (قل أو كثر؛). Set there in the English.

problems.arabic: إلى شيء: رب الدار، أُضيفَ، رب الثوب، رب الكتاب
problems.issue: Paragraph opens mid-sentence at the page turn: the subject and protasis of the sentence are lost, and the verb أُضيفَ sits displaced inside the list of construct examples (between رب الدار and رب الثوب) rather than governing إلى شيء. Word order left exactly as transmitted; nothing supplied.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the lost opening ran something like "الرب لا يُطلق إلا إذا أُضيفَ" with the sequence "[إذا] أُضيفَ إلى شيء: رب الدار، رب الثوب، رب الكتاب" — i.e. أُضيفَ belongs before إلى شيء and the three genitive examples form an uninterrupted list.

problems.issue: OCR deformation of the Qurʾānic lemma (Q. 2:116); initial alif-nūn for the assimilated tāʾ. Bracket also unclosed.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا. Translated on that reading.

problems.issue: مَامِحِ is an OCR fusion; the Qurʾānic text of Q. 2:116 requires two words. لَهُو for لَهُ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: بَل لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ. Translated on that reading.

problems.issue: فَنِتُونٌ is an OCR deformation (fāʾ/nūn for qāf/alif) of the end of Q. 2:116; كُلِّ carries a wrong case vowel. The footnote numeral [17] stands inside the running text, immediately after the closing bracket of the lemma and before the gloss that belongs to it; it has been left in place, unmoved.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: كُلٌّ لَهُ قَانِتُونَ. Translated on that reading; [17] is a footnote reference to the page-foot apparatus, not part of Niasse's words.

problems.issue: اكل carries an intrusive initial alif; the phrase is the standard Jalālayn gloss on قانتون and requires a nominative كلٌّ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: مطيعون، كلٌّ بما يراد منه. Translated as "obedient, each in accordance with what is wanted of it".

problems.issue: Three deformations in one lemma (Q. 2:117): بَإِنَّمَا for فَإِنَّمَا, لَهُو for لَهُ, and كُرٌّ for the imperative كُنْ.

problems.issue: Lemma brackets are unbalanced throughout the paragraph: several lemmata carry only a closing parenthesis and others only an opening one, so the boundary between lemma and gloss has to be fixed from the Jalālayn wording rather than from the punctuation. سبْحَنَةُ is deformed for سُبْحَانَهُ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the lemma/gloss divisions adopted here follow al-Jalālayn on Q. 2:116–119; سُبْحَانَهُ for سبْحَنَةُ.

problems.arabic: (وَلَا تَسْئَلْ عَنَ اصْحَبِ الْجَحِيم) ... (وَلَن تَرْضِىٰ عَنكَ الْيَهُودُ وَلَاَ النَّصَرِى حَتَّىٰ تَتَّبِعَ مِلَّتَهَمْ)

problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: وَلَا تُسْأَلُ عَنْ أَصْحَابِ الْجَحِيمِ; وَلَن تَرْضَىٰ عَنكَ الْيَهُودُ وَلَا النَّصَارَىٰ حَتَّىٰ تَتَّبِعَ مِلَّتَهُمْ. problems.issue: The paragraph breaks off inside an opening lemma, which is cut after two letters at the page turn. فَلِ is not a Qurʾānic word; the next paragraph resumes with إنَّ هُدَى اللَّهِ, which in Q. 2:120 follows قُلْ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: قُلْ ("Say"), the fāʾ being an OCR misreading of qāf. Left as [illegible] rather than translated, since only two letters survive.

problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِهِ. Translated on that reading.

problems.arabic: (ونَفْشُ عَى نَفْس شَيْئَا وَلاَ يَقْبَلُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ ... (وَلا تَنْجَعُهَا شَمَعَةٌ وَلاَ هَمْ يَنصَرَونَ كه
problems.issue: First citation of Q. 2:123 is deformed throughout: ونَفْشُ for نَفْسٌ, عَى for عَن, تَنْجَعُهَا for تَنْفَعُهَا, شَمَعَةٌ for شَفَاعَةٌ, هَمْ for هُمْ. The second citation of the same āya, in « », is comparatively clean, which confirms the readings.

problems.issue: كه stands inside the running text immediately after the lemma, detached from any word; it is not Arabic in this position. problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: وَإِذِ ابْتَلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ رَبُّهُ بِكَلِمَاتٍ. Translated on that reading.

problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: رَبُّهُ بِكَلِمَاتٍ. Translated on that reading; the unfinished clause is left unfinished.

English cannot postpone the subject behind the verb, so "[no soul]" is supplied in brackets in the first lemma and the Arabic نَفْسٌ is then translated again in its own place in the second. The repetition is an artefact of the split, not of the Arabic.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: no emendation needed; flagged so that a copy-editor does not delete the apparent doublet.

problems.issue: Word-order constraint rather than damage. The Arabic subject رَبُّهُ is a lemma of its own and follows both the verb and the object Ibrāhīm, and falls after the page turn in ¶36; English requires a subject before the verb, so "He" stands in at the verb in ¶35 and رَبُّهُ is then rendered appositionally in ¶36 ("He tried him, his Lord, with words"). The lemma boundaries are preserved and nothing is reordered.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: a running English text would read "when his Lord tried Ibrāhīm with certain words"; the appositional rendering is kept here to hold the lemma/gloss alternation intact.

problems.issue: Two words corrupt (dāl for qāf; جلح for فلح). Translated on the conjecture below.

problems.issue: أَوْلُبِكَ corrupt. Note also that the text gives this as the terminus of the ten-trait run (إلى ...), which is Q 23:10, not 23:11; cited accordingly.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْوَارِثُون (Q 23:10) — secure.

problems.issue: OCR damage inside the lemmata of Q. 2:128: مُسْلِمَةَ لَكٌ for مُسْلِمَةً لَّكَ; الرَّحِيمْ for الرَّحِيمُ; and the final lemma's opening bracket is never closed, so the boundary between it and the exposition that follows (بيت الله تبارك وتعالى...) is unmarked. problems.conjecture: Conjecture: an unbracketed allusion to وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا الْبَيْتَ مَثَابَةً لِلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًا (Q. 2:125); if set as a lemma, the brackets would fall around مثابة للناس وأمنا only.

problems.arabic: قالوا للرسول: ما كان يركب؟ قال: أي دابة تحمل آدم؟ لا تقدر أي دابة أن تحمل آدم حتى الفيل
problems.issue: Not OCR damage, but a register boundary the transcription does not mark. The question put to the Prophet and his answer are set as "h" in double quotation marks, the attributive frames (قالوا للرسول, قال) as "p". لا تقدر أي دابة ... حتى الفيل is kept as "p", reading it as Niasse's own expansion rather than a continuation of the ḥadīth; nothing in the Arabic settles where the quotation stops.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the quoted matter ends at أي دابة تحمل آدم؟ If the press prefers to carry the ḥadīth through حتى الفيل, that clause moves from "p" to "h".

problems.arabic: وجعلوه وديعة في جبل أبي فبيس بجوار الكعبة
problems.issue: فبيس is not a name. The referent is fixed by جبل أبي ... بجوار الكعبة and by the Black Stone tradition. Rendered "Mount Abū Qubays" rather than marked illegible; recorded here so the normalisation is not silent.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: أبي قُبَيس (Abū Qubays, the hill overlooking the Kaʿba), qāf read as fāʾ.

problems.arabic: وكان في نو قانون من أتى بإمرأة جميلة
problems.issue: نو is a two-letter stub where the governed noun of في belongs; the clause has no recoverable head. Marked [illegible: نو]. The paragraph also opens mid-sentence, continuing ¶47's فلما قرب من المكاس،, and no beginning has been invented for it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: an adverbial of place or time — most plausibly ديوانه ("his customs post", cf. الديوان later in the same paragraph) or زمنهم / بلدهم ("their time" / "their town"). On any of these the clause means "and there was a law in force [there]". Uncertain.

problems.arabic: قال له: قدِّر ما شئت فقط من المال أعطيك ديوانته
problems.issue: ديوانته is not a word. Marked [illegible: ديوانته]; the sentence that follows supplies the sense (a quarter of the declared value), but not the word.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: مَكْسَه ("its toll") or ضريبته ("its duty"); possibly a corruption of ديوانه, i.e. the levy of the dīwān. The arithmetic that follows (ربع المال) favours مكسه.

problems.arabic: هذا هو المكسس عندهم ربع المال
problems.issue: المكسس carries a doubled sīn for المكس. Rendered "the toll" rather than marked illegible, the word being fixed by المكاس and صاحب المكس earlier in the same stretch.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: المَكْس ("the toll, the excise").

problems.arabic: حتى فعلته النساء كلا إلى يومنا هذا
problems.issue: كلا does not agree with النساء and leaves the apposition ungoverned. Rendered "women have all done it" rather than marked illegible, since the quantifier is clear from the construction.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: كلهن ("all of them"), the nūn lost; كلها is also possible.

problems.arabic: فقالت لإبراهيم: أبشرْ فإن الله كف العدو ورزقني وليدة تخدمني[25]
problems.issue: Not OCR damage. Sāra's words are set as "p", like the rest of the dialogue in ¶¶49–50, but the wording answers closely to the report in al-Bukhārī (كف الله يد الكافر وأخدم وليدة) and the transcription attaches footnote [25] here, which suggests a cited source. Flagged rather than reassigned.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: if footnote [25] cites a ḥadīth collection, this clause should be set as "h" in double quotation marks; the footnote text is not in this chunk, so the register is left as "p".

problems.arabic: إذا خرجا إلى العب يضرب إسماعيل إسحاق
problems.issue: العب is not a word. OCR has dropped the lām of اللعب. Translated (“went out to play”) rather than marked illegible, since the syntax (خرجا إلى + the two boys at play) admits one candidate only; the damage is recorded here.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: اللعب, “play” — إذا خرجا إلى اللعب.

problems.arabic: فقال الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم: يرحم الله أم ‖ [¶52] إسماعيل لو تركت زمزم لكانت عينا معينا
problems.issue: The printed page break falls inside the ḥadīth: ¶51 ends at أم and ¶52 opens at إسماعيل. Not OCR damage. Translated as it stands, with no invented beginning for ¶52; the “h” run opens its quotation mark at the end of ¶51 and closes it at the start of ¶52.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: in continuous text, يرحم الله أم إسماعيل لو تركت زمزم لكانت عيناً معيناً (cf. al-Bukhārī, K. Aḥādīth al-anbiyāʾ); a press edition may wish to close the quotation at the paragraph join.

problems.arabic: داخله بحر ماءه تحت مكة كلا
problems.issue: كلا stands without its pronoun and cannot be read here as كَلَّا (“nay”), which the sense excludes. Translated “beneath the whole of Mecca”; the damage is recorded here.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: كلّها, i.e. ماءه تحت مكة كلّها — the OCR has lost the final ها.

problems.issue: سبحان لله for سبحان الله: the alif of the article has been lost and the lām doubled. Translated “Glory be to Allah”.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: سبحان الله.

problems.arabic: فنظروا إلى طائر يحوم حول هذه المرأة قالوا: ... هذه الطيور لا ترى
problems.issue: Number disagreement across one sentence: singular طائر يحوم is picked up by plural هذه الطيور لا ترى. Translated as it stands (“a bird circling” … “these birds are not seen”) rather than harmonised.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: either طيوراً تحوم in the first clause, or — more likely for transcribed speech — Niasse generalises from the one bird to the species, in which case nothing is damaged.

problems.arabic: قالت: لا لسنا في خير ... قال: هل عندكم عيش؟
problems.issue: An ellipsis stands in the printed text between the woman's answer and Ibrāhīm's next question. It is not OCR loss but an omission in the print; retained in the English as … and nothing supplied across it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: a short turn of dialogue dropped by the transcriber or the editor; the parallel in ¶53 (نحن بخير ما نحتاج لشيء) suggests the missing words continued her complaint.

problems.arabic: ذهب بعلي يتصيد فإن وجد شيئا وإلا فنحن بشر حالة
problems.issue: Elliptical conditional: the apodosis of فإن وجد شيئا is suppressed before وإلا. Kept elliptical, with the missing clause supplied in square brackets as “[well and good]”. Not damage.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فإن وجد شيئاً [فهو خير] وإلا فنحن بشرّ حالة.

problems.arabic: قال: ذلك أبي إبراهيم قال إني أطلقك وأنت طالق
problems.issue: قال إني أطلقك lacks the verb of command that the parallel in ¶53 carries (أمرني أن أمسكك ولا أطلقك), so the reported instruction and Ismāʿīl's own pronouncement run together. Translated as it stands: “He has said that I am to divorce you: I divorce you, and you are divorced.”
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: أمرني أن أطلقك ، وأنت طالق — on the pattern of ¶53; the إني of the text may be an OCR residue of أمرني.

problems.arabic: قالت له بشرط أن لا تنزل عن ‖ [¶53] الجمل
problems.issue: The printed page break falls inside the phrase أن لا تنزل عن الجمل: ¶52 ends at عن and ¶53 opens at الجمل. Not OCR damage. Translated as it stands — ¶52 closes “that you do not dismount from” and ¶53 opens “the camel” — with no invented beginning.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: in continuous text, بشرط أن لا تنزل عن الجمل, as at the first visit in ¶52.

problems.arabic: فلما رأته المرأة الثانية قالت: أهذا علي؟ ما أحسن هذا الرجل
problems.issue: أهذا علي؟ yields no sense in context — neither “Is this ʿAlī?” nor “Is this upon me?” fits the woman seeing a stranger who resembles her husband. Since this is Niasse's own narrative prose and not a fixed text, the span is marked [illegible: أهذا علي؟] rather than restored.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: أهذا بعلي؟, “Is this my husband?” — the bāʾ lost by OCR; supported by ما أشبهه ببعلي in the next clause and by بعلك/بعلي throughout ¶52.

problems.arabic: والله ما يميز بينهما إلا الشيب فقط، انزل اول
problems.issue: اول for أولاً: the hamza and the tanwīn alif are lost. Translated “Dismount first”.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: انزل أولاً.

problems.issue: حجر من حجر doubles the singular where a partitive plural is expected. Translated literally as “a stone from the stone of the Maqām”.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: من حجارة المقام, “from the stones of the Maqām” — حجارة reduced to حجر by OCR.

problems.arabic: وهي هذه الكعبة الموجوة الآن في مكة
problems.issue: الموجوة is not a word: the dāl of الموجودة has dropped out. Restored rather than marked illegible, since the attributive agrees with الكعبة and the adverb الآن fixes the sense.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: الموجودة, “this Kaʿba now standing in Mecca.” Orthographic only; the English is unaffected.

problems.issue: ناتي for نأتي — the hamza is unwritten. The object of نأتي is also elided; لها فضائل كثيرة supplies it, and it is given in brackets as “[them]”.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: نأتي إليها في سورة آل عمران. Orthographic; the bracketed pronoun is editorial.

problems.arabic: "جِيهِ ءَايّاتٌ بَيِّنَٰتٌ مََّفَام إِرَعِين وَمَ دَخَلَهُ و كَانَ ءَامِناً ،
problems.issue: OCR damage across a Qurʾānic lemma run: جِيهِ for فِيهِ (one dot below for one dot above); ءَايَّاتٌ for آيَاتٌ, with a spurious shadda; مَّفَام for مَقَامُ (fāʾ for qāf) and a doubled fatḥa; إِرَعِين for إِبْرَاهِيمَ; وَمَ for وَمَن; كَانَ ءَامِناً for كَانَ آمِناً. Translated rather than marked illegible, the underlying text being fixed and identifiable as Q. 3:97. The quotation is opened with a double quotation mark and never closed; it ends in a comma. Set in quotation marks rather than in the parentheses the edition uses for lemmata, which would suggest ḥadīth; it is Qurʾān, and is marked “q”.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): فِيهِ آيَاتٌ بَيِنَاتٌ مَقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمَن دَخَلَهُ كَانَ آمِناً. Bracketing to be normalised to the edition's lemma parentheses.

problems.issue: The sequence هُ + free-standing و recurs through this chunk (دَخَلَهُ و here, إَسْمَهُ و at ¶56, نَجْسَهُ و at ¶59). It is not a conjunction but the muṣḥaf's small superscript wāw (U+06E5) read as a separate letter. The same diacritic survives correctly at ¶59 in لَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥ, which confirms the diagnosis.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: دَخَلَهُۥ كَانَ, اسْمُهُۥ أَحْمَدُ, نَفْسَهُۥ. A global fix: delete every free-standing و that follows هُ. No English is affected.

problems.arabic: (من حج ولم يرفث ولم يفسق رجع من ذنوبه كيوم ولدته أمه)
problems.issue: Ḥadīth set in the parentheses the edition reserves for Qurʾānic lemmata. It is not Qurʾān, so it is marked “h” and given in double quotation marks. The wording also departs from the received text: رجع من ذنوبه كيوم ولدته أمه for رجع كيوم ولدته أمه, and من حج without هذا البيت فلم.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the received wording (al-Bukhārī, Ḥajj) is من حج هذا البيت فلم يرفث ولم يفسق رجع كيوم ولدته أمه. من ذنوبه looks like Niasse's own expansion in oral delivery rather than OCR damage, and is translated as it stands; the press may wish to collate against the footnoted source at [30].

problems.arabic: فصار يبكي أشد بكاء أنه لابد أن يذهب إلى بيت اللّٰه
problems.issue: The أنه clause hangs without a governing verb of speech — ordinary oral syntax rather than OCR damage. Kept elliptical, with the governing sense supplied in brackets as “[insisting]”.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فصار يبكي أشد بكاء [يقول] أنه لابد أن يذهب, or على أنه. Supplying the verb in the Arabic is not necessary; the bracket in the English carries it.

problems.arabic: ولهذا قالت رابعة مخاطبة الجنيد: يا جنيد تطوف بالبيت أم برب البيت؟
problems.issue: Not a textual defect, but an attribution the press should annotate: Rābiʿa al-ʿAdawiyya (d. 185/801) and al-Junayd (d. 298/910) cannot have met, so the exchange is anachronistic as transmitted. The three speeches are marked “h” — named authorities quoted verbatim — while the anonymous story of the pilgrim and his child that precedes them stays “p”.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: a floating Sufi ḥikāya attached to whichever pair the teller has to hand; the circumambulation dictum circulates under Rābiʿa's name with other interlocutors. Translated as it stands, with no silent correction of either name; a footnote at the press's discretion.

problems.issue: رَبَا for رَبَّنَا: the nūn has dropped and the shadda with it. Translated rather than marked illegible, the text being fixed as Q. 2:129.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): رَبَّنَا وَابْعَثْ فِيهِمْ رَسُولاً مِنْهُمْ.

problems.arabic: وقد أجاب اللّٰه دعاء إبراهيم تحمد صلى اللّه عليه وسلم
problems.issue: تحمد is not a word in this slot. The ﷺ that follows shows the referent to be the Prophet, but the exact form is not recoverable from the transcription, so the span is marked [illegible: تحمد] in the translation rather than restored. This is Niasse's own prose, not a fixed text.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: بمحمد, “Allah answered the supplication of Ibrāhīm by means of Muḥammad ﷺ.” — the bāʾ read as tāʾ and the mīm lost. Bare محمد, with the ت an intrusion, is the alternative. The sentence that follows (فلهذا قال صلى الله عليه وسلم) and تلك البشارة هي محمد below both support the reading.

problems.issue: A second ḥadīth set in the edition's lemma parentheses. Marked “h”, not “q”: the words are the Prophet's, introduced by فلهذا قال صلى الله عليه وسلم.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: bracketing to be normalised — quotation marks for ḥadīth, parentheses reserved for Qurʾānic lemmata, as the typography approved for the edition requires. No emendation of the wording is needed; cf. the footnote at [32].

problems.arabic: "وَمُبَقِراً بِرَسُولِ يَاتِى مِنْ بَعْدِىَ إَسْمَهُ و أَحْمَدً"
problems.issue: OCR damage across a Qurʾānic lemma: وَمُبَقِراً for وَمُبَشِّراً (shīn read as qāf, with loss of the shadda); بِرَسُولِ for بِرَسُولٍ; يَاتِى for يَأْتِي; مِنْ بَعْدِىَ for مِنْ بَعْدِي; إَسْمَهُ و for اسْمُهُۥ; أَحْمَدً for أَحْمَدُ. Translated rather than marked illegible, the text being fixed as Q. 61:6. Set in double quotation marks though it is Qurʾān, and so marked “q”.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَمُبَشِّراً بِرَسُولٍ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِي اسْمُهُۥ أَحْمَدُ (Q. 61:6), and the brackets to be normalised to lemma parentheses.

problems.arabic: تلك البشارة هي محمد صلى الّه عليه وسلم
problems.issue: الّه for اللّه. The chunk writes the divine name three ways — اللّٰه (most often), اللّه (¶55, ¶56), and الّه (here) — the lām having been lost in the last. An artefact of the ligature, not a variant.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: الله throughout, normalised at typesetting. The English is unaffected: “Allah”, never “God”.

problems.issue: Q. 2:129 is cited a second time, here in double quotation marks rather than in the parentheses used for the same words at the head of the paragraph. The run is clean of damage and is marked “q”; the reference is repeated after it, the convention being one reference per run of lemmata.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: bracketing to be normalised to (وَابْعَثْ فِيهِمْ رَسُولاً مِنْهُمْ). No emendation of the wording is needed.

problems.issue: Two defects at once. Bracketing: the first lemma opens with ( and is never closed, so the second ( opens inside it; the gloss القرآن therefore falls inside the first lemma's brackets although it is Niasse's gloss (“p”), not Qurʾān. OCR: يَالوا for يَتْلُو; اِكَ for آيَاتِكَ, of which only the final kāf and a stray alif survive; وَيَعَلِّمْهَمْ for وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ; الْكِتَّبَ for الْكِتَابَ. اِكَ is translated rather than marked illegible only because Q. 2:129 fixes it; nothing in the transcription itself would recover it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (يَتْلُو عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتِكَ) القرآن (وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ) ما فيه من الأحكام — the gloss order being the Jalālayn's: القرآن on آياتك, ما فيه من الأحكام on الحكمة.

problems.issue: OCR damage across the close of Q. 2:129: وَرَكَيِمَة for وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ (the zāʾ read as rāʾ and the pronoun هم as مة); أنَّ for إِنَّكَ, the kāf lost; الْغَزِيزُ for الْعَزِيزُ (ʿayn dotted as ghayn); الحَكِية for الْحَكِيمُ. Translated rather than marked illegible, the text being fixed. The loss of the kāf in إنك would leave the clause without its subject; the English supplies “You” from the muṣḥaf rather than from conjecture.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ).

problems.issue: The printed page break falls inside an iḍāfa: ¶58 ends at علم and ¶59 opens at القرآن, the two being one phrase, علم القرآن. Not OCR damage. Translated as it stands — ¶58 closes “what is meant is the knowledge” and ¶59 opens “of the Qurʾān” — with no invented beginning for ¶59.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: in continuous text the clause reads الحكمة حيث أطلقت في القرآن فالمراد علم القرآن ومواعظ القرآن وأحكام القرآن, “al-ḥikma, wherever it is used without qualification in the Qurʾān — what is meant is the knowledge of the Qurʾān, the admonitions of the Qurʾān, and the rulings of the Qurʾān.” A press edition may wish to close the phrase at the paragraph join.

problems.issue: Not a defect, but a register decision recorded for consistency: الحكمة here is the word under discussion, not a term in use, so it is set as transliteration (“i”: al-ḥikma) rather than translated. In the lemmata of ¶57 and ¶59 the same word is translated, “the wisdom”.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: none. If the press prefers a single policy, “the wisdom” with the Arabic in parentheses would serve, at the cost of the lexical point Niasse is making.

problems.issue: OCR damage through the opening lemma of Q. 2:132: وَوْصِى for وَوَصَّىٰ (the shadda and the medial alif lost); إِبْرَهِيمُ for إِبْرَاهِيمَ with the defective alif the edition uses throughout; بَنِيهٌ for بَنِيهِ, a case ending that cannot stand, بنيه being the object of وصّى. Translated rather than marked illegible, the text being fixed as Q. 2:132 and the gloss بالملة being the Jalālayn's on بها.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَوَصَّىٰ بِهَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بَنِيهِ وَيَعْقُوبُ. Because the gloss بالملة splits the lemma, the English divides it as "And he enjoined it" / "Ibrāhīm, upon his sons, and Yaʿqūb"; the preposition is required by English syntax and is not an editorial supplement.

problems.arabic: دين الإسلام بَلا تَمُوتنَّ إِلَّ وَأَنْتُم مُسْلِمُونَ)
problems.issue: بَلا for فَلَا — bāʾ for fāʾ, the one-dot-below for one-dot-above confusion recurring through this chunk; إِلَّ for إِلَّا; تَمُوتنَّ for تَمُوتُنَّ. The lemma also carries only a closing parenthesis, so the boundary between the gloss دين الإسلام and the resumed lemma has to be recovered from the āya.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): دين الإسلام (فَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ) — Q. 2:132. The missing opening parenthesis belongs before فَلَا.

problems.arabic: نزل أَمْ كُنتُمْ شُهَدَاءَ حضورا (ا۪ذْ حَضَرَ يَعْقُوبَ اَ۬لْمَوْتُ
problems.issue: أَمْ كُنتُمْ شُهَدَاءَ stands with no parentheses at all, between Niasse's نزل and the Jalālayn gloss حضورا. It is Qurʾān (Q. 2:133) and is marked "q"; حضورا glosses شهداء, as in the Jalālayn. Also ا۪ذْ for إِذْ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the lemma parentheses dropped in transcription — نزل (أَمْ كُنتُمْ شُهَدَاءَ) حضورا (إِذْ حَضَرَ يَعْقُوبَ الْمَوْتُ ...). نزل is elliptical, lacking its subject (الآية / هذه الآية); rendered "there came down" with no supplement, since the āya follows immediately as its content.

problems.issue: The gloss is elliptical: عدّ has no second object. It glosses آبائك in Q. 2:133, where Ismāʿīl was Yaʿqūb's paternal uncle rather than his father.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: عدّ إسماعيلَ أباً, "he reckoned Ismāʿīl a father" — the Jalālayn's point at this lemma is that the uncle is counted among the fathers. Rendered "he reckoned Ismāʿīl [a father]" with the supplement in brackets rather than silently expanded. Footnote marker [34] retained in place.

problems.arabic: (وَنَحْنُ لَهُۥ مُسْلِمُونَۖ تِلْكَ) الجماعة أمَّةٌ فَدْ خَلَت سلفت
problems.issue: أمَّةٌ فَدْ خَلَت carries no parentheses, so the lemma–gloss–lemma sequence has to be recovered; فَدْ for قَدْ (fāʾ for qāf). The preceding bracketed span also crosses a verse boundary, وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ closing Q. 2:133 and تِلْكَ opening Q. 2:134.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ) ... (تِلْكَ) الجماعة (أُمَّةٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ) سلفت — Q. 2:133–134, with الجماعة glossing تلك and سلفت glossing قد خلت, as in the Jalālayn. The English splits the crossing span into two lemma runs so that each verse can carry its own reference; no words are added or moved.

problems.arabic: (لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ من العمل جزاء (وَلَكُم) اليهود
problems.issue: The first lemma is never closed, and the gloss من العمل جزاء is elliptical, lacking the noun جزاء governs. A second bracketed span then runs from مَّا كَسَبْتُمْ through وَقَالُواْ كُونُواْ هُوداً اَوْ نَصَٰر۪يٰ تَهْتَدُواْ, crossing from Q. 2:134 into Q. 2:135 without a break.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ) من العمل، جزاء [ما عملت] (وَلَكُم) اليهود (مَّا كَسَبْتُمْ ...) — the Jalālayn glosses لها ما كسبت as جزاء ما عملت, which supplies the missing complement; rendered "of deeds, [that is,] recompense". The crossing span is divided in the English at the verse boundary, Q. 2:134 closing at وَلَا تُسْأَلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ.

problems.arabic: من كان يهوديا فيو على صراط مستقيم
problems.issue: فيو for فهو — wāw for hāʾ. Orthographic only; the parallel clause two lines later has فهو correctly.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فهو على صراط مستقيم. The English is unaffected.

problems.issue: فَلْ for قُلْ (fāʾ for qāf, as at قَوَيْلٌ in the preceding lesson). The printed page break then falls inside Q. 2:135: ¶60 closes at بَلْ and ¶61 opens with the gloss نتبع that the Jalālayn supplies for the verb elided after بل. Not OCR damage. ¶60 is translated to its end as it stands, with no second reference for an āya already cited in the paragraph.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (قُلْ بَلْ) نتبع (مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفاً) — Q. 2:135. In continuous text the clause reads قل بل نتبع ملة إبراهيم حنيفاً.

problems.issue: عِيبى for عِيسَى — bāʾ for sīn.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (وَعِيسَى) — Q. 2:136; fixed also by the gloss من الإنجيل.

problems.arabic: (وَمَا أوتِى ألتَيِيَثُونَ صِ رَيِهِمْ لا تُمَرِف بَيْنَ أَحَدِ مَنْهَزْيَه
problems.issue: Heavy damage across the remainder of Q. 2:136: ألتَيِيَثُونَ for النَّبِيُّونَ; صِ for مِنْ, reduced to a single letter; رَيِهِمْ for رَبِّهِمْ; تُمَرِف for نُفَرِّقُ, which as transcribed is also the wrong person; أَحَدِ for أَحَدٍ; مَنْهَزْيَه for مِنْهُمْ, with intrusive zāʾ, yāʾ and hāʾ. The single opening parenthesis is never closed, and لا تُمَرِف begins a new clause of the āya with no bracketing of its own. Translated rather than marked illegible, because the whole span is a continuous stretch of one āya whose wording is fixed, and because ¶63 resumes with its closing words.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (وَمَا أُوتِيَ النَّبِيُّونَ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ) (لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ) — Q. 2:136. صِ is the least secure of these restorations; مِنْ is required by رَبِّهِمْ and admits no alternative.

problems.arabic: فومن ‖ [¶63] ببعض ونكفر ببعض كاليهود والنصارى
problems.issue: فومن for فنؤمن — nūn lost and the hamza unwritten. The printed page break then falls inside the gloss: ¶62 ends at فنؤمن and ¶63 opens at ببعض. Not OCR damage.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فنؤمن ببعض ونكفر ببعض كاليهود والنصارى, the Jalālayn's gloss on لا نفرق بين أحد منهم. ¶62 closes "so we believe" and ¶63 opens "in some and disbelieve in some, as the Jews and the Christians do," with no invented beginning for ¶63.

problems.issue: وَتَحْنَ for وَنَحْنُ — tāʾ for nūn; an intrusive comma after لَهُ; the lemma is not closed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ) — Q. 2:136. The comma is an artifact, to be deleted.

problems.arabic: بَرانَ امَثَوايه أي اليهود ‖ [¶64] والنصارى (بِمثْلِ مَا ءَامَنهْم بِو)
problems.issue: بَرانَ امَثَوايه is not Arabic as it stands, carries no parentheses, and is marked [illegible: بَرانَ امَثَوايه] rather than restored. The intrusive rāʾ–alif in بَرانَ and the trailing يه in امَثَوايه are not explicable as letter confusions, and the span is longer than the reading the āya requires.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فَإِنْ آمَنُوا — Q. 2:137 opens فَإِنْ آمَنُوا بِمِثْلِ مَا آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ فَقَدِ اهْتَدَوْا, the gloss that follows (أي اليهود والنصارى, broken across the page) is the Jalālayn's on exactly that protasis, and ¶64 resumes with (بِمِثْلِ مَا آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ). On this reading bāʾ is a misread fāʾ and the hamza of إن was read as رَا; the trailing يه may be a displaced بِهِ anticipated from the following lemma. The bracketing is also to be supplied.

problems.arabic: (وَإِن تَوَلَّوا عن الإيمان به (قَاتَّمَا هُمْ مِي شِقَاتٍ ) خلاف معكم
problems.issue: The first lemma is not closed. قَاتَّمَا for فَإِنَّمَا (qāf for fāʾ, and the hamza read as alif); مِي for فِي; شِقَاتٍ for شِقَاقٍ, the final qāf read as tāʾ. In the gloss, خلاف معكم stands where the Jalālayn has خلاف معك; translated as it stands, since the plural may be Niasse's own adjustment to the audience and is not a letter confusion.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا) عن الإيمان به (فَإِنَّمَا هُمْ فِي شِقَاقٍ) خلاف معكم — Q. 2:137.

problems.issue: بَسَيَخْعِيكَهَم for فَسَيَكْفِيكَهُمُ — bāʾ for fāʾ, khāʾ for kāf, ʿayn for fāʾ; الَّمَ for اللَّهُ, mīm for hāʾ. The lemma is not closed, and the printed page break separates it from its gloss, which stands at the head of ¶66.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (فَسَيَكْفِيكَهُمُ اللَّهُ) يا محمد شقاقهم — Q. 2:137, the gloss being the Jalālayn's. ¶65 is cited at the page-break end of the run and ¶66 again at الْعَلِيم, where the āya closes; ¶66 opens from the gloss as it stands, with no invented beginning.

problems.issue: الْعَلِيمْ for الْعَلِيمُ, and a space inside the opening parenthesis. Orthographic only.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (الْعَلِيمُ) — Q. 2:137.

problems.issue: قريطة for قريظة — ṭāʾ for ẓāʾ, one dot lost. The reference is to Banū Qurayẓa, paired here with the expulsion of Banū al-Naḍīr.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: قريظة, rendered Qurayẓa. The transcription has the bare tribal name without بني; left unexpanded in the English.

problems.issue: Word division broken and a letter lost: آحْسَ مَ for أَحْسَنُ مِنَ, with the nūn of أحسن gone and the break falling inside مِنَ. صِبْعَةَ for صِبْغَةً, ʿayn for ghayn, the same confusion that governs the whole exposition of the āya. A prothetic hamza on أَللَّهِ, and وَمَنَ for وَمَنْ. Translated rather than marked illegible, the lemma being fixed as Q. 2:138 and confirmed by the gloss اللّٰه أحسن صبغة من كل صابغ that follows it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (وَمَنْ) لا أحد (أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ صِبْغَةً) — Q. 2:138.

problems.arabic: (كل مولود يولد على فطرة الإسلام فأبواه يهودانه أو ينصرانه أو يمجسانه كما تنتج البهيمة البهيمة هل تجدون فيها من جدعاء)[36]
problems.issue: The ḥadīth is set in the parentheses the edition reserves for Qurʾānic lemmata. It is ḥadīth, not Qurʾān, and is marked "h". كما تنتج البهيمة البهيمة repeats البهيمة where the received wording has a qualifier on the second noun.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the bracketing is to be normalised to the edition's quotation marks for ḥadīth. For البهيمة البهيمة read البهيمةُ بهيمةً جمعاءَ, "the beast gives birth to a beast whole in its limbs" — the contrast with جدعاء at the end of the ḥadīth turns on جمعاء, whose loss leaves the question unprepared. Rendered "the beast gives birth to a beast" as the transcription stands, without the supplement.

problems.arabic: خاطب عدما في عدم في عدم وأجابوه
problems.issue: في عدم stands twice. Probable dittography at a line break rather than deliberate repetition, but nothing in the transcription decides it. Kept in the English — "a nonexistent in nonexistence, in nonexistence" — under the verbatim standard, and not silently collapsed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: خاطب عدماً في عدم وأجابوه, with a single في عدم. A press edition that accepts the dittography should delete the second occurrence.

problems.issue: The quotation is set in double quotation marks rather than in the edition's lemma parentheses, which would suggest ḥadīth; it is Qurʾān, and is marked "q". قَالَواْ for قَالُوا and بَلِى for بَلَى are orthographic.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the words are Q. 7:172, أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى, cited as such; the āya continues شَهِدْنَا, which Niasse does not quote. The bracketing should be normalised to the lemma parentheses.

problems.arabic: بنو آدم يصبغون بالألوان يصبغون ‖ [¶67] الأبيض فيكون أسود
problems.issue: The printed page break falls inside the clause: ¶66 ends at يصبغون and ¶67 opens at الأبيض. Not OCR damage.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: in continuous text the clause reads بنو آدم يصبغون بالألوان، يصبغون الأبيض فيكون أسود. ¶66 closes "they dye" and ¶67 opens "the white, and it becomes black," with no invented beginning for ¶67.

problems.issue: عَبِدُونَ for عَابِدُونَ — the medial alif lost, as elsewhere in this chunk. Orthographic only.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (وَنَحْنُ لَهُ عَابِدُونَ) — Q. 2:138.

problems.arabic: قال اليهود المسلمين ... ولو كان محمد نيا لكان منا
problems.issue: المسلمين for للمسلمين — the lām of the indirect object lost, leaving قال with two accusatives and no addressee. نيا for نبيا, the bāʾ lost; without it the clause has no predicate for كان.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: قال اليهود للمسلمين, "the Jews said to the Muslims" — fixed by the direct address نحن أهل الكتاب الأول that follows; and ولو كان محمد نبياً لكان منا, "had Muḥammad been a prophet he would have been from among us" — fixed by النبوة لا تكون إلا في بني إسرائيل in the next clause. Both restorations are letter-level and are rendered in the English.

problems.issue: A prefixed wāw on the lemma and قُلَ for قُلْ; the lemma carries only a closing parenthesis, and the paragraph ends there, ¶68 resuming with the gloss لهم.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (قُلْ) لهم (أَتُحَاجُّونَنَا) — Q. 2:139. The prefixed wāw is an artifact, to be deleted; it cannot belong to the āya, which begins قُلْ. ¶67 closes "Say" and ¶68 opens "to them," with no invented beginning.

problems.arabic: (اتَحَآجُونَتَا) تخاصموننا مِ اللَّهِ) أن اصطفى نبيا من العرب (وَهُوَ رَبُّنَا وَرَبُّكُمِ )
problems.issue: اتَحَآجُونَتَا for أَتُحَاجُّونَنَا — the interrogative hamza written as alif and the first nūn of the two read as tāʾ. مِ for فِي, reduced to a single letter, with no opening parenthesis, so the boundary between the gloss تخاصموننا and the resumed lemma rests on the āya. رَبُّكُمِ for رَبُّكُمْ. Translated rather than marked illegible, the āya being fixed and the gloss تخاصموننا confirming the interrogative.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (أَتُحَاجُّونَنَا) تخاصموننا (فِي اللَّهِ) أن اصطفى نبياً من العرب (وَهُوَ رَبُّنَا وَرَبُّكُمْ) — Q. 2:139.

problems.issue: أعْمَالْنَا for أَعْمَالُنَا; لَكُمْوَ for لَكُمْ, with a stray wāw; أَعْتَلْكُمْ for أَعْمَالُكُمْ, the mīm read as tāʾ and the medial alif lost. The second lemma is not closed and the paragraph ends mid-āya.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (وَلَنَا أَعْمَالُنَا) نجازى بها (وَلَكُمْ أَعْمَالُكُمْ) — Q. 2:139, which then continues وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُخْلِصُونَ, beyond the end of this chunk. The stray wāw is an artifact. ¶69 is translated to its end as it stands.

problems.issue: The chunk opens mid-gloss with تحازون, which is not a word. The paragraph picks up the Jalālayn-style gloss on the preceding lemma وَلَكُمْ أَعْمَالُكُمْ (Q. 2:139), glossed in the Jalālayn as تُجازون بها. Translated from the restored reading ("you are requited for them"); no beginning has been invented for the clause.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: تُجازون بها, with ح for ج — a single-letter OCR substitution.

problems.issue: OCR damage inside a Qurʾānic lemma: وَنَحْرُ for وَنَحْنُ. The bracket also never closes before the gloss ونحن مخلصون له الدين والعمل, so the lemma/gloss boundary is set here on the sense (the lemma ends at مُخْلِصُونَ). Translated rather than marked illegible because the underlying text is fixed as Q. 2:139.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُخْلِصُونَ; and the closing bracket belongs after مُخْلِصُونَ.

problems.issue: The printed text reads يَقُولُونَ (third person) where Ḥafṣ has تَقُولُونَ at Q. 2:140. This is not necessarily OCR: أم يقولون is a canonical variant, and this edition follows the Warsh transmission throughout. Translated as it stands ("they say").
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the Madinan/Warsh reading يَقُولُونَ rather than OCR for تَقُولُونَ — to be verified against a Warsh muṣḥaf before the lemma is set.

problems.issue: OCR damage inside the lemma of Q. 2:140: كَاثُوا for كَانُوا (ث for ن) and نَصَرِى for نَصَارَى. Translated from the restored reading; the damage is recorded here.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَالْأَسْبَاطِ كَانُوا هُوداً أَوْ نَصَارَى.

problems.issue: OCR damage inside the lemma of Q. 2:140: فُلَ for قُلْ and أنتُمْوَ for أَأَنْتُمْ (the interrogative hamza lost, a stray واو added). Translated from the restored reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): قُلْ أَأَنْتُمْ أَعْلَمُ أَمِ اللَّهُ.

problems.issue: Heavy OCR damage across a Qurʾānic lemma: اترهِيمَ for إِبْرَاهِيمُ; يَهُود يَأ for يَهُودِيّاً (the tāʾ marbūṭa/yāʾ cluster broken by a space); تَصْرَائِيَا for نَصْرَانِيّاً. Translated rather than marked illegible because the verse is identifiable as Q. 3:67 and Niasse names the sūra in the next clause.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): مَا كَانَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ يَهُودِيّاً وَلَا نَصْرَانِيّاً.

problems.issue: OCR damage across a Qurʾānic lemma: التَّوْرِيَةُ for التَّوْرَاةُ; الأَمِنْ for إِلَّا مِنْ (the word boundary lost); بَعْدِمِة for بَعْدِهِ. Translated from the restored reading as Q. 3:65.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَمَا أُنْزِلَتِ التَّوْرَاةُ وَالْإِنْجِيلُ إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ.

problems.issue: The printed page break falls inside the name: ¶71 ends at الحجاج and ¶72 opens at بن يوسف. Not OCR damage. Translated as it stands — ¶71 closes with "al-Ḥajjāj" and ¶72 opens with "b. Yūsuf" — with no invented beginning for ¶72.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: in continuous text the clause reads كان الحجاج بن يوسف جبارا وفاجرا, "al-Ḥajjāj b. Yūsuf was a tyrant and a reprobate"; a press edition may wish to close the name at the paragraph join.

problems.issue: OCR damage at the end of the lemma of Q. 3:61: وَأَنْجُسَنَا for وَأَنْفُسَنَا and وَأَنمُسَكُمْ for وَأَنْفُسَكُمْ (ف read as ج and as م). Translated from the restored reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَأَنْفُسَنَا وَأَنْفُسَكُمْ.

problems.issue: Not damage. زَكَرِيَّاءَ with final hamza is the Madinan (Nāfiʿ/Warsh) reading of Q. 6:85 and has been kept; the yāʾ pointing in وَيَحْيِىٰ and وَعِيسِىٰ is this edition's orthography, not an error. Recorded so that a later pass does not "correct" it to زَكَرِيَّا.
problems.conjecture: No conjecture: the lemma stands as printed.

problems.issue: OCR damage inside the lemma of Q. 53:39: لِلانسَنِ for لِلْإِنْسَانِ and سَجِئُ for سَعَى. Translated from the restored reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَأَنْ لَيْسَ لِلْإِنْسَانِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَى.

problems.arabic: قال: من أنا؟ قل: أنت الذي إذا ظلم أحد
problems.issue: قل for قال inside the narrative frame: the imperative makes no sense in a chain of قال له / قال. Translated as the narrative verb ("He said").
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: قال: أنت الذي..., with the alif lost.

problems.arabic: "إِلَّ الابَارَلَعِي تَعِيمٌ وَانَّ ألْعَجَارَ لَصِى جَجِيم"
problems.issue: Heavy OCR damage across a two-verse lemma: إِلَّ for إِنَّ; الابَارَ for الْأَبْرَارَ; لَعِي for لَفِي; تَعِيمٌ for نَعِيمٍ; ألْعَجَارَ for الْفُجَّارَ; لَصِى for لَفِي; جَجِيم for جَحِيمٍ. Translated rather than marked illegible because the pair is identifiable as Q. 82:13–14 and the speaker's next clause ("I think you are in the second clause") depends on both halves standing.

problems.arabic: "جَإِذَا نُمِحَ في الصُّورِ وَلّاَ أَنسَابَ بَتَهُمْ يَوْمَيِذٍ وَلا يَتَسَآءَلُونَ"
