problems.issue: أَوْلِّبِكَ for أُولَٰئِكَ and يَلْعَنْهُمُ for يَلْعَنُهُمُ (a sukūn for the ḍamma of the imperfect). Translated from the restored reading; the gloss that follows at the head of ¶97 confirms the verb.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): أُولَٰئِكَ يَلْعَنُهُمُ اللَّهُ.

problems.issue: اخْتِلَك for اخْتِلَافِ (the final fāʾ read as kāf and the ʾalif lost) and التَّهار for النَّهَارِ (ن read as ه). Translated from the restored reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ.

problems.arabic: وَالْفُلْكِ) السفن التى تَجْرِ فِي البَحْرِ ولا ترسب موقرة
problems.issue: The opening bracket of وَالْفُلْكِ is lost, and التي تجري في البحر — the next Qurʾānic lemma of Q. 2:164 — carries no brackets at all, so lemma and gloss are indistinguishable in the print. Marked on the sense and on the Jalālayn: السفن is the gloss on والفلك, التي تجري في البحر is the lemma (q), and ولا ترسب موقرة is the gloss on it. تَجْرِ for تَجْرِي.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf and the Jalālayn): (وَالْفُلْكِ) السفن (الَّتِي تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ) ولا ترسب موقرة.

problems.issue: الشجارات is not a word here; the Jalālayn gloss on بما ينفع الناس is من التجارات والحمل. Translated from the restored reading ('of trade and transport').
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: من التجارات والحمل, with ش for ت.

problems.issue: بالنيات for بالنبات (ي for ب): the Jalālayn gloss on فأحيا به الأرض is بالنبات, 'with vegetation', which the following gloss بعد يبسها confirms. Translated from the restored reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: بالنبات.

problems.issue: مَزْنها for مَوْتِهَا in the lemma, and يسها for يبسها in the gloss (the bāʾ lost); the bracket closing the lemma is also lost, so lemma and gloss are not separated. Translated from the restored readings.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf and the Jalālayn): (بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا) بعد يبسها.

problems.issue: وَبَكَ for وَبَثَّ (the thāʾ read as kāf), and the bracket does not close before the gloss فرق ونشر, which is the Jalālayn gloss on وبث. Translated from the restored reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (وَبَثَّ) فرق ونشر.

problems.issue: Heavy OCR damage across the lemma: مِيهَا for فِيهَا, صٍ for مِن, تَاتً for دَابَّةٍ. Translated rather than marked illegible because the clause continues Q. 2:164 directly after وَبَثَّ and the verse is fixed; the bracket also never closes.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ).

problems.issue: بالخصر for بالخصب (ر for ب), and the Jalālayn gloss is cut at the page break — it runs لأنهم ينمون بالخصب الكائن عنه, of which الكائن عنه is missing. Translated from the restored reading as far as the text goes ('because they grow by the fertility'), with no ending supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لأنهم ينمون بالخصب الكائن عنه.

problems.issue: الرِّيَحِ for الرِّيَاحِ (medial ʾalif lost), and the bracket never closes before the gloss تقليبها جنوبا وشمالا حارة وباردة. The lemma/gloss boundary is set on the Jalālayn, at الرياح.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf and the Jalālayn): (وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ) تقليبها جنوبا وشمالا حارة وباردة.

problems.issue: The bracket of وَالسَّحَابِ does not close before its gloss الغيم, and the resumed lemma carries a prefixed wāw that the āya does not have: والْمْسَخُر for الْمُسَخَّرِ. Split on the sense into lemma, gloss, lemma; the stray wāw is not translated.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf and the Jalālayn): (وَالسَّحَابِ) الغيم (الْمُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ) بلا علاقة.

problems.arabic: هذه الثماني كلها لآيَاتِ) دالات على وحدانيته تعالى
problems.issue: The opening bracket of the lemma لَآيَاتٍ is lost, so Niasse's own aside هذه الثماني كلها ('these eight, all of them') and the Qurʾānic lemma are not separated in the print; لآيَاتِ also lacks the tanwīn of لَآيَاتٍ. Marked on the sense: the aside as p, the lemma as q.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf and the Jalālayn): هذه الثماني كلها (لَآيَاتٍ) دالات على وحدانيته تعالى.

problems.issue: أَنداداكه carries a prefixed wāw and a trailing كه that belong to neither the lemma nor the gloss; the lemma of Q. 2:164–165 is أَندَادًا and أصناما is the Jalālayn gloss on it. Translated from the restored reading, with أصناما kept as the gloss; the stray letters are not translated.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf and the Jalālayn): (أَندَادًا) أصناما — the كه probably a broken closing bracket.

problems.issue: تَحْبِ for كَحُبِّ (ك read as ت), and the bracket never closes before the gloss أي كحبهم له, which is the Jalālayn gloss on كحب الله and confirms the reading. Translated from the restored reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf and the Jalālayn): (كَحُبِّ اللَّهِ) أي كحبهم له.

problems.issue: Not necessarily OCR: the printed text reads تَرَى, second person, where Ḥafṣ has يَرَى at Q. 2:165, and the gloss يا محمد that follows presupposes the second person. The tāʾ reading is canonical and the Jalālayn records it. Translated as it stands ('and if you could see — O Muḥammad'). The opening bracket of the lemma is lost.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the reading وَلَوْ تَرَى rather than OCR for وَلَوْ يَرَى — to be verified against a Warsh muṣḥaf before the lemma is set.

problems.issue: In the gloss, ألجاته for أَلْجَأَتْهُ. In the lemma, عَادِه carries a stray hāʾ for عَادٍ, and the bracket never closes before the gloss متعد. The paragraph then breaks off mid-gloss at the page end.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf and the Jalālayn): أَلْجَأَتْهُ الضرورة ... (وَلَا عَادٍ) متعدٍّ — Q. 2:173.

problems.issue: الْبَسَءِ for الْبَأْسَاءِ, وَحِيرَ for وَحِينَ (nūn read as rāʾ), أَوْلُيِكَ for أُولَئِكَ. The glosses شدة الفقر, المرض and وقت شدة القتال confirm the sequence of Q. 2:177.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): الْبَأْسَاءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ وَحِينَ الْبَأْسِ … أُولَئِكَ.

problems.arabic: (رَبَّهَا ألذِيَ ءَامَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِصَاصُ فِي الْقَتْلَى)
problems.issue: رَبَّهَا ألذِيَ ءَامَنُوا for يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا — the vocative is badly garbled (yāʾ + ayyuhā read as rabbahā, الذين reduced to ألذي). The formula is fixed and the continuation is Q. 2:178, so it is translated rather than marked illegible.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِصَاصُ فِي الْقَتْلَى.

problems.issue: بِالْحَرِّ for بِالْحُرِّ — a vowelling error that would give “for the heat”; the Qurʾanic text and the gloss opening ¶108 (ولا يقتل الحر بالعبد) fix it as الحر بالحر. Also وصفا وفعلا in the preceding gloss is the Jalālayn’s on القصاص, retained and rendered literally (“in attribute and in act”).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): الْحُرُّ بِالْحُرِّ — Q. 2:178.

problems.issue: The most consequential misreading in the chunk: عُصِىَ (“was disobeyed”) for عُفِيَ (“was pardoned”), fāʾ read as ṣād, which reverses the sense of the ruling; also جَمَنْ for فَمَنْ and لَهُو for لَهُ. The glosses that follow (فعلى العافي اتباع القاتل) confirm عُفِيَ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): فَمَنْ عُفِيَ لَهُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ شَيْءٌ — Q. 2:178.

problems.arabic: (شَيْءٌ جَاتِّبَاعٌ) ... (بِالْمَعْرُوبِ) بأن بطالبه بالدية بلا عنف
problems.issue: جَاتِّبَاعٌ for فَاتِّبَاعٌ, بِالْمَعْرُوبِ for بِالْمَعْرُوفِ (final fāʾ read as bāʾ), and in the gloss بطالبه for يُطالبه.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): فَاتِّبَاعٌ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ … بأن يطالبه بالدية بلا عنف.

problems.issue: رَاكَ for ذَلِكَ (or ذَاكَ), with the opening parenthesis missing; تَخْعِيفٌ for تَخْفِيفٌ (fāʾ read as ʿayn); صِ for مِنْ. The intervening gloss الحكم identifies the demonstrative, which secures the reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (ذَلِكَ) الحكم (تَخْفِيفٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) — Q. 2:178.

problems.arabic: (جَسَ إعْتَدِى بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ) ... (قَلَهُو عَذَّابُ الِمُّ وَلَكُمْ مِ الْفِصَاص حَيوة
problems.issue: A run of damage across Q. 2:178–179: جَسَ إعْتَدِى for فَمَنِ اعْتَدَى, قَلَهُو for فَلَهُ, عَذَّابُ الِمُّ for عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ, مِ for فِي, الْفِصَاص for الْقِصَاصِ (qāf read as fāʾ), حَيوة for حَيَاةٌ. The lemma also runs on without a closing bracket into the gloss بقاء عظيم.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): فَمَنِ اعْتَدَى بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَلَهُ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ — وَلَكُمْ فِي الْقِصَاصِ حَيَاةٌ) بقاء عظيم.

problems.issue: فحيبت for فحَيِيَتْ in the gloss, and تَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَقَونَ for لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ (lām read as tāʾ, shadda lost) in the lemma of Q. 2:179. The following gloss تتقون القود confirms تتقون.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): فحَيِيَتْ بذلك نفسان (لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ).

problems.issue: بَدَّلَة for بَدَّلَهُ — the suffixed hāʾ taken as tāʾ marbūṭa. Translated rather than marked illegible, the lemma being fixed as Q. 2:181 and the Jalālayn's gloss الإيصاء following immediately.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): فَمَن بَدَّلَهُ.

problems.arabic: (بَإِنَّمَا إِنْمُهُو عَلَى ألذِينَ يُبَدِّلُونَةُ د إِنَّ اللَّه سَمِيعُ)
problems.issue: Four corruptions in one bracketed span: بَإِنَّمَا for فَإِنَّمَا (bāʾ for fāʾ, the one-dot-below for one-dot-above confusion recurring through this chunk); إِنْمُهُو for إِثْمُهُ; يُبَدِّلُونَةُ for يُبَدِّلُونَهُ; and a stray د standing where the waqf sign falls in the muṣḥaf.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): فَإِنَّمَا إِثْمُهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يُبَدِّلُونَهُ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ — Q. 2:181. The stray د is read as the waqf mark and is not translated.

problems.issue: The printed Jalālayn reads بفعل الوصي, 'of the deed of the executor'. الموصَى here is a passive participle with no له, so the referent is ambiguous between the executor and the legatee.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: بفعل الوصي. Rendered 'of the deed of the one to whom the bequest is entrusted', which holds both readings open; not emended in the text.

problems.issue: بَأَصْلَحَ for فَأَصْلَحَ — the same bāʾ-for-fāʾ substitution.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): فَأَصْلَحَ بَيْنَهُمْ — Q. 2:182.

problems.issue: تَتَّفُولَ for تَتَّقُونَ (qāf read as fāʾ, final nūn as lām). The bracket then closes nowhere: أَيَّاماً مَعْدُودَاتٍ opens Q. 2:184 but carries no parentheses of its own, so both the verse boundary and the boundary between lemma and the gloss قلائل have to be recovered.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ) (أَيَّامًا مَعْدُودَاتٍ) قلائل. The English splits the span into two lemma runs so that Q. 2:183 carries its own reference.

problems.arabic: (قَسَى كَانَ مِنكُم مَرِيضاً أوْ عَلَىٰ سَبَرِ)
problems.issue: قَسَى for فَمَن (fāʾ read as qāf, nūn as yāʾ) and سَبَرِ for سَفَرٍ. Both are fixed by the muṣḥaf and by the gloss مسافر سفر قصر that follows.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ — Q. 2:184.

problems.arabic: (قَعِدَّة) فعليه عدة ما أفطر مِ آَيَّامِ اخَرَم
problems.issue: قَعِدَّة for فَعِدَّةٌ; مِ for مِّنْ; اخَرَم for أُخَرَ with a stray mīm attached; and the second lemma carries no parentheses at all, so the boundary with the gloss فعليه عدة ما أفطر has to be recovered.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (فَعِدَّةٌ) فعليه عدة ما أفطر (مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ) يصومها بدله — Q. 2:184. The stray mīm is not translated.

problems.issue: Not OCR damage: the gloss negates the lemma. The muṣḥaf reads يُطِيقُونَهُ, 'those who are able for it', and the commentary glosses أي لا يطيقونه, taking the ruling to concern those unable to fast. Both are translated as they stand.
problems.conjecture: No emendation. The contradiction is the commentary's own, resting on the reading يُطَوَّقُونَهُ and on the exegesis of the fidya as a dispensation for the incapable; the following gloss من عجز عن الصوم يفدي confirms that this is the sense intended.

problems.issue: مِدْيَةُ for فِدْيَةٌ, and the span carries only a closing parenthesis. طَعَامِ مَسَكِينَ is written defectively and in the wrong case.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مَسَاكِينَ) — Q. 2:184. With the Warsh rasm used throughout this edition the plural مَسَاكِينَ is expected rather than Ḥafṣ's مِسْكِينٍ, and the defective spelling supports it; rendered as a plural, 'the feeding of needy persons'. The missing opening parenthesis belongs before فِدْيَةٌ.

problems.arabic: (قَمَر تَطَوَّعَ خَيْرَا) ... (بَهُوَ) ... (خَيْرلَّةُ وَأَن تَصُومُوا خَيْرٌ لَكُمُوَ)
problems.issue: قَمَر for فَمَن; بَهُوَ for فَهُوَ; خَيْرلَّةُ for خَيْرٌ لَّهُ, the two words run together; لَكُمُوَ for لَّكُمْ with a stray wāw.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيْرًا) ... (فَهُوَ) ... (خَيْرٌ لَّهُ وَأَن تَصُومُوا خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ) — Q. 2:184.

problems.issue: جَمَر for فَمَن and وَلْيَصْمْةٌ for فَلْيَصُمْهُ (fāʾ read as wāw, the suffixed hāʾ as tāʾ marbūṭa, the ḍamma lost). The second lemma is left unclosed. حضر is the Jalālayn's gloss on شهد.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (فَمَن شَهِدَ) حضر (مِنكُمُ الشَّهْرَ فَلْيَصُمْهُ) — Q. 2:185.

problems.issue: وَمَى for وَمَن, and the phrase stands unbracketed. The paragraph then breaks mid-phrase at عَلَىٰ, the printed page ending there; سَفَرِ opens ¶113.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ) — Q. 2:185. Translated as it stands, 'and whoever is ill or on a', with no ending supplied; the reference is carried in ¶113, where the run completes.

problems.issue: Unreadable as it stands. قل is an imperative, إن has no noun to govern, and قريب is indefinite and uninflected, so neither the speaker nor the sentence can be recovered. Marked illegible rather than guessed; it stands where the answer to the question put to the Prophet should fall.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: either the Jalālayn's فنزل followed by the Qurʾānic answer فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ, or Niasse's own فقال: إن الله قريب. Either way the sense is that the answer came that He is near. Footnote marker [52] retained in place.

problems.arabic: {أحيبُ دَعْوَةَ التَّاعِ" إِذَا دَعَابٍ» جَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِ وَلْيَومِنُوأ بِىَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشَدُونٌ
problems.issue: Heavy damage across Q. 2:186: أحيبُ for أُجِيبُ; التَّاعِ for الدَّاعِ; دَعَابٍ for دَعَانِ; جَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا for فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا; لِ for لِي; وَلْيَومِنُوأ for وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا; بِىَ for بِي; يَرْشَدُونٌ for يَرْشُدُونَ. The bracketing is also inconsistent, the span opening with { and a stray " and closing with ».
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ ۖ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا بِي لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ — Q. 2:186. Translated rather than marked illegible, every word being fixed by the āya.

problems.arabic: أجلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِيَامِ الرَّجَتْ نزل لما كان في صدر الإسلام من تحريم الجماع ليلا وقت رمضان «أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ اَ۬لصِّيَامِ اِ۬لرَّفَثُ»
problems.issue: Dittography: the opening of Q. 2:187 stands twice, once before Niasse's note on the occasion of revelation and once after it. The first instance is unbracketed and corrupt (أجلَّ for أُحِلَّ, الرَّجَتْ for الرَّفَثُ); the second is sound and bracketed. The repetition belongs to the transcription, not to the commentary.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the first instance is a duplicated line, to be deleted; read نزل لما كان في صدر الإسلام من تحريم الجماع ليلا وقت رمضان «أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيَامِ الرَّفَثُ». Neither instance has been deleted or reordered: both are rendered in the order they stand.

problems.issue: هَرَّ for هُنَّ; وَأَنتَمْ for وَأَنتُمْ; لَهَنَّ for لَّهُنَّ; لِبَاس without its case ending; and the span is left unclosed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (هُنَّ لِبَاسٌ لَّكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ لِبَاسٌ لَّهُنَّ) — Q. 2:187.

problems.arabic: نزلت هذه الآية والناس كانوا يفعلونه قبل عمر ويكتمونه
problems.issue: Not damage: the sentence is Niasse's own, absent from the Jalālayn, and is marked "p". ʿUmar is named without patronymic; the occasion of revelation requires ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb.
problems.conjecture: No emendation. ʿUmar is left as the text has him rather than expanded to ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb; footnote marker [53] retained at كما وقع لعمر.

problems.arabic: فتقولوا: اللهم جنبنا الشيطان وجنب الشيطان | ما رزقتنا[54] وتقولوا بسم اللّٰه
problems.issue: The duʿāʾ is broken across the paragraph boundary at وجنب الشيطان, ¶115 opening with ما رزقتنا. The basmala also stands after the duʿāʾ, where the ḥadīth has it first (بسم الله، اللهم جنبنا الشيطان وجنب الشيطان ما رزقتنا).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the transposition is the transcription's, the ḥadīth order placing بسم الله before اللهم جنبنا. Not reordered: the opening quotation mark is set in ¶114 and closed in ¶115, and the basmala is rendered where it stands. Footnote marker [54] retained in place.

problems.arabic: (وَكُلُواْ وَاشْرَبُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَّبَيِّنَ لَكْمُ الْخَيْطُ الأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ
problems.issue: يَتَّبَيِّنَ for يَتَبَيَّنَ (the shadda misplaced onto the tāʾ) and لَكْمُ for لَكُمُ. The paragraph breaks mid-phrase after الْخَيْطِ and the span is left unclosed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ — Q. 2:187; the continuation stands at the head of ¶116, so the reference is carried there.

problems.issue: الآنوَدِ for الْأَسْوَدِ (sīn read as nūn plus wāw) and الْمَجْرِم for الْفَجْرِ. Both are fixed by the āya and by the gloss كلوا حتى يطلع الفجر that follows immediately.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): الْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ — Q. 2:187.

problems.issue: قَمّ for ثُمَّ — three dots above read as one below.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا الصِّيَامَ — Q. 2:187.

problems.issue: Unreadable as it stands: nine letters in three groups, none of which forms an Arabic word, standing where the āya continues after أَتِمُّوا الصِّيَامَ and its gloss من الفجر. Marked illegible rather than guessed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): إِلَى اَ۬للَّيْلِ وَلَا, 'to the night, and do not', the negative governing تُبَاشِرُوهُنَّ at the head of ¶117. If that is right, the prohibition opening ¶117 has lost its negative particle into this illegible span, and ¶117's first lemma is accordingly translated without one.

problems.issue: تتشِرُوهَّ for تُبَاشِرُوهُنَّ, the first syllable lost and the final nūn written as hāʾ with shadda; عَيَبُونَ for عَاكِفُونَ; وَأنتَم for وَأَنتُمْ; الْمَسَجِدِ for الْمَسَاجِدِ, defective and in the wrong case. The paragraph opens mid-word, and the governing وَلَا lies in the illegible span closing ¶116.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): [وَلَا] تُبَاشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنتُمْ عَاكِفُونَ فِي الْمَسَاجِدِ — Q. 2:187. Translated from where it starts, with no negative supplied, since the particle is not in this paragraph.

problems.issue: حُدَرْلَّهِ for حُدُودُ اَ۬للَّهِ, the two words run together and the medial wāw lost; تِلْكَ carries only a closing parenthesis and حُدَرْلَّهِ only an opening one. الأحكام is the Jalālayn's gloss on تلك.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (تِلْكَ) الأحكام (حُدُودُ اللَّهِ) — Q. 2:187; the lemma continues with فَلَا تَقْرَبُوهَا at the head of ¶118, where the reference is carried.

problems.issue: The printed page break falls inside the gloss on أَوْ نُسُكٌ, which closes ¶120: ¶121 opens with its second half, بشاة. Not OCR damage. Translated as it stands — ¶121 opens 'with a sheep' — with no beginning supplied. The footnote marker [56] of the printing stands immediately after it and is retained in the translation, as in the preceding chunks.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: in continuous text the gloss reads (أَوْ نُسُكٌ) بِشَاةٍ — 'or a sacrificial offering — with a sheep' (Q. 2:196).

problems.issue: المدي for الهدي (hāʾ read as mīm). The same word stands undamaged in the lemma immediately before (مِنَ اَ۬لْهَدْيِ), which settles the reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ الْهَدْيُ — 'the sacrificial animal is incumbent upon him'.

problems.arabic: (جَمَى لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ... إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ إلى وطنكم وتِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ)
problems.issue: Two separate matters in one bracket. (1) جَمَى for فَمَن (jīm for fāʾ, and the nūn read as yāʾ). (2) The bracket has swallowed a gloss: إلى وطنكم is Niasse's gloss on إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ, not Qurʾān, and تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ resumes the lemma after it. Set as 'p' and 'q' respectively, per the rule that bracket content is 'q' only when it is actually Qurʾān. The wāw prefixed to وتِلْكَ is not in the muṣḥaf.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي ٱلْحَجِّ وَسَبْعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ) إلى وطنكم (تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ) — Q. 2:196.

problems.arabic: ثلاثة في الحج وسبعة إذا رجعتم "تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كَامِلَةً
problems.issue: The lemma تلك عشرة كاملة is quoted twice, once before its gloss and once after, the second time opened with a double quotation mark that is never closed and with كَامِلَةً for كَامِلَةٌ. Translated as it stands — the conventions keep repetition where the Arabic repeats — and set as 'q' without quotation marks, since this is Qurʾān and not a quoted authority. The repetition looks like the transcription of an oral restatement rather than OCR damage.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the second تلك عشرة كاملة is Niasse repeating the lemma after glossing it; a press edition may wish to mark it as a restatement. The stray quotation mark should be deleted and the accusative كاملةً corrected to كاملةٌ.

problems.arabic: (لِمَى لَمْ يَكْرَ آهْلُهُو حَاضِرِى الْمَسْجِدِ الترا ي أهل مكة
problems.issue: The most heavily damaged lemma in the chunk, with no closing bracket: لِمَى for لِمَن, يَكْرَ for يَكُنْ (nūn read as rāʾ), آهْلُهُو for أَهْلُهُو, and then الترا ي, in which the letters of الحرام are lost rather than merely mis-dotted. The first four are restored from the muṣḥaf and translated; الترا ي is marked [illegible] rather than guessed, even though its position after الْمَسْجِدِ leaves little room for doubt. The gloss أهل مكة follows without an opening bracket.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): لِمَن لَّمْ يَكُنْ أَهْلُهُو حَاضِرِى ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ — 'is for him whose family are not present at the Sacred Mosque' (Q. 2:196). Were the reading confirmed against the printing, the [illegible] mark should be replaced by 'Sacred'.

problems.issue: بَسَر for فَمَن (an almost total loss: bāʾ for fāʾ, sīn for mīm, rāʾ for nūn), قَرَضَ for فَرَضَ, and بِيهَِّ for فِيهِنَّ. The brackets are also disordered: على نفسه is the gloss on فرض and stands inside the lemma bracket, which never closes. Set as 'p'. The sequence الحج أشهر معلومات … فمن فرض فيهن الحج fixes all three words.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (فَمَن فَرَضَ) على نفسه (فِيهِنَّ ٱلْحَجَّ) بالإحرام — 'so whoever undertakes — upon himself — the pilgrimage therein — by entering iḥrām' (Q. 2:197).

problems.arabic: (بَلاَ رَقِتَ وَلاَ جُسُوقَ وَلاَ جِدَالَ فِي الخَيُّ
problems.issue: Four defects in one lemma, and no closing bracket: بَلا for فَلا, رَقِتَ for رَفَثَ, جُسُوق for فُسُوق (jīm for fāʾ again), and الخَيُّ for الحَجِّ. The triad رفث / فسوق / جدال is fixed by the muṣḥaf.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ فِي ٱلْحَجِّ — 'then no sexual intercourse, no transgression, and no disputing during the pilgrimage' (Q. 2:197).

problems.issue: التَّفْوى is التَّقْوى (fāʾ for qāf) and is restored without difficulty. The gloss, however, is not recoverable: سوال النلر is neither word as printed, and two readings are available that differ in substance — سؤال الناس ('begging from people') and سؤال النار / سوء النار ('the questioning of the Fire', 'the evil of the Fire'). Marked [illegible] in the translation rather than guessed; the readable part of the gloss, ما يتقى به, is translated.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ما يُتَّقَىٰ بِهِ سُؤَالُ النَّاسِ — 'that by which one guards against begging from people'. This is the likelier of the two, because the lemma it glosses, وتزودوا, was revealed about the people of Yemen who travelled without provisions and became a burden on others, and Niasse has just given that occasion. The alternative, سُؤَالُ النَّارِ, requires only one letter (lām for alif) and cannot be excluded. To be settled against the printing.

problems.issue: A run of single-letter losses, all fixed by the muṣḥaf and translated: وَتَّقُوبِ for وَاتَّقُونِ (the nūn read as bāʾ), جَتَاحُ for جُنَاحٌ, بَصْلًا for فَضْلًا, and صِ for مِّن — the last reduced to a single letter, but its place between فضلًا and ربكم admits nothing else. The bracket before رزقا closes after a stray space, and the lemma من ربكم never closes.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): وَٱتَّقُونِ يَٰأُوْلِي ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ (Q. 2:197); لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبْتَغُوا (فَضْلًا) رزقا (مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ) (Q. 2:198).

problems.arabic: (قَإِذَا أَبَضْتُم) دفعتم مِنْ عَرَقَتِ بَاذْكُرُواْ أَلَّ)
problems.issue: قَإِذَا for فَإِذَا, أَبَضْتُم for أَفَضْتُم, عَرَقَتِ for عَرَفَٰتٍ, بَاذْكُرُوا for فَاذْكُرُوا, and أَلَّ for ٱللَّهَ. The brackets around the second lemma are inverted — it opens without a bracket and closes with one — so that the gloss دفعتم, which belongs between the two lemmata, is left unenclosed. All five words are fixed by Q. 2:198 and translated.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (فَإِذَا أَفَضْتُم) دفعتم (مِنْ عَرَفَٰتٍ فَٱذْكُرُوا ٱللَّهَ) — 'And when you depart — you press on — from ʿArafāt, remember Allah' (Q. 2:198).

problems.arabic: (أَوَ اشدَّ ذِكْرا من ذكرهم (قَمِسَ النَّاس مَنْ يَقُولٌ
problems.issue: ¶122 opens inside the lemma run of Q. 2:200 that ¶121 breaks off (كَذِكْرِكُمْ آبَآءَكُمْ), and is damaged at both ends: أَوَ اشدَّ for أَوْ أَشَدَّ, and قَمِسَ for فَمِنَ (qāf for fāʾ, sīn for nūn), with an impossible tanwīn on the jussive-looking يَقُولٌ. The bracket before قمس opens a lemma without closing the preceding one, so the gloss من ذكرهم stands inside the lemma bracket; set as 'p'. من ذكرهم is an objective genitive — 'than your remembrance of them [the fathers]' — and the supplied pronoun is bracketed in the English.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): أَوْ أَشَدَّ ذِكْرًا (من ذكرهم) فَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ رَبَّنَآ آتِنَا فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا — 'or more intensely in remembrance … And among the people there is he who says: Our Lord, give us in this world' (Q. 2:200). The Jalālayn's gloss here is من ذكركم آباءكم.

problems.issue: The printed page break falls between the lemma حَسَنَةً at the end of ¶123 and its gloss نعمة at the start of ¶124. Not OCR damage. Translated as it stands — ¶124 opens 'a blessing' — with no beginning supplied. حَسَنَةَ in the second lemma lacks its tanwīn.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: in continuous text the clause reads (رَبَّنَآ آتِنَا فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً) نعمة (وَفِي ٱلْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً) هي الجنة — 'Our Lord, give us good in this world — a blessing — and in the hereafter good — which is the Garden' (Q. 2:201).

problems.issue: وَفِنَا for وَقِنَا (fāʾ for qāf) and اْلبَّارِ for ٱلنَّارِ (bāʾ for nūn, with a stray sukūn-bearing alif); the lemma opens without a bracket. In the next lemma أولِّئِكَ carries a spurious shadda and لَهَمْ is لَهُمْ. All restored from the muṣḥaf and translated.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ) بعدم دخولها (أُوْلَٰئِكَ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ) — 'and protect us from the punishment of the Fire — by not entering it — Those have a share' (Q. 2:201–202).

problems.issue: The lemma مِّن is reduced to صِ, as at Q. 2:198 in ¶121, and its bracket opens where it should close. The one-word gloss أجل glosses that مِّن in the sense of من أجل ('on account of'), and is translated accordingly rather than as the particle 'yes' or as أَجَل ('a term'). The muṣḥaf reads مِمَّا كَسَبُوا; Niasse's citation separates مِن and ما so as to gloss the preposition.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (مِّن) أَجْلِ (مَا كَسَبُوا) عملوا من الحج والدعاء — 'of — on account of — what they have earned — what they have done, of pilgrimage and supplication' (Q. 2:202).

problems.arabic: لحديث بذلك.[57] اللهم صل على سيدنا محمد.
problems.issue: Not damage. The gloss on وَٱللَّهُ سَرِيعُ ٱلْحِسَابِ appeals to a ḥadīth without naming it, and the printing's footnote marker [57] stands at that point; the marker is retained in the translation, as in the preceding chunks. The closing formula اللهم صل على سيدنا محمد ends Lesson 5 and is set as Niasse's own prose ('p'), not as a quoted authority.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: footnote [57] of the printing presumably cites the ḥadīth on the reckoning of creation in half a day; it should be checked against whatever it gives. No conjecture is needed for the Arabic, which is undamaged.

problems.issue: The paragraph opens mid-word: علهم is not an Arabic word but the tail of a word split by the printed page turn, whose head stands at the end of ¶97.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: read أعمالهم, Jalālayn's gloss on the preceding lemma وَأَصْلَحُواْ at the end of ¶97 («وأصلحوا» أعمالهم «وبينوا» ما كتموا). Rendered "their deeds" here. Flagged as a conjecture: if the translator of ¶97 also rendered the word, the English will duplicate it and one of the two should be struck.

problems.issue: رَبَينُوا is not an Arabic word; the shadda of the second radical is also lost.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: read (وَبَيَّنُواْ) (Q. 2:160) — ر is OCR for و. Confirmed by the gloss that follows, ما كتموا, which is Jalālayn on وبينوا. Translated on that reading.

problems.issue: بَأْوْلَيِكَ is corrupt: the first letter is wrong and the madda of أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ has been lost.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: read (فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ) (Q. 2:160) — ب for ف, a substitution recurring across this lesson. Confirmed by the gloss أقبل توبتهم, Jalālayn on أتوب عليهم. Translated on that reading.

problems.arabic: (وَأَنَا اَ۬لتَّوَّابُ اُ۬لرَّحِيمُۖ إِنَّ اَ۬لذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَمَاتُواْ وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ ا۟وْلَٰٓئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةُ اُ۬للَّهِ وَالْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ) مستحقون ذلك في الدنيا والآخرة
problems.issue: One bracket carries the close of Q 2:160 and the whole of Q 2:161, so a single lemma spans a verse boundary and the reference cannot sit after the bracket.
problems.conjecture: Not a defect in the Arabic. Split into two "q" runs — وأنا التواب الرحيم and إن الذين كفروا … أجمعين — with (Q. 2:160) in the intervening "p" run and (Q. 2:161) after the second, as the rest of this lesson references its runs. The gloss مستحقون ذلك في الدنيا والآخرة is Jalālayn on أولئك عليهم لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين and is attached to the Q 2:161 run accordingly.

problems.issue: خَلِدِيرَ is corrupt and the bracket is unbalanced: it closes without having opened, so the start of the lemma is unmarked.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: read (خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا) (Q. 2:162) — ر is OCR for ن — with the opening bracket lost before خالدين. Confirmed by the gloss خالدين في اللعنة أو خالدين في النار, which repeats the lemma's own word. Register assigned on that reading.

problems.arabic: (وَالَهْكُمُ إِلَةٌ وَاحِدُّ نزل في قوم سألوا الرسول
problems.issue: Three words are damaged (وَالَهْكُمُ, إِلَةٌ, وَاحِدُّ — the last carries ḍamma plus shadda where the Qurʾān has tanwīn) and the bracket does not close, so the lemma/prose boundary is unmarked.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: read (وَإِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٌ وَاحِدٌ) (Q. 2:163) — the alif-lām of وَالَهْكُمُ is OCR for إِلَٰـ, and the madda of إِلَٰهٌ is lost. The boundary is placed before نزل, which begins the occasion-of-revelation report. Registers assigned on that reading.

problems.issue: اوَالَمَكُمَ is not an Arabic word.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: read (وَإِلَٰهُكُمُ) (Q. 2:163) — م for ه, with the same damage to إِلَٰـ as in the first citation six words earlier. Confirmed by the gloss المستحق للعبادة, Jalālayn on وإلهكم (المستحق للعبادة منكم). Translated on that reading as a resumed citation of the same verse.

problems.arabic: (إلَة وَحِدَّ) لا نظير له في ذاته
problems.issue: Both words have lost their madda and tanwīn; وَحِدَّ carries a shadda the Qurʾānic وَاحِدٌ does not have.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: read (إِلَٰهࣱ وَاحِدࣱ) (Q. 2:163), the resumption of the lemma after the gloss المستحق للعبادة. Translated on that reading; no effect on sense.

problems.issue: مِ stands alone and خَلْو is not an Arabic word.

[8] And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, placed the blessing in progeny and in tillage, so that it is greater in these things than it is in all other things. If you reflect, you find that most people do not sow: few of them are those who occupy themselves with agriculture, and those who do occupy themselves with agriculture occupy themselves only in part of their time. Despite this, you see that a human being eats nothing but what is sown. Had Allah not sent down the blessing upon what is sown, this would not have been possible. And He placed the blessing in animals — sheep, cattle and camels. In most cases these livestock give birth only once in the year, and when one gives birth she bears a single offspring; and if it varies, she bears two. Whoever wants meat must slaughter one of them, and whoever wants to sell sells something of them; and you do not go out but that you meet

a herd of camels, or a herd of cattle or of sheep. And if you think about beasts of prey, and about dogs, and even about cats, you find them giving birth twice in the year; each time they bear eight young. And people do not occupy themselves with slaughtering them, nor with selling them, and you never see many of them at all. If you came across five dogs, you would say: this is a great many dogs. And you find a hundred cows, and you find a hundred sheep. Had the blessing not descended upon livestock, this would not be so. So for this reason this hypocrite has acted contrary to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in that he occupied himself with destroying the tilth and the livestock.

This is entering Islam wholly. This is the entry of the soul. And the heart strips off all blameworthy traits of character and puts on all praiseworthy traits; and the spirit leaves off turning toward any other than Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and the inmost secret passes away in the Essence of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and sees nothing other than Him. At the beginning of their affair the Muslims were harmed with every kind of harm; the unbelievers met them with every injury, until the Messenger ordered them to emigrate to Abyssinia. After that the Messenger ﷺ emigrated with his own noble person to Medina the Radiant, and the unbelievers did not cease to harm the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions. The severest thing he met from the unbelievers was the Day of the Trench: the unbelievers called one another from every quarter to Medina, while [the Muslims] were neighbours to their enemies the Jews, with the hypocrites among them, so that they met severe harm from the Jews. By Allah, Allah will surely bring this affair to completion, until the rider travels from Ṣanʿāʾ to Ḥaḍramawt fearing none but Allah, and the wolf for his sheep."

The occasion for the sending down of this āya: the Prophet ﷺ sent out the first of his raiding parties, with ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaḥsh over it and eight men with him. They fought the polytheists and killed Ibn al-Ḥaḍramī on the last day of Jumādā al-Ākhira, and it was confused for them with Rajab; so the unbelievers reproached them with having held it lawful.
The Prophet ﷺ sent out, two months before Badr, eight of his Companions, and he wrote a letter for their commander ʿAbdallāh b. Jaḥsh and sealed it, and he wrote him another letter, saying to him:

“Travel in Allah's Name, with Allah's blessing. Do not open this letter until you have travelled two days. When you have travelled two days, open the letter. And do not compel anyone to travel with you: whoever wishes to travel with you, let him travel, and whoever wishes to turn back, let him turn back.”
When he had travelled two days he opened the letter and found in it:
“By Allah's Name. Travel with Allah's blessing until you come to Baṭn Nakhla
— a place between al-Ṭāʾif and Mecca —
and when you meet the caravan of Quraysh, perhaps you will bring us some good from them.”

[18] So they travelled on until they reached Baṭn Nakhla on the last day of Jumādā al-Ākhira, before Rajab — and it is a month in which fighting is forbidden. When the unbelievers saw them, ʿAbdallāh b. Jaḥsh said to them: shave the head of one of you. problems.issue: Not OCR damage, but the clause is loose as transcribed: خبر appears twice with no stated connection, and جذلان is a bare predicate with no copula. Translated as it stands (“any piece of news is put to him … he mentions some piece of news about the Ḥijāz”), with nothing supplied beyond the sense of يعرض له.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the point is that whatever subject is raised with a returned pilgrim, he turns it to the Ḥijāz — أي جذلان بحجه, “exulting in his ḥajj”. If في الحجاز is itself damaged, عن الحجاز (“about the Ḥijāz”) would give the same sense.

problems.arabic: والعارف لا يجد غنى عن الله تبارك وتعالى
problems.issue: The chunk ends here, with no full stop in the Arabic; the comparison between the child and the knower is still running. Translated as the fragment it is, with no ending supplied and no closing punctuation.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the sentence continues on the following printed page, which opens L06c02.

problems.issue: تهيه for نهيه — ن read as ت. Translated from the restored reading ("His prohibition").
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: واجتناب نهيه.

problems.arabic: (من حج فلم يرفث ولم يغسل رجع من ذنوبه كيوم ولدته أمه)
problems.issue: ولم يغسل ("and did not wash") is nonsense in a ḥadīth on the pilgrimage. The same ḥadīth stands intact earlier in the same corpus — من حج ولم يرفث ولم يفسق رجع من ذنوبه كيوم ولدته أمه (chunk L05c03, ¶54) — so the reading is fixed and the clause is translated from it ("does not transgress") rather than marked illegible.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ولم يفسق, as at L05c03 ¶54.

problems.arabic: والحج المبرور علاين أن يرجع الحاج
problems.issue: علاين is not a word and the clause has no predicate without it. Marked illegible rather than emended, since this is Niasse's own prose and not a fixed text. ¶8 supplies the parallel فهذا علامة الحج المبرور, which is what makes the conjecture below plausible.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: علامته ("its sign"), i.e. والحج المبرور علامته أن يرجع الحاج متواضعا — supported by علامة الحج المبرور in ¶8.

problems.issue: The span is damaged and the paragraph ends on it; what the reprobate heard, and from where, is lost. Marked illegible. ¶8 opens with the words he heard — تفعل هذا وأنت حاج — so a voice or inward address is being reported.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فسمع من سِرِّهِ ("he heard from his inmost self"), with the final hāʾ read as tāʾ. A reading فسمع مَن سَرَّهُ cannot be excluded.

problems.issue: The lemma of Q. 2:203 is broken at the page turn and runs on into ¶9 (تُحْشَرُونَ). م م is unreadable and is marked illegible; وَاعْلَمُوَ for وَاعْلَمُوا and إِلْهِ for إِلَيْهِ are translated from the restored reading. The bracket never closes.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ — the full lemma stands intact at L06c01 ¶2 as وَاعْلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّكُمُۥٓ إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ, so م م is أَنَّكُمْ.

problems.issue: The paragraph opens mid-gloss on Q. 2:204 and the first word is damaged: بعجبك is not a word, the yāʾ of يعجبك having been read as a bāʾ. The governing negative is also absent, and with it the sense: the gloss on «يُعْجِبُكَ قَوْلُهُ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا» turns on the speech pleasing you in this world and NOT pleasing you in the Hereafter. Because restoring the word would also mean supplying a negative that reverses the clause, the span is marked illegible rather than emended, and the following clause is translated as it stands.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ولا يعجبك في الآخرة لمخالفته لاعتقاده, i.e. “but it does not please you in the Hereafter, because it runs counter to his belief.” The لا was most likely lost at the page break rather than in OCR; the press should check the printed page.

problems.issue: مِي for فِي — the fāʾ has lost its dot and gained one below. Restored rather than marked illegible: the lemma is fixed (Q. 2:204) and the gloss أنه موافق لمقوله depends on it. The brackets are also mismatched: the run opens with ( and closes with »).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَيُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِي قَلْبِهِ). Orthographic and bracketing only; the English is unaffected. Bracketing to be normalised to the edition's lemma parentheses.

problems.issue: أَلدَّ for أَلَدُّ — the vowelling of the muṣḥaf has not survived; the consonantal skeleton is intact. A stray space precedes the closing parenthesis.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ الْخِصَامِ). Vowelling only.

problems.issue: سَجىٰ for سَعَىٰ — the ʿayn read as a jīm. Restored rather than marked illegible, because Niasse's own gloss مشى (“he walks”) is the Jalālayn gloss on سعى and fixes the reading, and because Q. 2:205 is fixed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (سَعَىٰ) مشى. The English “he strives — he walks —” follows the restored reading.

problems.arabic: (مِي الاَرْضِ لِيُفْسِدَ بِيهَا وَبَهْلِكَ ألْحَرْثَ وَالتَّسْلَ
problems.issue: Four damaged words in one lemma run from Q. 2:205: مِي for فِي and بِيهَا for فِيهَا (fāʾ read as mīm, then as bāʾ); وَبَهْلِكَ for وَيُهْلِكَ (yāʾ read as bāʾ, vowelling lost); وَالتَّسْلَ for وَالنَّسْلَ (nūn read as tāʾ). Also ألْحَرْثَ for الْحَرْثَ, with the hamza of waṣl written as a hamza of qaṭʿ — a systematic habit of this transcription. Restored, the underlying āya being fixed and identifiable. The parenthesis is never closed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فِي الْأَرْضِ لِيُفْسِدَ فِيهَا وَيُهْلِكَ الْحَرْثَ وَالنَّسْلَ).

problems.issue: ألْمَسَادَ for الْفَسَادَ — the same fāʾ-to-mīm substitution as at مِي. Restored. The parenthesis is unclosed, and the gloss لا يرضى به follows outside it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْفَسَادَ).

problems.issue: Three defects in one sequence: مَحَسْبُهُ for فَحَسْبُهُ (fāʾ to mīm again); وَلَبِيسَ for وَلَبِئْسَ (the hamza unwritten); جَهَنَّمٌ with tanwīn, though جهنم is indeclinable and the muṣḥaf has جَهَنَّمُ. Restored. The lemma is split across the gloss كافيه, so the English splits with it (“so enough for him — [what] suffices him — is Hell”); the resulting English is awkward but the segmentation is the Arabic's.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَحَسْبُهُ) كافيه (جَهَنَّمُ وَلَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ).

problems.arabic: الفراش هي. الله لا يحب الفساد
problems.issue: After the gloss الفراش on الْمِهَادُ, a bare هي stands before the full stop with nothing to attach to: it has no predicate and no antecedent in agreement. Marked illegible rather than emended or dropped, since more than one reconstruction fits and the word may be an intrusion from the printed line above.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture, in order of likelihood: (1) a resumptive pronoun glossing جهنم — الفراش، هي جهنم, “the bedding — it is Hell,” with the predicate lost; (2) dittography from the following line and to be deleted; (3) a transcriptional remnant of a catchword. The printed page should be checked before the press decides.

problems.arabic: الله لا يحب الفساد لاسيما فساد هذا المنافق في الحرث والنسل
problems.issue: Niasse repeats the āya verbatim in his own exposition, unbracketed, and makes it the subject of his own sentence by means of لاسيما. Marked “q” and given its reference, on the principle that register follows what the words are rather than how the edition brackets them; the clause is left woven into the surrounding “p” run rather than being set off as a separate citation.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. A register decision, recorded for the press; if unbracketed repetitions are to be set as prose elsewhere in the volume, this run should be re-tagged “p”.

problems.arabic: لما خلق أدم ... علمه الحرف التي يعيش بها أولاده
problems.issue: أدم for آدم (the madda unwritten) — a recurring habit of this transcription, since آدم is written correctly four words later at حرفة آدم. الحرف is the plural of حرفة, i.e. الحِرَف, unvowelled here and liable to be misread as al-ḥarf (“the letter”); the feminine plural agreement of التي confirms the plural.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لما خلق آدم ... علمه الحِرَف التي يعيش بها أولاده. Orthographic and vowelling only; translated “the crafts by which his children would live.”

problems.arabic: وإذا ولدت ولدت ولدا واحدا، فإذا اختلف ولدت ولدين
problems.issue: اختلف stands without a subject, and its masculine agreement matches nothing in the sentence (الأنعام is treated as feminine singular throughout). Translated as it stands, with an impersonal subject (“and if it varies”); nothing is supplied in the Arabic.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فإذا اختلف [الأمر] ولدت ولدين, “and if the case differs, she bears two.” An ellipsis of oral delivery rather than OCR damage.

problems.arabic: (وَإِذَا تَوَلَى ... (سَجىٰ) ... (مِي الاَرْضِ ... (وَاللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ ألْمَسَادَ ... (وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُ اُ۪تَّقِ اِ۬للَّهَ)
problems.issue: Systemic, not local: in this paragraph the lemma parentheses open and are mostly never closed, so the boundary between lemma and gloss has to be recovered from the Jalālayn gloss pattern rather than from the punctuation. The segmentation of “q” and “p” runs in the output rests on that recovery, and at وَإِذَا تَوَلَى / انصرف عنك and ألْمَسَادَ / لا يرضى به the boundary is editorial.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the printed edition closes these parentheses and the closing brackets have been lost in transcription. A whole-volume bracketing pass is advisable; the two boundaries named above should be verified against the printed page.

problems.arabic: والناس م يشتغلوا بذبحها ولا ببيعها
problems.issue: م is not a word: the negative particle has been truncated. Restored rather than marked illegible, because both candidates give the same English and the following ولا ترى fixes the sense.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لم يشتغلوا (lām lost) or ما يشتغلوا (alif lost); the first is likelier given the surrounding written register. Either way, “people do not occupy themselves with slaughtering them.”

problems.arabic: من قيل له اتق اللّٰه ولم يتواضع فهو متكي
problems.issue: متكي cannot stand. Read as it is written it is مُتَّكِئ, “reclining,” which the sentence does not admit; the predicate required is an adjective of arrogance, against ولم يتواضع and the preceding هذا غاية في الكبر. Because متكي is itself a readable word, the damage is not self-evident, so the span is marked illegible rather than emended.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فهو متكبر, “then he is arrogant.” The loss of bāʾ and rāʾ is heavier than the other substitutions in this chunk, so the printed page should be checked; if it reads متكبر, the English becomes “…does not humble himself is arrogant.”

problems.issue: قبل for قيل — the yāʾ read as a bāʾ, the same substitution as at بعجبك and وَبَهْلِكَ. Restored: قبل (“before”) yields no construction with لعمر, and the passive قيل answers من قيل له اتق اللّٰه in the preceding clause.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فلهذا قيل لعمر اتق اللّٰه. The words اتق اللّٰه spoken to ʿUmar are left inside the “p” run without quotation marks: the speaker is unnamed, so the span is neither ḥadīth nor a named authority, and the quotation marks of the “h” register would overstate it.

problems.arabic: وقتلوا أصحابه كلا حتى بقي هو
problems.issue: كلا for كلهم — the pronoun suffix has dropped. Restored; كلا with no suffix cannot serve as an apposition to أصحابه.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وقتلوا أصحابه كلهم, “and killed his companions, all of them.”

problems.arabic: «وَإِذَا قِيَلَ لَه إِتَّقِ اللَّهَ أَخَذَتْهُ أُلْعِزَّةُ»
problems.issue: Vowelling damage across a repeated lemma from Q. 2:206: قِيَلَ for قِيلَ (a fatḥa where the long ī belongs); لَه for لَهُ; إِتَّقِ for اتَّقِ, the hamza of waṣl again written as qaṭʿ; أُلْعِزَّةُ for الْعِزَّةُ, with the article vowelled as a hamza of qaṭʿ. Restored, the consonantal skeleton being intact and the āya fixed. Here the lemma is in guillemets, whereas the first citation of the same words in ¶10 is in parentheses; the edition's bracketing is not consistent.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: «وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ أَخَذَتْهُ الْعِزَّةُ». Vowelling and bracketing only.

problems.issue: The footnote marker [9] has been carried inside the lemma parenthesis, ahead of the first word of the āya. Set before the lemma in the output. يَشْرِى for يَشْرِي is an orthographic variant (alif maqṣūra for yāʾ), not damage.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the marker belongs to the end of the preceding sentence, after تواضعا لله تعالى, where the other markers in this chunk sit ([8] at the end of a sentence in ¶10). Placement to be verified against the printed page.

problems.arabic: يا قوم لقد علمتم أني أرماكم وكنانتي هذه مملوءة سهاما
problems.issue: أرماكم is the elative أرمى with the pronoun suffix, “the best archer among you,” not a verb; unvowelled it is open to being read as a first-person verb (“I shoot you”), which the following وكنانتي هذه مملوءة سهاما excludes. Ṣuhayb's speech here, and Abū Bakr's ربح البيع below, are set in the “h” register with quotation marks, as the verbatim words of named authorities.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. The received wording of the report adds the tamyīz — أني أرماكم رجلاً — and the press may wish to collate against the source footnoted at [2] (al-Qurṭubī, al-Jāmiʿ li-aḥkām al-Qurʾān, iii, 20), which also tells the story with Ṣuhayb detained alone rather than with eight companions killed.

problems.arabic: فتلا عليه هذه الآية2 «وَمِنَ اَ۬لنَّاسِ مَنْ يَّشْرِے نَفْسَهُ»
problems.issue: Two things. (1) The footnote numeral 2 is attached to الآية with no bracket and no space; it is the marker answering the footnote transcribed as ¶12, and is rendered “[2]”. (2) The lemma carries Warsh-tradition orthography that OCR has partly broken: اَ۬لنَّاسِ for النَّاسِ (the small hamza of waṣl above the alif read as a separate sign) and يَّشْرِے for يَشْرِي, with a spurious shadda and the final yāʾ set as ے (U+06D2).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فتلا عليه هذه الآية[2] «وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَن يَشْرِي نَفْسَهُ». A global fix for the chunk: normalise اَ۬ل to ال and ے to ي. No English is affected.

problems.issue: اللَّهِه carries a supernumerary hāʾ — a duplicated letter at the line end. إبْتِغَآءَ writes the hamza of waṣl as qaṭʿ, as elsewhere in this chunk. The parenthesis is unclosed, and the gloss رضاه follows immediately with no separation.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (ابْتِغَاءَ مَرْضَاتِ اللَّهِ) رضاه.

problems.issue: A consistency matter for the volume rather than a defect in this chunk: the two place names are rendered “Mecca” and “Medina,” following the IJMES word list, but the chunks already translated use both “Makka” (L05c01) and “Mecca” (L05c03).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: none needed. Recommend “Mecca” and “Medina” throughout, with a single pass over the earlier files to bring “Makka” into line.

problems.arabic: 2 - راجع القرطبي في تفسيره الجامع لأحكام القرآن ج3/ ص20.
problems.issue: This paragraph is not Niasse's text. It is the editor's footnote, keyed to the numeral 2 in ¶11, which the transcription has carried into the running text at the page foot. Translated in the “p” register with the title transliterated (“i”), and kept at its own paragraph number; the press will want it set as a note rather than as prose.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. The reference resolves to al-Qurṭubī, al-Jāmiʿ li-aḥkām al-Qurʾān, vol. 3, p. 20, for the Ṣuhayb report under Q. 2:207; the volume and page should be checked against whichever printing the edition used, since they vary between the Būlāq and Dār al-Kutub printings.

problems.arabic: ولا ينظر بعينيه إلا يأمر الله
problems.issue: إلا يأمر for إلا بأمر — the bāʾ of the preposition lost, which turns the phrase into a finite verb and breaks the series. The clause immediately before it reads ولا يبطش بيديه إلا بأمر الله, which fixes the reading. Restored.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ولا ينظر بعينيه إلا بأمر الله — “and does not look with his eyes except by Allah's command.”

problems.arabic: (بَإِن زَلَلْتُم) … مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَتْكُمُ الْبَيِّنَتُ) … (حَكِيمُ في صنعه
problems.issue: بَإِن for فَإِن — the fāʾ read as a bāʾ (one dot above taken as one dot below), the commonest defect in this chunk. Restored; Q. 2:209 is fixed. Also three bracketing failures in one stretch: the lemma مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَتْكُمُ الْبَيِّنَتُ has no opening parenthesis, and (حَكِيمُ is never closed, so the gloss في صنعه runs on outside the lemma. الْبَيِّنَتُ for الْبَيِّنَاتُ reflects the muṣḥaf orthography and is not damage.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَإِن زَلَلْتُمْ) … (مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْكُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ) … (حَكِيمٌ) في صنعه (Q. 2:209).

problems.issue: مِ الْغَمَمِ for مِنَ الْغَمَامِ — the nūn of من lost and the alif of الغمام swallowed. Restored: Q. 2:210 is fixed, and Niasse's gloss السحاب (“the clouds”) is the Jalālayn gloss on الغمام and settles the reading. The lemma also lacks its opening parenthesis.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (مِنَ الْغَمَامِ) السحاب.

problems.issue: وَالْمَلْيِكَةُ for وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ (the alif of the hamza seat lost, the vowelling scrambled) and إنيان for إتيان (the tāʾ's two dots above read as one dot below, giving a nūn). Both restored, and the second is settled by the lemma it glosses. The closing parenthesis is doubled.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ) وهو إتيان الملائكة — “and the angels — and that is the coming of the angels.”

problems.issue: Two words run together: ألَّهِتُرْجَعُ for اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ, the word space lost. Also وَإلَى for وَإِلَى and ألَّهِ, الأُمُورُ for اللَّهِ, الْأُمُورُ (hamzat waṣl written as qaṭʿ). Restored; Q. 2:210 is fixed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ) (Q. 2:210).

problems.arabic: سَلْ يا محمد رَنِِّ إِسْرَاءِيلَ) تبكيتا
problems.issue: رَنِِّ for بَنِي — the bāʾ's single dot below read as a rāʾ with no dot, and the final yāʾ reduced to a doubled kasra. Restored: Q. 2:211 is fixed, إِسْرَاءِيلَ follows immediately, and the Jalālayn construction being reproduced here is «وَاسْأَلْ» يا محمد «بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ» تبكيتاً. The opening parenthesis before سَلْ is missing, so the interpolated address يا محمد — which is Niasse's gloss, not Qurʾān — has been marked "p" and the lemma split around it. Also إِسْرَاءِيلَ for إِسْرَائِيلَ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (سَلْ) يا محمد (بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ) تبكيتا (Q. 2:211).

problems.issue: مِنْ بَعْدٍ for مِنْ بَعْدِ (the muḍāf given tanwīn, which the construction forbids) and جَاءَتُهُ for جَاءَتْهُ (sukūn read as ḍamma). Vowelling only; the consonantal skeleton is intact. Restored.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُ) (Q. 2:211). Vowelling only; the English is unaffected.

problems.issue: The opening of the lemma has largely collapsed: إِّ الَهُ for فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ — the fāʾ gone, إِنَّ reduced to a bare alif with a shadda, and the two lāms of الله resolved to one. A stray space follows the opening parenthesis. Restored and not marked illegible, because the tail شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ is intact and unique to this position in Q. 2:211, and the gloss له that follows belongs to the Jalālayn treatment of that clause.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ) له (Q. 2:211) — “then Allah is severe in punishment — for him.”

problems.issue: The same lemma of Q. 2:212 is damaged differently on each of its two appearances. زُيِّرَ and زُّيِّسَ for زُيِّنَ (the nūn read first as a rāʾ, then as a sīn, and a shadda misplaced onto the zāy); كَبَرُوا and كَبَرْوا for كَفَرُوا (the fāʾ read as a bāʾ both times — كبروا would mean “they grew old,” which the sabab al-nuzūl rules out); لِلذِينَ for لِلَّذِينَ (shadda lost) in both. Restored: the occasion of revelation Niasse gives (the Meccan unbelievers mocking Bilāl, ʿAmmār and Ṣuhayb) is the standard one for زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا, and the next chunk opens with أهل مكة followed by the lemma الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا, continuing the same āya.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) … «زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا» (Q. 2:212).

problems.issue: The paragraph stops at من, mid-genitive. This is the printed edition's pagination, not OCR damage: the following chunk (¶17) opens أهل مكة, completing the phrase. Translated to the point where the transcription stops, with nothing supplied — the English ends “— of”.
problems.conjecture: No conjecture needed: the continuation is من أهل مكة, “of the people of Mecca,” and is carried by ¶17. Noted so that the press joins the two paragraphs rather than reading a lacuna.

problems.issue: The paragraph opens mid-gloss. The preceding chunk (L06c04, ¶16) ends with «زُّيِّسَ لِلذِينَ كَبَرْوا» من, so أهل مكة here completes من أهل مكة, the Jalālayn gloss on زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا. Translated from where it begins, with nothing supplied. Within the lemma: ٱلْحَيَوةَ for الْحَيَاةُ (wāw for the alif of حياة, and the nominative of the muṣḥaf — الحياة is the subject of زُيِّنَ — written as an accusative); الدَّنْيا for الدُّنْيَا. The parenthesis is never closed, so the boundary between lemma and gloss rests on Jalālayn, where بالتمويه فأحبوها is the gloss.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ... من أهل مكة (الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا) بالتمويه فأحبوها. Orthographic and bracketing only; the English is unaffected.

problems.arabic: كانوا يحبون الدنيا ويروهًا كل شيء
problems.issue: ويروهًا is not a word: the nūn of يرونها has been lost and a tanwīn fatḥ left over the hāʾ. Restored rather than marked illegible, because the clause has only one construction (يرونها كل شيء, two accusatives after رأى) and the sense follows directly from يحبون الدنيا.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: كانوا يحبون الدنيا ويرونها كل شيء, “they used to love this world and to see it as everything.”

problems.issue: Three defects in one short lemma from Q. 2:212: صَ for مِنَ (the mīm and nūn collapsed into a single letter); ألذِيسَ for الَّذِينَ, the final nūn read as a sīn, with the hamza of waṣl written as qaṭʿ; ءَامَنُوا for آمَنُوا, the madda resolved into a free-standing hamza plus alif. Restored, the āya being fixed and يسخرون من governing the preposition.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا). The nūn-to-sīn substitution recurs through this chunk (النَّبِيسنَ in ¶17, ألذِيسَ again in ¶19) and should be fixed globally.

problems.arabic: (وَ) يستهزئون بفقراء المسلمين (الذينَ إتَّقَوْا الشرك وهم هؤلاء
problems.issue: The bracketing has come apart around وَالَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا (Q. 2:212). The connective wāw is bracketed by itself as a lemma, the gloss يستهزئون بفقراء المسلمين is interposed between it and the rest of the lemma, and الشرك — Jalālayn's gloss supplying the object of اتقوا, not Qurʾān — falls inside the unclosed lemma parenthesis. وهم هؤلاء is Niasse's own aside, identifying the godfearing with the poor Muslims just named. The q/p segmentation of this stretch is therefore editorial, recovered from the Jalālayn gloss pattern rather than from the punctuation; الشرك is set as a gloss and transliterated.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَ)[يستهزئون بفقراء المسلمين](الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا) الشرك وهم هؤلاء. The printed edition probably sets the whole of وَالَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا as one lemma, with the gloss following; the page should be checked, since the English order depends on it.

problems.issue: بَوْفَهُمْ for فَوْقَهُمْ — the fāʾ read as a bāʾ and the qāf as a fāʾ, a chain of dot-errors; الْفِيَمَةٍ for الْقِيَامَةِ, with the qāf again read as fāʾ, the alif of قيامة lost, and the genitive after يوم written as tanwīn. Restored; the āya is fixed and Niasse's exposition immediately repeats يكونون فوقهم يوم القيامة in unbracketed prose.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ).

problems.arabic: الرسول صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم أتِي بخزائن الأرض ... وأهدته الملوك شرقا وغربا الأموال الطائلة
problems.issue: أتِي for أُتِيَ (the passive unvowelled, and liable to be misread as the active أتى). In وأهدته الملوك ... الأموال الطائلة the verb takes two accusatives without the usual إليه, and الملوك is given feminine singular agreement; this is oral syntax rather than OCR damage, and is translated as it stands.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: أُتِيَ بخزائن الأرض ... وأهدت إليه الملوك شرقا وغربا الأموال الطائلة. Vowelling and an ellipsis of delivery; the English (“kings east and west presented him vast wealth”) is unaffected.

problems.arabic: مات ودرعه مرهونة عند يهودي في نفقة عياله.[12]
problems.issue: A register decision, recorded for the press. Niasse gives this report in his own prose, unquoted and unbracketed, and the footnote marker [12] carries whatever attribution the edition supplies; the span is therefore tagged “p” rather than “h”, since the h register is reserved for ḥadīth and named authorities quoted verbatim. The marker is kept in place, after عياله, as in the earlier chunks.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. The note at [12] should be collated with the body of the volume's apparatus; the received report (ḥadīth of ʿĀʿisha, Bukhārī, “his coat of mail pledged with a Jew for thirty ṣāʿs of barley”) specifies the quantity, which Niasse does not.

problems.issue: A run of Q. 2:213 lemmata broken the same way three times over. جَبَعَثَ for فَبَعَثَ (fāʾ read as jīm); النَّبِيسنَ for النَّبِيِّينَ; مُبَشِّرِيرَ and وَمُنذِرِيرَ for مُبَشِّرِينَ and وَمُنذِرِينَ, the final nūn read as a rāʾ in both. The last two also lack their opening parentheses, so each stands with a closing bracket only. Restored; the āya is fixed and the glosses (من آمن بالجنة, من كفر بالنار) are Jalālayn's on these two words.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيِّينَ) إليهم (مُبَشِّرِينَ) من آمن بالجنة (وَمُنذِرِينَ) من كفر بالنار.

problems.issue: الْكِتَبَ for الْكِتَابَ (alif lost), and مَعَهُمْ for the muṣḥaf's مَعَهُمُ. The gloss that follows, الكتب, is unvowelled and looks like dittography of the lemma, but it is Jalālayn's gloss الكُتُب — the singular الكتاب of the āya read as a generic standing for the several scriptures. Translated “the books”; the press should vowel it الكُتُب so that it is not mistaken for a repetition and deleted.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَأَنزَلَ مَعَهُمُ الْكِتَابَ) الكُتُب.

problems.arabic: (كَانَ اَ۬لنَّاسُ أُمَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ) ... (لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ اَ۬لنَّاسِ فِيمَا اَ۪خْتَلَفُواْ فِيهِۖ)
problems.issue: Systemic orthographic noise rather than local damage, running through the lemmata of this chunk, and best fixed by a global pass rather than paragraph by paragraph. The Warsh-tradition hamza of waṣl over the alif of the article is transcribed as a free-standing sign: U+06EC ARABIC ROUNDED HIGH STOP WITH FILLED CENTRE in اَ۬لنَّاسُ and اُ۬لذِينَ, and U+06EA ARABIC EMPTY CENTRE LOW STOP in اَ۪خْتَلَفُواْ (4 and 2 occurrences). Tanwīn is set with U+08F0 ARABIC OPEN FATHATAN (أُمَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ). Long ā is written with U+0670 SUPERSCRIPT ALEF, 21 times. U+06D6 (ṣilā) and U+06E2 survive erratically from the muṣḥaf's recitation marks. None of these readings is in doubt and no English is affected.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: normalise U+06EC and U+06EA after a vowelled alif to the plain article ال, U+08F0 to ً, and U+0670 to ا, and strip U+06D6 and U+06E2, throughout the volume — the same global pass already recommended for L06c03. The consonantal text is untouched by it.

problems.arabic: ( مسَّتهم لأس شدة الر والضَّرَاء) المرض
problems.issue: Two separate failures in one lemma run from Q. 2:214. (a) لأس is not a word: البأساء has lost its alif-lām and its final alif-hamza. (b) The lemma parenthesis has been set in the wrong place, so that it swallows the gloss on البأساء (شدة الر) and the following lemma وَالضَّرَّاء, while only المرض — the gloss on وَالضَّرَّاء — is left outside. البأساء is restored in the English because the slot is fixed: in Q. 2:214 the subject of مَسَّتْهُمُ before وَالضَّرَّاءُ can only be الْبَأْسَاءُ. The bracketing is NOT silently repaired: the runs are translated in the order the transcription gives them.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: «مَسَّتْهُمُ الْبَأْسَاءُ» شدة الفقر «وَالضَّرَّاءُ» المرض — i.e. “there touched them hardship — the severity of poverty — and affliction — illness —”. The press should reset the lemma parentheses around الْبَأْسَاءُ and وَالضَّرَّاءُ separately.

problems.issue: The gloss on الْبَأْسَاء is truncated: the second word is reduced to الر. Marked illegible rather than emended, because the wording of the gloss is not fixed — Jalālayn glosses الْبَأْسَاءُ simply as الشدة, while شدة الفقر is the gloss of the wider commentary tradition, and either could stand in the printed edition. Niasse's own expansion is not recoverable from the surviving letters.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (flagged as conjecture): شدة الفقر, “the severity of poverty”, the final ر being the ر of الفقر. Alternative: الشدة alone, following Jalālayn, with الر then being a stray. The printed page must be consulted.

problems.issue: The final vowel of the verb has not survived, and it carries the reading: Q. 2:214 is read both حَتَّى يَقُولَ (naṣb) and حَتَّى يَقُولُ (rafʿ). Niasse's gloss حتى قال الرسول (perfect) resolves it — he is reading the rafʿ, on which the clause reports a completed saying — so the English keeps the present in the lemma and the past in the gloss, as the transcription has them. Also الرَّسُول for الرَّسُولُ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (حَتَّىٰ يَقُولُ الرَّسُولُ), with the rafʿ, since the gloss قال presupposes it. Vowelling only; the English is unaffected.

problems.issue: الذِيرَ for الَّذِينَ — the nūn read as a rāʾ, and the shadda and vowelling lost. Restored rather than marked illegible: the lemma is fixed (Q. 2:214) and the following gloss استبطاء للنصر, which Jalālayn attaches to this clause, depends on it. A stray space precedes the closing parenthesis.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَالَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا مَعَهُ). Orthographic only.

problems.issue: وَلَى for وَلَنْ — the nūn of the negative particle lost, leaving a final yāʾ. Restored rather than marked illegible, because the quotation is fixed scripture and is completed at the head of ¶22 (اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا). The quotation is also marked with double quotation marks rather than the lemma parentheses used elsewhere in the paragraph; it is Qurʾān, so it is tagged "q".
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: "وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا". Orthographic only; the English “and you will never find, for the way of Allah, any alteration” follows the restored reading.

problems.arabic: هذه سنة اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى "وَلَى تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ / اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا"
problems.issue: The citation is ambiguous, not damaged: وَلَن تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا stands word for word at both Q. 33:62 and Q. 48:23, and the transcription gives no reference. Q. 33:62 is printed here because its first half (سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ فِي الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِن قَبْلُ) answers the الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِن قَبْلِكُم of Q. 2:214, which is the āya Niasse is glossing.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: Q. 33:62, on the strength of the خلوا من قبل parallel. The press should verify against the printed edition's own reference, since Q. 48:23 is textually indistinguishable.

problems.arabic: فوجد فيه (بسم اللّٰه سر على بركة اللّٰه حتى تأتي بطن نخلة - محل بين الطائف ومكة - فإذا لقيت عير قريش فلعلك تأتينا منهم بخير[18]
problems.issue: Bracketing damage, with a consequence for the register markup. The parenthesis opened at بسم اللّٰه is never closed, so the whole of the letter's text, Niasse's parenthetical gloss on Baṭn Nakhla, and the sentence that follows all stand inside it. The content is not Qurʾān — it is the Prophet's written instruction — so it is tagged "h" and not "q", and the interposed gloss محل بين الطائف ومكة is tagged "p" and set off with dashes. The quotation is therefore closed in the English after بخير, where footnote [18] stands.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the parenthesis should close after بخير, and the aside محل بين الطائف ومكة should be set in the dashes the transcription already gives it rather than inside the quotation. Only بسم اللّٰه is given, not the full basmala, so the fixed rendering of the full formula is not used.

problems.issue: عمرابن for عمرو بن — the wāw of عمرو is lost and the name has run into ابن with no space. Restored: the man is ʿAmr b. al-Ḥaḍramī, named as Ibn al-Ḥaḍramī at the end of ¶22, and the shooter is Wāqid b. ʿAbdallāh, to whom the edition's footnote [19] is keyed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فرمى واقدٌ عمرَو بنَ الحضرمي. Word-division and one letter only.

problems.issue: The paragraph breaks off mid-clause at the printed page break, with the verb standing without its subject: فرّ is third-person masculine singular, which in Arabic VSO order can govern a following plural subject (فرّ الباقون) just as well as a singular one. The subject falls in the next chunk, so the number of the English pronoun cannot be read off the verb, and “[they]” is supplied editorially in brackets rather than guessed at as “he”.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وفرّ الباقون or وفرّ بقيتهم, “and the rest fled” — on the standard report the caravan's men scattered, one being taken captive. Flagged as a conjecture: the continuation must be read from the following page before the bracket is resolved.

problems.arabic: نوفل وأسروا عثمان بن عبد اللّه والحكم بن كيسان
problems.issue: The paragraph opens mid-sentence on a bare name, نوفل, with the clause that governed it lost at the printed page break. The two captives are named correctly for the raid at Nakhla that occasions Q. 2:217 (ʿUthmān b. ʿAbdallāh b. al-Mughīra and al-Ḥakam b. Kaysān), so the missing clause reported the fate of the remaining two men of the caravan. Translated from نوفل, with nothing supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the lost clause named the killing of ʿAmr b. al-Ḥaḍramī and the escape of Nawfal b. ʿAbdallāh — e.g. فقتلوا عمرو بن الحضرمي وأفلت نوفل — the sariyya's leader being ʿAbdallāh b. Jaḥsh. The press should recover the sentence from the printed page; in a closed English text the name alone will read as a fragment.

problems.issue: Two damaged words in one clause. بعبرين is not a word: بعيرين, “two camels,” with the yāʾ read as a bāʾ — the commonest substitution in this transcription. المير lacks the tāʾ marbūṭa of الميرة, “provisions,” the standard term for a supply caravan's load. Both restored and translated (“two camels and much provision”), since بعبرين admits no other reading and كثيرا من requires a mass noun.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وغنموا بعيرين وكثيرا من الميرة. If the printed page reads العير rather than الميرة the sense would be “much of the caravan,” which the reports of Nakhla would also support; the page should be checked.

problems.arabic: صار يستحل الأشهر الحرم وحرّمَ اللهِ تبارك وتعالى
problems.issue: وحرّمَ اللهِ cannot stand as pointed: a verb حرّم with a genitive اللهِ after it yields no construction. The genitive marks an iḍāfa, and the parallel clause two lines above — تقاتل في أرض الحرم وفي الأشهر الحرم — fixes the reading as وحَرَمَ اللهِ, “and the Sanctuary of Allah,” the second object of يستحل. Restored; the shadda is spurious.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: صار يستحل الأشهر الحرم وحَرَمَ اللهِ تبارك وتعالى.

problems.arabic: فقال النبي صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم ما أمرّهم بالقتال في الأشهر الحرم
problems.issue: أمرّهم carries a spurious shadda for أمرهم. The larger difficulty is person: قال introduces speech, but the verb is third person, so the sentence reads as Niasse's report rather than as the Prophet's words. Translated as it stands (“said: he had not commanded them to fight”) and kept in the “p” register without quotation marks, since marking it “h” would assert a verbatim quotation the Arabic does not give.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما أمرتهم بالقتال في الأشهر الحرم, “I did not command them to fight in the sacred months,” which would move the clause to the “h” register with quotation marks. To be settled against the printed page.

problems.issue: The lemma is corrupt in every letter but one: فِيَالِ for قِتَالٍ (qāf read as fāʾ, tāʾ as yāʾ) and مِيةِ for فِيهِ (fāʾ as mīm, final hāʾ as tāʾ marbūṭa) — all three substitutions are documented elsewhere in this chunk. Restored rather than marked illegible, because Niasse's own gloss بدل identifies the words as the badal of الشهر الحرام in Q. 2:217, which can only be قتالٍ فيه, and because he quotes the same words again in the next clause.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: «قِتَالٍ فِيهِ» بدل. Translated “fighting in it — a substitution [for ‘the sacred month’] —”.

problems.issue: فُلْ for قُلْ and فِتَالٌ for قِتَالٌ — the qāf-to-fāʾ substitution again. كَبِير lacks its tanwīn. Restored; Q. 2:217 is fixed and the gloss عظيم follows. The parenthesis is never closed, so the boundary between كبير and the gloss عظيم is editorial.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (قُلْ قِتَالٌ فِيهِ كَبِيرٌ) عظيم. كبير is rendered “great” and the gloss عظيم “enormous” throughout this chunk, and أكبر / أعظم وزرا as “greater” / “more enormous in sin,” so that the Jalālayn's intensification survives in English.

problems.issue: كُبْرَبِهِ for كُفْرٌ بِهِ: the fāʾ read as a bāʾ and the word boundary lost. Restored — Niasse's own gloss repeats the word (وكفر بالله تبارك وتعالى), which fixes the reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَكُفْرٌ بِهِ) وكفر بالله تبارك وتعالى.

problems.issue: الْمِتْنَةُ for الْفِتْنَةُ — the fāʾ-to-mīm substitution, as at مِيةِ. Restored. ألْقَتْلِ writes the hamza of waṣl as a hamza of qaṭʿ, a systematic habit of this transcription. الفتنة is rendered “sedition,” following the translation of the same word at Q. 2:191 in L05, with Niasse's gloss الشرك منكم carried separately as “polytheism on your part.”
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَالْفِتْنَةُ) الشرك منكم (أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ) لكم. Orthographic only; the rendering of الفتنة is a volume-wide consistency matter rather than a defect.

problems.issue: Three damaged words in the closing lemma run of Q. 2:217: يُفَتِلُونَكُمْ for يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ (qāf as fāʾ, the alif of the third form lost); عَى for عَن (the nūn lost), the same loss as at عَى دِينِهِ in ¶26; إسْتَطَعُوا for اسْتَطَاعُوا (the alif of the stem lost, the hamza of waṣl written as qaṭʿ). دِينِكُمُ is mis-vowelled for دِينِكُمْ. All restored, the āya being fixed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَلَا يَزَالُونَ) ... (يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ) ... (حَتَّىٰ يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَن دِينِكُمْ) إلى الكفر (إِنِ اسْتَطَاعُوا). Vowelling and letter restoration; the English is unaffected.

problems.arabic: (عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) دينه الذي هو عملهم هم
problems.issue: دينه is the Jalālayn gloss on سبيل الله, but الذي هو عملهم هم is Niasse's own addition and its antecedent is unclear: grammatically الذي attaches to دينه (“His religion, which is their own doing”), which makes no sense, while the sense requires it to reach back over the gloss to الصد — the barring is what the Quraysh themselves do. Translated as it stands, with the emphatic هم kept (“which is their own doing, theirs”).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the referent is الصد, i.e. وَصَدٌّ ... الذي هو عملهم هم, “and a barring — which is their own doing.” No emendation proposed; a note in the English edition would serve better than a silent repair.

problems.arabic: (وَصَدُّ) ... (وَ) صد عن (وَالْمَسْجِدِ اِ۬لْحَرَامِ وَإِخْرَاجُ أَهْلِهِۦ مِنْهُ)
problems.issue: Systemic bracketing damage, as in the chunks already translated: the lemma parentheses open and are mostly never closed, so the boundary between āya and gloss has to be recovered from the Jalālayn pattern. Here the isolated (وَ) is the Jalālayn's device for carrying the conjunction, with صد عن supplied as gloss, after which the lemma repeats the wāw (وَالْمَسْجِدِ) — so the wāw stands twice. The segmentation in the output follows the Jalālayn. وَصَدُّ also lacks its tanwīn (وَصَدٌّ), and أَهْلِهِۦ carries the small yāʾ of the Warsh orthography.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَصَدٌّ) منع الناس (عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) ... (وَ) صد عن (الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَإِخْرَاجُ أَهْلِهِ مِنْهُ). A whole-volume bracketing pass is advisable. The footnote marker [20] stands at من القتال في الحرم[20]; its note text is not in this chunk.

problems.issue: الصباة is the Quraysh's name for the Muslims — the plural of صابئ used in the sense of those who have left their ancestral religion. No English word carries it, so it is left transliterated in the “i” register with a bracketed gloss (“you ṣubāh [renegades]”). The Quraysh's two speeches in this paragraph are kept in the “p” register without quotation marks: the speakers are unnamed, so they are neither ḥadīth nor a named authority, and the “h” register would overstate them — the same decision as for اتق الله spoken to ʿUmar in L06c03 ¶11.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. If the press prefers quotation marks for reported speech generally, this paragraph and the parallel passages in the earlier files should be re-tagged together.

problems.arabic: المسلمين الذين بمكة ... والمومنون الذين معه ... (عِندَ ألَّهِ)
problems.issue: Recurrent orthographic damage, listed once for the chunk: المومنون and المومنين for المؤمنون / المؤمنين, the hamza unwritten (also أيها الصباة, أوطائهم in ¶30); ألَّهِ for اللَّهِ; and the hamza of waṣl written as a hamza of qaṭʿ in ألْقَتْلِ, أَلنَّارِ (¶29), اِ۬لشَّهْرِ, اِ۬لْحَرَامِ. None affects the English.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: a global normalisation pass — restore the hamza of المؤمنون, normalise اَ۬ل and أل to ال, as recommended for L06c03.

problems.issue: The paragraph opens mid-clause on منا, “from us,” whose governing noun fell at the printed page break: a feminine or masculine singular subject of لا يزول is required, and nothing in ¶24 can supply it, since ¶24 ends on the lemma إن استطعوا. Translated from where it starts, with nothing invented; the English accordingly opens in mid-sentence.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: a noun of enmity or appetite governing منا — e.g. عداؤهم منا لا يزول أبدا or طمعهم منا لا يزول أبدا, “their enmity toward us never ceases.” The printed page should be consulted; if the clause is short, the press may wish to supply it in square brackets.

problems.issue: The first word of the paragraph is unreadable. الرَ is not Arabic and no single substitution produces it; what the lemma of Q. 2:217 requires here is وَمَنْ, reachable only through three misreadings at once (wāw as alif, mīm as lām, nūn as rāʾ).
