Marked illegible rather than emended, since the restoration would be of the relative pronoun on which the whole conditional hangs; “[whoever]” is supplied in brackets in the lemma so that the English can be read. The lemma's opening parenthesis is also absent — the paragraph begins inside a citation whose bracket is lost — and عَى stands for عَن.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَمَن يَرْتَدِدْ مِنكُمْ عَن دِينِهِ), “and whoever of you turns back from his religion.” High confidence as to sense, low as to the letters; the printed page should be checked.

problems.arabic: يُرَدِدْ ... قَيَمَتْ وَهُوَ كَامِر بَأَوْلْيِكَ عَيِطَتَ) بطلت ( أعْمَلَهَنْ)
problems.issue: Six damaged words in one lemma run from Q. 2:217: يُرَدِدْ for يَرْتَدِدْ (the tāʾ lost); قَيَمَتْ for فَيَمُتْ (fāʾ as qāf, the vowelling wrong); كَامِر for كَافِرٌ (fāʾ as mīm); بَأَوْلْيِكَ for فَأُولَٰئِكَ (fāʾ as bāʾ); عَيِطَتَ for حَبِطَتْ (ḥāʾ as ʿayn, bāʾ as yāʾ); أعْمَلَهَنْ for أَعْمَالُهُمْ (the alif of the plural lost, the mīm read as nūn). All restored: the āya is fixed, and Niasse's gloss بطلت on حبطت confirms the verb. A comma also stands inside the lemma after دِينِهِ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَمَن يَرْتَدِدْ مِنكُمْ عَن دِينِهِ فَيَمُتْ وَهُوَ كَافِرٌ فَأُولَٰئِكَ حَبِطَتْ) بطلت (أَعْمَالُهُمْ).

problems.issue: A segmentation problem rather than damage. The gloss بطلت is interposed between حبطت and its subject أعمالهم, so a register-faithful English cannot keep normal word order: the output gives “— those, there have come to nothing / — have become void — / their works,” with the verb stranded before the gloss. The awkwardness is the Arabic's, and the alternative — moving “their works” forward — would silently re-order the lemma.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. If the press sets glosses as parenthetical notes rather than inline em-dashes, this sentence should be re-cast as “those — their works have come to nothing (i.e. have become void)”, and the same treatment applied to the split lemma at L06c03 ¶10 (فحسبه ... جهنم).

problems.issue: العالحة for الصالحة — the ṣād read as ʿayn with the alif absorbed. Restored: the word is the Jalālayn's gloss on أعمالهم at the end of ¶26 (أعمالهم الصالحة), and the feminine singular agreement fits nothing else here. In the lemma, بي stands for فِي (fāʾ as bāʾ) and الدَّنْبَا for الدُّنْيَا (yāʾ as bāʾ, the vowelling wrong); وَالآخِرَة lacks its final kasra. All restored.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: الصالحة (فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ). Rendered “the righteous [ones] — in this world and the Hereafter —”, the bracketed word marking that the gloss qualifies “their works” across the paragraph break.

problems.arabic: والتقييد بالموت عليه يفيد أنه لورجع إلى الإسلام لم يبطل عمله ... وعليه الشافعي
problems.issue: لورجع is printed as one word for لو رجع. The clause is the Jalālayn's own note, whose received wording has أن المرتد لو رجع where this transcription has أنه لو رجع; translated as it stands (“that, had he returned to Islam”). التقييد بالموت عليه is the Jalālayn's technical phrase for the restriction of the ruling to one who dies in apostasy, rendered “the qualification by dying in that [state],” the bracketed word supplying what عليه points back to.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: والتقييد بالموت عليه يفيد أن المرتد لو رجع إلى الإسلام لم يبطل عمله. No emendation made. The attribution وعليه الشافعي is rendered as a separate sentence (“Al-Shāfiʿī holds this”) so that it does not read as part of the Jalālayn's reasoning.

problems.issue: The paragraph opens on the tail of a word broken across the printed page: ¶27 ends on فلما and ¶28 begins on الت, which is what remains of نزلت. Marked illegible rather than joined up, since the repair belongs to the pagination and not to the translation; the two halves should be reunited when the chunks are set as continuous text.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فلما نزلت هذه الآية فرح المسلمون, “when this āya was sent down, the Muslims rejoiced.” Certain as to sense. The same page-break breakage recurs at ¶28/¶29 (رجاء) and ¶30/¶31 (السرية).

problems.arabic: علموا أتهم بروا من النب في ملهم هذا
problems.issue: Four damaged words in one clause: أتهم for أنهم (nūn as tāʾ); بروا for بَرِئوا, the hamza unwritten; النب for الذنب (the dhāl lost); ملهم for عملهم (the ʿayn lost). Restored: بَرِئَ من الذنب is the idiom the sense requires — the āya cleared the raiders of the charge of fighting in a sacred month — and عملهم هذا refers back to the raid. Translated “they knew that they were absolved of sin in this deed of theirs.”
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: علموا أنهم بَرِئوا من الذنب في عملهم هذا. If the printed page reads بَرُّوا the clause would have to be read otherwise, but no construction with من الذنب then survives.

problems.issue: The paragraph is a single word, the direct object left stranded when the printed page broke the sentence وقسم الباقي للذين حضروا | السرية. Kept as its own numbered paragraph and translated in place (“the raiding party.”), rather than being joined to ¶30, so that the paragraph numbering continues to answer to the printed pagination.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وقسم الباقي للذين حضروا السرية, “and divided the rest among those who were present at the raiding party.” The press should reunite the halves in continuous setting; سرية is translated rather than transliterated, since Niasse uses it as a plain noun here.

problems.arabic: (لا هجرة بعد الفتح)[21] ... (رجعنا من الجهاد الأصغر إلى الجهاد الأكبر)
problems.issue: Both parenthesised spans in this paragraph are ḥadīth, not Qurʾān, so they are tagged “h” and set in double quotation marks, against the default that bracketed material is a lemma. The Companions' question الضرب بالسيوف هو الجهاد الأصغر؟ and the answer نعم are also tagged “h”: the speakers are unnamed, but the exchange is part of the report Niasse is quoting, which is the ḥadīth register itself rather than the quotation of a named authority. Note the inconsistency this forces: jihād is marked “i” in Niasse's own prose but left unmarked inside the “h” runs, since splitting a quotation into “h” and “i” runs would break its quotation marks.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. The second report (رجعنا من الجهاد الأصغر) is the ḥadīth of the greater jihād, whose attribution is weak; the footnote marker [22] stands at its end and presumably discusses it, but the note text is not in this chunk. Markers [21] and [22] are rendered as in the earlier files and their notes should be keyed up when the apparatus is assembled.

problems.arabic: وهجرة من أوطان النفس من الشهوات البشرية إلى عبادة اللّٰه
problems.issue: The two من phrases stand in apposition without a conjunction — من أوطان النفس then من الشهوات البشرية — so the second specifies the first rather than coordinating with it. Kept elliptical, as the conventions require (“from the homelands of the self, from human appetites, to the worship of Allah”), with no “that is” supplied. هجرة is translated “emigration” throughout, following the earlier files, rather than transliterated.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage; an ellipsis of oral delivery. If the press prefers, the second phrase may be set as “[that is,] from human appetites.”

problems.arabic: بدليل الآية "مِسَ التَبِّيسَ وَالصِّدَيقِين وَالشَّهَدَاءِ وَالصِّلِحِينُ"
problems.issue: The most heavily damaged lemma in the chunk, from Q. 4:69: مِسَ for مِنَ (nūn as sīn); التَبِّيسَ for النَّبِيِّينَ (nūn as tāʾ, the plural ending collapsed); وَالصِّدَيقِين for وَالصِّدِّيقِينَ; وَالصِّلِحِينُ for وَالصَّالِحِينَ (the alif lost, the case ending wrong). Restored rather than marked illegible: the āya is fixed, the four nouns are recoverable in order, and Niasse's argument — ذكر الصديقين قبل الشهداء — depends on the sequence. The citation is in double quotation marks in the Arabic but is Qurʾān, so it is tagged “q” and the marks are dropped, as the conventions direct.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ وَالصِّدِّيقِينَ وَالشُّهَدَاءِ وَالصَّالِحِينَ (Q. 4:69). In the lemma الصديقين is rendered “the truthful ones,” plain English being required inside a “q” run; in Niasse's exposition the term is kept as ṣiddīq / ṣiddīqūn in the “i” register, because there he treats it as the name of a rank measured against the martyrs. The press may prefer “the veracious” in the lemma for consistency.

problems.arabic: غايته أن يفنى في ذات اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى ويكون عارفا صدّيقا
problems.issue: Three renderings recorded rather than defects. يفنى في ذات الله is translated “be annihilated in the Essence of Allah,” keeping the Sufi term's force without transliterating fanāʾ. عارفا صدّيقا is two accusative predicates in apposition with no conjunction; translated “a knower, a ṣiddīq,” the first word Englished and the second kept in the “i” register for the reason given above. غايته, used twice in ¶32–33 of the two arenas, is rendered “the utmost of his case is that,” not “his aim is,” since the contrast is between the furthest each struggle can reach.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage.

problems.arabic: إلى ما يحبه الرب جل وعلا
problems.issue: جل وعلا is not in the fixed renderings. Rendered “Majestic and Exalted,” which keeps it distinct from تبارك وتعالى (“Blessed and Exalted”) and سبحانه وتعالى (“Glorified and Exalted”), and is consistent with “Majestic is His Majesty” for جل جلاله in the earlier files.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. Recommend adding جل وعلا = “Majestic and Exalted” to the fixed renderings so that it does not drift across the volume.

problems.arabic: "وَصٍ ثَمَرَّتِ النَّخِيلِ وَالاَعْتَلبِ تَتَّخِذُونَ مِنْهُ سَكّراً وَرِزْقاً حَسَنا"
problems.issue: Q. 16:67, damaged in four places: وَصٍ for وَمِن (mīm as ṣād, the nūn collapsed into tanwīn); ثَمَرَّتِ for ثَمَرَاتِ (the alif lost, a spurious shadda); وَالاَعْتَلبِ for وَالْأَعْنَابِ (nūn as tāʾ, alif as lām); سَكّراً for سَكَرًا (a spurious shadda). Restored, the āya being fixed and its subject — the first revelation touching wine — explicit in Niasse's frame. The citation is in double quotation marks but is Qurʾān, so it is tagged “q” and the marks dropped.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: «وَمِن ثَمَرَاتِ النَّخِيلِ وَالْأَعْنَابِ تَتَّخِذُونَ مِنْهُ سَكَرًا وَرِزْقًا حَسَنًا». سكرا is rendered “an intoxicant,” which is what Niasse's argument needs (هذه الآية مدحت الخمر).

problems.arabic: هذه الآية مدحت الخمر | "سَكَراً وَرِزْفاً حَسَناً
problems.issue: The citation of Q. 16:67 is split across the page break and repeated at the head of ¶35, where رِزْفاً stands for رِزْقاً (qāf as fāʾ) and the opening quotation mark is never closed. Restored and tagged “q” in both places, with the reference given twice, since the two paragraphs will be read apart. The repetition is the text's, not an artefact.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: هذه الآية مدحت الخمر: «سَكَرًا وَرِزْقًا حَسَنًا». If the press sets ¶34–35 as continuous prose the second reference may be dropped.

problems.arabic: حتى سأل عمر ابن الخطاب رضي اللّٰه عنه رسول اللّٰه صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم يقول يا رسول اللّٰه
problems.issue: عمر ابن الخطاب is printed with the alif of ابن, normalised to “ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb” per the conventions. يقول introduces direct speech with no particle; ʿUmar's words are tagged “h” with double quotation marks, as the verbatim speech of a named authority, and his request runs on to the end of في هذا — the whole stretch from يا رسول الله to أن يبين لنا الحكم في هذا is one speech, since سل الله is repeated inside it rather than resumed by a new verb of saying.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. The same request recurs in ¶37 as اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا, addressed to Allah rather than to the Prophet; both are tagged “h”.

problems.arabic: ( وَمَنَجِعُ لِلنَّاس) ... «مَنَاجِعُ لِلنَّاس» ... (أَكْبَرُ مِن نَبْعِهِمَا) ... إن الإئم الكبير
problems.issue: Four defects: مَنَجِعُ and مَنَاجِعُ for مَنَافِعُ (fāʾ as jīm, twice, in the lemma and in its repetition); لِلنَّاس for لِلنَّاسِ; نَبْعِهِمَا for نَفْعِهِمَا (fāʾ as bāʾ), which matters because the whole clause turns on the balance of إثم against نفع; الإئم for الإثم. Also بلاكد printed as one word for بلا كدٍّ. All restored; Q. 2:219 is fixed and the Jalālayn gloss ما ينشأ عنهما من المفاسد confirms the sense.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَمَنَافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ) ... «مَنَافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ» ... (أَكْبَرُ مِن نَّفْعِهِمَا); وإصابة المال بلا كدٍّ في الميسر.

problems.arabic: بعضهم قال «مَنَاجِعُ لِلنَّاس» إنه يتناول المنافع
problems.issue: إنه يتناول المنافع is ambiguous and the ambiguity bears on the report. يتناول may be “comprises, covers” with the āya as subject — the verse allows for benefits — or “partakes of” with the drinker as subject, in which case إنه refers to the Companion who went on drinking. Translated “that it comprises the benefits,” the reading that matches the answering argument إن الإثم الكبير لا فائدة فيه, which is about what the verse implies and not about what a man does.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. The alternative rendering — “that he partakes of the benefits” — should be recorded in a note if the press wants the ambiguity visible.

problems.arabic: فلما نزلت هذه الآية شرب بعض الصحابة الخمر وتركها بعضهم ... لما نزلت شربَها قوم وامتنع آخرون
problems.issue: The same event is reported twice in one paragraph, in different words, with the second notice falling after the lemma وإثمهما أكبر من نفعهما. Both are kept, as the verbatim standard requires; the repetition is characteristic of the oral delivery and is not an artefact of transcription.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. If the printed page sets the second notice as a footnote or an editorial recapitulation, it should be marked as such; the transcription gives no indication either way.

problems.arabic: فلما حضرت صلاة المغرب قدموا واحدا منهم وهو
problems.issue: The chunk ends mid-clause on وهو, the predicate falling in the next chunk; translated to that point and no further (“they put forward one of them, and he”). قدموا واحدا منهم is elliptical for putting a man forward as prayer leader; nothing is supplied. صلاة المغرب is rendered “the sunset prayer,” following L05.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the continuation is the incident behind Q. 4:43 — the man led the prayer drunk and misrecited Sūrat al-Kāfirūn — which is the third of the four āyāt on wine Niasse announced in ¶34. The sentence should be reunited with the opening of the next chunk.

problems.issue: The chunk opens on a bare predicate. سكران has no subject here: the subject stands at the close of ¶37 in the preceding chunk (فقدموا واحدا منهم وهو), so the clause is 'they put forward one of them, and he was drunk'. Translated from where the text starts — 'drunk, and he recited' — with no beginning supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage; a chunk boundary falling mid-clause, which the printed pagination produced. If the press sets ¶37 and ¶38 continuously the English joins without repair.

problems.issue: كلا for كلها — the feminine plural suffix has dropped, exactly as كلا stands for كلهم at L06c03 ¶11. Restored: كلا with no suffix cannot serve as an apposition to اللاءات. The word اللاءات (plural of the particle لا) is left transliterated in the 'i' register and glossed in brackets, since what is at issue is the four negatives of Sūrat al-Kāfirūn (لا أعبد / لا أنتم عابدون / ولا أنا عابد / ولا أنتم عابدون), whose omission inverts the sūra into a profession of idolatry — the point of the anecdote, which an English paraphrase would lose.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وحذف اللاءات كلها. Also سورة الكافرون, left as a sūra title in the nominative; not an error.

problems.arabic: "لا تَقْرَبُواْ ألصَّلَوْةَ وَأَنتُمْ سَكَرِىٰ حَتَّىٰ تَعْلَمَواْ مَا تَقُولُونَ"
problems.issue: Three defects in the lemma from Q. 4:43: ألصَّلَوْةَ for الصَّلَاةَ, with the hamza of waṣl written as a hamza of qaṭʿ (the systematic habit of this transcription) and the older الصلوة orthography; سَكَرِىٰ for سُكَارَىٰ, the alif lost and the vowelling wrong; تَعْلَمَواْ for تَعْلَمُوا, a fatḥa where the ḍamma belongs. Restored, the āya being fixed and identifiable. The lemma is set in double quotation marks here, whereas elsewhere in Lesson 6 the edition uses parentheses and guillemets for the same purpose; tagged 'q' because the words are Qurʾān, not because of the bracketing.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): لَا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَأَنتُمْ سُكَارَىٰ حَتَّىٰ تَعْلَمُوا مَا تَقُولُونَ (Q. 4:43). Note for the press: the citation leaves Sūrat al-Baqara for Sūrat al-Nisāʾ because Niasse is narrating the stages by which wine was forbidden; it is not a misattribution.

problems.arabic: فقال عمر اللهم بيّن لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا
problems.issue: ʿUmar's invocation stands three times in close succession — at ¶37 (after Q. 2:219), here at ¶38 (before Q. 4:43), and again at ¶39 (before Q. 5:90–91). Not treated as dittography and not pruned: the three occurrences mark the three stages of the prohibition, which is the structure of the report, and the English repeats where the Arabic repeats. Set in the 'h' register with quotation marks, as the verbatim words of a named authority, following the treatment of ʿUmar's concurrence at L04c07 ¶56 and of the duʿāʾ at L05c10 ¶114.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. بيانا شافيا rendered 'a clarification that heals', keeping the medical figure of شافٍ rather than flattening it to 'a clear answer'.

problems.arabic: حرمت، وقال بعضهم: لا، حرمت في أوقات الصلاة فقط
problems.issue: ¶39 opens on the answer to فقال بعضهم: at the close of ¶38, so the first word is the content of a speech whose frame is in the previous paragraph. Translated from where it starts. The two opinions are spoken by unnamed persons (بعضهم), so they are left inside the 'p' run without quotation marks, on the principle stated at L06c03 ¶11: an unnamed speaker is neither ḥadīth nor a named authority, and the 'h' register would overstate it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage.

problems.issue: صاحبا for صاحيا — a yāʾ read as a bāʾ, the same substitution as قبل for قيل and وَبَهْلِكَ for وَيُهْلِكَ in L06c03. Restored to 'sober'. صاحبا is itself a readable word ('a companion'), so the damage is not self-evident; but the construction أصبح صاحبا ويصلي requires the antonym of the preceding ويبيت سكران, and a single dot is at stake rather than the two or more lost letters that led متكي to be marked illegible at L06c03 ¶11. The doubled أصبح is idiomatic (إذا أصبح أصبح), not dittography.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وإذا أصبح أصبح صاحيا ويصلي — 'and when morning came he came to the morning sober and prayed.' Worth a glance at the printed page, since the restoration turns on one dot.

problems.arabic: "تَأَيُّهَا ألذِيسَ ءَامَنُوَاْ ... وَالأَنصَابِ وَالأَزْلَمَ ... فَاجْتَنِبُوةُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَفْلِحُونْ ... إِنَّمَا يْرِيدُ الشَّيْطَنُ ... وَيَصَدَّكُمْ ... فَهَلَ انتُم مُنتَهَونَ"
problems.issue: Eleven defects across one lemma run from Q. 5:90–91. تَأَيُّهَا for يَٰأَيُّهَا (the yāʾ read as a tāʾ); ألذِيسَ for الَّذِينَ (nūn read as sīn, the hamza of waṣl written as qaṭʿ); ءَامَنُوَاْ for آمَنُوا; وَالأَنصَابِ for وَالْأَنصَابُ and وَالأَزْلَمَ for وَالْأَزْلَامُ, both miscased, the second having also lost its alif — they are coordinated with الْخَمْرُ and must stand in the nominative; الشَّيْطَن and الشَّيْطَنُ for الشَّيْطَانِ / الشَّيْطَانُ (the dagger alif of the muṣḥaf lost, and the first miscased); فَاجْتَنِبُوةُ for فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ, a hāʾ read as a tāʾ marbūṭa; تَفْلِحُونْ for تُفْلِحُونَ; يْرِيدُ for يُرِيدُ; وَيَصَدَّكُمْ for وَيَصُدَّكُمْ; فَهَلَ for فَهَلْ; انتُم for أَنتُم; مُنتَهَونَ for مُّنتَهُونَ. Restored throughout, the two āyāt being fixed and identifiable, and the consonantal skeleton intact.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّمَا الْخَمْرُ وَالْمَيْسِرُ وَالْأَنصَابُ وَالْأَزْلَامُ رِجْسٌ مِّنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطَانِ فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ. إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ الشَّيْطَانُ أَنْ يُوقِعَ بَيْنَكُمُ الْعَدَاوَةَ وَالْبَغْضَاءَ فِي الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْسِرِ وَيَصُدَّكُمْ عَن ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَعَنِ الصَّلَاةِ فَهَلْ أَنتُم مُّنتَهُونَ (Q. 5:90–91). The one-word gloss انتهوا that follows the lemma is Niasse reading the interrogative فَهَلْ أَنتُم مُّنتَهُونَ as a command, and is kept in the 'p' register.

problems.arabic: فقال عمر: اللهم انتهيا اللهم انتهينا
problems.issue: انتهيا for انتهينا — the nūn of the first-person plural has dropped in the first member of the pair, while the second member two words later is written correctly. Restored; انتهيا is neither a dual imperative that fits the address to Allah nor a form that governs anything here.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: اللهم انتهينا اللهم انتهينا — 'O Allah, we have ceased; O Allah, we have ceased,' the received wording of the report, which answers the gloss انتهوا immediately before.

problems.arabic: فلهذا قال علي كرم اللّٰه وجهه
problems.issue: كرم الله وجهه is not in the volume's table of fixed renderings, and no earlier chunk has it. Rendered 'may Allah ennoble his face'. Flagged because the formula is specific to ʿAlī and will recur: the choice should be fixed once for the whole volume rather than settled chunk by chunk.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. Recommend adding 'كرم الله وجهه — may Allah ennoble his face' to the fixed-renderings table, alongside رضي الله عنه.

problems.arabic: لو صب خمر في بئر وبنيت منارة عليها لا أؤذن عليها، ولو صب | في بحر
problems.issue: ʿAlī's saying is cut by the page break: the protasis begins in ¶39 and the apodosis completes in ¶40. Set in the 'h' register as the verbatim words of a named authority; the opening quotation mark stands at the end of ¶39 and the closing one at the head of ¶40, rather than closing and reopening the quotation across the paragraph boundary. لا أؤذن is rendered 'I would not give the call to prayer' instead of transliterating al-adhān, to keep a transliteration out of an 'h' run.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. If the press sets the two paragraphs continuously, the quotation closes once, after دوابي.

problems.arabic: في بحر فانكشف البحر ونبت حشيش لا أرعاه دوابي
problems.issue: لا أرعاه دوابي puts the second object before the first (أرعى زيدًا الحشيشَ is the expected order), and the pronoun of أرعاه refers back to حشيش across the intervening verb. Translated as it stands — 'I would not pasture my beasts on it' — with nothing supplied. فانكشف البحر is rendered 'the sea were laid bare' rather than 'receded', keeping the figure of كشف.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage; a feature of oral delivery. The received wording of the saying is ولو صب في بحر ثم جمد ونبت فيه الكلأ ما رعيته, which the press may wish to cite in the apparatus at footnote [24].

problems.arabic: قال جبريل للرسول صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم إن اللّٰه مدح أربع خصال في جعفر الطيار
problems.issue: Jibrīl's words are unbracketed and function as narrative dialogue carrying the story forward, so they are left in the 'p' register without quotation marks, following the practice at L04c07 ¶56, where the Prophet's own utterances were set in 'h' and his interlocutors' replies kept in 'p'. Recorded because the speaker here is an angel bearing revelation, which could be argued either way.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. If the press prefers every named speaker in 'h', this run and the parallel ones in ¶42 and ¶45 should be re-tagged together.

problems.arabic: (ما أربع خصال مدحها اللّٰه فيك في الجاهلية؟ قال: والله يا رسول اللّٰه ... دناءة.
problems.issue: The parenthesis opens before the Prophet's question and is never closed; it encloses the question, the narrative frame قال:, and the whole of Jaʿfar's answer. Because the material is a report and not Qurʾān, it is tagged 'h' and not 'q', on the rule that bracket content counts as 'q' only when it is actually Qurʾān. The frame قال: is set in 'p' between two 'h' runs — matching the handling of 'He said to him:' at L06c03 ¶11 and L04c07 ¶56 — even though it falls inside the parenthesis in the Arabic.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the printed edition closes the parenthesis after دناءة and the closing bracket has been lost; the same loss of closing brackets runs through the whole of Lesson 6. A whole-volume bracketing pass is advisable.

problems.arabic: والثالث ما زنيت قط في الجاهلية لأتي غيور
problems.issue: لأتي for لأني — a nūn read as a tāʾ, the same substitution as ألذِيسَ for الَّذِينَ in ¶39 and وَالتَّسْلَ for وَالنَّسْلَ at L06c03 ¶10. Restored: لأني is written correctly three times in this same paragraph (لأني أحوج, لأني رأيته, لأني رأيت), which settles it. غيور is rendered 'a jealous man' rather than transliterated, since the word is doing ordinary work here and not functioning as a technical term.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لأني غيور.

problems.arabic: أنا ما شربت الخمر قط ... والثاني ... والثالث ... والرابع
problems.issue: The enumeration is defective: the second, third and fourth traits are numbered, but the first is introduced by the bare pronoun أنا instead of الأول. Translated as it stands, with nothing supplied, since the sequence remains clear from the three numerals that follow.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: أنا [الأول] ما شربت الخمر قط, or الأول ما شربت الخمر قط. An ellipsis of oral delivery rather than OCR damage; no English is affected.

problems.issue: Five footnote markers fall in this chunk, at the ends of sentences in ¶39, ¶40 (twice), ¶41 and ¶45, and all are retained in place in the English. None of the note texts appears here: unlike L06c03 ¶12, this chunk carries no interposed footnote matter, so the markers run unanswered. The marker in ¶40 is followed in the Arabic by a space and a comma (دوابي[24] ،), which has been normalised.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. Notes [23]–[27] are to be recovered from the page feet of the printed volume and keyed to these markers; [24] should carry the source for ʿAlī's saying and [25] the source for the Jaʿfar report.

problems.issue: A consistency matter for the volume rather than a defect. الجاهلية is rendered 'the Jāhiliyya' inside the 'p' and 'h' runs, following L05c10 ¶118, rather than being set apart in the 'i' register as sharīʿa was at L04c01 ¶14. The two practices are in tension across the files already translated.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: none needed. Recommend that proper-noun period names such as al-Jāhiliyya stay in 'p', and that 'i' be reserved for technical vocabulary and untranslated common nouns; a single pass over the earlier files would settle it.

problems.issue: The opening bracket of the lemma has been replaced by an asterisk, and only the closing parenthesis survives. No run is emitted for the asterisk, since it carries no text; the lemma boundary has been recovered from the Jalālayn gloss pattern instead. يُنِعِفُونَ for يُنفِقُونَ — the fāʾ read as an ʿayn, with a spurious kasra. وَيَسْئَلُونَكَ for وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ is an orthographic variant, not damage.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنفِقُونَ) — Q. 2:219. The asterisk is most likely a page-marker or reference artefact standing where the opening parenthesis was.

problems.arabic: (فَلِ) لهم انفقوا (الْعَجْوَ) أي الفاضل عن الحاجة
problems.issue: Two damaged lemmata. فَلِ for قُلِ — a qāf read as a fāʾ and the ḍamma flattened to a fatḥa; فَلِ yields no construction with the gloss that follows, and the Jalālayn unit here is «قُلِ» أنفقوا «الْعَفْوَ» أي الفاضل عن الحاجة. الْعَجْوَ for الْعَفْوَ — a fāʾ read as a jīm, the dot moving from above the tooth to below it. That same substitution recurs twice in ¶46 (تَجْلِحُونَ for تُفْلِحُونَ, تَتَجَكَّرُونَ for تَتَفَكَّرُونَ) and once more as وَاجْعَلُواْ for وَافْعَلُوا, so it is systematic in this chunk rather than local. Both restored.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (قُلِ) لهم انفقوا (الْعَفْوَ) أي الفاضل عن الحاجة. A global fix for the chunk: wherever a ج stands in a Qurʾānic lemma and yields no word, read ف.

problems.arabic: (بداً بنفسك ثم يمن تعول أفضل الصدقة ما كان عن ظهر غنى)
problems.issue: Two defects, and a structural point. بداً for ابدأ — the initial alif of the imperative lost and the hamza written as a tanwīn; يمن for بمن — a bāʾ read as a yāʾ, the mirror of the صاحبا defect in ¶39. Restored, the received wording of the ḥadīth being ابدأ بنفسك ثم بمن تعول. Structurally, two separate reports have been run together inside one parenthesis with no separation — ابدأ بنفسك ثم بمن تعول and أفضل الصدقة ما كان عن ظهر غنى; the English marks the join with a full stop but keeps them in a single 'h' run, as the edition sets them.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (ابدأ بنفسك ثم بمن تعول. أفضل الصدقة ما كان عن ظهر غنى). عن ظهر غنى is rendered 'out of a surplus of wealth'; the idiom is 'from the back of riches', i.e. from what is left once one's own needs are met, which is also the sense of الفاضل عن الحاجة in the gloss just above.

problems.arabic: قال عمر فوافق مالا عندي وافق أني وجدت ثمانية آلاف دينار
problems.issue: وافق is repeated asyndetically, the second occurrence restating the first in more exact terms. Translated as it stands, with both clauses kept and joined by a semicolon; nothing is compressed. ʿUmar's narration from here to his oath in ¶45 is first-person reported speech introduced by قال عمر, and is kept in the 'p' register, with only the discrete weighty utterances inside it — the Prophet's two sayings, Abū Bakr's two answers and ʿUmar's closing oath — raised to 'h'. This follows L04c07 ¶56, where a long stretch of reported dialogue stayed in 'p'.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage; self-correction in oral delivery. If the press prefers the whole of ʿUmar's narration in 'h', the inner utterances will need single quotation marks, and ¶42–¶45 must be re-tagged as one unit.

problems.arabic: جاء يسبقني إلي أو بر اليوم أن أب أب، أ ب لا ين
problems.issue: This paragraph is substantially destroyed, and is the worst damage in the chunk. Only جاء يسبقني إلي and اليوم survive as words; أو بر is a mutilated name, and أن أب أب، أ ب لا ين is letter-debris with no recoverable word boundaries. The two damaged stretches are marked illegible in place and the order of what survives is kept, with no rearrangement. إلي for إليه is restored silently in the English as 'to it', since يسبقني إلي ('outstrips me to me') is not a construction; the governing verb of ¶44 (fa-akhadhtu, 'so I took') has been lost inside this damage, which is why ¶44 opens on a bare object, نصف ما عندي من المال.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (reconstructed from the received report and from the surviving letters): [كل خير] جاء يسبقني إليه أبو بكر، [فقلت:] اليوم [أسبق] أب[ا بكر، فأخذت] — 'Every good deed, Abū Bakr came and outstripped me to it. So I said: today I shall outstrip Abū Bakr. So I took half of the property I had.' أو بر is read as the wreck of أبو بكر (the bāʾ of أبو and the kāf of بكر lost), and أب أب / أ ب as the wreck of أبا بكر, repeated. لا ين is not accounted for; it may belong to أسبق or to a word now wholly lost. Not adopted: this paragraph should be reset from the printed page before the volume goes to press, since no English can be trusted here.

problems.arabic: نصف ما عندي من المال وجئت به إلى الرسول
problems.issue: ¶44 opens on a direct object with no verb, the verb having been lost in the damage of ¶43. Translated from where it starts, with nothing invented. أربعة ... وأربعة stands for أربعة آلاف ... وأربعة آلاف, the counted noun elided after ثمانية آلاف دينار in the preceding clause; '[thousand]' is supplied in brackets at the first occurrence only, as the Arabic elides it at both.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: [فأخذت] نصف ما عندي من المال — 'so I took half of the property I had.' See the entry at ¶43.

problems.issue: Unvowelled, ما تبقي admits both تُبقي ('what are you keeping back?') and تَبقى ('what remains?'). Read as تُبقي, the fourth form, which Abū Bakr's answer يكفيهم الله ورسوله requires: the question is what he has retained, not what is left over. بينكما ما بين كلمتيكما is rendered literally — 'Between the two of you is what lies between your two sayings' — rather than paraphrased as a comparison of rank, since the Arabic states the measure and leaves the application to the hearer.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ما تُبقي لعيالك؟ Vowelling only.

problems.arabic: وكان أبو بكر الغالب عليه حال المعرفة، وعمر ... الشريعة، وعثمان ... الطريقة، وعليٌّ الغالب عليه | الحقيقة
problems.issue: The fourfold scheme is cut by the page break: ʿAlī's predicate, الحقيقة, is the first word of ¶46, so ¶45 ends on 'and in ʿAlī what predominated was the' and ¶46 opens on 'ḥaqīqa'. The four terms are left transliterated in the 'i' register, following sharīʿa at L04c01 ¶14; they name the standard fourfold ascent and an English equivalent ('law', 'path', 'reality', 'gnosis') would prejudge Niasse's use of them. الغالب عليه is rendered 'what predominated in him was', repeated at each member as the Arabic repeats.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no damage. A volume-wide decision is wanted on whether maʿrifa, sharīʿa, ṭarīqa and ḥaqīqa are transliterated throughout; this chunk assumes they are.

problems.arabic: وتجد الناس متفاوتين، تحد هذا كاملا من هذا الوجه
problems.issue: تحد for تجد — a jīm read as a ḥāʾ, the dot lost. Restored: تحد ('you delimit') takes no construction here, and تجد is written correctly immediately before and four times after.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: تجد هذا كاملا من هذا الوجه.

problems.arabic: فتح اللّٰه عليه في الصلاة وم يفتح عليه في الصيام
problems.issue: م is not a word: the negative particle has been truncated, the same defect as at L06c03 ¶11. Restored. ولم يفتح is written correctly four times in the lines that follow, which fixes the reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ولم يفتح عليه في الصيام (the lām lost). فتح الله عليه is rendered 'Allah has opened upon him', keeping the idiom of futūḥ rather than resolving it to 'granted him success'.

problems.arabic: فالزم ذلك الياب فقط تجد الخير
problems.issue: الياب for الباب — a bāʾ read as a yāʾ, the third instance of that substitution in this chunk (with صاحبا in ¶39 and يمن in ¶41). Restored: الياب is not a word, and باب is written correctly two lines above, at يكون هو بابه.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فالزم ذلك الباب فقط تجد الخير — 'keep to that door alone and you will find the good.'

problems.issue: Two instances of the fāʾ-to-jīm substitution in a single lemma from Q. 22:77: وَاجْعَلُواْ for وَافْعَلُوا and تَجْلِحُونَ for تُفْلِحُونَ. Restored; واجعلوا الخير corresponds to no āya, and لعلكم تفلحون is fixed. The quotation mark opens before the lemma and is never closed, so the boundary between the lemma and the following وكَذَلِكَ is editorial.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): "وَافْعَلُوا الْخَيْرَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ" — Q. 22:77. Rendered 'And do good, that you may prosper', following لعلكم تفلحون at L05c10 ¶118.

problems.arabic: وكَذَلِكَ ) كما بين لكم ما ذكر { يُبَيِّ ألَهَ لَكُمُ الأَيْتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَجَكَّرُونَ
problems.issue: The bracketing has broken down entirely across the close of Q. 2:219. وكَذَلِكَ carries a closing parenthesis with no opening one; the next lemma opens with a brace that is never closed; and three words inside it are damaged — يُبَيِّ for يُبَيِّنُ (the nūn lost), ألَهَ for اللَّهُ (one lām lost, and miscased: it is the subject of يبين and must be nominative), and تَتَجَكَّرُونَ for تَتَفَكَّرُونَ, the fāʾ-to-jīm substitution a third time. الأَيْتِ for الْآيَاتِ is the muṣḥaf's dagger-alif orthography, not damage, and its case is correct. All restored. The wāw of وكَذَلِكَ is kept and rendered 'And thus': it is Niasse's connective, not part of the āya, which begins كَذَٰلِكَ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (كَذَلِكَ) كما بين لكم ما ذكر (يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآيَاتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ) — Q. 2:219. Rendered 'Thus does Allah make clear to you the signs, that you may reflect', following كذلك يبين الله at L05c10 ¶118.

problems.issue: The chunk ends on two letter-fragments with no recoverable word boundaries, cut by the printed pagination. Marked illegible; nothing is read into them. Both are truncations, not whole words: فِ carries a kasra and so is not the preposition as written, and أم stands outside any bracket.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فِ[ي] أم[رِ] — the opening of the Jalālayn unit on Q. 2:220, whose shape is «فِي» أمرِ «الدُّنْيَا وَالآخِرَةِ», a lemma followed by the one-word gloss أمر followed by a second lemma. The next chunk (L06c09 ¶47) opens on exactly that second lemma, (الدُّنْيَا وَالآخِرَةِ), which makes the reconstruction near-certain: 'in' — the matter of — 'this world and the Hereafter'. Not adopted here, since the surviving letters cannot carry it; the press should restore it from the printed page and join ¶46 to ¶47.

problems.arabic: اللّه بين كل آية ليكون العبد متفكرا في جميع الأحوال
problems.issue: Not OCR damage but a recorded reading: بين is unvowelled, and could be read as the verb بَيَّنَ ("He made clear") or as the preposition بين ("between"). The lemma being glossed is «كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآيَاتِ» (Q. 2:219), and the Jalālayn gloss فتأخذون بالأصلح لكم فيهما follows in the same breath, so the verb is taken. The paragraph also closes with two dots (..), the edition's ellipsis leading into the verse quoted at ¶48–49.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: اللهُ بَيَّنَ كلَّ آيةٍ, "Allah has made every sign clear." Read as "between every āya" the clause does not construe with ليكون العبد متفكرا.

problems.arabic: [ وفي كل شيء له آية / تدل على أنه واحد ]
problems.issue: The printed edition sets this verse in its own square brackets, the opening bracket falling in ¶48 and the closing one in ¶49 because the transcription follows the pagination. The brackets are not reproduced in the English: square brackets are reserved by these conventions for the translator's editorial additions, and the verse is marked instead as a quoted authority (register "h", double quotation marks), opening in ¶48 and closing in ¶49 so that the page break is preserved. The line is the well-known hemistich pair ascribed to Abū al-ʿAtāhiya; Niasse quotes it without attribution and none has been supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (presentation only, no change of sense): the press may prefer to set the two half-lines as a single verse citation across the page break, or to restore the edition's brackets with a note that they are the edition's own.

problems.arabic: وما في الجنة من شيء حمن
problems.issue: حمن is not a word. The span is marked illegible rather than emended because nothing in the sentence pins the reading: the clause would construe with any of several adjectives, and the choice changes what is being promised. The rest of the clause is translated as it stands.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: حسن, i.e. ... من شيء حسن, "and of whatever lovely thing is in the Garden" — the sīn read as a mīm, a substitution this OCR makes elsewhere (cf. ¶52 الْيَتَابِى). The printed page should be checked; a reading حَسَن fits the parallel with شيئا جميلا earlier in the sentence.

problems.arabic: "إِنَّ ألذِينَ يَاكْلُونَ أَمْوَلَ اليَتَمِى ظَلْماً إِنَّمَا يَاكُلُونَ فِي بُطَونِهِمْ نَاراً وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيرًا
problems.issue: The citation of Q. 4:10 is damaged at several points — ألذِينَ for الَّذِينَ (the hamza carried onto the article), يَاكْلُونَ / يَاكُلُونَ for يَأْكُلُونَ (loss of hamza), بُطَونِهِمْ for بُطُونِهِمْ (vowelling) — and the opening double quotation mark with which the edition marks the citation has no closing mate: the quotation runs on without interruption into شكوا من أمر اليتامى. Restored rather than marked illegible, since the consonantal skeleton is complete and Q. 4:10 is fixed; the English closes the citation before شكوا, where the sense requires it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: «إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوَالَ الْيَتَامَى ظُلْمًا إِنَّمَا يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ نَارًا وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيرًا» (Q. 4:10), with the closing quotation mark supplied after سَعِيرًا. Orthography and punctuation only; the sense is unaffected. أَمْوَلَ and اليَتَمِى are the edition's muṣḥaf rasm, not errors.

problems.issue: الْيَتَابِى for الْيَتَامَى — the mīm read as a bāʾ. Restored rather than marked illegible: the same lemma stands undamaged at the head of ¶51, and Q. 2:220 is fixed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: «وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْيَتَامَى». Orthography only.

problems.issue: Three consonantal substitutions, all restored because the Qurʾānic text is fixed and Niasse's own glosses pin the readings. بَإِخْوَانُكُمْ for فَإِخْوَانُكُمْ (fāʾ read as bāʾ); الْمَبْسِدَ for الْمُفْسِدَ (the same fāʾ/bāʾ substitution, with the gloss لأموالهم عند المخالطة and the following من قصد الإفساد fixing "the one who corrupts"); بشحريم for بتحريم (tāʾ read as shīn), where the gloss on «لَأَعْنَتَكُمْ» requires "by forbidding the mingling" — a prohibition, not any other act.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَإِخْوَانُكُمْ), (وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْمُفْسِدَ), بتحريم المخالطة. The English follows the restored readings.

problems.issue: صَ for مِنَ: the whole word reduced to a single letter. Restored rather than marked illegible on three grounds — Q. 2:220 reads «وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْمُفْسِدَ مِنَ الْمُصْلِحِ»; the construction يعلم ... من requires it; and this OCR makes the same reduction of مِن to ص again in ¶53 (خَيْرِ صِ مُشْرِكَةٍ for خَيْرٌ مِنْ مُشْرِكَةٍ), so the two occurrences confirm one another as a systematic defect of this scan rather than a reading of the printed page.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (مِنَ الْمُصْلِحِ). A search of the whole corpus for a bare ص / صِ standing between two nouns would be worth running: the substitution is likely to recur.

problems.issue: Vowelling only, with no consequence for the English: قَلِ for قُلْ, خَيْرَ for خَيْرٌ, اللَّهُ for the accusative اللَّهَ after إِنَّ, and حَكِيم unvowelled. A stray space falls inside the parentheses of ( حَكِيم ), and إِصْلَحٌ is the edition's rasm.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (قُلْ إِصْلَاحٌ لَهُمْ) ... (خَيْرٌ) ... (إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ) ... (حَكِيمٌ). Vowelling and spacing to be normalised to the edition's lemma style.

problems.issue: Presentation, recorded for the press: the paragraph opens with two lemma brackets standing side by side with no gloss between them, the first in guillemets and the second in parentheses. Both are Qurʾān and both belong to Q. 2:220, so they are given as a single "q" run and a full stop has been supplied between them — the one piece of punctuation in this chunk that is not in the Arabic. It is not bracketed, since bracketing a full stop would be unreadable. The reference is given once, after the last lemma of the run (حَكِيم), as the conventions direct, and not after this opening re-citation.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: none needed — no damage beyond the الْيَتَابِى noted above. The edition's mixing of guillemets and parentheses for lemmata within one paragraph should be normalised to one style.

problems.arabic: فإنه رب لكمة خير اليتيم من لقمة حلوة أكلها
problems.issue: خير اليتيم lacks the lām of the dative: with رُبَّ لَكْمَةٍ as subject the predicate must be خَيْرٌ لِلْيَتِيمِ. Restored rather than marked illegible because مِن لقمة immediately following makes خير a comparative and so fixes the construction. The wordplay لَكْمَة / لُقْمَة (blow / morsel) is Niasse's and is kept in the English as "blow" against "morsel".
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فإنه ربَّ لَكْمَةٍ خيرٌ لليتيمِ من لُقْمَةٍ حلوةٍ أكلها, "for many a blow is better for the orphan than a sweet morsel he has eaten."

problems.issue: الآم is not a word here. Restored rather than marked illegible because the antithesis is explicit two clauses earlier — فلا حرج في ذلك ولا إثم — so the man who strikes the orphan only for his weakness is the one who does incur إثم. The candidate readings (الآثم, الظالم) agree in sense, so the restoration does not turn the clause.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فذلك هو الآثم, "that one is the sinner" — the thāʾ dropped. الظالم would give "the wrongdoer"; either way the English stands.

problems.arabic: سبِب فروطا كان واحد من الصحابة تزوج بأمة
problems.issue: سبِب فروطا does not construe. سبِب is plainly سبب, but فروطا answers to no word that fits after it, and the phrase carries the whole function of introducing what follows as an occasion-of-revelation report. Marked illegible rather than emended because the candidate restorations differ graphically from فروطا and from one another, and because a wrong restoration here would misattribute a genre label to Niasse.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: سبب نزولها or سبب ورودها, "the occasion of its revelation" / "the occasion of its coming down" — ورودها the closer graphic match (wāw read as fāʾ, dāl as ṭāʾ, final hāʾ lost). The printed page should be checked.

problems.arabic: وحذيفة بن اليمان كلافما كان يملك أمة
problems.issue: كلافما for كلاهما — the hāʾ read as a fāʾ followed by a mīm. Restored rather than marked illegible: two men have just been named (ʿAbd Allāh b. Rawāḥa and Ḥudhayfa b. al-Yamān), and كلاهما is the only word that fits both the skeleton and the sense. Note that the sentence is loose as printed — it opens with كان واحد من الصحابة, "one of the Companions," and then names two; the English keeps the looseness rather than mending it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: كلاهما كان يملك أمة, "both of them owned a slave woman."

problems.arabic: (وَلَا تَنْكِحُواْ أُلْمَشْرِكَتِ حَتَّىٰ يَومِنَّ ) ... (وَلا تَنكِحْوا الْمُشْرِكِّتِ) ... (حَتَّىٰ يُومِنُّ) ... (وَلَامَةٌ مُومِنَةٌ خَيْرِ صِ مُشْرِكَةٍ) ... (وَلَوْ اعْجَبَتْكُمْ))
problems.issue: Q. 2:221 is cited twice and damaged at both citations, in every case by loss of hamza or by vowelling: أُلْمَشْرِكَتِ and الْمُشْرِكِّتِ for الْمُشْرِكَاتِ, يَومِنَّ and يُومِنُّ for يُؤْمِنَّ, وَلَامَةٌ مُومِنَةٌ for وَلَأَمَةٌ مُؤْمِنَةٌ, اعْجَبَتْكُمْ for أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ. Restored, Q. 2:221 being fixed. The last lemma closes with a doubled parenthesis, and a stray space precedes the closing parenthesis of the first citation. For خَيْرِ صِ مُشْرِكَةٍ see the ¶52 entry on صَ for مِنَ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: «وَلَا تَنْكِحُوا الْمُشْرِكَاتِ حَتَّىٰ يُؤْمِنَّ ۚ وَلَأَمَةٌ مُؤْمِنَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ مُشْرِكَةٍ وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ». Orthography, vowelling and bracketing only; the English is unaffected.

problems.issue: بآة for بآية. Restored: the āya meant is quoted immediately, at the head of ¶54, so the reading is pinned by what follows.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: بآية, "by the āya" — the yāʾ lost.

problems.issue: These words do not stand together anywhere in the Qurʾān: Q. 5:5 has «وَالْمُحْصَنَاتُ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ» and, earlier in the same verse, «وَطَعَامُ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ حِلٌّ لَكُمْ». The citation is the conflated form in which Jalālayn gives it at Q. 2:221, and Niasse reproduces it from there; the edition's own description — التي نزلت في آخر سورة نزلت, "sent down in the last sūra to be sent down" — identifies it as al-Māʾida and so confirms Q. 5:5. Translated as cited rather than corrected to the muṣḥaf, with the reference given as "cf. Q. 5:5" so that the press is not made to vouch for a verse in that form. الذِينَ for الَّذِينَ is vowelling only.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the lemma to be left as Niasse cites it, with the reference as cf. Q. 5:5 and, if the press wants it, a footnote recording the conflation and its source in Jalālayn ad Q. 2:221.

problems.arabic: من أراد أن يتروج فليختر مسلمة مؤمنة
problems.issue: يتروج for يتزوج — the zāʾ read as a rāʾ. Restored: فليختر مسلمة مؤمنة admits of no other verb.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: من أراد أن يتزوج, "whoever wishes to marry."

problems.issue: Not damage but the page break: the ḥadīth is cut after the second of its four terms, so the parenthesis in which the edition sets it never closes and the English quotation mark is likewise left open. Nothing has been supplied — the remaining two terms fall in the next chunk.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the ḥadīth continues ولجمالها ولدينها, "and for her beauty, and for her religion," with the closing parenthesis falling in the following chunk; the run should be joined to its continuation before typesetting.

problems.issue: A closing parenthesis with no opener in this chunk: the hadīth «تنكح المرأة لأربع» opens inside ¶54, at the foot of the previous printed page, and closes here. The footnote marker [31] is set hard against the parenthesis with no space. Not OCR damage proper; bracketing across the page break.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the hadīth should be bracketed continuously from ¶54 (تنكح المرأة لأربع … تربت يداك). Rendered as a hadīth continued from ¶54, with no opening quotation mark; the press should set the footnote marker after a space.

problems.issue: كلا cannot stand after الرجال: neither كِلا (“both”) nor كلا (“no”) construes. Unlike the damaged Qurʾānic lemmata elsewhere in this chunk, no fixed text and no gloss constrains the reading, so the span is marked illegible rather than emended.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وخطبها الرجال كلهم, i.e. “and all the men sought her hand” — the terminal هم lost. The sense is secured by فخطبها الرجال من كل النواحي earlier in the same paragraph; the press should check the printed page.

problems.arabic: (حَتَّىٰ يُومِنُواْ وَلَعَبْدٌ مُومِنِّ خَيْرصِّ مُشْرِكِ وَلَوَ اعْجَبَكُمْ
problems.issue: Five damaged words in one lemma run from Q. 2:221. يُومِنُواْ for يُؤمِنُوا and مُومِنِّ for مُؤمِنٌ — the hamza written as a plain wāw, a systematic habit of this transcription. خَيْرصِّ is two words run together, خَيْرٌ مِنْ, the nūn-mīm ligature read as a ṣād. مُشرِكِ has lost its tanwīn, and وَلَوَ اعْجَبَكُمْ has lost the hamza of أَعْجَبَكُمْ. The parenthesis opened at حَتَّىٰ is never closed; the gloss لماله وجماله follows unmarked. Restored, the āya being fixed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (حَتَّىٰ يُؤمِنُوا وَلَعَبْدٌ مُؤمِنٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ مُشرِكٍ وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَكُمْ). The emphatic lām of وَلَعَبْدٌ is carried in the English by “certainly”.

problems.issue: أَوْلَبِكَ for أُولَٰٰئِكَ — the seat of the hamza read as a bāʾ and the long alif lost. Restored; Q. 2:221 is fixed and the gloss أهل الشرك identifies the referent.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (أُولَٰئِكَ). Orthography only; the English is unaffected.

problems.issue: أَلنَّارِ and ألْجَنَّةِ write the hamza of waṣl as a hamza of qaṭʿ — the same systematic habit noted for this transcription in earlier chunks.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: إِلَى النَّارِ and إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ. Orthography only.

problems.issue: The lemma والله يدعو has lost its opening parenthesis but keeps its closing one, so the run reads as though وَاللَهُ belonged to the preceding gloss فلا تليق مناكحتهم. يَدْعُواْ also carries an otiose alif.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَاللَّهُ يَدْعُو). The English treats والله يدعو as lemma and على لسان رسله as gloss, with Jalālayn.

problems.issue: بإِذْنِهُ، — the vowelling of the pronoun is wrong (بِإِذْنِهِ) and an Arabic comma has been pulled inside the lemma parenthesis.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (بِإِذْنِهِ). Vowelling and punctuation only.

problems.issue: وَيَسْلُونَكَ for وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ — the hamza-seat lost. Restored; the lemma recurs intact at the head of ¶56.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْمَحِيضِ) (Q. 2:222).

problems.arabic: وبعضهم لا بتجنب المرأة وقت حيضها
problems.issue: بتجنب for يتجنب — the yāʾ read as a bāʾ, the commonest single error in this transcription. Without the restoration لا بتجنب does not construe. Restored: the clause sits in antithesis to يعتزلونها، يخرجونها من البيت and supplies the reason for the question put to the Prophet.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وبعضهم لا يتجنب المرأة وقت حيضها, i.e. “and some of them did not avoid the woman at the time of her menstruation.”

problems.issue: الْمَجِيضِ for الْمَحِيضِ — the ḥāʾ read as a jīm. The lemma is also bracketed with « » here and with ( ) in ¶55, within the same lemma run.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: «وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْمَحِيضِ». Bracketing to be normalised to the edition's lemma parentheses.

problems.issue: فُلْ for قُلْ — the qāf read as a fāʾ (one dot lost). Restored; Q. 2:222 is fixed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (قُلْ هُوَ).

problems.issue: فاعْتَرِلواْ for فَاعْتَزِلُوا — the zāʾ read as a rāʾ — and النسَاءَ without its article vowelled. The opening parenthesis is never closed: the gloss أي اتركوا وطأهن runs on inside it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَاعْتَزِلُوا النِّسَاءَ) أي اتركوا وطءهن.

problems.issue: فيِ for فِي (the kasra under the yāʾ rather than the fāʾ), and ٱلمحيض with a waṣla sign and no final kasra.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فِي الْمَحِيضِ). Vowelling only.

problems.issue: The lemma تَقْرَبُوهُنَّ opens in ¶57 as (وَلا and closes here, with the closing parenthesis detached as its own token after a space. Bracketing across the page break; no damage to the words.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَلا تَقْرَبُوهُنَّ). Translated continuously across the ¶57/¶58 break.

problems.issue: يَظْهَرْنَ for يَطْهُرْنَ — ṭāʾ read as ẓāʾ — and يعتسلن for يغتسلن, the ghayn read as an ʿayn. Both restored: the āya is fixed and the Jalālayn gloss on يطهرن is يغتسلن بعد انقطاعه.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (حَتَّىٰ يَطْهُرْنَ) يغتسلن بعد انقطاعه.

problems.issue: The worst-damaged lemma in the chunk: three of its words are corrupt and it is bracketed with an opening brace that never closes. جَإِذَا for فَإِذَا (fāʾ read as jīm); تَطَهَرْسَ for تَطَهَّرْنَ (final nūn read as sīn); بَاتُوهَرَّه for فَأْتُوهُنَّ. Restored rather than marked illegible: Q. 2:222 is fixed, and the gloss that follows, بالجماع, is the Jalālayn gloss on فأتوهن and so fixes the verb.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: {فَإِذَا تَطَهَّرْنَ فَأْتُوهُنَّ} بالجماع. Bracing to be normalised to the edition's lemma parentheses.

problems.issue: حَيْثَ for حَيْثُ, and أَمَرَكُمْ اللَّهُ for أَمَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ. The closing parenthesis is doubled.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ). Vowelling and bracketing only.

problems.arabic: رِنَّ ألَهَ يُجِبُّ ي يثيب ويكرم * التَوَبِينَ)
problems.issue: رِنَّ ألَهَ يُجِبُّ for إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ (alif read as rāʾ, the lām-lām collapsed, ḥāʾ read as jīm), and التَوَبِينَ for التَّوَّابِينَ. The lemma has no opening parenthesis, and two stray glyphs sit inside the gloss: a bare ي before يثيب ويكرم and an asterisk after it. Restored; the āya is fixed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ) يثيب ويكرم (التَّوَّابِينَ). The stray ي and * are compositor's noise and are not translated.

problems.issue: الأقدار (“measures, fates”) for الأقذار (“filth”) — the dhāl read as a dāl. Restored: من الأقدار is not a possible gloss on المتطهرين, and Jalālayn reads من الأقذار.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: من الأقذار, “from filth” — answering من الذنوب in the preceding gloss.

problems.arabic: عن لك ال نَوْكُمْ) أزواجكم حَرْتُ لَكُمْ )
problems.issue: The whole paragraph — a single printed line — is damaged at three points. عن لك for عن ذلك; ال نَوْكُمْ) for (نِسَاءُكُمْ), the opening parenthesis read as ال and the sīn-alif-hamza lost; and حَرْتُ for حَرْثٌ, with a detached closing parenthesis after it. Restored rather than marked illegible: this is a verbatim re-citation of نِسَاءُكُمْ حَرْثٌ لَكُمْ (Q. 2:223), which stands intact at the end of ¶58, and the gloss أزواجكم fixes the first word.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: عن ذلك (نِسَاءُكُمْ) أزواجكم (حَرْثٌ لَكُمْ).

problems.issue: جَاتُواْ for فَأْتُوا (fāʾ read as jīm, hamza lost); the lemma has lost both parentheses. The particle introducing the gloss stands as a bare و where the sense requires أي, so “that is” is supplied in square brackets in the English rather than silently restored.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَأْتُوا حَرْثَكُمْ) أي محله وهو القبل, with Jalālayn (أي محل حرثكم وهو القبل).

problems.issue: أَنَبى شٍتُمُ for أَنَّىٰ شِئْتُمْ — the shadda read as a bāʾ and the hamza-seat of شِئْتُمْ lost. Restored: Q. 2:223 is fixed and the gloss opening ¶61, كيف شئتم, is the Jalālayn gloss on أنّى شئتم.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (أَنَّىٰ شِئْتُمْ).

problems.issue: لَانْجُسِكُمْ for لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ — the fāʾ read as a jīm and the hamza lost — and وَقَدّمُواْ for وَقَدِّمُوا. The footnote marker [32] has been set inside the lemma parenthesis, before the first word, where it belongs after يفعل; the opening parenthesis is followed by a space. Restored; the āya is fixed and the lemma recurs at the head of ¶63.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: يفعل[32] (وَقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ). The marker is rendered after “used to do”.

problems.arabic: بسم اللّٰه الرحمن الرحيم اللهم جنبنا الشيطان وجنب الشيطان ما رزقتنا[33]،
problems.issue: The duʿāʾ is unbracketed in the transcription, so that the basmala and اللهم جنبنا الشيطان run on from Niasse's own prose without a mark of quotation; the footnote marker [33] is set hard against رزقتنا and before the comma. No letters are damaged.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the formula should be set off as a quoted hadīth text (اللهم جنبنا الشيطان وجنب الشيطان ما رزقتنا)[33]. It is marked as hadīth in the English.

problems.issue: لَا نْجُيكُمْ for لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ — the word is broken across a space, the fāʾ read as a jīm and the sīn as a yāʾ. The same word is damaged differently in ¶61, which confirms that the corruption is the transcription's and not the edition's.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: «وَقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ».

problems.issue: اللَّةَ for اللَّهَ — the final hāʾ read as a tāʾ marbūṭa.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ). Orthography only.

problems.issue: وَاعْلَمَوْاْ for وَاعْلَمُوا and مَلَقَوه for مُلَاقُوهُ — the long alif of the active participle lost. Restored; Q. 2:223 is fixed and the gloss بالبعث fixes the sense.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ مُلَاقُوهُ).

problems.issue: وَتَقْرِ for وَبَشِّرِ — the worst single-word distortion in the chunk; the bāʾ-shīn-rāʾ skeleton has been read as tāʾ-qāf-rāʾ. Also الْمَومِنِينَ for الْمُؤمِنِينَ. Restored rather than marked illegible: Niasse's own gloss بشرهم بالجنة names the verb, and the āya is fixed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤمِنِينَ) الذين اتقوا بشرهم بالجنة.

problems.arabic: (وَلا تَجْعَلُواْ أَللَّهِ) الحلف باللّه (عَرْضَةٌ) علة مانعة (لَا يْمَنِكُمْ أَن تَبَرَّوا) أن لا تبروا (وَتَتَّقُوأ)
problems.issue: Four damaged words across the lemma run of Q. 2:224. أَللَّهِ for اللَّهَ (hamza of qaṭʿ for hamza of waṣl, and the wrong case ending); عَرْضَةٌ for عُرْضَةً; لَا يْمَنِكُمْ for لِأَيْمَانِكُمْ, broken across a space with the long alif lost; and وَتَتَّقُوأ for وَتَتَّقُوا, the otiose alif written as a hamza. Restored; the āya is fixed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَلا تَجْعَلُوا اللَّهَ) (عُرْضَةً) (لِأَيْمَانِكُمْ أَنْ تَبَرُّوا) (وَتَتَّقُوا). Note that the gloss on أن تبروا is Niasse's own, أن لا تبروا — the oath as a barrier to doing good — and is translated as it stands.

problems.arabic: لا تجعلوا الحلف علة تنعكم من أن تفعلوا البر
problems.issue: تنعكم for تمنعكم — the mīm lost. Restored: the same verb stands intact a few words earlier in منعني الحلف.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لا تجعلوا الحلف علة تمنعكم من أن تفعلوا البر.

problems.issue: النَّاس and سَمِيعُ + عَلِيمٌ have lost their case endings, and the lemma parenthesis runs from وَتُصْلِحُواْ straight through وَاللهُ سَمِيعُ without a break, so that the closing words of Q. 2:224 are bracketed as one lemma.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَتُصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ النَّاسِ) (وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ) لأقوالكم (عَلِيمٌ). Case endings and bracketing only.

problems.arabic: أرادوا الرجوع إلى الجماع بعد اليمين[34]
problems.issue: The paragraph opens mid-gloss and the lemma it glosses is not on this page. The words gloss «فَإِن فَاءُوا» of Q. 2:226 (Jalālayn: فإن فاءوا — رجعوا عن اليمين بالوطء), so the Arabic as it stands lacks the conditional that governs أرادوا. No damage: the break is the printed pagination. Translated from where it starts, with no beginning supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the preceding page ends «فَإِن فَاءُوا» followed by the gloss of which this clause is the tail. The press should confirm against the previous page that nothing is lost between the pages.

problems.issue: Three defects in one lemma. (1) جَإِلَّ is not a word: the fāʾ of فَإِنَّ has been read as a jīm and the nūn-shadda resolved as a lām-shadda. (2) رَجِيمُ for رَحِيمٌ — ḥāʾ read as jīm; as it stands the word means 'accursed', the exact opposite of the divine name. (3) At the re-quotation the same word appears as رَحِيمُم, with a stray mīm for the tanwīn. The run is also unclosed: it opens with ( and never closes. Restored rather than marked illegible, because the lemma is fixed by the muṣḥaf and because Niasse's two following glosses are keyed word by word to غفور and رحيم.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ), Q. 2:226, and «رَحِيمٌ» بهم at the re-quotation. Orthographic only; the English is unaffected.

problems.arabic: والأشدية التي يقول الفقهاء أنا ما عرفتها
problems.issue: الأشدية is not a term I can identify, and the feminine-singular pronoun of عرفتها treats it as a collective, so the ending is not merely OCR noise. It stands in a sentence rejecting a juristic doctrine of oath, and getting the word wrong would misreport what Niasse rejects, so the span is marked illegible rather than emended. The rest of the sentence (أنا ما عرفتها, colloquial for لا أعرفها) is translated as it stands.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture, offered as a conjecture only: al-ashdiya, i.e. the intensified or reinforced forms of oath (from شدّ) that the jurists distinguish in the chapter on īlāʾ — this fits the context, since Niasse has just said that the four-month rule 'holds in every kind of oath'. A second possibility is a corruption of الأسئلة ('the questions the jurists raise'); الأشهر ('the months') is ruled out by the preceding sentences, which affirm the four months. The press should read the printed page.

problems.issue: ألطَّلَقَ for الطَّلَاقَ: the alif of the article carries a stray hamza and the alif of the second syllable is lost. Restored, the lemma being fixed (Q. 2:227).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَإِنْ عَزَمُوا الطَّلَاقَ). Orthographic only.

problems.issue: The Q. 2:228 lemma chain is damaged throughout: الْمُطَلَّفَتُ for الْمُطَلَّقَاتُ (qāf read as fāʾ); يَتَرَبَّصْ for يَتَرَبَّصْنَ (the nūn of the feminine plural lost, leaving a jussive that has no subject); بِأَنفُسهَِّ for بِأَنفُسِهِنَّ, with the vowel marks displaced onto the hāʾ; فَرْوَءِ for قُرُوءٍ (again qāf read as fāʾ, and the wāw misvocalised). Restored rather than marked illegible: the verse is fixed, and Niasse's gloss (حاضت وطهرت, three times over) confirms both يتربصن and قروء.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَالْمُطَلَّقَاتُ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ) ... (بِأَنفُسِهِنَّ) ... (ثَلَاثَةَ قُرُوءٍ). Orthographic only. Note that قروء is rendered neutrally as 'courses' in the lemma and left untransliterated as qurūʾ in Niasse's closing clause, since his gloss commits him to the menstruation reading without his saying so.

problems.arabic: من الولد أو الحيض هواد طرّ يَومِنَّ بالّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرٌ
problems.issue: هواد طرّ is not Arabic. It stands exactly where the conditional governing يؤمنّ must stand, and the lemma that follows has lost its opening bracket (the run closes with ) after وَبُعُولَتْهَرَّ, so the edition's bracketing cannot be used to locate the lemma's start). Marked illegible rather than emended, because supplying the conditional changes the force of the clause from a statement to a condition. يَومِنَّ for يُؤْمِنَّ and الآخِرٌ for الْآخِرِ are ordinary orthographic damage and are restored; the lemma is Q. 2:228.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: من الولد أو الحيض (إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ), i.e. 'if they believe in Allah and the Last Day' — this is the Jalālayn lemma at this point, and هواد طرّ is most plausibly إن كنّ, with the kāf-nūn-shadda misread. The press should read the printed page; if the conjecture holds, the English clause takes 'if' and the illegible marker comes out.

problems.arabic: (وَبُعُولَتْهَرَّ ) ... (أحَوُّ بِرَدِّهِىَ » ... (وَلَهْرَّ ) ... مِثْلَ ألذِى عَلَيْهِنَّ ) ... (بِالْمَعْرُوب) ... (وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيْهِنَّ دَرَجَةً)
problems.issue: The Q. 2:228 lemma chain is damaged at every feminine plural suffix and at two word-stems. وَبُعُولَتْهَرَّ and وَلَهْرَّ for وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ and وَلَهُنَّ: the nūn-shadda has been read as a rāʾ-shadda throughout, which is the single most frequent defect in this chunk. أحَوُّ for أَحَقُّ (qāf read as wāw) and بِرَدِّهِىَ for بِرَدِّهِنَّ. مِثْلَ for مِثْلُ and ألذِى for الَّذِي. بِالْمَعْرُوب for بِالْمَعْرُوفِ (final fāʾ read as bāʾ). دَرَجَةً for دَرَجَةٌ. Brackets are also mismatched: the أحق run opens with ( and closes with »), and the مثل الذي run has a closing bracket with no opening one. All restored rather than marked illegible: the verse is fixed, and each gloss is keyed to the word it follows.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ) ... (أَحَقُّ بِرَدِّهِنَّ) ... (وَلَهُنَّ) ... (مِثْلُ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِنَّ) ... (بِالْمَعْرُوفِ) ... (وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيْهِنَّ دَرَجَةٌ). Orthographic and bracketing only; the English is unaffected. Bracketing to be normalised to the edition's lemma parentheses.

problems.issue: ي ذَلِكَ for في ذلك — the fāʾ is lost. The deeper problem is the bracketing: في ذلك is not in Q. 2:228 at all; it is the Jalālayn's own back-reference, which the printed edition has wrongly dressed as a lemma with an opening parenthesis (and no closing one). Translated as Niasse's prose, not as Qurʾān, in line with the rule that bracket content is 'q' only when it is actually Qurʾān.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: في ذلك، في زمن التربص, i.e. 'in that, [that is] in the time of waiting'. The stray parenthesis should be removed in the edition.

problems.arabic: للمرأة حق على الرحل كما أن الرجل له حق على المرأة
problems.issue: الرحل for الرجل — jīm read as ḥāʾ. Restored: the same word stands correctly twice in the immediately following clause, which is built on the symmetry of man and woman.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: للمرأة حق على الرجل. Orthographic only.

problems.arabic: فدعا اللّهَ النبيُّ صلى اللّه عي وسلم
problems.issue: عي for عليه — the lām and hāʾ are lost. Restored, the formula being fixed. Note separately for the press that the honorific is applied here to the unnamed prophet of the story, not to Muḥammad; the transcription is translated as it stands rather than corrected.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: صلى الله عليه وسلم, rendered ﷺ per the fixed renderings. Orthographic only.

problems.arabic: إذا عاشروهن وشاوروهن لحسن العشرة وخالفوهن لأنّهن ناقصات العقول.[36]
problems.issue: إذا cannot govern the three imperatives that follow (عاشروهن، شاوروهن، خالفوهن). The reading is almost certainly إذن, the tanwīn of which has been read as the alif of إذا. Restored, since the sentence is otherwise ungrammatical; it is Niasse drawing the practical conclusion from the two ḥadīths he has just quoted.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: إذن عاشروهن وشاوروهن..., i.e. 'So keep company with them and consult them...'. The English takes 'so'; the sense of the clause is unchanged either way.

problems.arabic: (ما رأيت من ناقصات عقل ودين أذهب بلب الرجل الحازم من إحداكن[35]
problems.issue: Bracketing only: the run opens with ( and is never closed, and the opening parenthesis is the edition's lemma marker, which here encloses a ḥadīth rather than Qurʾān. Marked as 'h' with quotation marks accordingly. The wording matches the canonical ḥadīth and needed no reconstruction.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the parenthesis should be closed after إحداكن and normalised to the edition's ḥadīth marker. No change to the English.

problems.arabic: فقال: اللهم الحاجة الثانية أن مسخها قِرْدة، فرجعت قردة.
problems.issue: أن مسخها will not parse: أن requires a verb, and مسخها is a maṣdar with a pronoun suffix. Either the tāʾ of the second-person verb has been lost (أن تمسخها) or the printed text has a maṣdar construction without أن. Restored on the first reading, since the sentence is a petition addressed to Allah; the English supplies 'let' in the predicate, bracketed in the Arabic apparatus only, not in the translation, because the vocative اللهم already carries it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: اللهم الحاجة الثانية أن تمسخها قردة, i.e. 'O Allah, let the second request be that You turn her into an ape.' Alternatively الحاجة الثانية مسخها قردة, with the same sense and no أن.

problems.arabic: فُفدت الحوائج كلا لم يجد شيئا لحماقة زوجته.[37]
problems.issue: Two defects. فُفدت for فُقدت — qāf read as fāʾ; the same verb stands correctly as فُقدت two clauses earlier (¶68, فُقدت حاجتان), which fixes the reading. كلا for كلها — the hāʾ of the pronoun is lost, leaving a word that would have to be read as the dual كِلا or the negative كلّا, neither of which agrees with الحوائج. Both restored: the clause is the story's closing tally and the arithmetic of the three requests settles it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فُقدت الحوائج كلها لم يجد شيئا لحماقة زوجته, i.e. 'All the requests were lost; he gained nothing, because of his wife's folly.' Orthographic only.

problems.issue: The Q. 2:229 lemma chain is damaged at three of its four words. وقَإمْسَاك: the opening parenthesis has been read as a wāw-qāf pair and the fāʾ of فَإِمْسَاكٌ is lost. يتَعْرُوب for بِمَعْرُوفٍ — the bāʾ read as a yāʾ-tāʾ pair and the final fāʾ as a bāʾ; as it stands the word is not Arabic. ياحْسَرِ for بِإِحْسَانٍ, with the alif-nūn lost and the bāʾ again read as a yāʾ; the run also has a closing bracket with no opening one. أوْ تَسْرِيحٌ is sound. All restored rather than marked illegible: the verse is fixed, and each of Niasse's glosses (من غير ضرر, إرسال لهن) is keyed to the word it follows.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَإِمْسَاكٌ) ... (بِمَعْرُوفٍ) ... (أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌ) ... (بِإِحْسَانٍ). Orthographic and bracketing only; the English is unaffected.

problems.issue: أغرى for أخرى — khāʾ read as ghayn — and the clause then runs over the page break into ¶72, whose first word أبتها is the predicate. أبتها as printed is not a word; read as أبَتَّها (from بتّ, to make final) it completes the sentence exactly: a third pronouncement makes the divorce irrevocable, which is the ruling the following lemma presupposes. Restored, and the two paragraphs are translated in place without reordering, so the clause is split across them as the printed pagination splits it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: إن زاد طلقة أخرى أبَتَّها, i.e. 'If he adds another pronouncement of divorce, he makes it irrevocable.' A less likely reading of أبتها is بَتَّها with a stray alif, with the same sense.

problems.issue: يَجِلُّ for يَحِلُّ — ḥāʾ read as jīm, as at ¶66 — and لَكْمَ for لَكُمْ, with the vowel marks displaced. The run also opens with ( and closes with "), a mismatched pair. Restored, the lemma being fixed (Q. 2:229).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ). Orthographic and bracketing only.

problems.issue: The paragraph ends on this fragment, which opens a bracket and never closes it and is cut off by the page break. Marked illegible: it could be the remains of the lemma شَيْئًا that completes «وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَأْخُذُوا مِمَّا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ شَيْئًا», or the first letters of متاع, the word Niasse uses when he paraphrases the ruling in his own words at the head of ¶73 (شيئا من متاعها). The two give different texts, so neither is supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture, offered as a conjecture only: (شَيْئاً) of Q. 2:229 is the likelier of the two, since the lemma is otherwise incomplete at exactly this point; but متاع cannot be ruled out, and the printed page should be read before either is set.

problems.issue: الاَّ for إِلَّا, with the hamza lost and a stray alif, and يِخَابَا for يَخَافَا — the fāʾ read as a bāʾ and the vowelling displaced. The run also closes a bracket it never opened. Restored, the lemma being fixed (Q. 2:229) and confirmed by the gloss الزوجان that opens ¶74 and by خافا in the paraphrase that follows it. قبل is read as the adverb closing Niasse's own sentence ('that he gave to her previously'), not as the preposition قبل introducing the lemma.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ... الذي أعطى لها قبل. (إِلَّا أَنْ يَخَافَا). Orthographic and bracketing only; the English is unaffected.

problems.arabic: (فَإِنْ خِفْتُمُۥٓ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اَ۬للَّهِ ...) إن كان.
problems.issue: The long lemma is sound (the small superscript marks of خِفْتُمُۥٓ and اَ۪فْتَدَتْ are the edition's Qurʾānic orthography, not damage) and needed no reconstruction. The paragraph then ends on إن كان, a conditional with nothing after it, cut off by the page break. Translated as it stands, 'if it was', with no apodosis supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the next page is expected to continue with the protasis's completion, something on the order of إن كان سبب الطلاق من قبلها or إن كان الخوف منهما جميعا. The press should join this clause to the opening of the following chunk before setting it.

problems.arabic: حتى تحققا أنَّهما عجرا عن إقامة حدود اللّٰه
problems.issue: عجرا is not a word: the zāy of عَجَزَا has been read as a rāʾ. Restored rather than marked illegible, because عن إقامة حدود الله fixes the verb (ʿajaza ʿan, “to be unable to”) and no other reading of the skeleton fits the construction.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: حتى تحققا أنَّهما عَجَزَا عن إقامة حدود الله. The English “they are unable to uphold Allah's limits” follows the restored reading.

problems.arabic: جاءت إحدى الصحابيات إلى الني صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم
problems.issue: الني for النبي — the bāʾ and its dot have dropped out. Restored: the honorific ﷺ immediately following fixes the referent.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم. Orthographic only.

problems.arabic: يا رسول اللّٰه أنا زوجي لا أنقم منه دينا ولا شيئا
problems.issue: أنا زوجي leaves the sentence without a predicate for أنا and without a topic marker for زوجي. Either the transcription preserves an oral anacoluthon (“I — my husband, I hold nothing against him”), which is characteristic of this commentary, or أنا is a misreading of أما, which would give the normal topic construction. Translated as it stands, with “as for me” carrying the pronoun, since the sense is unaffected either way.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: يا رسول الله أما زوجي فلا أنقم منه دينا ولا شيئا, i.e. “Messenger of Allah, as for my husband, I hold nothing against him in religion, nor in anything else.” Flagged as a conjecture; the press should check the printed page before emending, since the anacoluthon may be genuine.

problems.issue: التنتين for الثنتين — the thāʾ read as a tāʾ. Restored; the ruling (a third pronouncement of divorce following two earlier ones) fixes the numeral, and Q. 2:230 is the āya under gloss.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: الزوج بعد الثنتين, “the husband, after the two [pronouncements].”

problems.issue: غَيْرَةٌ for غَيْرَهُ — the final hāʾ of the pronoun suffix has been read as a tāʾ marbūṭa and given nominative tanwīn. Restored, the underlying āya (Q. 2:230) being fixed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (زَوْجاً غَيْرَهُ). Orthographic and vowelling only.

problems.arabic: يروى أن امرأة من الصحابة جميلةً جاءت
problems.issue: جميلةً carries accusative tanwīn where an attributive adjective following امرأة (itself governed by أن) should be accusative to agree — امرأةً … جميلةً — but امرأة is written without its tanwīn. The transcription has vowelled the adjective and not the noun. Noted for the press; the English is unaffected.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: أن امرأةً من الصحابة جميلةً جاءت. Vowelling only.

problems.arabic: لا حتى تذوقي عسيلته ويذوق عسيلتك).[40]
problems.issue: The ḥadīth closes with an unmatched ) and the footnote marker [40] outside it; no opening bracket corresponds to it anywhere in the report, which begins with the unbracketed يروى أن امرأة. The printed edition evidently bracketed the quotation and the opening mark has been lost. The quotation boundary adopted here runs from إن زوجي طلقني to ويذوق عسيلتك, and يعني الجماع that follows is treated as Niasse's own gloss, not part of the ḥadīth.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the quotation opened at (إن زوجي طلقني ثلاثا. Bracketing only; the division between ḥadīth and gloss should be checked against the printed page.

problems.arabic: فقال عمر: حضرتُ محبئكِ للرسول صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم ولابي بكر
problems.issue: محبئكِ is not a word and the span is marked illegible rather than emended. حضرتُ + a verbal noun with the second-person feminine suffix + للرسول ولأبي بكر requires something like “your coming” or “your petition,” but the restoration is not fixed by any quoted text — this is Niasse's own narration of the report — and the choice between مجيئكِ and a noun of asking (e.g. مسألتكِ) changes what ʿUmar claims to have witnessed. Left marked.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: حضرتُ مجيئكِ للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم ولأبي بكر, “I was present at your coming to the Messenger ﷺ, and to Abū Bakr.” مسألتكِ (“your petition”) is a weaker alternative. Flagged as a conjecture.

problems.issue: ولابي for ولأبي — the hamza of the alif is unwritten. This transcription treats hamza erratically throughout (compare ألنِّسَآءَ and ألَّهِ below, where a hamza of waṣl is written as one of qaṭʿ). Normalised silently in the English; recorded here so the press can regularise the Arabic.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ولأبي بكر. Orthographic only.

problems.arabic: (فَان طَلَّقَهَا ) الزوج الثاني (فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا) الزوجة والزوج الأول (أن رَجَاه)
problems.issue: (أن رَجَاه) is corrupt for (أَنْ يَتَرَاجَعَا). Restored rather than marked illegible on two grounds: Q. 2:230 is fixed and reads أَنْ يَتَرَاجَعَا at exactly this point in the run, and the gloss إلى النكاح that opens ¶78 is the Jalālayn gloss on يتراجعا and so presupposes it. فَان for فَإِنْ in the same run is the usual unwritten hamza.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَإِنْ طَلَّقَهَا) الزوج الثاني (فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا) الزوجة والزوج الأول (أَنْ يَتَرَاجَعَا). The English “that they return to one another” follows the restored reading; the stray space before the first closing parenthesis is editorial debris.

problems.arabic: (إن ظَنَّا أَن يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ألَّهِ وَتِلْكَ المذكورات (حُدُودُ اُ۬للَّهِ
problems.issue: Bracketing has broken down across the whole paragraph. Here the lemma parenthesis opens at (إن ظنا and is never closed, so وَتِلْكَ — which belongs to Q. 2:230 — stands outside any bracket, and the gloss المذكورات sits between two Qurʾānic stretches with no mark dividing them. وتلك is marked as Qurʾān in the output on the strength of the āya, not of the brackets. ألَّهِ writes the hamza of waṣl as one of qaṭʿ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (إِنْ ظَنَّا أَنْ يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ. وَتِلْكَ) المذكورات (حُدُودُ اللَّهِ يُبَيِّنُهَا لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ). Bracketing and orthography only; the register assignment follows the āya.

problems.issue: Two bāʾ-for-fāʾ substitutions in sequence — the commonest OCR fault in this transcription. (بَأَمْسِكُوهُنّ) is for (فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ) in Q. 2:231, and the gloss بَن is for بأن. Both restored: the āya is fixed, and تراجعوهن قبل انقضاء العدة is the Jalālayn gloss on فأمسكوهن.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ) بأن تراجعوهن قبل انقضاء العدة.

problems.arabic: (بِمَعْرُوبٍ) من غير ضرار (أوْ سَرِّحُوهنَّ بِمَعْرُوُما اتركوهن
