problems.issue: بِمَعْرُوبٍ and بِمَعْرُوُما are both for بِمَعْرُوفٍ (fāʾ read as bāʾ, then the word running into the following material). The Qurʾānic text is restored in both places. The residue ما after the second بمعروف cannot be accounted for: it is neither part of the āya nor a word of the gloss that follows (اتركوهن حتى تنقضي عدتهن), so that span is marked illegible rather than absorbed into either register. The closing parenthesis is missing.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (بِمَعْرُوفٍ) من غير ضرار (أَوْ سَرِّحُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ) أي اتركوهن حتى تنقضي عدتهن — the ما most likely standing for أي, which the edition uses to introduce such glosses elsewhere. Flagged as a conjecture.

problems.issue: عدئُن for عدتهن — the tāʾ and hāʾ collapsed into a single pointed form. Restored; the same gloss (قاربن انقضاء عدتهن) stands correctly earlier in the paragraph and again in ¶79, where it is damaged differently (عديهن).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: حتى تنقضي عدتهن.

problems.issue: تُمْسِكُوهُرَّ for تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ — nūn read as rāʾ, a substitution that recurs in ¶79 (يَنكِحْرَ, أَزْوَاجَهُرَّ). Restored from the fixed āya. The gloss بالرجمة is for بالرجعة: the ʿayn has been read as a mīm. Restored because the sentence that follows (لكن الرجعة للصلح فقط أما الرجعة لقصد الضرار) spells رجعة correctly twice and fixes the term; the homograph is worth flagging, since رجم (stoning) does appear in this chunk at ¶76 (لأرجمنك).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَلَا تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ) بالرجعة (ضِرَاراً), “and do not retain them — by taking [them] back — to cause harm.”

problems.arabic: (وَمَنْ يَبْعَلْ ذَلِكَ وَقَد ظَلَمَ نَبْسَةُ بتعريضها إلى عذاب اللّٰه
problems.issue: Three faults in one lemma from Q. 2:231: يَبْعَلْ for يَفْعَلْ (fāʾ as bāʾ), وَقَد for فَقَدْ (fāʾ as wāw), and نَبْسَةُ for نَفْسَهُ (fāʾ as bāʾ, hāʾ as tāʾ marbūṭa). All restored, the āya being fixed; the gloss بتعريضها (“by exposing it,” feminine, referring to النفس) independently confirms نفسه. The parenthesis is unclosed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ) بتعريضها إلى عذاب الله.

problems.issue: الْحِكْتَةِ for الْحِكْمَةِ — the mīm read as a tāʾ. Restored: Q. 2:231 is fixed, and the gloss that opens ¶79 (ما فيه من الأحكام) is the Jalālayn gloss on الحكمة.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَالْحِكْمَةِ).

problems.arabic: (وَاتَّقُواْ اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمَوْ أَ اللَّهَ بِكْلِّ شَءٍ عَلِيمٌ لا يخفى عليه شيء
problems.issue: وَاعْلَمَوْ أَ for وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ — the final alif of the verb and the shadda of أنَّ lost, with a spurious word break; بِكْلِّ for بِكُلِّ and شَءٍ for شَيْءٍ (the yāʾ dropped). All restored from the fixed āya. The parenthesis is unclosed, so the gloss لا يخفى عليه شيء falls inside the lemma run in the transcription; it is marked as Niasse's prose here.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ) لا يخفى عليه شيء.

problems.arabic: (وَإِذَا طَلَّفْتُمْ النِّسَآءَ سبب نزول هذه الآيةِ
problems.issue: طَلَّفْتُمْ for طَلَّقْتُمُ — the qāf read as a fāʾ. Restored; the same lemma is repeated correctly a few words later in the paragraph. The parenthesis is unclosed, which is why Niasse's remark on the occasion of revelation runs on directly from the lemma without a dividing mark.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَإِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ) — then the comment on the sabab al-nuzūl.

problems.issue: وامتع for وامتنع — the nūn has dropped out. Restored: the contrast with ورضيت هي (“she consented”) requires a verb of refusal, and this is the standard occasion of revelation for Q. 2:232, in which Maʿqil b. Yasār refuses to let his sister return to the husband who divorced her.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ورضيت هي وامتنع أخوها فنزلت, “and she consented, but her brother refused. So it was revealed.”

problems.issue: عديهن for عدتهن (tāʾ read as yāʾ) — restored, the identical gloss standing correctly earlier in ¶78. وباً is for فَلَا: fāʾ read as wāw and lām as bāʾ, with the alif of لا taking tanwīn. Restored on three grounds: Q. 2:232 is fixed, Niasse's own gloss لا تمنعوهن carries the negative, and the vocative أيها الأولياء presupposes the prohibition.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: قاربن انقضاء عدتهن (فَلَا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ) أيها الأولياء لا تمنعوهن.

problems.issue: Two more nūn-as-rāʾ substitutions — يَنكِحْرَ for يَنْكِحْنَ and أَزْوَاجَهُرَّ for أَزْوَاجَهُنَّ — both restored from the fixed āya. The run also opens with a doubled bracket {( where the edition's convention is a single pair; one of the two is stray.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (أَنْ يَنْكِحْنَ أَزْوَاجَهُنَّ) المطلقين لهن. The brace should be deleted.

problems.issue: The paragraph ends in an unreadable fragment and the span is marked illegible rather than emended. Its place in the run is certain — it stands where Q. 2:232 reads إِذَا تَرَاضَوْا, immediately before the lemma (بَيْنَهُم بِالْمَعْرُوفِ) that opens ¶80, and ¶80's opening gloss الأزواج والنساء glosses the subject of تراضوا. But the surviving glyphs do not map onto إذا تراضوا, so the fragment may instead be the tail of a gloss lost at the page break rather than the lemma itself. Left marked.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (إِذَا تَرَاضَوْا, “when they agree together.” Flagged as a conjecture; the press should check whether the printed page carries a gloss here as well.

problems.issue: بِالْمَعْرُوبِ for بِالْمَعْرُوفِ — the same fāʾ-as-bāʾ substitution as twice in ¶78. Restored from the fixed āya; the gloss شرعا (“according to the Law”) is the Jalālayn gloss on بالمعروف.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ) شرعا.

problems.arabic: (يُوعَظُ بِهِ، مَن كَانَ مِنكُمْ يَومَ بِاللَهِ وَالْيَوْمِ ٱلآخِرِ لأنه المنتفع به
problems.issue: يَومَ for يُؤْمِنُ — the hamza-bearing wāw and the nūn lost, leaving a form identical to يوم, which then stands absurdly beside the genuine وَالْيَوْمِ ٱلآخِرِ two words later. Restored from the fixed āya. A comma has also intruded inside the lemma after بِهِ, where the āya has no pause, and the parenthesis is unclosed, so the gloss لأنه المنتفع به runs on inside it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (يُوعَظُ بِهِ مَنْ كَانَ مِنْكُمْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ) لأنه المنتفع به. Delete the comma.

problems.issue: ذَلِكُمُوَ for ذَٰلِكُمْ — a spurious wāw with vowelling after the pronoun. أَزْكِىٰ for أَزْكَىٰ and وَأَطْهَرَ for وَأَطْهَرُ are vowelling errors only; the consonantal skeletons are intact. All normalised to the fixed āya, as is (وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمْ) for (وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ) at the end of the paragraph, where the sukūn has displaced the indicative ḍamma.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (ذَٰلِكُمْ) ترك العضل (أَزْكَىٰ) خير (لَكُمْ وَأَطْهَرُ) … (وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ). Vowelling and one spurious letter; the English is unaffected.

problems.issue: وَالْوَلِدَاتُ for وَالْوَالِدَاتُ — the alif of the second syllable has dropped out, as it does again in (وَلِدَةٌ) later in the same paragraph. The lemma parenthesis is also unclosed, so the gloss الأمهات stands inside it. يَرْضِعْرَ for يُرْضِعْنَ is the nūn-as-rāʾ substitution that runs through this transcription (compare رِزْفُهُرَّ below and تُمْسِكُوهُرَّ in ¶78). All three restored: Q. 2:233 is fixed, and the gloss ليرضعن presupposes the plural feminine verb.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَالْوَالِدَاتُ) الأمهات (يُرْضِعْنَ) أي ليرضعن. Bracketing and orthography only; the English is unaffected.

problems.issue: أَوْتَدَهُنَّ for أَوْلَادَهُنَّ — the lām read as a tāʾ and the alif of the plural lost; حَوْلَيْ for حَوْلَيْنِ — the nūn of the dual lost, exactly as in (يَتَرَبَّصْ) for يَتَرَبَّصْنَ in ¶82. Both restored from the fixed āya; the gloss عامين (“two years”) independently fixes the dual حولين, and the lemma (كَامِلَيْن) that follows agrees with it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (أَوْلَادَهُنَّ حَوْلَيْنِ) عامين.

problems.arabic: (لِمَنَ ارَادَ أَنْ يَتمَّ الرّضَعَةَ ولا زيادة عليه
problems.issue: الرّضَعَةَ for الرَّضَاعَةَ — the alif of the second syllable lost, the same fault as in الوالدات above. لِمَنَ carries a spurious fatḥa for لِمَنْ, ارَادَ leaves the hamza unwritten, and يَتمَّ is vowelled for يُتِمَّ. The parenthesis is unclosed, so the gloss ولا زيادة عليه falls inside the lemma in the transcription; it is marked as prose here on the strength of the āya.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُتِمَّ الرَّضَاعَةَ) ولا زيادة عليه. Orthography, vowelling and bracketing only.

problems.issue: Two faults in one word: رِزْفُهُرَّ for رِزْقُهُنَّ — the qāf read as a fāʾ (as in طَلَّفْتُمْ in ¶79 and بالْمَعْرَوقِ in ¶83) and the nūn as a rāʾ. Restored from the fixed āya; the gloss إطعام الوالدات (“the feeding of the mothers”) confirms رزق. The stray space before the closing parenthesis is editorial debris.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (رِزْقُهُنَّ) إطعام الوالدات.

problems.issue: بِالْمَعْرُوبُ for بِالْمَعْرُوفِ — the fāʾ read as a bāʾ, the commonest OCR fault in this transcription (compare بِمَعْرُوبٍ in ¶78 and بِالْمَعْرُوبِ in ¶80), with the final vowel wrongly nominative. Restored from the fixed āya; بقدر طاقته is the Jalālayn gloss on بالمعروف here.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (بِالْمَعْرُوفِ) بقدر طاقته.

problems.issue: وَلِدَةٌ for وَالِدَةٌ — the alif lost again. The lemma also closes with a doubled parenthesis, as (بِصَالًا)) does at the end of the paragraph; one of the two marks is stray. Restored from the fixed āya.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (لَا تُضَارَّ وَالِدَةٌ بِوَلَدِهَا). Delete the second parenthesis.

problems.arabic: بأن تكره على إرضاعه إذا امتعت
problems.issue: امتعت for امتنعت — the nūn has dropped out, the same fault as وامتع for وامتنع in ¶79. Restored: the gloss requires a verb of refusal (she is compelled to suckle only if she declines), and امتع is not a form that fits here.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: بأن تُكرَه على إرضاعه إذا امتنعت, “by being compelled to suckle him when she has refused.”

problems.issue: لَهُو for لَهُ — a spurious wāw after the pronoun, matching ذَلِكُمُوَ for ذَٰلِكُمْ in ¶80 and عَلَيْكُمُوَ elsewhere in this transcription. Restored; the same phrase stands correctly as (وَعَلَى الْمَوْلُودِ لَهُ) earlier in the paragraph.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (مَوْلُودٌ لَهُ بِوَلَدِهِ). Orthographic only.

problems.arabic: (مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ الذي على الأب للوالدة من الرزق والكسوة
problems.issue: The lemma parenthesis is unclosed, so the relative clause الذي على الأب — which is the gloss on مثل ذلك, not part of Q. 2:233 — runs on inside it. The register division adopted here follows the āya: (مِثْلُ ذَٰلِكَ) is Qurʾān, everything from الذي is gloss.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (مِثْلُ ذَٰلِكَ) الذي على الأب للوالدة من الرزق والكسوة. Bracketing only.

problems.issue: Two fāʾ-as-bāʾ substitutions frame the clause: بَإِنَ for فَإِنْ and (بِصَالًا) for (فِصَالًا). آرادًا is vowelled for أَرَادَا. Both lemmata restored from the fixed āya, and the gloss that opens ¶82 (فطاما له قبل الحولين) is the Jalālayn gloss on فصالا, which independently fixes it. The gloss الوالدان stands without the edition's usual أي, and the closing parenthesis is doubled.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَإِنْ أَرَادَا) أي الوالدان (فِصَالًا). Delete the second closing parenthesis.

problems.issue: A stray opening guillemet inside the lemma parenthesis. The edition brackets lemmata with parentheses here, and the guillemet corresponds to no closing mark anywhere in the paragraph. Treated as debris; the span is Qurʾān either way.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (مِنْهُمَا وَتَشَاوُرٍ). Delete the guillemet.

problems.issue: بَلاَ for فَلَا — fāʾ as bāʾ. Restored from the fixed āya. The parenthesis is unclosed, so the gloss في ذلك falls inside the lemma; it is marked as prose here.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا) في ذلك.

problems.issue: وَانَ for وَإِنْ — the hamza unwritten, with a spurious fatḥa; آرَدتُّمُ for أَرَدْتُمْ, with a madda on the alif and a shadda on the tāʾ that the form does not carry. Restored from the fixed āya; the gloss خطاب للآباء (“an address to the fathers”) confirms the second-person plural.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَإِنْ أَرَدْتُمْ) خطاب للآباء. Orthography and vowelling only.

problems.arabic: ( أَن تَسْتَرْضِعُوا أَوْلَدَكُمْ) مراضع غير الوالدات
problems.issue: أَوْلَدَكُمْ for أَوْلَادَكُمْ — the alif of the plural lost, as in أَوْتَدَهُنَّ in ¶81. Restored from the fixed āya. The stray space after the opening parenthesis is debris.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (أَنْ تَسْتَرْضِعُوا أَوْلَادَكُمْ) مراضع غير الوالدات.

problems.issue: Three faults in one lemma: بَلا for فَلَا (fāʾ as bāʾ, as above), جُتَاحَ for جُنَاحَ (nūn read as tāʾ, the same substitution as in جُتَاحَ/جُنَاحَ pairs elsewhere in this chunk), and عَلَيْكُمةَ for عَلَيْكُمْ with a spurious tāʾ marbūṭa. All restored: the identical formula stands correctly as (بَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا) a few words earlier and the āya is fixed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ) فيه.

problems.arabic: (مَا اَتَيْتُم) أردتم إيتاءه لهن من الأجرة
problems.issue: اَتَيْتُم for آتَيْتُمْ — the madda over the alif lost, so the form reads as أَتَيْتُمْ (“you came”) rather than آتَيْتُمْ (“you gave”). Restored: the gloss أردتم إيتاءه لهن (“what you intended to give them”) fixes the fourth-form verb, and Q. 2:233 is fixed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (مَا آتَيْتُمْ) أردتم إيتاءه لهن من الأجرة.

problems.arabic: (وَاتَّقُواْ أللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ)
problems.issue: أللَّهَ writes the hamza of waṣl as one of qaṭʿ, a fault that recurs through this transcription (ألنِّسَاءِ in ¶84, اَ۬للَّهَ and أللَّهَ in ¶85); وَاعْلَمُوْا carries a sukūn on the wāw of the plural, where the same verb appears correctly as وَاعْلَمُوٓاْ in ¶85. Normalised silently in the English; recorded here so the press can regularise the Arabic.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ). Orthography and vowelling only.

problems.issue: The opening lemma of Q. 2:234 is damaged at three points and mis-bracketed. وَالذِيسَ for وَالَّذِينَ — the nūn read as a sīn; يُتَوَقَّوْتَ for يُتَوَفَّوْنَ — the fāʾ read as a qāf and the nūn as a tāʾ. The brace { opens a lemma that is never closed, so the gloss يموتون stands inside it. All restored: the āya is fixed, and the gloss يموتون (“they die”) is the Jalālayn gloss on يتوفون and fixes the passive.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ) يموتون. The brace should be a parenthesis and the lemma closed before يموتون.

problems.issue: يَتَرَبَّصْ for يَتَرَبَّصْنَ — the nūn of the feminine plural lost, as in حَوْلَيْ for حَوْلَيْنِ in ¶81 and بَلَغْرَ in ¶83. Restored: the āya is fixed and the gloss ليتربصن carries the nūn.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (أَزْوَاجاً يَتَرَبَّصْنَ) أي ليتربصن.

problems.issue: بِأَنجُسِصَِّ for بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ. The fāʾ is read as a jīm (the same substitution as أَنْجُيهِنَ in ¶83 and أَنْجُسِكُمْ in ¶84) and the suffix هِنَّ has collapsed into a single pointed form carrying stray vowels. Restored rather than marked illegible: Q. 2:234 is fixed, the preceding lemma (أَزْوَاجاً يَتَرَبَّصْنَ) immediately precedes بأنفسهن in the āya, and the gloss بعدهم عن النكاح is the Jalālayn gloss on it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ) بعدهم عن النكاح. The damage is heavy enough that the press should collate this word against the printed page.

problems.arabic: وهذا في غير الحوامل فعدتُن أن يضعن حملهن
problems.issue: فعدتُن for فعدتهن — the hāʾ of the suffix lost, with its ḍamma transferred to the tāʾ. Restored: the sense requires the pregnant women's own waiting period, and أن يضعن حملهن that follows is third-person feminine plural.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فعدتهن أن يضعن حملهن, “their waiting period is that they deliver their burden.”

problems.issue: وَإِذَا for فَإِذَا — the fāʾ read as a wāw, as in وَقَد for فَقَدْ in ¶78; بَلَغْرَ for بَلَغْنَ — nūn as rāʾ. Both restored from the fixed āya. The English “Then when” follows the restored فإذا.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَإِذَا بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ) انقضت عدة تربصهن.

problems.arabic: أَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ جِيمَا بَعَلْتَ بِّ أَنْجُيهِنَ)
problems.issue: The worst-damaged span in the chunk: five faults in six words, and the opening parenthesis is missing so the whole lemma runs on from the preceding gloss. أَلاَ for فَلَا (fāʾ lost, hamza written in its place), جِيمَا for فِيمَا (fāʾ as jīm), بَعَلْتَ for فَعَلْنَ (fāʾ as bāʾ, nūn as tāʾ), بِّ for فِي (fāʾ as bāʾ, the yāʾ lost), أَنْجُيهِنَ for أَنْفُسِهِنَّ (fāʾ as jīm, sīn as yāʾ). Restored rather than marked illegible, because Q. 2:234 is fixed and the damaged words map onto it one for one in sequence, and because the gloss that follows (من التزين والتعرض للخطاب, “of adorning themselves and making themselves available to suitors”) is the Jalālayn gloss on فيما فعلن في أنفسهن and fixes the whole phrase.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا فَعَلْنَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِنَّ). Flagged as a conjecture despite the one-for-one mapping: the span should be collated against the printed page before it is set, and the edition may also carry the Jalālayn's أيها الأولياء after عليكم, which this transcription does not have.

problems.issue: للحطّاب for للخُطَّاب — the khāʾ has lost its dot, turning “the suitors” into “the woodcutters.” Restored, and worth flagging because the damaged form is itself a real word: التعرض (“making oneself available”) requires suitors, and خِطْبَة النِّسَاء (“proposing to the women”) is the lemma under gloss a few lines later in ¶84.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: من التزين والتعرض للخُطَّاب, “of adorning themselves and making themselves available to suitors.”

problems.issue: بالْمَعْرَوقِ for بِالْمَعْرُوفِ — the fāʾ read as a qāf, the reverse of the qāf-as-fāʾ substitution in رِزْفُهُرَّ (¶81), with the ḍamma displaced onto the rāʾ. Restored from the fixed āya; the gloss شرعا that opens ¶84 is the Jalālayn gloss on بالمعروف here.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (بِالْمَعْرُوفِ) شرعا.

problems.arabic: ( وَاله بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَيِيره عالم بباطنه كظاهره
problems.issue: وَاله for وَاللَّهُ — one lām and the shadda lost; خَيِيره for خَبِيرٌ — the bāʾ read as a yāʾ and a spurious hāʾ added where the tanwīn belongs. Both restored from the fixed close of Q. 2:234; the gloss عالم بباطنه كظاهره (“knowing its inward as He knows its outward”) is the Jalālayn gloss on خبير and fixes it against the alternative بصير. The parenthesis is unclosed, so the gloss falls inside the lemma.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ) عالم بباطنه كظاهره.

problems.arabic: ( وَلَاَ جَنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِيمَا عَرَّطْنُ لوحتم بهِ، مِنْ خِطْبَةِ ألنِّسَاءِ)
problems.issue: مِيمَا for فِيمَا — the fāʾ read as a mīm (as again in مِي for فِي below); عَرَّطْنُ for عَرَّضْتُمْ — the ḍād read as a ṭāʾ and the tāʾ-mīm of the second-person plural collapsed into a nūn, which would make the verb feminine plural and so change who is doing the hinting. Both restored from the fixed opening of Q. 2:235, and the gloss لوحتم (“you intimate”) is itself second-person plural and fixes عرضتم. Bracketing has also broken down: the single parenthesis encloses lemma, gloss and lemma together, and an intrusive comma stands after بهِ where the āya has no pause. جَنَاحَ is vowelled for جُنَاحَ and ألنِّسَاءِ writes the hamza of waṣl as one of qaṭʿ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُمْ) لوحتم (بِهِ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ النِّسَاءِ). Delete the comma; the register division in the output follows the āya rather than the brackets.

problems.issue: المتوف for المتوفى — the final yāʾ lost. Restored; the construction المتوفى عنهن أزواجهن (“those whose husbands have died”) is standard and recurs correctly in ¶88 (المتوفى عنها زوجها).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: المتوفى عنهن أزواجهن في العدة. Orthographic only.

problems.issue: Two faults: مِي for فِي (fāʾ as mīm, as in مِيمَا above) and أَنْجُسِكُمْ for أَنْفُسِكُمْ (fāʾ as jīm, as in بِأَنجُسِصَِّ in ¶82 and أَنْجُيهِنَ in ¶83). Restored from the fixed āya. The paragraph then breaks off at the preposition من, whose complement (قصد نكاحهن) opens ¶85; the English is left correspondingly open.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ) من قصد نكاحهن.

problems.issue: تَوَاعِدُوهُنَّ is vowelled for تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ and سِرَا lacks the shadda and tanwīn of سِرًّا. Vowelling only; normalised to the fixed āya. Recorded because the gloss نكاحا is doing real interpretive work here — سرّا is glossed as “marriage,” not as “secretly” in the adverbial sense — and the press will want the lemma vowelled correctly for that gloss to read.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَلَكِنْ لَا تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا) أي نكاحا.

problems.issue: The lemma closes with a doubled parenthesis, as (بِصَالًا)) and (بِوَلَدِهَا)) do in ¶81; one mark is stray. اِلَّآ carries a hamza of waṣl with a kasra and a madda where the āya has إِلَّا. Bracketing and orthography only.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (إِلَّا أَنْ تَقُولُوا قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفًا). Delete the second closing parenthesis.

problems.issue: الْكِتَبُ for الْكِتَابُ — the alif lost, as in الرّضَعَة and الوالدات in ¶81; يَبْلَغَ is vowelled for يَبْلُغَ; أَجَلَةُ for أَجَلَهُ — the hāʾ of the suffix read as a tāʾ marbūṭa and given nominative tanwīn, exactly as نَبْسَةُ for نَفْسَهُ in ¶78. All restored from the fixed āya. The first parenthesis is unclosed, so the gloss المكتوب من العدة stands inside the lemma; in the English the gloss is placed with الكتاب, which it glosses, rather than where the brackets leave it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ الْكِتَابُ) المكتوب من العدة (أَجَلَهُ) بأن ينتهي.

problems.arabic: (وَاعْلَمُوَا أَنَّ أللَّهَ يَعْلَمْ مَا قِ أَنمسكُمْ من العزم وغيره
problems.issue: مَا قِ for مَا فِي — the fāʾ read as a qāf and the yāʾ lost, leaving a bare letter; أَنمسكُمْ for أَنْفُسِكُمْ — the fāʾ read as a mīm, a third variant of the same substitution after أَنْجُسِ- and أَنْجُي-. يَعْلَمْ carries a sukūn where the indicative takes a ḍamma, وَاعْلَمُوَا a spurious fatḥa, and أللَّهَ the usual waṣl-as-qaṭʿ hamza. All restored from the fixed āya; the gloss من العزم وغيره (“of resolve and otherwise”) presupposes ما في أنفسكم. The parenthesis is unclosed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ) من العزم وغيره.

problems.issue: بَاحْذَرُوه for فَاحْذَرُوهُ — fāʾ as bāʾ, the same fault as بَأَمْسِكُوهُنّ in ¶78 and بَلاَ/بَلا in ¶82. Restored from the fixed āya; the gloss لمن يحذره two lemmata later uses the same root and confirms it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَاحْذَرُوهُ) أن يعاقبكم.

problems.issue: Not damage but a bracketing convention the press should decide on: where the edition encloses the lemmata under gloss in parentheses, it puts the Qurʾānic verses Niasse cites in his own exposition into double quotation marks instead — here Q. 2:240, and again "خُلِقَ الإنسَ مِنْ عَجَلِ" (Q. 21:37) in ¶87. Both are marked "q" in the output on the strength of the text, not of the marks, since double quotation marks are reserved in this translation for ḥadīth and quoted authorities. اُلْحَوْلِ also carries a ḍamma on the alif of waṣl.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: مَتَاعاً إِلَى الْحَوْلِ, to be set as a Qurʾānic lemma rather than in quotation marks. Flagged for a general decision, since the same convention appears in ¶87.

problems.issue: خُلقت is vowelled only on the khāʾ, leaving the person of the verb open: خُلِقْتَ (“you were created,” the angels addressing Ādam) or خُلِقْتُ (“I was created,” Ādam speaking). Translated as second person, which the preceding وقالت (the angels as subject) requires. Recorded so the press can vowel the printed form.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وقالت: لهذا خُلِقْتَ, “and they said: for this you were created.” Vowelling only.

problems.issue: The paragraph carries nothing but a full stop: the printed line was lost in transcription, as at ¶69 of Lesson 3. ¶85 breaks off mid-sentence at فلما مر and ¶87 resumes with الروح حتى بلغ ركبتيه, so the two halves of one clause survive on either side of it and nothing of the sentence itself is missing. Marked illegible; nothing supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the lost line is most likely the tail of footnote [46] (on the hundred and twenty years of Ādam's forming) carried over from the foot of the preceding page, rather than body text — the clause that straddles ¶85 and ¶87 is continuous without it. Needs collation against the printed edition.

problems.issue: الإنسَ for الْإِنْسَانُ — the alif and nūn of the final syllable lost, leaving a different Qurʾānic word (الإنس, “humankind” as against the jinn) in its place, and the case ending made accusative. عَجَلِ lacks the tanwīn of عَجَلٍ. Restored from Q. 21:37, which is fixed; the sentence Niasse draws from it (فما زال يستعجل أولاد آدم) turns on عجل as haste in the individual human being.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ (Q. 21:37).

problems.issue: بستعجل for يستعجل — the yāʾ read as a bāʾ, the mirror of the fāʾ-as-bāʾ substitutions throughout. Restored: ما زال requires a verbal predicate and بستعجل is not a form. The clause also leaves ما زال without a formal subject, أولاد آدم standing after the verb rather than before it; this is the oral syntax of the commentary and is translated as it stands.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فما زال يستعجل أولاد آدم, or, regularised, فما زال أولاد آدم يستعجلون — “and the children of Ādam have never ceased to be hasty.” The loose agreement is probably genuine and should not be emended without the printed page.

problems.arabic: وأول من قال اللّٰه أكبر إبراهيم، هي الباقيات الصالحات وأول من قال لاحول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم محمد رسول اللّٰه صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم
problems.issue: هي الباقيات الصالحات stands inside the list, between the clause on Ibrāhīm and the clause on the Prophet, where it has no antecedent: هي is feminine plural and refers to the five formulae collectively, so the clause belongs after the last of them, not between the fourth and the fifth. The transcription follows the printed pagination and a line has evidently been set out of order. Translated in place, as an interposed clause between dashes, and not moved. لاحول is also written as one word for لا حول.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: … وأول من قال لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم محمد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، هي الباقيات الصالحات — the clause closing the list, “these are the enduring righteous [deeds].” Flagged as a conjecture; the press should check the printed line order before moving it.

problems.arabic: ولاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمُوَ إِى طَلَّفْتُمُ أُلنِّسَاءَ مَا لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ)
problems.issue: The first lemma of the Q 2:236 run has a closing parenthesis after تَمَسُّوهُنَّ and no opening one, so the new āya is not marked off from the preceding prose on the waiting period. Two further points. عَلَيْكُمُوَ carries a spurious vowelled wāw after -كُمْ, the same tic that produced ذَلِكُمُوَ at ¶80 and that recurs twice in this chunk (بَرَضْتُمْ وَ at ¶91, بَيْنَكُمُ وَ at ¶92). And the initial wāw of ولا جناح is probably intrusive, carried over from Q 2:235, whose identical opening وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ Niasse glossed a few paragraphs earlier at ¶84. Translated as it stands, “And there is no blame upon you.”
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (لَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنْ طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ مَا لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ). The missing opening parenthesis is certain; the wāw is flagged as a conjecture and should be checked against the printed page and against the Warsh text, since Q 2:235 does open with it.

problems.issue: Three faults in three words, all of classes already documented for this transcription. إِى for إِنْ — the nūn has dropped out, the same loss as مِ for مِنْ at ¶91. طَلَّفْتُمُ for طَلَّقْتُمُ is the Maghribī qāf/fāʾ substitution: the printed face dots qāf above and fāʾ below, and the OCR was trained on the Mashriqī convention, so it read qāf as fāʾ. The same word is damaged the same way at ¶91 (طَلِّفْتَمُوهَنَّ). أُلنِّسَاءَ writes the hamza of waṣl as one of qaṭʿ and gives it a ḍamma. All restored from the fixed āya.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: إِنْ طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ. The English follows the restored reading.

problems.arabic: الطلاق قبل المسيس لا باس به
problems.issue: لا باس for لا بأس — the hamza is unwritten, as it is erratically throughout this transcription. Normalised silently in the English; recorded so the press can regularise the Arabic.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لا بأس به. Orthographic only.

problems.issue: ٱلْمَوبِيع is corrupt for الْمُوسِعِ in Q 2:236: the sīn has been read as a bāʾ and a yāʾ has intruded before the final ʿayn. Restored rather than marked illegible, because the āya is fixed and because Niasse's gloss الغني منكم is the Jalālayn gloss on الموسع — “the one of ample means” explained as “the wealthy among you” — which cannot gloss anything else in the verse.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (عَلَى الْمُوسِعِ) الغني منكم.

problems.issue: قَتْرَدُ is corrupt for قَدَرُهُ — the dāl read as a tāʾ and the final hāʾ as a dāl — with a stray full stop inside the parenthesis. Restored: Q 2:236 repeats قَدَرُهُ, and the first of the two stands four words earlier in this same paragraph, itself mis-vowelled as قَدْرُه. ألْمَقْتِرِ writes the hamza of waṣl as one of qaṭʿ (for الْمُقْتِرِ), and the gloss الضيق lacks the shadda of الضيّق.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (قَدَرُهُ وَعَلَى الْمُقْتِرِ) الضيّق الرزق (قَدَرُهُ). Delete the full stop.

problems.issue: بالْمَعْرُوقُ for بِالْمَعْرُوفِ — qāf for fāʾ again, with the final kasra replaced by a ḍamma. The same word is damaged the same way twice in the immediately preceding chunk (بالْمَعْرَوقِ at ¶83, بالْمَعْرُوقِ at ¶84) and as بِالْمَعْرُوبِ at ¶80. Restored from the fixed āya; the gloss شرعا that opens ¶91 is the Jalālayn gloss on بالمعروف and confirms it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (بِالْمَعْرُوفِ) شرعا.

problems.arabic: يفيد أنه لا ينظر إلى قدر الزوجة بل إلى حالة الزوج فقط
problems.issue: The sentence has no stated subject and comments on the āya from outside it — “it conveys that …” — which is how the printed edition phrases its own notes, not how Niasse speaks in this commentary. It may be footnote matter set into the body at this page break. Translated in place, as the conventions direct, and marked as prose, but the register assignment is provisional: if the sentence is the editor's, it is not Niasse's exposition.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the sentence is the edition's note on عَلَى الْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ وَعَلَى الْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ, observing that the measure of the gift tracks the husband's means and not the wife's standing. Flagged as a conjecture; the press should check whether the printed page carries it as a footnote.

problems.arabic: (وَان طَلِّفْتَمُوهَنَّ مِ قَبْلِ أَن تَمَسُّوهُنَّ وَقَدْ بَرَضْتُمْ لَهنَّ بَرِيضَةً مَنِصْفُ مَا بَرَضْتُمْ وَ
problems.issue: Seven faults in one lemma from Q 2:237, every one of a documented class. وَان for وَإِنْ (unwritten hamza). طَلِّفْتَمُوهَنَّ for طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ (qāf as fāʾ, with the vowels displaced). مِ for مِنْ (nūn lost, as إِى at ¶88). بَرَضْتُمْ twice and بَرِيضَةً for فَرَضْتُمْ and فَرِيضَةً (fāʾ as bāʾ, the commonest fault in this transcription). مَنِصْفُ for فَنِصْفُ (fāʾ as mīm). All restored: the āya is fixed, and Niasse's own gloss immediately after — فنصف الصداق للمرأة ونصفه يبقى للزوج — spells out فنصف ما فرضتم and independently fixes the three fāʾs. The trailing وَ is the spurious vowelled wāw of ¶88 and ¶92, standing here where the closing parenthesis should be; the parenthesis is unclosed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَإِنْ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ وَقَدْ فَرَضْتُمْ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً فَنِصْفُ مَا فَرَضْتُمْ). Delete the wāw and close the parenthesis.

problems.issue: إِلَّ for إِلَّا — the final alif has dropped out; the gloss لكن that stands between the two lemmata is the Jalālayn gloss on إلا and confirms the particle. يَعْبُونَ for يَعْفُونَ — fāʾ as bāʾ once more. Both restored from the fixed āya, and the gloss الزوجات that opens ¶92 is the Jalālayn gloss on يعفون, which fixes it a second way. A stray space stands after the second opening parenthesis.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (إِلَّا) لكن (أَنْ يَعْفُونَ).

problems.issue: حَقَّاً for حَقًّا — the fatḥatān written after the alif rather than on the letter before it. Vowelling only; the English is unaffected.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (حَقًّا عَلَى الْمُحْسِنِينَ).

problems.issue: These forms are the edition's own orthography, not OCR damage, and must not be normalised. The printed ten-volume edition follows the Warsh ʿan Nāfiʿ rasm. ے (U+06D2, yeh barree) is how Warsh writes a final yāʾ, so اَ۬لذِے is الَّذِي and nothing is wrong with it; ۦ (U+06E6, small yeh) in بِيَدِهِۦ is the silent yāʾ of the pronominal suffix; ۬ (U+06EC) over the alif of اَ۬لذِے and اُ۬لنِّكَاحِ marks the hamza of waṣl; ۖ after النكاح is a pause mark; and the open fatḥatān (U+08F0) at فَرِيضَةࣰ in ¶88 is the Maghribī vowel sign. The alif of يَعْفُوَاْ for يَعْفُوَ is likewise probably the rasm's otiose alif, and قَنِتِينَ for قَانِتِينَ later in this paragraph is ordinary defective rasm. None of these is emended here. Earlier chunks of this lesson recorded some such forms (أُلنِّسَآءَ, ألَّهِ, اَ۬لنِّكَاحِ) as faults of transcription; that judgement should be revisited, since the hamza-of-waṣl notation at least is deliberate.
problems.conjecture: No emendation proposed. The genuine faults in this transcription are the letter substitutions — qāf/fāʾ, bāʾ/fāʾ, fāʾ/mīm, nūn/rāʾ, nūn/lām, fāʾ/ʿayn — and the lost or spurious brackets, not the Warsh signs. Recorded so that a copy-editor does not regularise the rasm out of the Arabic.

problems.issue: The third instance in this chunk of a spurious vowelled wāw after a word-final mīm (compare عَلَيْكُمُوَ at ¶88 and بَرَضْتُمْ وَ at ¶91, and ذَلِكُمُوَ at ¶80). Here it stands inside the closing parenthesis, which rules out the possibility that the mark is a misread bracket: it is a recurring fault of the transcription itself, and the press can treat it as one class. Q 2:237 reads وَلَا تَنْسَوُا الْفَضْلَ بَيْنَكُمْ, with nothing after the pronoun. تَنسَوْا for تَنْسَوُا is vowelling only.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَلَا تَنْسَوُا الْفَضْلَ بَيْنَكُمْ). Delete the wāw.

problems.arabic: فيجازيكم به حَمِظُواْ عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ) … قال «حَٰعِظُواْ عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتٍ»
problems.issue: The opening word of Q 2:238 is damaged twice in one paragraph, in two different ways: حَمِظُواْ, where the alif and fāʾ of حَافِظُوا have collapsed into a single mīm, and حَٰعِظُواْ, where the fāʾ has been read as an ʿayn and the alif reduced to a superscript. Each restores the other, and the āya is fixed. The first instance also lacks its opening parenthesis, so the lemma runs on directly from Niasse's فيجازيكم به with no mark dividing the registers. الصَّلَوَاتٍ in the second instance carries kasratān for the kasra of الصَّلَوَاتِ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ) in both places, with the opening parenthesis supplied after فيجازيكم به.

problems.arabic: «وَالصَّلَوَةِ الْوُسْطِىٰ» … (وَأَن تَعْفَوَا أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوىٰ) … (وَقُومُواْ لِلهِ قَنِتِينَ)
problems.issue: Three vowelling faults with the consonantal skeletons intact: الْوُسْطِىٰ for الْوُسْطَىٰ (kasra for fatḥa), تَعْفَوَا for تَعْفُوا (fatḥa for ḍamma), and لِلهِ for لِلَّهِ (the shadda lost). Normalised to the fixed āya; the English is unaffected. قَنِتِينَ is left as it stands, being rasm rather than damage.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: «وَالصَّلَاةِ الْوُسْطَىٰ» … (وَأَنْ تَعْفُوا أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ) … (وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قَانِتِينَ).

problems.arabic: والصلوات جمع وأقل الجمع ثلاثة «وَالصَّلَوَةِ الْوُسْطِىٰ» عطف عليها الصلاة الوسطى، والصلاة الوسطى مختلف فيها فخرج من هذا خمس صلوات
problems.issue: As transcribed the argument does not reach its conclusion. A plural of at least three, plus the middle prayer conjoined to it, yields four, not the five that فخرج من هذا خمس صلوات asserts. The step that carries it to five is the one the text only gestures at with مختلف فيها — that a middle term requires an equal number on either side of it, so a set with a distinct middle must be odd and cannot be four. Either a clause was lost at this page break or Niasse compressed the argument in delivery. Translated as it stands, with nothing supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: a clause of the order وللوسطى ما قبلها وما بعدها فلا تكون الصلوات أربعا — “and the middle prayer has what is before it and what is after it, so the prayers cannot be four” — stood between مختلف فيها and فخرج من هذا. Flagged as a conjecture; the press should check the printed page for a dropped line before the reader is left with the arithmetic.

problems.issue: The ḥadīth is transmitted as إِنَّ فِي الصَّلَاةِ لَشُغْلًا, with the emphatic lām on the predicate; the lām is absent here. The sense is unaffected and the quotation is translated as it stands. Noted also because the parentheses here enclose a ḥadīth rather than Qurʾān, and are marked as ḥadīth in the output accordingly; the same is true of (الصلوات الخمس كفارة لما بينهن) later in the paragraph.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (إن في الصلاة لشغلا). Flagged as a conjecture; Niasse may well have recited it short.

problems.arabic: قال له: أعطي محمدا وأمته صلاة هي أربع ركعات
problems.issue: أعطي is unpointed for mood and person and could be read أُعْطِي (“I give”), أَعْطَى (“he gave”) or an imperative. First person is fixed by the rest of the same speech — أغفر لهم and لا أعذبه — and by the continuation on the next printed page, where the speaker settles His own good pleasure upon them. Translated as first person throughout. يارسول الله earlier in the paragraph is written as one word for يا رسول الله.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: أُعْطِي محمدا وأمته صلاة. Vocalisation only.

problems.arabic: وفي الثالثة تفتح لهم أبواب السماء ويستجاب
problems.issue: The paragraph, and the chunk, break off in mid-clause: ويستجاب is a passive with no stated subject, the subject standing on the next printed page (ويستجاب لهم الدعاء). Translated here as an unfinished clause closed with an ellipsis, with nothing supplied, so that the two halves join across the break instead of each inventing a subject.
problems.conjecture: No emendation: the division follows the printed pagination, not a defect in the text.

problems.issue: بَنْ for فَإِنْ — the fāʾ read as a bāʾ and the hamzated alif of إِنْ lost. Restored rather than marked illegible: the lemma opens Q. 2:239 and the glosses that follow (من عدو أو سيل أو سبع, then فَرِجَالًا) fix the āya beyond doubt.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ), “But if you fear.” Orthographic only.

problems.issue: جَرِجَالًا for فَرِجَالًا — the fāʾ read as a jīm, with the rāʾ then doubled in the skeleton. Restored; the gloss فصلوا رجالا جمع راجل immediately following repeats the word correctly.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَرِجَالًا), “then on foot.”

problems.issue: آوْ for أَوْ — the hamzat al-qaṭʿ has been set over a madda. Restored, the āya being fixed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (أَوْ رُكْبَاناً), “or mounted.” Orthographic and vowelling only.

problems.issue: Two faults in one lemma: بَإِذَآ for فَإِذَا (fāʾ read as bāʾ, final alif given a madda), and مِنتَمْ for أَمِنتُمْ (the initial hamzated alif dropped and the vowelling of the verb lost). The closing bracket is also missing. Restored; the gloss من الخوف that follows fixes the verb as أَمِنَ, “to be secure,” and Q. 2:239 is the āya under gloss.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَإِذَا أَمِنتُمْ), “And when you are secure.”

problems.issue: بَاذْكُرُواْ for فَاذْكُرُوا — again the fāʾ read as a bāʾ, the same substitution recurring four times in this paragraph and so evidently a defect of the scan rather than of the printed page. Restored.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ), “then remember Allah.”

problems.issue: نعليمه for تعليمه — the tāʾ read as a nūn. Restored; تعليم is the verbal noun demanded by قبل and by the preceding lemma مَا لَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْلَمُونَ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: قبل تعليمه, “before His teaching it.” Orthographic only.

problems.arabic: لهم الدعاء، وفي الرابعة أحل عليهم رضواني فلا أسخط عليهم بعد.
problems.issue: The paragraph opens mid-quotation, the printed pagination having cut it, so no beginning has been supplied. The first-person divine voice (رضواني, أسخط) marks it as a ḥadīth qudsī rather than Niasse's prose, and it has been set in the ḥadīth register accordingly, with an opening ellipsis in place of the lost words and no opening quotation mark. Not OCR damage.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: none offered for the missing words. The surviving clause belongs to a tradition enumerating what is granted on successive nights (وفي الرابعة, “and on the fourth”), carried over from the discussion that precedes this chunk; the press should set it against the previous page before closing the quotation.

problems.issue: بيوتّهم carries a stray shadda on the tāʾ. Restored. Recorded only because the ḥadīth is quoted verbatim and the press will want the quotation clean.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وبيوتهم. Vowelling only.

problems.issue: يُتَوَقَّوْلَ for يُتَوَفَّوْنَ — the fāʾ read as a qāf and the final nūn broken into لَ; الذِينَ also lacks its shadda. Restored: the gloss يموتون that follows, and Q. 2:240, fix the verb as تُوُفِّيَ in the passive.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنكُمْ), “And those of you who are taken in death.”

problems.issue: A doubled closing bracket, and the accusative tanwīn of أَزْوَاجاً lost. Bracketing normalised silently in the English; recorded here for the press.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (أَزْوَاجاً). Punctuation and vowelling only.

problems.arabic: لَازْوَاجِهِم) ويعطوهن مَتَعاً) ما يمتعن به … إِلَى) إتمام (الْحَوْلِ)
problems.issue: Three lemmata in this paragraph have lost their opening bracket, keeping only the closing one: لِأَزْوَاجِهِم, مَتَاعاً and إِلَى. مَتَعاً also lacks the alif of مَتَاعاً. The registers have been assigned from the Jalālayn's own alternation of lemma and gloss, which Q. 2:240 confirms throughout; nothing here is doubtful in substance.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (لِأَزْوَاجِهِم) … (مَتَاعاً) … (إِلَى). Bracketing and orthography only.

problems.issue: Not a defect but a possible snare for the compositor: the اللّه standing after the closing bracket is the Jalālayn's gloss supplying the object of الْمُتَّقِينَ, not a new sentence and not part of the lemma. It has been translated as prose continuous with the lemma (“those who are mindful of Allah”), and كرره taken with Allah as its subject.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no emendation. Recorded so that the English “of Allah” is not mistaken for an unmarked addition.

problems.arabic: كيف أسقيك يا رب؟ قال: استسقاك عبدي فلان
problems.issue: The third exchange of the ḥadīth lacks the قال that introduces the servant's question in the first two (قال: كيف أعودك، قال: كيف أطعمك), and also lacks the وأنت رب العالمين that closes them. Translated as it stands, elliptically, since an oral abbreviation of a formula already given twice is as likely as a dropped word.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: قال: كيف أسقيك يا رب وأنت رب العالمين؟ Flagged as a conjecture; the ellipsis may be Niasse's own.

problems.arabic: نزلت فيهم "مَ جَآءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ جَلَهُو عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا فقال الرسول
problems.issue: Two faults in the lemma from Q. 6:160. مَ is for مَنْ (the nūn lost), and جَلَهُو is for فَلَهُ — the fāʾ read as a jīm, with a spurious wāw after the pronoun suffix. Both restored, the āya being fixed and the tenfold reward being exactly the point Niasse is making against the eighteenfold of the loan. The edition marks this lemma with a double quotation mark rather than parentheses, and the closing mark is missing, so the narrative frame فقال الرسول runs on inside the quotation.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: نزلت فيهم "مَنْ جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا" فقال الرسول. The closing quotation mark should be supplied before فقال.

problems.arabic: كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ آنْبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنَابِلَ" جزء بسبعمائة
problems.issue: جزء بسبعمائة is readable as it stands and is translated as it stands (“one part for seven hundred”): the construction X بـ Y is the one Niasse has just used twice in the inscription on the gate of the Garden (الصدقة بعشر أمثالها والقرض بثمانية عشر), and the arithmetic of Q. 2:261 (seven ears, a hundred grains in each) gives the seven hundred. Recorded only because a dropped alif would give جزاء, “recompense,” the word Niasse uses three times in the surrounding lines (جزاء صدقته، جزاء القرض، جزاء الصدقة).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: جزاء بسبعمائة, “a recompense of seven hundred.” Flagged as a conjecture and not adopted; the press should check the printed page.

problems.arabic: "مَثَلْ ألذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ أَمْوَلَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ آنْبَتَتْ"
problems.issue: Vowelling and hamza only in the lemma from Q. 2:261: مَثَلْ for مَثَلُ (sukūn for the nominative ḍamma), ألذِينَ for الَّدِينَ — read الَّذِينَ — with the hamza of waṣl written as one of qaṭʿ, and آنْبَتَتْ for أَنْبَتَتْ. Normalised to the fixed āya; the English is unaffected. The defective alif in أَمْوَلَهُمْ is not damage but this edition's Qurʾānic orthography — compare الصَّبِرُونَ below, دِيٰ٪رِنَا and مُلْكَهُۥ in ¶111, and likewise عَسِيتُمۥٓ and نبيئهم there, which are the Warsh readings and should not be emended.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: "مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ أَمْوَلَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أَنْبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنَابِلَ". Orthography and vowelling only.

problems.arabic: "مَن ذَا ألذِى يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً بَيْضَعِفُهُ لَهُ وَ أَضْعَاباً كَثِيرَةْ إلى أكثر من سبعمائة
problems.issue: Two fāʾ-for-bāʾ substitutions in the lemma from Q. 2:245 — بَيْضَعِفُهُ for فَيُضٰعِفَهُ and أَضْعَاباً for أَضْعَافاً — together with a spurious وَ and word break before the second, and كَثِيرَةْ for كَثِيرَةً. All restored from the fixed āya, which Niasse is citing for the sake of its أضعافا كثيرة (hence his إلى أكثر من سبعمائة immediately after). As in the Q. 6:160 lemma above, the opening double quotation mark is never closed, so Niasse's own remark falls inside it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: "مَن ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً فَيُضٰعِفَهُ لَهُ أَضْعَافاً كَثِيرَةً" إلى أكثر من سبعمائة.

problems.issue: أمني for أمتي — the tāʾ read as a nūn. Restored: the same petition stands correctly twice earlier in the paragraph (يا رب زد أمتي) and once in ¶108.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: يا رب زد أمتي. Orthographic only.

problems.arabic: فنزلت "إنَّمَا يُوَجَّى الصَّبِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابِ"
problems.issue: يُوَجَّى for يُوَفَّى — the fāʾ read as a jīm, the same substitution as in جَلَهُو at ¶108. Restored; Q. 39:10 is fixed, and the point of the citation is the unreckoned reward that caps the sequence tenfold → seven hundredfold → without reckoning. حِسَابِ for حِسَابٍ is vowelling only.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فنزلت "إنَّمَا يُوَفَّى الصَّبِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ".

problems.arabic: وهم الذين عبروا النهر مع طالوت كما سياني
problems.issue: سياني for سيأتي — the hamza unwritten and the tāʾ read as a nūn. Restored: the cross-reference is to Q. 2:249, where the crossing of the river with Ṭālūt is narrated, so the forward reference is to material still to come in the lesson.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وهم الذين عبروا النهر مع طالوت كما سيأتي, “as will come.”

problems.arabic: (فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ اڬلْقِتَالُ تَوَلَّوِاْ) وجبنوا اِلَّ قَلِيلاً مِنْهُمْ
problems.issue: اِلَّ قَلِيلاً مِنْهُمْ belongs to Q. 2:246 but stands outside any bracket, the lemma parenthesis having closed after تَوَلَّوِاْ so that the āya resumes after the gloss وجبنوا with no mark. Marked as Qurʾān in the output on the strength of the āya, not of the brackets — the same failure of bracketing as in ¶78 of the preceding chunk. اِلَّ is for إِلَّا.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: تَوَلَّوْا) وجبنوا (إِلَّا قَلِيلاً مِنْهُمْ). Bracketing and orthography only.

problems.arabic: (وَقَالَ لَهُمْ نَبِيّئُهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ فَدْ بَعَثَ لَكُمْ طَالُوتَ مَلِكا
problems.issue: فَدْ for قَدْ — the qāf read as a fāʾ. Restored from the fixed āya (Q. 2:247). The parenthesis is unclosed, so the gloss الله جعل طالوت ملكا عليكم runs on inside the lemma.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَقَالَ لَهُمْ نَبِيّئُهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ بَعَثَ لَكُمْ طَالُوتَ مَلِكاً).

problems.arabic: قَالَ) لهم نبيئهم (إِلَّ أللَّهَ إَصْطَمِيْهُ) اختاره للملك
problems.issue: Three faults. قَالَ) carries a closing parenthesis with no opening one. إِلَّ is for إِنَّ (nūn read as lām), as at اِلَّ قَلِيلاً above. إَصْطَمِيْهُ is badly garbled for اصْطَفَاهُ — the fāʾ read as a mīm and the alif as a yāʾ. Restored rather than marked illegible because two things fix it: Q. 2:247 reads اصطفاه عليكم at exactly this point, and Niasse's gloss اختاره للملك (“He chose him for the kingship”) is the Jalālayn gloss on اصطفاه.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (قَالَ) لهم نبيئهم (إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَاهُ) اختاره للملك.

problems.arabic: (مِ اِلْعِلْمِ وَالْحِسْمُ) فكان أعلم بني إسرائيل يومئذ وأجملهم
problems.issue: مِ for فِي (the fāʾ read as a mīm, the yāʾ lost) and وَالْحِسْمُ for وَالْجِسْمِ (jīm read as ḥāʾ, with the wrong case ending). Both restored from the fixed āya; the gloss that follows (أعلم بني إسرائيل … وأتمهم خلقا) glosses knowledge and body in that order and fixes both words.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (مِنَ الْعِلْمِ وَالْجِسْمِ) — more precisely the Warsh spelling فِے الْعِلْمِ وَالْجِسْمِ, as at فِے سَبِيلِ اڬللَّهِ earlier in the paragraph.

problems.arabic: (قَالُوَاْ أَنَى يَكُونُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ … (وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعُ) فضله (عَلِيم بمن هو أهل له (وَقَالَ لَهُمْ نَبِيِّهُمْ )
problems.issue: Vowelling and bracketing slips through the rest of the paragraph, none of which affects the English: أَنَى for أَنَّى (shadda lost), قَالُوَاْ with a spurious fatḥa, وَاسِعُ for وَاسِعٌ, and two unclosed lemma parentheses, at (عَلِيم and at the paragraph's last lemma. The final نَبِيِّهُمْ is also spelled without the hamza that the same word carries twice earlier in the paragraph (نَبِيّئُهُمْ، نبيئهم), the Warsh reading; the edition should be regularised to نَبِيْءُهُمْ throughout.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (قَالُوا أَنَّى …) … (وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ) فضله (عَلِيمٌ) بمن هو أهل له (وَقَالَ لَهُمْ نَبِيْءُهُمْ). Vowelling, bracketing and the stray space before the last closing parenthesis.

problems.issue: يَاتِبَكُمُ is not a word: the yāʾ of يَأْتِيَكُمُ has been read as a bāʾ. Restored rather than marked illegible, because the lemma is Q. 2:248 verbatim and no other reading of the skeleton fits.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ التَّابُوتُ, “that the Ark will come to you.” Orthographic only; the English follows the restored reading.

problems.arabic: أَنْ يَاتِبَكُمُ التَّابُوتُ الصندوق، كان عند الأنبياء
problems.issue: The lemma's closing parenthesis is lost, so the transcription runs the Qurʾānic lemma and the gloss together in one unclosed bracket. The boundary is fixed by sense: الصندوق is the Jalālayn-style gloss on التابوت, not part of the āya, so it is set as Niasse's prose.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (إِنَّ آيَةَ مُلْكِهِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ التَّابُوتُ) الصندوق. Punctuation only; no word is in doubt.

problems.issue: جِيهِ for فِيهِ — the fāʾ read as a jīm. Restored; Q. 2:248 and the following gloss طمأنينة fix the reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فِيهِ سَكِينَةٌ), “in it is a sakīna.” Orthographic only.

problems.arabic: (وَءَالَ هَرُونَ) يعني هارون قد تركاه لهما
problems.issue: لهما gives “the two of them left it to the two of them,” since Mūsā and Hārūn are already the subject of تركا. Either a dropped alif in Jalālayn's لهم (“to them,” the Children of Israel) or an oral slip preserved by the transcriber. Translated as it stands (“to them”) since the sense is unaffected either way, but the press should check the printed page.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: قد تركاه لهم, “the two of them had left it to them [the Children of Israel],” as in the Jalālayn. Flagged as a conjecture.

problems.arabic: وقفيز من المن الذي كان ينزل عليه
problems.issue: عليه (“upon him”) where the manna came down upon the Children of Israel, not upon Hārūn or Mūsā alone; the Jalālayn reads عليهم. A dropped final mīm is the likely damage. Translated as it stands.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: الذي كان ينزل عليهم, “that used to come down upon them.” Flagged as a conjecture.

problems.issue: Marked illegible in the translation. The span between the gloss كثيرا and the gloss جماعة should carry the lemma مِن فِئَةٍ, but what stands in the transcription is a bare ص followed by جِيَّةِ and a stray closing parenthesis. The ص is not recoverable from the skeleton as it stands, so the span is flagged rather than silently emended.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (مِنْ فِئَةٍ) جماعة, i.e. “of a company — a company —,” with ص a corruption of مِن and جِيَّةِ of فِئَةٍ. The following gloss جماعة and Q. 2:249 both support it. Flagged as a conjecture.

problems.arabic: (قَالَوَأ لا طَاقَةَ لَنَا … (أَنَّهُم مُلَفُوا اللَّهِ) … (فَلِيلَةٍ غَلَبَتْ بِيَّةً كَثِيرَةً بِإِذْبِ اللهِ
problems.issue: The dotting of this paragraph's Q. 2:249 lemmata is damaged at four points: قَالَوَأ for قَالُوا, مُلَفُوا for مُلَاقُو, فَلِيلَةٍ for قَلِيلَةٍ, بِيَّةً for فِئَةً, and بِإِذْبِ for بِإِذْنِ. Restored as one class of damage, since the āya is quoted continuously and each skeleton admits only the Qurʾānic reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (قَالُوا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا …) … (أَنَّهُمْ مُلَاقُو اللَّهِ) … (قَلِيلَةٍ غَلَبَتْ فِئَةً كَثِيرَةً بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ). Orthographic only; the English supplies “[company]” in brackets where the first فئة is flagged illegible above.

problems.arabic: (رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغُ) أصبب … كسروهم ( بإِذْلِ اللّهِ … (وَفَتَّلَ دَاوْرد)
problems.issue: Four points of damage in the Q. 2:250–251 lemmata: أَفْرِغُ for the imperative أَفْرِغْ, بإِذْلِ for بِإِذْنِ (nūn read as lām), وَفَتَّلَ for وَقَتَلَ (qāf read as fāʾ, with a spurious shadda), and دَاوْرد for دَاوُودُ. Restored; the āya fixes every reading, and بِإِذْنِ recurs correctly glossed بإرادته in the same line as in ¶115.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ) أصبِبْ … (بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ) … (وَقَتَلَ دَاوُودُ). Orthographic only; the English follows the restored readings.

problems.arabic: وكان في عسكر طالوت جَالُوتَ الجبار واتِيهُ آتى اللَّهُ) دور الْمُلْكَ)) في
problems.issue: The line is scrambled and has been translated in the order transcribed, not reordered. Three faults compound: (i) Niasse's aside وكان في عسكر طالوت, which belongs to Dāwūd, stands between the verb وقتل داود at the end of ¶116 and its object جَالُوتَ, so the Arabic reads as though Jālūt were in Ṭālūt's army; (ii) the lemma delimiters are lost or doubled — جَالُوتَ and واتِيهُ open no bracket, and الْمُلْكَ closes two; (iii) واتِيهُ for the lemma وَآتَاهُ. دور, which should be the gloss naming the referent of the pronoun in وَآتَاهُ, is marked illegible in the translation.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وكان [داود] في عسكر طالوت (جَالُوتَ) الجبار (وَآتَاهُ) آتى الله داود (الْمُلْكَ) في بني إسرائيل — “And [Dāwūd] had been in Ṭālūt's army. Jālūt — the tyrant. And He gave him — Allah gave Dāwūd — the kingship among the Children of Israel.” دور is a corruption of داود; the Jalālayn glosses the pronoun of وَآتَاهُ with the name at just this point. Flagged as a conjecture; the press should set the printed page beside it before emending.

problems.arabic: (وَالْحِكْمَةَ) كان النبوءة والملك لا يجتمعان لأحد
problems.issue: كان for كانت with the feminine النبوءة (for النبوّة) as subject. Either OCR loss of the tāʾ or an oral slip preserved by the transcriber. Translated without the auxiliary, which English does not need here; no sense is at stake.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: كانت النبوّة والملك لا يجتمعان لأحد. Orthographic and grammatical only.

problems.issue: نقصها has lost the shadda of نَقُصُّها, and ايَتُ the alif of آيَاتُ (as العَلَمِينُ earlier in the paragraph for الْعَالَمِينَ). All three are the printed edition's defective alifs or dropped diacritics rather than doubtful words; restored.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (آيَاتُ اللَّهِ نَتْلُوهَا) نَقُصُّهَا (عَلَيْكَ), “are Allah's signs, which We recite — which We relate — to you.” Orthographic only.

runs: — it is ‘those’ and ‘the messengers,’ subject and predicate; or [the reading is] ‘those messengers.’
We favoured some of them above others.
Allah favoured some of the prophets above others by His singling [one] out with a merit that belongs to no other.
Among them is one to whom Allah spoke
and He raised some of them

(Q. 2:253) above the rest, by the universality of the summons, the sealing of prophethood, the preferment of his community above all other communities, the multiplying miracles, and the many distinguishing properties. He mentions in this āya that Allah favoured some of the prophets above others. They agreed that some of the prophets are more excellent than others, and they reached consensus that Muḥammad ﷺ is the most excellent of the prophets and the messengers; and that [rests] on many grounds. One of them is that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, reported in the Qurʾān that He sent the Prophet ﷺ as a mercy to the worlds, in His words:
We sent you only as a mercy to the worlds

(Q. 21:107) Since he was a mercy to all the worlds, it is established that he is the most excellent of all the worlds — because every single one in the world is shown mercy by reason of Muḥammad ﷺ, so Muḥammad became more excellent than all of them. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, joined obedience to him to obedience to Himself, the pledge of allegiance to him to the pledge of allegiance to Himself, his good pleasure to His good pleasure, and his might to His might. He, Exalted, said:
Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah
Those who pledge allegiance to you pledge allegiance only to Allah; the hand of Allah is above their hands
(Q. 48:10) And this hand is the hand of Muḥammad
ﷺ — and his good pleasure to His good pleasure:
And Allah and His Messenger are more worthy that they should please Him
(Q. 9:62) — and his might to His might:
and to Allah belongs the might, and to His Messenger, and to the believers
(Q. 63:8) And also: as for the Prophet ﷺ, Allah reported in His Book that He raised his renown
And We raised your renown for you
(Q. 94:4) That [was] by His joining mention of him to the mention of Allah at the

— that is, at the pronouncing of the two testimonies: whoever says ‘I bear witness that there is no deity but Allah’ says ‘and I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah.’ This belonged to no other of all the prophets. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, reported in His Book that he is the seal of the prophets, and this shows that he is more excellent than all of them, because it is not intelligible that something excellent be sealed with something of lesser worth. When the craftsman comes to the last of his work, he brings out the mastery of his work and makes it the seal. So since Muḥammad was the seal of the prophets, it became clear that he is more excellent than all of them, because sealing with something of lesser worth is neither intelligible nor wise. And Allah reported in His Book that the community of Muḥammad is the best of all communities:
You were the best community brought forth for mankind

(Q. 3:110) Whence did they come by this? From the Prophet ﷺ. Since we were the best community by reason of Muḥammad ﷺ, it became clear that Muḥammad is more excellent than the prophets who were sent to the communities before us; and his Book is more excellent than their books, his religion more excellent than their religions, and his law more excellent than their laws. Along with that, he has the most miracles of them all. Mūsā is the prophet with the most miracles: Allah mentioned that He gave him nine clear signs, and [to] Muḥammad ﷺ Allah gave of clear signs what He gave to none of the prophets before him. Along with that, Allah issued a challenge in the Qurʾān with a single sūra:
then bring a sūra like it
(Q. 2:23) And the shortest of the sūras is

(Q. 108:1), and it is three āyas. From this it emerged that every three āyas in the Qurʾān are a miracle, and the Qurʾān is more than six thousand āyas. So the Qurʾān alone comprises, of miracles, more than two thousand miracles — knowing that Mūsā had only nine signs — to say nothing of the miracles that appeared to his Companions,
and he left behind, of the Companions, one hundred and fourteen thousand, [1] each one of whom witnessed a miracle that no one else witnessed. And [each] prophet used to be sent
to his own people, whereas the Chosen One ﷺ was sent to mankind entire — rather, to the jinn and mankind [alike]. And Allah says in His Book:
And We sent you only as one [sent] to mankind entire
(Q. 34:28) And since he was a messenger to all mankind, his hardship was greater than the hardship of all the prophets, because every one of them was sent only among his own people.
And when the hardship is greater, the merit is greater. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ is more excellent than all the prophets. And also, the Prophet ﷺ says:
“I am the master of the children of Ādam, and [this is] without boasting. Ādam and those below him are under my banner on the Day of Resurrection.”
[2] It emerged from this that he is more excellent than Ādam and than all the sons of Ādam. ʿAlī came up one day, and the Prophet ﷺ looked at him and said:

My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You
As for Muḥammad ﷺ, the Qurʾān reported:
The heart did not lie about what it saw
And Mūsā fell down in a swoon:
and Mūsā fell down in a swoon
that is, unconscious; whereas Muḥammad ﷺ:
The eye did not swerve, nor did it transgress

Allah addressed all the prophets and messengers by their names: O Nūḥ, O Ibrāhīm, O Mūsā, O ʿĪsā, O Ādam, O Dāwūd — every one of them He calls by his bare name, because, for all the majesty of their stations, every one of them is only a servant of His.
As for Muḥammad ﷺ, He did not call him by his name even once: O Messenger, O Prophet, O you wrapped in a cloak.

Yes, He mentioned his name in the Qurʾān, because had He not mentioned his name we would not know who this mighty creature is; so He mentioned him, and He mentioned him only by joining the messengership to the mention of him:
Muḥammad is nothing but a messenger
Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah

The cock has appetite in it always, the appetite for intercourse; the crow is covetous; the vulture loves eating and never slackens from eating; and the peacock loves adornment and boasting. [26] When a man purifies his soul of these dispositions he dwells in the dominion of the heavens and the earth. When he struggles against his soul until he has severed it from appetite, from much eating, from boasting and self-adornment, and from covetousness, he enters the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Man was created from the four elements: from water, earth, air and fire — these are the four elements. From the nature of water and earth came covetousness and miserliness; from air and fire came anger and appetite. These are four. Covetousness married envy, miserliness married rancour, anger married pride, and appetite has no spouse: it is a beloved, like a woman held in common among men. So these are seven: there appeared covetousness and its wife envy, miserliness and its wife rancour, anger and its wife pride, and appetite, which has no spouse. These seven are the gates of Hell:
It has seven gates; to each gate a portion of them is assigned (Q. 15:44)

So whoever struggles against his soul and purifies it of covetousness and of miserliness, of envy, of rancour, of anger, of pride and of appetite has freed his soul from the Fire. Covetousness is the first thing by which Allah was disobeyed: Adam ate from the forbidden tree after he had possessed the Garden and what is in it, out of covetousness on his part for remaining in the Garden — and so he went out of the Garden. And envy is the first thing by which Iblīs disobeyed: he envied Adam and so refused to prostrate to him, and contrived against him until he brought him out of the Garden, out of envy. And by envy Qābīl killed Hābīl. These three acts of disobedience are the first acts of disobedience upon the face of
the earth: covetousness, envy and killing.

armed to the teeth in weapons, and they came to Badr. In this there was a sign, that is, a lesson, because the Prophet ﷺ announced that they would be victorious, and he announced the places where the people would fall: so-and-so is struck down here, and so-and-so is struck down here, and
is struck down here, to the last of them; and the matter fell out as he had said. So they met, and the Muslims overcame them, and they took captive from among them
chiefs from among their chiefs, among them al-ʿAbbās b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. This is a lesson for whoever takes a lesson. More of
The love of desires has been made alluring to people

— what the soul craves and is drawn to. Allah made them alluring as a trial, or Satan [did]. In this āya He mentioned seven things that a human being loves, seven things in which a human being's desires lie; love is gathered in them. And you know that a person loves a thing and does not love to love it, as a Muslim loves something forbidden — so then, that is, he does not love to love it; and he loves a thing that he loves to love and in which his desire does not lie; and he loves a thing that he loves to love and in which his desire does lie — this is the stronger. All of them came together in the āya: the love of desires. He mentioned that they are desires made alluring to them and that they loved them.
— when a man comes of age, the first thing he attaches himself to is to find a wife who suits him.
— when he has found a wife, he loves that Allah provide him with children.
and heaped-up hoards of gold and silver
— and when he has found women and sons, he loves to find much gold and silver. As for gold, its own word makes you renounce it:
, going away; so everything you own of gold must go away. And silver,
, which is scattering: everything you own of silver must be scattered. Women and sons and gold and silver.
— camels and cows and sheep and goats.
That is the enjoyment of the life of this world
— all these things are goods enjoyed in this world,
and with Allah is the best of returns (Q. 3:14)
That is the goodly place of return, which is the Garden, with Allah, Blessed and Exalted; so one should desire it and nothing else.
ʿAlī, may Allah ennoble his face, said:
"Man's appetites are in women, food, drink, clothing, and mounts."

"The best food is honey, and it is only the excrement of a fly; the best drink is water, in which people, beasts, livestock and wild animals are all alike; women are only a urinary passage within a urinary passage; the best of mounts are horses, and upon them men are killed; and the finest clothing is silk, which is only the excrement of a worm."
None of this deserves attention. Attention belongs to what is with Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and that is attained only by obeying Him, by carrying out His command and avoiding what He forbids.
O Allah, bless our master Muḥammad.
