problems.issue: Not OCR damage but a probable factual/transcription slip: al-Ḥajjāj b. Yūsuf (d. 95/714) did not live to see the caliphate of ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb. Translated as it stands.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: either an oral slip for a comparison of reputation only (the scholars invoking ʿUmar as the standard), or ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz was meant; no emendation made.

problems.issue: كلا is not a possible reading after الدنيا; final hāʾ lost in OCR. Rendered 'the ruin of the world [entire]', with the supply bracketed.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: كلّها.

problems.arabic: فلما نوى التوبة رجعت ورجعت الثمار بحالها
problems.issue: رجعت ورجعت may be dittography in the transcription. Kept as it stands, repetition and all, per the verbatim standard.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: a single رجعت الثمار بحالها, or رجعت [حالته] ورجعت الثمار بحالها.

problems.issue: The lemma is printed with third-person يُخْرِجُ, but Q. 3:27 reads تُخْرِجُ (second person, addressing Allah), and Niasse's own gloss immediately afterwards uses تخرج. Translated as it stands ('He brings'), which leaves the lemma at odds with the gloss that follows.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: تُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ, i.e. 'You bring the living out of the dead'; the English would then run on directly into the gloss.

problems.arabic: تحد جاهلا يلد ولدا فيكون عالما
problems.issue: تحد has no sense here; dāl/jīm confusion in OCR. Translated as 'you find'.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: تَجِدُ.

problems.issue: حبي is not a verb form that fits; the sentence requires the counterpart of ماتت. Translated as 'the heart comes alive'.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: حَيِيَ القلب.

problems.issue: مَ is a truncated preposition and the alifs carry no hamza; the lemma is otherwise recoverable as Q. 3:27. Translated from the standard reading.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: وَتُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ الْحَيِّ.

problems.issue: حيبت is not a possible form; parallel to the preceding clause requires the perfect of حَيِيَ in the feminine. Translated as 'when the soul comes alive'.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: حَيِيَت.

problems.issue: The sūra name after من is missing, and a stray colon stands in its place. Supplied in brackets in the translation as [Āl ʿImrān], since both verses quoted next are from that sūra.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: وآيتان من آل عمران.

problems.arabic: "قَهِدَ ألَّهَ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَ إِلَّ هَوَ وَالْمَلِّئِكَةُ وَأوْلُوا الْعِلْمِ قَايِماً بالْقِسْطَ لآ إِلَة إِلَّ هَوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ إِنَّ ألدِينَ عِندَ أللَّهِ الإسْلَمُ"
problems.issue: Heavily damaged but continuous and recoverable: shīn read as qāf (قَهِدَ), lost long alifs (إِلَ, الإسْلَمُ), hamza/alif confusion throughout, case endings scrambled (بالْقِسْطَ, حِسَابٌ below). Translated from the standard text of Q. 3:18–19 rather than marked illegible, because every word is identifiable.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَأُولُو الْعِلْمِ قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ. إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِندَ اللَّهِ الْإِسْلَامُ.

problems.issue: Not text of the commentary but the running head of the printed page, carried into the transcription as a paragraph and corrupted. Marked illegible rather than translated, so that no sentence is invented for it; an editor should delete the paragraph and close up ¶29 and ¶31, whose sentence runs across it (… وقل اللهم | مالك الملك).
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: في رياض التفسير (the book's title as running head).

problems.arabic: من لازم قراء هن فله ما ذكر
problems.issue: قراء هن is a broken word split by a spurious space; the construction requires a verbal noun with the feminine plural pronoun. Translated as 'reciting them'.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: قراءتهنّ.

problems.issue: Orthographic corruption of Q. 3:28 (lost long alifs in الْكَفِرِينَ, hamza written as wāw in ٱلْمُومِنُونَ, doubled yāʾ in أَوْلِيَّاءَ). Identifiable throughout, so translated from the standard text.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: لَا يَتَّخِذِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ.

problems.issue: Unreadable as it stands; marked [illegible] in the translation rather than reconstructed in the text. Its position between the lemma أولياء and the gloss لا تترك المومنين وتصادق الكفار, and the gloss itself, fix what it must be.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: مِن دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ, 'rather than the believers'.

problems.issue: A fragment opening the paragraph: the tail of the gloss on وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ, broken at the page edge. Marked [illegible] rather than completed, since the paragraph begins mid-word and nothing in the chunk fixes the form.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: بمُوالاتهم ('by allying with them') or يواليهم; the sense required is 'whoever does that, that is, allies with them'.

problems.issue: Damaged Q. 3:28: fāʾ read as tāʾ, اللَّهِ broken by a spurious space, and فِي شَيْءٍ collapsed into شنع. The closing bracket is also missing. Recoverable, so translated from the standard text; Niasse's gloss (فليس من دين اللّه في شيء) confirms the reading.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (فَلَيْسَ مِنَ اللَّهِ فِي شَيْءٍ).

problems.issue: A stray exclamation mark closes the paragraph after the ḥadīth's closing bracket. Not rendered, since nothing in the Arabic warrants it and the register excludes exclamation marks.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: a misread closing bracket or full stop in the printed edition.

problems.issue: نَجْسَةُ is not a word. The fāʾ of نَفْسَهُ has been read as jīm and the final hāʾ as tāʾ marbūṭa — the same corruption recurs in ¶37 as نَمْسَةٌ. Translated from the conjecture.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: read اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ (Q. 3:28).

problems.issue: Three defects in one lemma: وَالَى for وَإِلَى (the hamza of إلى lost, so the reading becomes the verb wālā, which would duplicate واليتموهم in the preceding gloss); الّهِ for اللَّهِ with one lām dropped; and the lemma opens with { and is never closed. Translated from the conjecture.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: read {وَإِلَى اللَّهِ الْمَصِيرُ} (Q. 3:28).

problems.issue: Stray glyphs at the paragraph end. The ؟ closes the question that begins كيف يقدر, but the bare 2 and the Latin y between the footnote marker and the question mark correspond to nothing in the sentence. Not rendered; the footnote marker [21] and the question mark are kept.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the 2 is a second, page-restarted footnote number (the printing restarts its footnote count on every page) and the y is scanner noise, most likely the tail of the following line. Neither is text.

problems.issue: The paragraph opens on the tail of a word, not on a clause. Translated from where it starts, as the bare verb with a leading ellipsis, with no beginning invented.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: read لا يستطيع ('he cannot'), completing the rhetorical question that closes ¶34 (كيف يقدر على غضب الرب). كيف يستطيع is also possible, but ¶34 already carries كيف يقدر.

problems.arabic: يتفكر في غضب اللّٰه تبارك   ||   [¶36] المكتونة …   ||   [¶37] وتعالى وشدة عقابه
problems.issue: ¶35 breaks off inside the formula تبارك وتعالى, which ¶37 completes with وتعالى. ¶36 stands between the two halves and is not part of the exposition at all: it is printed footnote matter — a ḥadīth closing with a Suyūṭī reference — that the pagination dropped between ¶35 and ¶37. The paragraphs have NOT been reordered; ¶35 is translated as ending at 'Blessed', ¶36 is translated where it stands, and ¶37 opens with 'and Exalted'.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the running text reads يتفكر في غضب اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى وشدة عقابه, i.e. ¶35 joins directly to ¶37, and ¶36 belongs in the apparatus, keyed to the footnote marker [21] at the end of ¶34.

problems.arabic: الإنسان يحجبه عن المعصية، إذا تفكر، ثلاثة أشياء
problems.issue: Not damage. الإنسان is a dangling topic resumed by the pronoun of يحجبه, with ثلاثة أشياء following as the subject of the verb — ordinary oral syntax. Translated as a single clause ('Three things screen a person from disobedience') rather than reproducing the anacoluthon.
problems.conjecture: No emendation. The three things are then given as غضب الله, شدة عقابه and ضعفه هو across ¶35 and ¶37, which confirms the count.

problems.issue: Marked illegible in the translation. The word cannot be read, and because the paragraph opens here the verb that should govern سبعين نظرة is lost with it, so there is no syntax to recover the word from.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: المكنونة ('the treasured', 'the hidden') is the nearest graphic reading — a dropped nūn and a tāʾ for bāʾ. المكتوبة ('the prescribed [prayer]') is graphically closer still but does not construe with في كل يوم سبعين نظرة. Neither is secure, and a whole word may be missing before it.

problems.arabic: في كل يوم سبعين نظرة وإلا قضيت له …
problems.issue: The paragraph opens mid-sentence, after the main clause of the ḥadīth has been lost with the page. سبعين نظرة stands as an accusative object with no verb, and the series of وإلا clauses has no ما … إلا frame to attach to. Translated from where it starts, as first-person divine speech on the strength of قضيت، أعذته، نصرته, with a leading ellipsis inside the quotation.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: a lost frame of the type ما … إلا نظرت إليه في كل يوم سبعين نظرة. The ḥadīth has not been identified; the protasis naming who earns the promise is not in the chunk.

problems.issue: The volume and page of the reference are transposed: ج marks a volume number, so ج99 would be volume 99 of a work in far fewer. Rendered as printed ('99/2') rather than silently corrected.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: read ج2/99 — al-Jāmiʿ al-Kabīr, vol. 2, p. 99.

problems.issue: فَلِ is not a word. The qāf of قُلْ has been read as fāʾ and the lām has taken a kasra. The same corruption closes the paragraph as فَلِ)) لهم يا محمد, there with a doubled closing bracket and no opening bracket. Translated as 'Say' in both places.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: read (قُلْ) in both occurrences (Q. 3:29 and Q. 3:31).

problems.issue: Four defects in one lemma: a spurious wāw before إن, which the muṣḥaf does not have after قل; تُخْبُوا for تُخْفُوا, fāʾ read as bāʾ; a stray ـوَ on the end of صدوركم; and the lemma closes with ) having never been opened. Translated from the conjecture.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: read (إِنْ تُخْفُوا مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ) (Q. 3:29).

problems.issue: The divine name is written with hamzat qaṭʿ on the article and with tāʾ marbūṭa for the final hāʾ. The same pair of errors appears in the corpus elsewhere (cf. فَقَدَ آطَاعَ اللَّةَ in ¶38).
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: read (يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ) (Q. 3:29).

problems.arabic: (و) هو ويَعْلَمُ مَا مِي السَّمَٰوَاتِ … قَدِيرَ٣
problems.issue: Four defects across this lemma run. (a) The conjunction is set twice, once bracketed as (و) and again at the head of ويعلم. (b) مَا مِي for ما في, fāʾ read as mīm. (c) The long lemma from ويعلم to قدير carries no brackets at all and stands in the line as though it were Niasse's prose; set as lemma on the strength of Q. 3:29. (d) A stray ٣ follows قَدِيرَ. هو between the two wāws is taken as Niasse's deictic gloss and marked 'p'.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: read (وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) (Q. 3:29). The ٣ is most likely a scan of the āya-end ornament or a page-restarted footnote number, not text.

problems.arabic: (ص سُوْءِ تَوَدَّ لَوْ آنَّ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَهُ أَمَداً بَعِيداً)
problems.issue: Three defects in one lemma: ص for مِنْ, the preposition reduced to a single letter; تَوَدَّ for تَوَدُّ; and آنَّ for أَنَّ, the hamza having broken into alif plus madda. Translated from the conjecture.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: read (مِنْ سُوءٍ تَوَدُّ لَوْ أَنَّ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَهُ أَمَداً بَعِيداً) (Q. 3:30).

problems.issue: نَمْسَةٌ for نَفْسَهُ — the same word corrupted a second way in the same chunk (¶34 has نَجْسَةُ), which is itself the evidence for the reading. Niasse's own gloss, كررها للتأكيد, confirms that this is the repetition of the ¶34 lemma. Translated identically in both places.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: read (وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ) (Q. 3:30).

problems.issue: The lemma has no opening bracket and رَءُوفْ carries sukūn where the muṣḥaf has رَءُوفٌ. Set as lemma on the strength of Q. 3:30 and of Niasse's gloss, which repeats شديد الرأفة بعباده.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: read (وَاللَّهُ رَءُوفٌ بِالْعِبَادِ) (Q. 3:30).

problems.arabic: «وَمَا عَمِلَتْ صِ سُوءِ تَوَدُّ لَوَ آنَّ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَهُ د أَمّداً بَعِيداً»
problems.issue: Niasse's re-quotation of the same words carries four further defects: صِ for مِنْ again; لَوَ for لَوْ; a bare د standing free in the line; and أَمّداً with shadda for أَمَداً. Translated identically to the first occurrence, since he is quoting the same words back.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: read «وَمَا عَمِلَتْ مِنْ سُوءٍ تَوَدُّ لَوْ أَنَّ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَهُ أَمَداً بَعِيداً» (Q. 3:30). The free د is most likely a scan of a hamza seat or of a verse ornament.

problems.arabic: ما نعبد الأصنام إلا حبا لله ليقربونا إليه
problems.issue: ليقربونا has a plural subject where the Jalālayn occasion-of-revelation formula has ليقربنا. Not emended: with الأصنام as antecedent the plural construes, and the oral delivery may simply have levelled it. Translated as 'that they may bring us near to Him'.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the printed exegetical formula reads ليقربنا إليه; no emendation made.

problems.arabic: يقول له: أبعد عني … يقول: أنا عملك الصالح طالما ركبتك فاليوم تركبني
problems.issue: Register decision, not damage. The dialogue of the two deeds in the grave, and the Prophet's exchange with the Jews and the Najrān delegation later in the same paragraph, are direct speech inside Niasse's own narration, with no isnād and no named speaker for the deeds. Marked 'h' with double quotation marks, following the treatment of the Companions' unattributed exchange in Lesson 7 ¶7; the narrative frames (قال لهم، قالوا، يقول) stay 'p'.
problems.conjecture: No emendation. If 'h' is to be reserved strictly for isnād-bearing ḥadīth and named authorities, the deeds' speech would move to 'p'; flagged for AK's decision.

problems.arabic: وَاد كُنْتَمْ تُجِبُونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَبِعُونِ يُحْبِبْكُمْ أللَّهِ )
problems.issue: Five defects in one lemma: وَاد for إِنْ, which is graphically remote and may conceal a dropped word; كُنْتَمْ for كُنْتُمْ; تُجِبُونَ for تُحِبُّونَ, ḥāʾ read as jīm; فَاتَبِعُونِ for فَاتَّبِعُونِي, without shadda and with the final yāʾ lost; and أللَّهِ for اللَّهُ, with hamzat qaṭʿ on the article and the wrong case. Translated from the conjecture, which Niasse's own re-quotation of the same words later in the paragraph — «اِن كُنتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اَ۬للَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِے يُحْبِبْكُمُ اُ۬للَّهُ», correct apart from its Warsh orthography — confirms.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: read (إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي يُحْبِبْكُمُ اللَّهُ) (Q. 3:31).

problems.issue: Four defects in one lemma: وَيَغْمِرْ for وَيَغْفِرْ, fāʾ read as mīm; ذُنَوبَكُمُ for ذُنُوبَكُمْ; غَبَورَ for غَفُورٌ, fāʾ read as bāʾ and the case ending lost; and the lemma opens with { and is never closed, the run continuing into the gloss لمن اتبعني. Translated from the conjecture.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: read {وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ} (Q. 3:31).

problems.arabic: لمن اتبعني ما سلف منه قبل ذلك
problems.issue: The gloss on غفور stands in the first person (اتبعني) where the printed exegetical gloss has the third (لمن اتبعه). Not emended: the lemma it glosses is itself first-person (فاتبعوني), so the shift follows the verse. Translated as 'to whoever follows me'.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the Jalālayn gloss reads لمن اتبعه ما سلف منه; no emendation made.

problems.issue: Three defects, and a bracket decision. الرَسُولَ lacks the shadda; فَقَدَ آطَاعَ for فَقَدْ أَطَاعَ, the hamza broken into alif plus madda; and the divine name written with tāʾ marbūṭa. The citation is set in straight double quotation marks, which elsewhere in the chunk are not used for lemmata, but the words are Qurʾān and are marked 'q' accordingly, with no quotation marks in the English.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: read مَنْ يُطِعِ الرَّسُولَ فَقَدْ أَطَاعَ اللَّهَ (Q. 4:80).

problems.arabic: من يحبب حبيبا أحب ملابسيه من الأنام
problems.issue: The sentence scans as a hemistich and sits between two prose sentences that paraphrase it, so it may be quoted verse rather than Niasse's own words. No poet is named and no metre can be confirmed from a single line, so it is left as 'p'. ملابسيه is read as mulābisīhi, 'those in contact with him'.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: a quoted hemistich; if it is verse, the preceding وهذا واضح من أحب شخصا… is Niasse glossing it in advance. No emendation.

problems.arabic: لو كان حبك صادقا لأطعته إن المحب لمن يحب مطيع
problems.issue: The paragraph is the second line of a well-known couplet and nothing else; the first line is not in the transcription. Translated as it stands. Marked 'p' rather than 'h' because the text names no author, although the couplet is a quotation.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the missing first line is تَعْصِي الإِلٰهَ وَأَنْتَ تُظْهِرُ حُبَّهُ / هٰذَا لَعَمْرِي فِي الفِعَالِ بَدِيعُ, the couplet being attributed variously to ʿAbdallāh b. al-Mubārak and, in the Dīwān al-Shāfiʿī, to al-Shāfiʿī. Attribution not supplied in the translation, since the text supplies none.

problems.arabic: جَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُو نَمْسُهُ, فَثْلَ أَخِيهِ مَفَتَلَهُ, بَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ الْخَسِرِين
problems.issue: OCR letter-substitution throughout the lemma (ف>ج, ف>م, ق>ث, ف>ب); the lemma is identifiable as Q. 5:30 and has been translated from the restored reading rather than marked illegible.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُ نَفْسُهُ قَتْلَ أَخِيهِ فَقَتَلَهُ فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِين (Q. 5:30)

problems.arabic: وَاتَّبَعَ هَوِيَةٌ جَمَثَلُهُو ... يَلْهَثَ أوْ تَتْرَكْهُ يَلْهَثَّ
problems.issue: هوية for هواه, جمثله for فمثله, and both occurrences of يلهث mis-vowelled; identifiable as Q. 7:176 and translated from the restored reading.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ فَمَثَلُهُ كَمَثَلِ الكَلْبِ إِن تَحْمِلْ عَلَيهِ يَلْهَثْ أَو تَتْرُكْهُ يَلْهَثْ (Q. 7:176)

problems.arabic: اتَّبَعُوًا أَمْرَ فِرْعَوْنَ ... بِرَشِيدٌ ... وَبِيسَ الوِرْدُ المَوْرُود
problems.issue: Initial و of واتبعوا lost; برشيدٌ for برشيدٍ; وبيس for وبئس. Two āyas run together without a break.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: وَاتَّبَعُوا أَمْرَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَا أَمْرُ فِرْعَوْنَ بِرَشِيدٍ / يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُ يَوْمَ القِيَامَةِ فَأَوْرَدَهُمُ النَّارَ وَبِئْسَ الوِرْدُ المَوْرُودُ (Q. 11:97–98)

problems.arabic: وَخَلَقَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ آضَاعُواْ الصَّلَوْةَ
problems.issue: وخلق (“and he created”) for فخلف (“then there succeeded”) — a substitution that changes the sense; آضاعوا for أضاعوا. Translated from the restored reading.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: فَخَلَفَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ أَضَاعُوا الصَّلاَةَ وَاتَّبَعُوا الشَّهَوَاتِ فَسَوْفَ يَلْقَوْنَ غَيًّا (Q. 19:59)

problems.issue: In ¶40–¶41 the Qurʾānic lemmata are delimited by straight double quotation marks rather than the ( ) { } « » ⟨ ⟩ forms the conventions name; the quotation marks are also misplaced in ¶41. Marked “q” on identification of the text as Qurʾān, not on the delimiter.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the printed edition set these lemmata in « » and the transcription flattened them to " ".

problems.issue: نعصي (“we disobey”) cannot stand with وأنت تظهر حبه; a single-dot OCR slip for تعصي. Translated from the restored reading.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: تعصي الإله وأنت تظهر حبه (al-Warrāq)

problems.issue: The attested text of al-Warrāq’s poem reads في المقال (var. في الفعال); القياس may be the edition’s reading rather than OCR damage, so it has been translated as transmitted (“in reasoning”). Also لعمرى for لعمري, and لو كان حبك lacks the attested connective ولو.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: هذا لعمري في المقال بديع / ولو كان حبك صادقا لأطعته

problems.arabic: [¶42–¶44] تعصي الإله ... وأنت لشكر ذلك مضيع
problems.issue: One poem of three bayts split across ¶42, ¶43 and ¶44 by the page break. The hemistich order as transcribed is correct, so nothing has been reordered; quotation marks have been supplied at each paragraph’s edges rather than once around the whole.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: تعصي الإله وأنت تظهر حبه / هذا لعمري في المقال بديع // ولو كان حبك صادقا لأطعته / إن المحب لمن يحب مطيع // في كل يوم يبتديك بنعمة / منه وأنت لشكر ذلك مضيع

problems.arabic: وقد أورد البيتين الأولين المراغي في تفسيره وعزاهما للوراق. مج 1/ج140 /3.
problems.issue: This is the editor’s footnote on the poem, not Niasse’s speech; marked “p” for want of an editorial register. The volume/part/page numerals are transposed — ج140 cannot be a juzʾ number.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: مج 1/ج 3/ 140 = Tafsīr al-Marāghī, vol. 1, pt. 3, p. 140.

problems.arabic: حتى أحبه[25] 1 فإذا أحببته كنته   /   الولد سر أبيه[26] 2
problems.issue: Footnote anchors carry doubled numbering — a bracketed number plus the printed superscript ([25] 1, [26] 2). Rendered once each as [n. 25] and [n. 26], in the position the Arabic puts them (the ¶46 anchor falls inside the ḥadīth, after حتى أحبه).
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: the bracketed figure is the transcription’s own note number and the bare figure the printed edition’s.

problems.arabic: (قُلَ اطِيعُوا اللَّه وَالرَّسُولَ ... جَتَ اللَّه لا يُحِبُ
problems.issue: جتَ for فإنَّ — the OCR has reduced فإن to a single malformed word; also قُلَ اطيعوا for قُلْ أَطيعوا. Identifiable as Q. 3:32 and translated from the restored reading.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: قُلْ أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ ... فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الكَافِرِينَ (Q. 3:32)

problems.issue: عنرتَ for عمرانَ and العلمين for العالمين; the lemma also continues the وآل broken off at the end of ¶47. Translated from the restored reading, which the in-situ gloss يعني عمران confirms.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: وَآلَ عِمْرَانَ ... عَلَى العَالَمِينَ (Q. 3:33)

problems.arabic: جعلهم اللّه قرية بعضها من ولد بعض
problems.issue: قرية (“village”) for ذرية (“progeny”) in Niasse’s own paraphrase of the lemma; the lemma itself is also loosely vowelled (ذَرِيَّةُ بَعْضُهَا مِنْ بَعْضِ for ذُرِّيَّةً بَعْضُهَا مِنْ بَعْضٍ). Translated from the restored reading.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: جعلهم اللّه ذرية بعضها من ولد بعض

problems.arabic: إبراهيم من ذرية نوج ... فأنبياء بني إسرايل كلا من إسحاق
problems.issue: نوج for نوح, إسرايل for إسرائيل, هولاء for هؤلاء, and كلا standing where the sense requires كلهم. Translated as “all of them from Isḥāq.”
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: فأنبياء بني إسرائيل كلهم من إسحاق

problems.arabic: إِذْ قَالَتِ اذكر إذ قالت (إمْرَأَتُ عِمْرَنَ)
problems.issue: إِذْ قَالَتِ carries no brackets although it is the lemma that the following اذكر إذ قالت glosses; marked “q” on that basis. Also إمرأت for امرأت and عمرنَ for عمرانَ.
problems.conjecture: CONJECTURE: (إِذْ قَالَتِ) اذكر إذ قالت (امْرَأَتُ عِمْرَانَ) (Q. 3:35)

problems.issue: OCR garble of a Qurʾānic lemma: ف read as ج and ق as ف (the ق/ف confusion that runs through this scan).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (certain from the muṣḥaf): فَتَقَبَّلْ مِنِّي, Q. 3:35. Translated as restored, ‘so accept from me’.

problems.issue: ب stands for ف at the head of the lemma.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (certain from the muṣḥaf): فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتْهَا, Q. 3:36. Translated as restored.

problems.issue: The mother's patronymic as the transcription prints it; the form usually given in the tafsīr tradition is فاقوذ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: حَنَّة بنت فَاقوذ = Ḥanna bint Fāqūdh. Left as printed in the translation (Fāqūdā) pending the printed page.

problems.arabic: قالت: يا رَبِّ إِنّى نَذَرْتُ) … (( قَالَتْ)
problems.issue: Bracket damage: no opening bracket before the first lemma, a doubled opening bracket before قالت, and an extraneous يا standing outside the lemma although it is not in the Qurʾānic text.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (رَبِّ إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ … (قَالَتْ). Lemma boundaries set from the muṣḥaf; the non-Qurʾānic يا is not translated.

problems.issue: The same bracket damage: يا outside the lemma, and no opening bracket before كَالأنثى.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the يا is not Qurʾānic and is left untranslated; read (كَالأُنثَى).

problems.issue: وهبت is unpointed at its first occurrence: either wuhibat (‘was bestowed on me’) or wahabta (‘You bestowed on me’). The second occurrence, in Niasse's exposition, is pointed وهبتَ.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: both are wahabta. Rendered passive at the first occurrence and second-person at the second, following the pointing as printed rather than harmonising them.

problems.arabic: يحتمل معنيين: وليس الذكر الذي طلبت … وما يعتريها من الحيض
problems.issue: The paragraph announces two senses of وليس الذكر كالأنثى and then breaks off inside the first at the page end. The second sense is not in this chunk.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the second sense (the standard one, that the female bestowed is not like the male requested, i.e. the comparison reversed) stands at the head of the next page. Nothing supplied; the English ends unpunctuated where the Arabic stops.

problems.arabic: ودهنها، فيجد عندها فاكهة الصيف في الشتاء
problems.issue: The paragraph opens on the tail of a list — بطهورها وشربها وأكلها ودهنها — whose head stands on the preceding page, and the same list recurs mid-paragraph in Niasse's own repetition, which can read like a duplicated line.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: a page-break continuation, not a reordering. Translated from where it starts; no line moved and no beginning invented.

problems.issue: The clause breaks off with no apodosis, followed by a full stop and a new sentence.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the apodosis is the one given earlier in the same paragraph, فقد كذب بمائتي آية وما يزيد على خمسمائة حديث. Marked in the translation as ‘[sentence incomplete]’ rather than completed.

problems.issue: No closing bracket before the gloss الغرفة, so the gloss falls inside the lemma.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: الْمِحْرَابَ) الغرفة. الغرفة is Niasse's Jalālayn-style gloss on al-miḥrāb and is marked as prose, not as Qurʾān.

problems.issue: الولد sits loose after the name, with no connective.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: عيسى الوَلَد, ʿĪsā the son — the son to be born to her, whose muʿjizāt this karāma prefigures. Translated ‘ʿĪsā, the child’.

problems.issue: كلا is not a possible reading in this position.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: كلهم — ‘the people of the house all ate’. The supplied word is bracketed in the translation.

problems.issue: الصفة is under-dotted and unshadded.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: أهل الصُّفَّة, the people of the portico of the Prophet's mosque (aṣḥāb al-ṣuffa). Glossed in square brackets.

problems.arabic: فقال يرسل إلى كل بيت في المدينة
problems.issue: يرسل is unpointed, so the voice is undetermined, and the speaker of فقال is not named.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فقال: يُرسَلُ (‘let it be sent’) or فأرسل (‘and he sent’). Rendered as a jussive with the Prophet as the implied speaker, as the narrative requires.

problems.issue: The lām of the genitive is lost from the formula.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (certain): الحمد لله الذي جعلك. Rendered with the fixed form, al-Ḥamdu li-Llāh (The Praise is for Allah).

problems.issue: Footnote anchors come through as a bracketed number followed by a stray superscript digit (affects ¶52 and ¶54).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the bracketed number is the anchor and the loose digit is the printed superscript read twice. Kept as [27], [28], [29] at the point of attachment; the loose digit dropped.

problems.arabic: فصنعوا طعاا لما لم يبق إلا الأكل
problems.issue: طعاا has lost its final letters, and the connective fāʾ is missing from لما.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فصنعوا طعاماً فلما لم يبق إلا الأكل — ‘and prepared food; when nothing was left but the eating’.

problems.arabic: فخرج على فلقي رجلو يبيع جملا … فأخذ على الجمل
problems.issue: على stands where a proper name is required (twice), and رجلو is not an Arabic form.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: عليٌّ — ʿAlī, Fāṭima's husband and al-Ḥasan's father — and رجلاً. Translated accordingly; the name carries the whole narrative.

problems.issue: درها lacks its mīm.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: درهماً.

problems.issue: The interrogative particle and the interrogative pronoun are both missing, although the sentence is punctuated as a question.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: أعلمتَ من البائع؟ or أتعلم من البائع؟ — ‘Do you know the seller?’, as translated.

problems.arabic: … والسائل الأول … هو جبريل، جبريل هو || جائع قالت لا والله
problems.issue: ¶55 ends mid-sentence at جبريل هو and ¶56 opens at جائع, which does not continue it. ¶56 then gives a fuller telling of the Fāṭima bowl story already told in ¶54.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: text is missing between the two paragraphs, including the head of the Prophet's question — something on the order of هل عندك شيء؟ إني جائع, which جائع ends. Within each paragraph the lines stand in order, so nothing was moved in the translation; ¶56 opens inside the Prophet's speech and is marked as quotation with the supplied ‘[I am]’.

problems.issue: The paragraph opens in the middle of a transmitted narration — first-person, with the bowl already in the narrator's hands — so the report's opening (its isnād and the beginning of the story) lies outside this chunk. Nothing has been supplied: the English begins where the Arabic begins. An opening double quotation mark has been set so that the ḥadīth register can be marked at all, and the closing mark falls at the end of the narration, before the citation.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the preceding chunk (L08-08, ¶¶52–56) carries the opening of the same report — Fāṭima's want, ʿAlī's errand, and the covering of the jafna — which the printed page continues across the page-break. To be verified against the printed volume; not supplied here.

problems.issue: The source citation's numerals are out of order: the siglum ج (juzʾ/volume) stands before 361, and the 1 trails after the slash, so the transcription reads 'volume 361, [page] 1'. Rendered literally as 'part 361 /1' rather than silently corrected.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the printed citation was ج1/ص361 — Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, vol. 1, p. 361 — and the OCR lifted the page number ahead of the volume siglum. Not adopted.

problems.arabic: المسكين والبائع الأول رضوان خازن الجنة، والمشتري ميكائيل
problems.issue: This paragraph is page-foot apparatus (note 30), not running commentary: it identifies the characters of a story — a beggar, a first seller, a buyer, six dirhams turned into sixty-six — that is nowhere in this chunk. The transcription has set it between the end of the Fāṭima narration (¶57) and the resumption of the gloss on Q. 3:38 (¶59). It has been translated in place and not moved.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the anchor for note 30 lies in the preceding chunk (L08-08), in the story of the six dirhams given in alms, and the note belongs at the foot of that page. Reconstruction recorded, not applied.

problems.issue: Each footnote anchor in this chunk carries two numbers: a bracketed figure in the transcription's own sequence ([30]–[35]) and a bare figure that follows it (1–4), which is the note's number on its printed page. Both have been kept exactly as they stand, in Niasse's prose register, rather than merged or dropped. The same doubling occurs at ¶59 ([31]) and ¶61 ([32]), where the page number is absent.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the printed page footnotes were numbered 1–4 and the bracketed figures are the transcription's continuous numbering across the lesson; the bare figures should be suppressed in the English edition once the apparatus is keyed. Not done here.

problems.issue: The transcription gives Khadīja's patronymic as خويلد here and at ¶63 (three times). Rendered as it stands.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: خويلد is the correct form (Khadīja bt. Khuwaylid b. Asad), so no emendation is called for; recorded only because the name recurs and should be checked for uniformity against the printed volume.

problems.arabic: فلو كان النساء كما ذكرنا لفضلت النساء على الرجال
problems.issue: The first hemistich does not match the Dīwān, which ¶68 itself cites as the source: al-Mutanabbī's line reads ولو كان النساء كمن فقدنا / لفضلت النساء على الرجال. Here كما ذكرنا ('as we have mentioned') stands for كمن فقدنا ('like the one we have lost'). Translated as transcribed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: either Niasse adapted the hemistich to his own list of the perfected women, or the transcription has replaced كمن فقدنا with a paraphrase. Not emended; to be checked against the printed volume.

problems.arabic: كما أني سيد الرجال) هي أفضلهم
problems.issue: A closing parenthesis stands between the end of the ḥadīth and the gloss هي أفضلهم, with no opening bracket anywhere in the paragraph. Marked [illegible: )]; nothing is read into it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the remnant of the bracket that closed a lemma or a quotation in the printed line — most likely the mark that closed the ḥadīth, the printed edition having used ( ) for quoted matter here as it does for lemmata. Not adopted.

problems.issue: The paragraph consists of a full stop and a stranded lemma-opening, يَا مَرْيَمُ, with nothing after it: the running text it belongs to resumes only at ¶69 (اقنتي لربك), four paragraphs later, because the page's footnote block (¶¶65–68) has been transcribed in between. The lines have NOT been reordered: each is translated where it stands.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the printed body text read (يَا مَرْيَمُ اقْنُتِي لِرَبِّكِ) أطيعيه — Q. 3:43 — so that ¶64 + ¶69 are one continuous unit and ¶¶65–68 are the apparatus at the foot of that page (notes 32–34: the Bukhārī and Muslim references, the second hemistich, and the Dīwān citation). Reconstruction recorded, not applied.

problems.arabic: باب قوله تعالى وضرب اللّٰه مثلا للذين آمنوا امرأة (3411) وفي صحيع
problems.issue: Two defects. The āya quoted in the chapter-heading breaks off at امرأة, which is not a possible stopping point: Q. 66:11 reads امرَأتَ فِرْعَوْنَ, and the heading in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī carries فرعون. '[of Pharaoh]' has been supplied in square brackets. And صحيع is صحيح with the final ح read as ع; translated as Ṣaḥīḥ. The title Ṣaḥīḥ is itself split across the paragraph break, 'Muslim' standing at the head of ¶66.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored): باب قوله تعالى وضرب الله مثلا للذين آمنوا امرأت فرعون (3411), وفي صحيح مسلم — the two ḥadīth references for note 32 or 33.

problems.issue: A bare second hemistich with no first hemistich and no introduction, sitting inside the footnote block between a ḥadīth reference (¶66) and a Dīwān citation (¶68). Translated where it stands, with no companion line supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the missing first hemistich is al-Mutanabbī's نعد المشرفية والعوالي ('we count up our Mashrafī blades and our tall lances'), from the same elegy for Sayf al-Dawla's mother that ¶68 cites; the printed page quoted two lines of it and the transcription has kept only this half. Not supplied.

problems.issue: The citation's numerals are out of order, as at ¶57: the siglum م (mujallad/tome) stands before 2, ج (juzʾ/part) before 149, and a bare 3 trails after the slash. Rendered literally ('tome 2 / part 149 / 3') rather than silently corrected.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the printed citation was م2/ج3/ص149 — Dīwān al-Mutanabbī, tome 2, part 3, p. 149 (Dār al-Kitāb al-ʿArabī, Beirut) — the page number having been lifted ahead of the part siglum. Not adopted.

problems.issue: افتتي stands for اقْنُتِي (Q. 3:43): the ق read as ف and the ن reduced to a tooth. The lemma also has no opening bracket, its opening having been stranded at ¶64. Translated, the āya being fixed and identifiable, and the gloss أطيعيه confirming the reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): (يَا مَرْيَمُ اقْنُتِي لِرَبِّكِ).

problems.issue: OCR damage inside the lemmata of Q. 3:44. نُوجِيهِ stands for نُوحِيهِ (ح read as ج); يَكْفَلَ مَرْيَمٌ for يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ, the case endings reversed. Translated, the āya being fixed and identifiable.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored from the muṣḥaf): ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنبَاءِ الْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ ... أَيُّهُمْ يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ.

problems.issue: The last words of the chunk have run together and lost letters: وهوادْ is وهو followed by إِذْ with the alif-hamza and ذال collapsed, and الْتَلْيِكَةُ is الْمَلَائِكَةُ with the م read as ت and the alif lost. Translated as 'And it is' plus the lemma 'when the angels said', because the following words are identifiable as the opening of Q. 3:45; the syntax of وهو remains uncertain and no word has been supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture (restored): وهو إِذْ قَالَتِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ, Niasse referring ذلك من أنباء الغيب back to the angels' annunciation. An alternative is واذكر إذ قالت الملائكة, on the pattern of ¶60. Neither adopted.

problems.issue: The chunk ends in the middle of the lemma that opens Q. 3:45, so no āya reference has been placed after it: the run continues into the next chunk. The āya numbers given in this chunk are placed at the end of each completed run (Q. 3:38–39, 3:39, 3:40, 3:41, 3:42, 3:43, 3:44) and not after every fragment.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the lemma continues يَا مَرْيَمُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ بِكَلِمَةٍ مِنْهُ (Q. 3:45) at the head of L08-10, where the reference belongs.

problems.issue: The paragraph, and with it the chunk, opens with a bare proper name and no governing verb: جبريل is a gloss on a lemma that fell on the preceding printed page. Translated from where it starts, with nothing supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the lost words were the lemma (إِذْ قَالَتِ الْمَلَـٰئِكَةُ) of Q. 3:45, which جبريل glosses after the manner of the Jalālayn ("إذ قالت الملائكة" أي جبريل). Not adopted; the English keeps the bare name.

problems.issue: Both اسمه and ابن are written with hamzat qaṭʿ (إِسْمَهُ, إِبْنُ) instead of the elidable hamza of the Qurʾānic rasm.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: اسمه المسيح عيسى ابن مريم (Q. 3:45). Read as the lemma and translated accordingly.

problems.issue: م is not a word, and the lemma brackets that should enclose في الدنيا have been lost, so a Qurʾānic phrase stands inside what reads as continuous gloss. The span is marked illegible and the surrounding words translated as the gloss the transcription makes them.

problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (قَالَ) تعالى (أَأَقْرَرْتُمْ) (Q. 3:81).

problems.issue: OCR corruption of the final vowel of 'ذَلِكُمْ'. 'إِصْرِي' rendered 'My bond'; the gloss opening ¶91 ('عهدي') confirms the reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: عَلَى ذَلِكُمْ إِصْرِي (Q. 3:81).

problems.issue: Both divine names are corrupt and the first has lost its parentheses; the glosses 'لهم' and 'يهم' have lost their prepositions.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (اللَّهُ غَفُورٌ) لهم (رَحِيمٌ) بهم (Q. 3:89); عَجُونَ = غَفُورٌ, رَحِيٌّ = رَحِيمٌ, يهم = بهم.

problems.issue: The chunk ends mid-lemma: 'عْدَ' is a truncated 'بَعْدَ' followed by a stray closing parenthesis, and the rest of Q. 3:90 is not in this chunk. Translated as far as it goes; no continuation supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) بعيسى (بَعْدَ إِيمَانِهِمْ) (Q. 3:90), following Jalālayn, who glosses 'بعد إيمانهم' as 'بموسى'.

problems.issue: Scope note, not an OCR fault: the chunk was assigned as Q. 3:15–91, but the text in it runs from the gloss on 'وَهَذَا النَّبِيُّ' in Q. 3:68 to a truncated lemma in Q. 3:90. Nothing from Q. 3:15–67 or Q. 3:91 appears here.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the assignment covers the whole of Lesson 8 and this is its final chunk; Q. 3:15–67 lies in earlier chunks.

problems.issue: The paragraph opens on a stray wāw and an unmatched closing parenthesis where the printed edition has the opening bracket of the first lemma. Restored rather than marked illegible: the gloss that immediately follows, يا محمد لقومك, is the Jalālayn gloss on قل at Q. 3:15, and no other reading of the skeleton fits.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (قل). Translated as “Say”, set as a Qurʾānic lemma.

problems.issue: Two lemmata carry heavy letter substitution: the hamza-nūn-bāʾ cluster of أؤنبئكم has been read as وتبي, and in the second lemma the bāʾ is read as yāʾ, من is split, and the final mīm of ذلكم is read as nūn. Restored, not marked illegible: the pair is the continuous opening of Q. 3:15 and the intervening gloss هل أخبركم is Jalālayn's gloss on أؤنبئكم.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (أؤنبئكم) … (بخير من ذلكم), per Q. 3:15. The English follows the restored reading.

problems.issue: فيها with the fāʾ read as mīm. Restored: the lemma sits inside the running citation of Q. 3:15 immediately after خالدين.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فيها), “therein”. Orthographic only.

problems.issue: The lemma ورضوان من الله is damaged (final nūn of رضوان read as lām; من read as مي), and the closing bracket is missing, so the boundary between lemma and gloss is unmarked in the transcription. Restored, and the bracket supplied before رضى كثير, which is Jalālayn's gloss, not Qurʾān; the register split in the output follows that division.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (ورضوان من الله) رضى كثير. Flagged as a conjecture as to the bracket placement; the press should check the printed page.

problems.issue: والله بصير with one lām of the divine name dropped. Restored; Q. 3:15 fixes the reading and the gloss عالم follows.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (والله بصير), “and Allah is seeing”. Orthographic only.

problems.issue: كوكُم is not a word, and it stands at the page break: the sentence runs on unfinished into ¶4, which opens رضوا عن الله. Marked illegible rather than restored, because the reading governs the syntax of the join across the page break and nothing in the transcription settles it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: كونهم, giving “the greatest of it in their eyes is their being pleased with Allah and Allah's being pleased with them”, with ¶4's finite verbs رضوا / رضي then read as a verbal complement. Flagged as a conjecture: on that reading ¶4's opening would also need repointing, so the paragraphs have been translated separately and the finite verbs left standing in ¶4.

problems.issue: ارجعي with the final yāʾ read as tāʾ marbūṭa. Restored: the rest of the citation (راضية مرضية) identifies Q. 89:28 unambiguously.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية (Q. 89:28). Orthographic only.

problems.arabic: {الذِيسَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّنَآ ءَامَنَّام … ومَاغْمِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَفِنَا عَذَابَ ألبَّارِه
problems.issue: Q. 3:16 damaged throughout: final nūn of الذين read as sīn; a stray mīm closes آمنا; فاغفر opens with wāw-mīm and has a ghayn for the fāʾ; وقنا has qāf read as fāʾ; and the closing bracket after النار has been read as hāʾ. Restored; the āya is the one under gloss and the interposed صدقنا بك وبرسولك is Jalālayn's gloss, kept as prose.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (الذين يقولون ربنا إننا آمنا) … (فاغفر لنا ذنوبنا وقنا عذاب النار). Note that the transcription reads إنَّنَا where the muṣḥaf has إنّا. The doubled nūn is left unemended, since the lesson's own prose paraphrase a few lines below also reads إننا آمنا and the reading may be Niasse's oral form rather than OCR; the English renders it “we have believed” either way, the emphatic particle carrying no separate weight in translation.

problems.issue: الصابرين with the alif lost and the final nūn read as yāʾ. Restored: Q. 3:17 follows directly on Q. 3:16, and the gloss أمدح الصابرين — which reads the accusative as governed by an implied verb of praise — spells the word out in full.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (الصابرين), Q. 3:17. Orthographic only.

problems.arabic: يا أهل الجنة … فلا أسخط عليكم بعده أبدا)
problems.issue: Not OCR damage but a dislocation of the printed apparatus: this paragraph is the edition's own footnote on the ḥadīth of al-riḍwān, set into the body at the page break. It opens mid-quotation — the frame (إن الله يقول لأهل الجنة or similar) and the opening bracket are absent, while the closing bracket survives. Translated in place and from where it starts; no opening was invented and no reordering performed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the note originally opened with a frame such as يقول الله تبارك وتعالى: (يا أهل الجنة …). Note also that ¶3 gives Niasse's own looser retelling of the same ḥadīth, which is why ¶3's dialogue is set as prose and ¶5 as a quotation.

problems.arabic: والصبر الكبير هو الصن عن المعصية
problems.issue: الصن is not a word. Marked illegible rather than restored, since the damaged word is the head of the predicate and the restoration, though near-certain, is an editorial emendation of the lemma under discussion.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: الصبر عن المعصية, “patience in abstaining from disobedience” — fixed by the two parallel clauses in the same sentence (الصبر على البلاء, الصبر على الطاعة) and by the sentence that follows it.

problems.issue: The run of lemmata from Q. 3:17 is damaged: الصادقين has qāf read as fāʾ and the alif lost; القانتين is read as الفيتين; والمنفقين has lost its opening bracket; المستغفرين has a spurious sukūn-less sīn-sīn sequence; بالأسحار is undotted. Restored: the Jalālayn glosses attached to each (المطيعين لله, المتصدقين, أواخر الليل) and Niasse's own full-form enumeration of the five attributes further down the paragraph fix every reading.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (والصادقين) … (والقانتين) … (والمنفقين) … (والمستغفرين) … (بالأسحار), all Q. 3:17. Orthographic only.

problems.issue: بالمكّ is not a word and the skeleton is too far from any candidate to be read off the page. Marked illegible. The parallel in Jalālayn on Q. 3:17 reads خصت بالذكر لأنها وقت الغفلة ولذة النوم, which the rest of the clause reproduces word for word.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: خصت بالذكر, “they were singled out for mention”. Flagged as a conjecture resting on the Jalālayn parallel rather than on the letter shapes.

problems.arabic: مقام الصبر من رُزقه فهو من الصالحين. والصدق مقام «وَالْفَنِتِينَ وَالْمُنفِقِين»
problems.issue: The passage is dislocated, not merely misread. فهو من الصالحين الصابرين leaves الصابرين in apposition with no governor; والصدق مقام then has no predicate, and the lemma that follows it stands with no comment attached. The lines appear to have been set out of order at the page break. Translated as it stands and left unreordered, as the conventions require.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the sequence was probably … فهو من الصالحين. الصابرين: مقام الصبر, من رُزقه فهو من الصالحين; والصدق مقام [كذلك]; «والقانتين والمنفقين» … — that is, an enumeration in which each attribute is named as a station in turn. Flagged as a conjecture; the press should collate the printed page before emending.

problems.issue: Apparatus mismatch: the footnote marker in the body is numbered 2, but the note supplied at ¶7 is numbered 1, and ¶7's content (the ḥadīth of the descent in the last third of the night) is the note belonging to this marker on بالأسحار. The marker is retained as printed and the note translated in place.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the body marker should read [1]. Either the marker or the note number is a typographical error in the printed edition; flagged as a conjecture rather than corrected.

problems.issue: لاحتجنا split across a spurious space with the alif of the eighth form lost. Restored; the conditional لو قال governs it.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لاحتجنا إلى الجمع, “we would have needed to combine”. Orthographic only.

problems.issue: Two letter misreadings in one lemma: المستغمرين for المستغفرين (fāʾ read as mīm) and بالأسجار for بالأسحار (ḥāʾ read as jīm). Restored rather than marked illegible: the lemma is Q. 3:17, the same words are cited correctly at ¶6 of this lesson as (وَالْمستَغْفِرِين) ... (بالاسحار) أواخر الليل, and the same gloss أواخر الليل follows here.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: «المُستَغفِرِينَ بِالأسْحارِ» (Q. 3:17). The English 'those who seek forgiveness in the pre-dawn hours' follows the restored reading.

problems.issue: A bare numeral 1 stands after the question mark, following the editor's sequential marker [3]. It is the printed edition's own footnote number, whose text stands in this lesson at ¶7 ('1 - قد ورد تخصيص هذا الوقت في الحديث...'), so the transcription carries both numbering systems at the same point. Only [3] is reproduced in the English; the stray 1 is dropped as duplicate apparatus.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فأغفر له[3]؟ — the loose 1 to be deleted. The press should confirm that marker [3] and the original note 1 refer to the same ḥadīth of the descent, in which case the two are redundant.

problems.arabic: إن اللٰه يمهل حتى يمضي شطر الليل
problems.issue: Readable as it stands (يُمهِل, 'grants respite'), and translated so, but this wording of the ḥadīth al-nuzūl is not the usual one and differs from the version the edition itself gives in the footnote at ¶7 (ينزل ربنا تبارك وتعالى كل ليلة...). Flagged only because a transcriber's يمهل for ينزل would change the sense of the clause.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: no emendation made. If the printed page reads يمهل, the oral wording stands; the press should collate against the manuscript before adopting ينزل.

problems.arabic: فلهذا يرغب أن يكون العبد عمله في الليل يؤخره إلى الجزء الأخير منه
problems.issue: أن يكون العبد عمله leaves العبد without a predicate: either an oral anacoluthon, characteristic of this commentary, or a dropped preposition. Translated as it stands, with the possessive supplied in brackets ('the servant['s] work'), and the asyndetic يؤخره kept as a second clause.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: فلهذا يُرغَّب للعبد أن يكون عمله في الليل, 'the servant is encouraged to have his work be in the night'. Flagged as a conjecture; the anacoluthon may be genuine and should not be emended silently.

problems.arabic: يقول الصوفية: كن نجما فإن لم تستطع فكن قمرا
problems.issue: No damage — a register decision. الصوفية is an unnamed collective, not a named authority, so the maxim is kept in the 'p' register without quotation marks, following the treatment of وقال أخرون at L06c08 ¶39. The same decision governs قالت اليهود at ¶9.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: none. A volume-wide ruling is wanted on whether quoted maxims of unnamed collectives (الصوفية, العلماء, اليهود) take the 'h' register; this chunk assumes they do not.

problems.arabic: والكبرى العارفون، من عرف اللٰه المعرفة العيانية
problems.issue: No damage — a terminology decision at a paragraph that opens mid-sentence. The subject الولاية stands at the end of ¶6 (هذه الولاية الصغرى, in L08c01), so the feminine الكبرى has been completed with a bracketed [walāya] rather than given an English equivalent; العارفون is Englished as 'the knowers [of Allah]' after L06c01, and المعرفة العيانية as 'the maʿrifa of direct vision', keeping maʿrifa in the 'i' register as at L06c08 ¶46.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: none. L08c01 ¶6 should render الولاية الصغرى as 'the lesser walāya' so that the bracketed completion here reads continuously.

problems.arabic: كما أن النجم يبيت الليل كله سانا
problems.issue: سانا is not a word, and more than one reading fits the skeleton, so the span is marked illegible rather than restored. The ḥāl describes what the star does all night long, in contrast with the moon, which يسري for part of the night only.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ساريا ('coursing'), the rāʾ and yāʾ having been read as a single nūn; the parallel القمر يسري في جزء من الليل in the next clause supports it. ساهرا ('wakeful') is also possible and would suit كن متعبدا الليل كله. Flagged as a conjecture; the printed page must decide.

problems.arabic: القمر يسري في جزء من الليل ويغير في جزء آخر
problems.issue: يغير gives no sense here. Restored to يغيب (bāʾ read as rāʾ): the clause contrasts the part of the night through which the moon travels with the part in which it is not there, and يغيب is the only reading of the skeleton that completes the contrast.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ويغيب في جزء آخر, 'and is absent during another part'.

problems.issue: A comma intrudes between وبين and الليل, which suggests the transcription has broken at this word. Translated as it stands, taking بين adverbially ('amid the night are the prayers of the khalawāt'), which follows the preceding sentence on the lover's love of khalwa; the span is not marked illegible because بين الليل is readable Arabic once the comma is set aside.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وبين الليل صلوات الخلوات, with the comma deleted; وفي الليل صلوات الخلوات is the alternative, and would not change the English.

problems.arabic: (قَدَ الّٰه أَهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ )
problems.issue: The opening lemma of Q. 3:18 is badly broken: قَدَ for شَهِدَ (the shīn and its dots lost, the hāʾ dropped) and أَهُ for أَنَّهُ. Restored, not marked illegible: the same lemma recurs two lines later as «قَهِدَ ألَّه» and in full in the ḥadīth at the end of the paragraph, and the āya is fixed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ), Q. 3:18.

problems.arabic: قال: «قَهِدَ ألَّه» بيِّن لخلقه بالدلائل والآيات
problems.issue: قَهِدَ for شَهِدَ again (shīn read as qāf) and ألَّه for اللَّهُ. Restored on the same ground as the preceding entry.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: «شَهِدَ اللَّهُ». Orthographic only; the Jalālayn gloss بين لخلقه بالدلائل والآيات confirms the verb.

problems.arabic: لا معبود في الوجود بحق سوله
problems.issue: سوله is not a word; the ālif of سواه has been read as a lām. Restored: the Jalālayn gloss on Q. 3:18 reads لا معبود في الوجود بحق إلا هو, and the lemma «إِلاَّ هُوَ» follows immediately.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لا معبود في الوجود بحق سواه, 'there is no object of worship in existence, by right, other than He'.

problems.issue: Four lemmata of Q. 3:18–19 carry letter-level damage: والملبكة for والملائكة; فائما for قائما and بالفسط for بالقسط (qāf read as fāʾ twice); إل الدين for إن الدين; الاسلم for الإسلام. All restored, the āyāt being fixed and each gloss confirming the reading (بتدبير مصنوعاته, بالعدل, الشرع المبعوث به الرسل).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ), (قَائِمًا), (بِالْقِسْطِ), (إِنَّ الدِّينَ), (الْإِسْلَامُ). Orthographic and vowelling only; no English is affected.

problems.issue: Opening parentheses have dropped out before الحكيم, عند الله and فائما, leaving closing brackets without openers. The words are nonetheless Qurʾānic lemmata under gloss (in His making; Blessed and Exalted; by governing the things He has made), and they are marked 'q' accordingly.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (الْحَكِيمُ), (عِندَ اللَّهِ), (قَائِمًا) — the openers restored. Typographic only.

problems.arabic: «شَهِدَ الَّهُ أَنَّهْ, لَا إِلَهَ إِلاَّا هُوَ ... ٱلْعَزِيْزِ الْحَكِيمُ إِنَّ ألدِّينَ عِندَ أللَّهِ الإسلَم»
problems.issue: The full citation of Q. 3:18–19 inside the ḥadīth carries scattered noise: الَّهُ for اللَّهُ, أَنَّهْ with a stray comma, إِلاَّا with a doubled ālif (twice), المليكة for الملائكة, العزيز in the genitive where the āya has الْعَزِيزُ, and الإسلَم for الْإِسْلَامُ. Restored as one span, the āyāt being fixed.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the Qurʾānic text of Q. 3:18–19 as printed in the muṣḥaf. Orthographic and vowelling only.

problems.arabic: (من قرأ: ... الإسلم) وأنا أستودع هذه الشهادة عندك
problems.issue: The ḥadīth moves from the words recited to the reciter's own words with no introducing verb, only و—; 'and [then says]' is supplied in brackets. The closing parenthesis of the Qurʾānic citation also falls after الإسلم rather than after the ḥadīth, so the brackets do not mark the limits of the quotation.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: و[ثم يقول] أنا أستودع هذه الشهادة عندك. The paragraph ends mid-sentence with the Lord's speech, so the English opens the ḥadīth's quotation and leaves it unclosed, as at L06c09 ¶54.

problems.arabic: روى وائل عن عبد اللٰه بن مسعود
problems.issue: No damage, but the isnād is given with a bare وائل and no nisba. Translated as it stands ('Wāʾil related from ʿAbdallāh b. Masʿūd') with nothing supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: Wāʾil b. Dāwūd, the Kūfan transmitter who reports from Ibn Masʿūd in the ḥadīth on reciting Q. 3:18. Flagged as a conjecture; the press should verify the isnād before adding the nisba.

problems.issue: فها for فيها — the yāʾ has dropped out at the page break. Restored rather than marked illegible: ¶16 ends with ومكث, which requires the prepositional phrase, and النار is the only available antecedent.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: ومكث فيها مدة, “and remained in it for a time.” Orthographic only.

problems.arabic: ب حنان بامنان باذا الجلال والإكرام
problems.issue: Each vocative يا has been read as ب: ب حنان / بامنان / باذا. Restored, since the three-term invocation is a fixed formula and ذا الجلال والإكرام admits no other vocative particle. The same يا → ب substitution recurs at ¶22 (باله), which confirms it as a systematic misreading in this stretch of the transcription rather than a one-off.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: يا حنان يا منان يا ذا الجلال والإكرام.

problems.issue: الملالكة for الملائكة — the hamza-seat read as a lām. Restored; الملائكة is spelled correctly later in the same paragraph (قال الرب للملائكة).
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: قالت الملائكة. Orthographic only.

problems.issue: The angels’ question is damaged beyond secure reading and is marked illegible in the translation. الكلي is not a word; الندار carries an intrusive dāl for النار; لي stands where a preposition is required. Only هذه and يا رب are certain.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: هذه الكلمة في النار يا رب؟ — “This word, from within the Fire, my Lord?”, the angels marvelling that the invocation comes from inside the Fire. The following أخرجوا صاحبها supports it, since the feminine pronoun of صاحبها needs a feminine antecedent and الكلمة supplies one. Flagged as a conjecture: the press should read the printed page before emending, and the English “the one who uttered it” leaves the antecedent open.

problems.arabic: وأوقفوه بين يدي الله تبارك وتعالى وقا اسود واحترق
problems.issue: وقا is not a word: the dāl of وقد has been read as an alif. Restored; اسود واحترق is a perfect-tense circumstantial clause and requires قد.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وقد اسودّ واحترق, “and he had turned black and had been burned.”

problems.issue: Ambiguous as transcribed, and no emendation is proposed. Read as لِمَ تلتفتُ إليَّ (“Why do you keep turning toward Me?”), picking up وهو يلتفت يمينا وشمالا just above. The alternative, لم تلتفتَ إليَّ as a negative (“you did not turn toward Me”), does not fit the narrative, since the servant has just been turning.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: لِمَ تلتفتُ إليَّ. Vocalization only; the consonantal text is sound and was translated as it stands.

problems.issue: The whole paragraph is a two-word page-foot fragment in which the article’s alif has been displaced to the end: لجنة ا for الجنة. Not reordered in the Arabic; translated in place as the completion of ¶17’s فأدخلوه.
problems.conjecture: Reconstruction: الجنة, giving فأدخلوه الجنة across the two paragraphs, “and they admitted him to the Garden.”

problems.arabic: (لاَ رَيْبَ) لا شك (جِيدِ) وهو يوم القيامة
problems.issue: جِيدِ is corrupt for the Qurʾānic فِيهِ. Restored rather than marked illegible: Q. 3:25 reads لا ريب فيه, and the gloss sequence here reproduces the Jalālayn on that āya verbatim ((لا ريب) لا شك (فيه) وهو يوم القيامة), which fixes both the lemma and its position.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فِيهِ), rendered “about it.”

problems.issue: وَوَفِيتُ for وُوَفِّيَتْ: the shadda and the passive vocalization are lost, and the final tāʾ is pointed as a first-person rather than a feminine ending. The consonantal skeleton is intact and the case endings of كل نفس are likewise unvocalized for the nominative.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وُوَفِّيَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ (Q. 3:25), “and every soul will be paid in full.” Vocalization only.

problems.arabic: مَنْ يَعْمَل مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرَا يَرَةٌ ... شَرَآ يَرَةٌ
problems.issue: يَرَةٌ twice for يَرَهُ — the pronominal hāʾ read as a tāʾ marbūṭa. Restored from Q. 99:7–8. Niasse cites the verses without the opening فاʾ (من يعمل for فمن يعمل); the citation is rendered as he gives it, not normalized to the āya.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: يَرَهُ in both places.

problems.arabic: لما اجتمع المشركون من كل جهة وأتوا إلى مدينة
problems.issue: Not OCR damage but a transcription gap the press should know about. ¶20 breaks mid-phrase at مدينة, which stands in a construct state with nothing following it, and ¶21 opens at لأجل شدة الجوع — a clause that cannot continue it. Text is missing between the two paragraphs, to the extent of the Prophet binding a stone to his belly, which ¶24’s footnote quotes. Translated as it stands, with no beginning supplied to ¶21.
problems.conjecture: Reconstruction: وأتوا إلى مدينة الرسول or إلى المدينة for the broken phrase. The lost passage between ¶20 and ¶21 cannot be reconstructed from this chunk and should be collated against the printed page.

problems.issue: The paragraph opens on an elliptical phrase with no governing verb, تقوية standing as a bare verbal noun. Kept elliptical in the English, with the missing element supplied in brackets as “[by way of] strengthening”; the subject of the omitted clause (the Prophet binding the stone to his belly, per ¶24) is not supplied.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: the lost main clause ran to the effect of عصب بطنه بالحجر لأجل شدة الجوع, تقويةً [له]. Flagged as a conjecture and not translated into the text.

problems.arabic: كأن مصباحا كبيرا أوقد ل بيت مظلم
problems.issue: ل بيت for في بيت — the preposition reduced to a single detached letter. Restored, and the restoration is certain: ¶22 repeats the same simile intact as كأن مصباحا أوقد في بيت مظلم.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: أوقد في بيت مظلم, “had been lit in a dark house.”

problems.arabic: فانكسر ثلث الجبل وضاء نور عظيم
problems.issue: وضاء lacks the alif of وأضاء. Translated as “and a great light shone”, which holds on either reading (أضاء transitive-intransitive, or ضاءَ), so nothing turns on the choice. Noted for completeness.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: وأضاء نور عظيم. الجبل in the same clause is rendered “the rock” rather than “the mountain”: the report concerns a boulder in the trench, and jabal carries that sense.

problems.issue: مي for فِي — the fāʾ read as a mīm. Restored from Q. 3:27 (تولج الليل في النهار); ¶25 has the matching clause فِڭ اِڬليْلِ with the preposition intact.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: (فِي النَّهَارِ), “into the day.”

problems.arabic: البل اثنتا عشرة ساعة والنهار كذلك
problems.issue: البل for الليل. Restored: the predicate اثنتا عشرة ساعة and the contrast with والنهار كذلك leave no alternative, and the hour-counts that follow in ¶23 and ¶25 turn on the night-day pair.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: الليل اثنتا عشرة ساعة, “the night is twelve hours.”

problems.arabic: قام وبطنه معصوب بحجر ولبثنا ثلاثة أيام لا نذوق ذواقا.. الحديث.
problems.issue: Not damage: the paragraph is the printed edition’s own footnote matter, interposed in the body between ¶23 and ¶25 and splitting Niasse’s sentence on the hours of night and day. Translated in place, not moved. The note quotes the ḥadīth from mid-sentence and breaks it off with the conventional الحديث after an ellipsis, so no beginning has been supplied; it is the source of ¶21’s لأجل شدة الجوع.
problems.conjecture: No emendation required. The press should set this paragraph as a footnote rather than as body text, and should restore the full ḥadīth from the edition’s apparatus if it is to be quoted beyond لا نذوق ذواقا.

problems.arabic: حتى دخلت دولة المسلمين في أروبا
problems.issue: أروبا for أوروبا. A spelling variant rather than a doubtful reading; the referent is not in question.
problems.conjecture: Conjecture: في أوروبا, “into Europe.”
